Patio_Lawn_and_Garden.reviewText:
I will update this as i have more information.

For now, i can only rate the company itself. The seeds arrived promptly and were well protected. They came with complete instructions for successful planting, which many seeds dont. The seeds themselves are pea sized and furry looking. In fact, they almost look like tiny candy corns.

For now, i am in the midst of stage one, which is to refrigerate the seeds for 14 days. I put them in on June 13th. On June 27th, i will continue on with the planting process and will update this review then.

June 28: Alright, pulled them out of the fridge, soaked them for around three hours, nicked the shells, and put them in soil (Miracle Grow mix with some Flower mix on top and Osmocote pellets mixed in. Turns out there were actually twelve seeds total. Put them in three starter pots (4 each)(6 inch pots, put the seeds 1/2 inch down) and set them inside my greenhouse. Now, the real waiting process begins. They are hot weather, moist soil, humid air thriving plants, so if you grow these, make sure to keep the conditions right, at least until you can put them in soil. I see them in the neighborhood, and there is basically no humidity here, so i assume as long as you keep the soil moist and they get plenty of sun, they will thrive. We shall see though.

July 15th: The first seed sprouted around five days ago. So far, that's all that has happened as of yet.

August 20th: Alright, the one that sprouted was in fact the only seed to sprout. I did follow the instructions provided to a letter,and so i am quite disappointed by the 10% germination rate. The orange "fungus" mentioned in another review might very well have been the problem. I'm left wondering if perhaps, it was actually the seed sprouting due to exposure to heat and/or humidity, thus rendering the steps provided unnecessary and harmful. Dont know for sure. The one plant that is growing is quite healthy, and seems eager to reach its full potential. However, i must change my previous glowing rating to one star. For the $8 you are going to pay overall for this product, the germination rate and questionable seed quality was unacceptable.
Patio_Lawn_and_Garden.summary: Pretty flowers. I see them throughout my neighborhood. (Updated) Only 10% germination rate.

Patio_Lawn_and_Garden.reviewText:
I have always been a wood fire BBQ kind of guy - I like meat cooked over a *real* flame, and even charcoal has always seemed to me like cheating (though I've been using charcoal Weber kettle grills for 20 years).  I never even considered a gas grill for myself for these reasons.

For my senior Mom & Dad, however, the task of lighting charcoal, etc was too much hassle, so this past weekend I went out shopping for a gas grill for them.  After going back and forth between three different home centers and Costco, I settled on this unit as by far the best "bang for the buck" in terms of build quality, performance characteristics, and ease of use for under $500.  I seriously considered going up to the Weber Genesis, but for 50% more, I just couldn't quite justify it. My requirement was good quality for under $500.  At this price point, its all about QPR (quality price ratio)...

After about a one-hour erector set project putting it all together (not difficult, just tedious and time consuming), I fired it up and let heat for about 10-15 minutes to get the manufacturing residue completely burned off.  I was immediately impressed with how hot the cooking surfaces became (and how quickly).  The nifty temp sensors at the grate level registered 700+ degrees, though I don't know how accurate they really are.

After burn-off, I tried it out with what I have found to be one of the trickiest things to grill over open flame (gas or wood/charcoal): raw marinated bone-in chicken parts.  To be done right, the chicken has to be crispy on the outside - not burned, and moist and completely cooked on the inside.  With unevenly shaped and sized chicken parts, this can be devilishly tricky.

But with this grill, I found I was able to keep the left most burner at full throttle, and the two right burners at low settings and get creative.  This allowed me to beautifully sear the skin using the left side of the grill, then finish cooking on the right side (with the BBQ closed).  The results were impressive for a gas grill, which in my experience usually turn out either damp, gray, limp chicken with no BBQ taste, or something resembling the effects of a structure fire (charred and dried out) .

One of my favorite things about this grill turned out to be that it is really easy to add wood chips for smoke flavor.  Because there is a perforated metal "screen" (the infrared reflector) under the food, it catches the wood chips and holds them at a perfect smoking temperature where they will smolder but not burn up.

Speaking of flare-ups, this grill did NOT exhibit flare-ups at all.  Even with fatty pieces of chicken that had been marinated in an olive oil mixture, there was almost no burning or excessive smoking, even on the "searing" side of the hot grill.

When turned down low, I also found the evenness of the heating surface to be impressively consistent, and the large stainless "grill" surface not only made great marks on the food, but also did not stick as badly as most coated steel or iron grill surfaces do.

On the con side, I can imagine that the perforated screen is going to require some periodic maintenance to keep it clean.  The good news is that it comes out in three easy-to-handle sections shaped like little trays, each holding a section of grill.  You pull the "tray" up and out, then lift the grill surface out of the tray making both very easy to clean.

One final note - I also prepared a boneless leg of lamb on the grill using a "generic" rotisserie (Grill-Pro brand).  it *barely* fit between the closed lid and the grill surface, but again, the infrared cooking system worked great.  I warmed it up at full throttle for about 5-10 minutes before mounting the marinated lamb roast, then allowed it to sear beautifully for about 15 minutes.  Then I turned the burners all down to their lowest settings, threw on a thumb-sized stick of oak from one of our trees, and dropped the lid.

An hour and a half later, we enjoyed one of the best lamb roasts I have ever had.

Recommended, especially if you can get it for the price I paid (which was about less than Amazon's currently listed price)

Pros:
*Great heat output for searing.  I've not used a gas grill that gets a hotter cooking surface (other than commercial equipment)
*Even distribution of heat for predictable results, very little flare-up.
*Good low-temp performance
*Easy to use wood chips for flavor, unlike many gas grills
*Good (for its price-point) build quality in the hood and firebox.  Cabinets are thin stainless steel.

Cons:
*Bottom 1/2 of construction is a bit flimsy, but better than many at this price point
*Requires pre-heating for about 10 minutes for best results
*Periodic clean-up will be required for optimum performance, and cleanup will be messy

----------
September 2014 update

I can't believe it has been over 5 years since I originally wrote this review.  Interestingly, it has gotten more attention that a lot of my other reviews, so I'll felt I should write a quick update.  I'm visiting my folks and used it three times in the last 4 days.  It has been outside, but covered by a good quality "Brinkmann" cover.  It still performs great and works as well as it did on Day 1.  One thing I've noticed is that it is very sensitive to getting low on fuel.  When the propane tank gets down to about 1/4 full, I swap out to a fresh tank - otherwise it just doesn't get as hot (and I like grilling steaks on a HOT grill).

Great for grilling steaks, chicken, and fish.  Not so great for rotisserie.  if you want to be able to put stuff on a rotisserie, I'd recommend looking elsewhere (the lid fits too close and rubs against the meat).  But for grilling cuts of meat, chicken, or fish, this is a really great piece of gear for the money.  Even fillets of relatively soft fish like trout and salmon don't stick to the grill, and fatty pieces of steak or chicken don't flare up and burn.  I continue to be impressed.
Patio_Lawn_and_Garden.summary: After first couple of uses, I am very impressed!

Patio_Lawn_and_Garden.reviewText:
I bought this unit because I was hoping to become a little greener by ditching my gas powered trimmer and I was willing to make some trade-offs to get there.  Dragging a drop cord around my yard was actually less work than I thought and not having to maintain a second gas can in my garage is a plus.  Anyway, the unit is well balanced and adequately powered to cover all my needs on my 1/2 acre suburbia-land yard.  I use the edging configuration the most.  It covers my landscaping brick borders, sidewalks, driveway and curb edges.  Switching between trimming and edging configurations is a fairly easy operation involving pushing a button to rotate the head 180 degrees and snaping a guide into or out of position.
My only real gripe is with the automatic string advance.  When it works it is great.  However, when it doesn't, you have to turn the unit over, pop the orange cap off and careful unwind a half turn off both spools without letting the string fly off the spools into a giant mess.  In general, it advances the string too slowly for rough surfaces like concrete or brick but too quickly for vinyl or wood.  When someone figures out how to let the operator unwind the string manually from a trigger/release without stopping they will dominate this market.
I took a star off my rating because of the automatic string advance, and overall I still like and use the unit because on every other aspect it met or exceeded my expectations.
Patio_Lawn_and_Garden.summary: Pretty Good Trimmer

Patio_Lawn_and_Garden.reviewText:
Over the last 8 years I've gone through 2 of the smaller Farmhouse model, and have been very pleased with the how they protected my tropical plants from the occasional freezes we get in South Louisiana.  This year I needed more space so I decided to get the larger Farmhouse XL version.  I figured it would be more difficult it would be to assemble, but I had put together the smaller version by myself so I figured I would be able to manage this one too.

Well I was wrong.  Believe me and the instruction that come with the XL version: you will need 3 people to put this thing up!!! (Or two people and two sturdy trees.)

Assembly of the greenhouse is pretty straightforward if you follow the instruction to the letter, and keep telling yourself that all the pieces WILL eventually fit together.  You also need a lot of brute strength, sweat, and some cursing.  The fit is unbelievable tight, and after assembling the first few poles you think, "no way will this thing fit together, they sent me the wrong poles."  But in the end all the pieces do fit, and you will get the greenhouse in the picture.

Observations:

&#10003 The greenhouse is easy to assemble if you have 3 people and a lot of brute strength to push, pull and force the poles into position.

&#10003 You will need a heater to keep the greenhouse warm on cold days/nights.  Without a heater the interior of the greenhouse is the same temperature as the air outside.

&#10003 On a sunny day the temperature inside the greenhouse will skyrocket.  You need to monitor the temperature and open the windows and the doors as needed.

&#10003 It gets very humid inside the greenhouse.  You need a heater that can take all the moisture or move the heater in and out every day.

&#10003 The greenhouse will only last 3-4 seasons.  The fiberglass frame creates a lot of pressure against the plastic shell, and after a few years the plastic around the pressure points starts to fray.  The greenhouse also gets very dirty from dead leaves and bugs that accumulate around the bottom edge.

&#10003 Even though the product description says the XL has 2 screen doors and 12 screen windows there is NO screening.  Honestly I never used the door screens on my smaller Farmhouse so the lack of screens does not bother me.  The greenhouse is in my fenced back yard so I don't have a problem with animals getting in.  Although I do get lots of flying bugs, frogs, and once a small grass snake.

&#10003 The product description also said that the XL can zip to another greenhouse, but this is not accurate either.  The regular size Farmhouse had the zipper which allowed you to chain multiple greenhouses together, but the XL does not.

&#10003 This is a minor issue, but I not like the green cords that are used for high wind tie downs.  The green color makes them hard to see.  I've run into them many times while taking the dog outside in the middle of the night.  I now use neon orange cord as my tie downs.

&#10003 Disassembling the green house is a snap. One person can take it down in a matter of minutes.  But good luck getting the greenhouse back into its storage bag.  Folding it small enough takes a lot of brute force and "Twister" like moves.

 So all-in-all I'm very pleased with my XL Farmhouse.  It is a pain to assemble, but 45 minutes of aggravation is worth it to save all my delicate plants.
Patio_Lawn_and_Garden.summary: Great Greenhouse but really do need 3 people to assemble

Heavy duty tubing is perfect for waterfalls that have a lot of power in pushing the water long and tall distances.  My pump is a 5500gph pump and this tubing handles it just fine.  The tubing I had in place was chewed up by my dogs, so I cannot discount the quality of the tubing for that.  he previous tubing (same as this one), lasted me for 5 years without any issue.  If you are doing a waterfall project and need some nice, high quality, heavy duty tubing, this is your best bet!
For installation, it is best to let this sit in the sun for at least 15 minutes to get nice and soft.  It makes it easier to put onto connectors, fittings and bending.  It is virtually impossible to do this in cold or cool weather.  If you have to install in cool weather, use a hair dryer around the fittings to get it warm.

Pros:
Heavy duty!
Lasts for a long time.
Handles high water pressure/volume.

Cons:
Somewhat pricey.

Patio_Lawn_and_Garden.reviewText:
Last winter the deer ate almost everything in the yard, even though most were surrounded by 4' fencing that had deterred them in the past. The deer just pushed them down and stood on the crumpled remains to get to higher branches. Even the supposedly deer-resistant holly bushes got eaten. Lo, these many months later, they still look ragged. This winter, we're trying out this netting.

It went on with little trouble, it just took the first bush to figure out how best to handle it - one roll wrapped two holly and two rhododendron. From a distance, I can't tell they're wrapped at all - the mesh is so fine, and the black color helps to hide it as well. The netting is doubled over on the roll so after unrolling you have to unfold it to its full height. I found the best way to do this is to first find the side where the fold is and keep that on top. Put the roll against the bush, positioning it so the roll is on the outside. Affix the end of the back side to the bush with zip ties, attaching at the top by the fold and at the bottom. This keeps the netting from moving while unrolling. Unroll the netting, walking around the bush and keeping the netting snug until the starting point is reached. This stuff stretches, so overlap wasn't really needed. Cut with scissors. Secure the bottom of the cut end with zip ties. Now find the free bottom edge and lift the netting to full height, placing it on the shrub at the desired height. Secure top and bottom edges with zip ties in several spots around the bush.

The netting sticks to every twig and branch, so not many zip ties are needed, especially at the top - just enough to keep it from blowing or falling as wind moves the tree. More zips were needed at the bottom, as this is where the deer will try to push under it. In the spring it'll likely be difficult to remove intact - it catches on everything - so I'm anticipating this to be a single-use product. I'll report back in the spring and give it five starts if it keeps the deer from eating the landscaping.

Update 3/27/17: It worked great in year 1 but year 2 saw a heavy snowfall and pack of ravenous deer combine to overwhelm it. The weight of 2' of snow pushed holly and rhododendron branches toward the ground. Some of the netting tore from the stress. The deer, standing in the deep snow and on top of the lower branches, could reach the unprotected upper branches while their weight pulled the netting lower and tore it further.
Patio_Lawn_and_Garden.summary: Worked well until 2' of heavy snow made for easy pickings

Patio_Lawn_and_Garden.reviewText:
I have 7 of these around the perimeter of my yard and they have worked fine for the past 2 years.  I bought these (one or two at a time) because I have very hard well water and normal impact sprinklers would clog up with calcium deposits.  I haven't had any problems with these Orbit gear-drive sprinklers.

There are 3 controls for the units.  The green disk on top sets the spray effect (short, medium, or long) buy inserting a tooth into the water stream.  So if you want a long distance, the tooth is minimal.  If you want a short distance then the tooth is large.  I just rotate the top green disk to set this.

The second control is the next ring down that controls the spray pattern: stream, mist, etc.  There are about 8 options (sorry, I didn't walk outside to count them).

The last control are the two green rings at the bottom and these control the start and stop sweep angle.  So I can go all the way around (360 degrees), or limit it to a smaller angle.  Note however, that even if you a line the start and stop, it goes all the way around one way, then back all the way around the other.  That's just the way the gear-drive Orbit unit works.  It won't keep spinning around and around the same way like a free spinning impact sprinkler (with the reversing stops removed).  It isn't a problem, just be aware of it ahead of time.

I gave this only 4 stars because there are 2 things that this design lacks:  (1) a hose screw ring and (2) a range limiter.  (1) In order to screw this onto a garden hose, you have to spin the entire silver colored body onto the hose.  Not a big deal since I use this in a semi-permanent installation.  (2) A range limiter would allow me to set some small portion that limits the range (instead of limiting the range for the whole circle).  I'd like to use the "long" range to form a large circle, but also have some range limiter to prevent the spray from hitting the house (and calcifying the wall and wooden fence).  Other people make stand-alone metal posts that do this, I'd just like it to be included in the sprinkler.

Anyway, I've been very happy with my seven 2-year old units.

Scott Nelson
Patio_Lawn_and_Garden.summary: greater sprinkler that doesn't clog up

Patio_Lawn_and_Garden.reviewText:
Here is what I like:

Fairly lightweight

Sharp

Nice holder/protector

Handle shape shouldn't allow flying out of hand

What I found a bit unlikeable:

Sharp edge is a bit fragile. After using for a few hours the edge was a bit beat-up-looking. And no, I did not strike anything but the end of the log I was splitting.

The axe will get stuck. It comes out fairly easily most of the time but several times I had to work to get the blade free.

The axe bounced off some of the wood I was attempting to split - would not penetrate. Bouncing off was nowhere near as bad as it was with my 8 pound splitter, but was still more of a problem than I expected from reading the reviews. On the other hand I also have a Gransfors-Bruks small splitting axe and it does NOT bounce off.

Some logs I worked on (all cut to 16" long and from 6" to 16" diameter hardwoods - oak, maple, some kind of nut) required multiple hits to start a split. I beat a few into submission with this axe and was disappointed that it took so many hits to finish splitting. I found the easiest way to do the job was to use this axe to make starter splits (one or two hits on each spot I wanted a split) then finish it with the 8 pounder.

Bottom line is this axe is very good for some logs, especially straight-grained oak, which split cleanly with one hit. It is not as good if the wood is hard enough and dense enough to cause the axe to bounce off. You will also NOT want to leave your heavy splitting maul in the garage - it will still be the best tool for some wood. I haven't touched up the edge of this axe yet to remove the ragged edge from a few hundred hits on log ends but when I do I think I will try making the edge angle a bit less acute to give it a bit more strength. As is the case with every hand-splitting tool the wood is the determining factor. No one tool works for everything.

I have a LOT of experience splitting firewood by hand. I've been splitting my own wood since 1978 (with a few years break when I didn't have a stove) and have tried lots of different tools. Most have been commercial axes and various wedges plus a few I've made myself. In the end nothing beats wedges and a sledge hammer when a splitting axe just doesn't do the job.
Patio_Lawn_and_Garden.summary: Not quite as good as I hoped

With this unit, I placed the "outdoor" probe inside of the fridge, and then just propped the unit on top of the fridge.  So the "inside" temp reading is the office temp, while the "outside" reading is actually the inside of the refrigerator.  Now the first thing I do each morning is to check the recorded MIN / MAX temperature readings since the last time I reset them.  If the "outside" MAX reading (i.e., the inside of the fridge) is something well over 50 deg F, I know that the power had been out for a while.  It's paid off several times already.

Patio_Lawn_and_Garden.reviewText: My husband loves this leaf blower!  He has had a few corded blowers before, but really wanted a cordless one.  We looked for quite some time and the ones we found didn't have enough power.  This blower has plenty of power and the battery lasts a long time.  It's so light and easy he uses it a couple of times a week.
Patio_Lawn_and_Garden.summary: light and easy to use.

Patio_Lawn_and_Garden.reviewText: I originally bought this pressure washer to pressure clean the moss on my stone patio. It was starting to cause people to slip. The build and setup out of the box was straight forward and I away a gliding through the moss like hot knives through butter. I've have since found myself pressure washing all my decks, the wood siding on my house and also now have started using it to wash my car. The built quality is superb. The hardware and attachments work flawlessly. And, whats nice is how the compressor inside only makes noise when the trigger in engaged. I am super happy with this purchase.

Patio_Lawn_and_Garden.reviewText: Squirrels have destroyed a lot of our patio furniture.  Through trial and (mostly) error, we learned not to buy aluminum or outdoor wicker or wood.  They will leave steel furniture alone after a taste nibble, but it's harder to find and there is maintenance and winter storage involved.  We thought we would give Polywood a try (what were we thinking?  Well, to be honest we were thinking "lazy":  soap and water for maintenance and leaving the furniture outside in the winter; it still sounds like a good idea.)  All went well the first season, but this summer the chewy rascals wreaked havoc on the expensive stuff.  This product is the only one that has deterred the squirrels for longer than an a few hours.  We sprayed it on every morning and again in the late afternoon for 3 or 4 days.  The squirrels, so far (fingers crossed, knock on wood, all that) have left the furniture alone now.  We'll keep spraying mornings till squirrels have been re-trained to go to the neighbors' furniture.  If this product does not keep performing the remainder of this season, we will update our review to let you know.
Patio_Lawn_and_Garden.summary: Finally, something that works!

Patio_Lawn_and_Garden.reviewText: I bought this to use with a Traeger and it is awesome.  I have been eating veggies cooked on the grill that I marinated and they are delicious.  It goes in the dishwasher, is sturdy and easy to use.  I marinate in a bag/dish, pour right through the grill basket to drain and into the grill it goes.  It is also large and will hold lots of food.  Great purchase for the grill.  I have not used it with fish yet but plan on cooking some soon.

Patio_Lawn_and_Garden.reviewText: We bought this not sure what to expect, but it has exceeded what we "thought" might happen.  It has raised the temperature of our pool by 10-12 degrees.  It has kept it free of Algae now that the sun is not beating down on the water.  It keeps the chemicals from dissipating so quickly.  Our vacuum is not having to be used as often. Our pool is crystal clear for the first time ever!  We couldn't be happier.  We are just thrilled. We live in So. Cal and for the first time we were swimming in our pool in Mid-May.  The best part was that it was 85 degrees in the water and we didn't have to use our heater at all. The temps have been seasonal-not too hot during the day and cool at night.  This same product at our local pool store was 215.00.  Highly recommend to anyone with a pool.  It will certainly extend your pool season.
Patio_Lawn_and_Garden.summary: AWESOME!  Saves $$$$

Patio_Lawn_and_Garden.reviewText: Great can, in use for 3 years, no problems. The optional hose allows me to pour can in a cars tank. The spout on most cans will do this easy. Patio_Lawn_and_Garden.reviewText: The manufacturer claims that the Dynatrap produces carbon dioxide (CO2) through an exclusive titanium dioxide (TiO2) surface.  Indeed TiO2 surfaces will catalyze the production of CO2 when a suitable hydrocarbon is present.  I am a chemist and know about these things.  Since the Dynatrap does not use propane, what is the source of hydrocarbon?  Insect bodies?  Small amounts of hydrocarbons in the air?  Because the claim did not make sense to me, I decided to use a CO2 meter (a CO2Meter model AZ0004) to  determine whether CO2 is actually produced by the Dynatrap. I placed the meter just below the basket where the insects are trapped due to the downward flow air from the fan.  The CO2 meter read 396 ppm, which is the same as outdoor air in my area.  I placed the meter at several spots  around the Dynatrap and detected NO CO2 above the ambient level of 396 ppm normally found in air.  In other words, the Dynatrap did not produce any measurable CO2.  By comparison, one breath from me toward the meter caused it to spike its reading from 396 ppm to 1944 ppm - a five fold increase!  I then measured the CO2 output from a Megacatch Ultra mosquito trap that runs on a CO2 cylinder.  The Megacatch releases CO2 in puffs.  At a modest CO2 release setting of 2 (the Megacatch has release settings between 1 and 5), the CO2 meter reading would spike to about 950 ppm with each puff - about 2.5-fold increase over the ambient level in air.  Since CO2 is the major attractant for mosquitos, the test with the Dynatrap was disappointing.  However, its black color, water tray and UV light serve as insect attractants despite no CO2 being produced by the Dynatrap  After running the Dynatrap 24/7 for a week, the basket was filled mostly with moths but there were some mosquitos as well.  The Megacatch had trapped about five times more mosquitos than the Dynatrap.  The water tray of the Dynatrap had some drowned beetles and moths.  I give the Dynatrap a 3 star rating because it does catch some mosquitos and it is not terribly expensive as mosquito traps go.  It is much less expensive than Mosquito Magnets and Megacatchs.  The Dynatrap would likely trap many more mosquitos if it actually produced CO2.
Patio_Lawn_and_Garden.summary: Does NOT produce CO2.

Patio_Lawn_and_Garden.reviewText:
We were told by local nursery that these tree's were real expensive and do not do well in Wisconsin weather.  We ignored the nursery and ordered a 3 year graft through Amazon. it was not much more than a real frail branch grafted onto a root but the color of the leaves was amazing.  For about two weeks that is when the leaves started falling off.  Been about 4 weeks now and showing no sign of growth and very few leaves left on it.

Update 1-2012:
Not really any thing positive about this tree yet.  After a complete summer several of the few leaves that came out since planting had blown off the tree.  The tree did not grow a bit during the summer and only 2 new leaves grew out all summer.  We'll see what nex year brings.

Update 2-2013:
This tree did leaf out very nicely the second year.  Not a lot of growth but leaves are very nice.  Wisconsin weather had no ill affects on the tree.  Another 10 years and it might get 6 ft tall, but i doubt it.  If planning as a centerpiece in the front yard you may want to find something that would have a little faster growth.
Patio_Lawn_and_Garden.summary: Emperor 1 Japanese Maple, 3 year graft

Patio_Lawn_and_Garden.reviewText: These were just the right size for my fairy garden.  I actually thought when I ordered them that they would be make from some sort of plastic.  They are actually made from Styrofoam.  After I added them to my garden, after a couple days a couple of the mushroom had the top melted off. Bought new from Amazon. Absolutely no instructions included. The SunJoe (SnowJoe) website wasn't that great. I finally found quick-start guide which also sucked and doesn't address the state the product arrived in. It was very simple to put together, but the the Type A part of me wanted to be sure I was doing it correctly. They also have a YouTube video, but it skips several steps as I received many more pieces not assembled than were in their video.

Product works ok, but the head could stand to be a little heavier. It has a mind of its own from time-to-time. As with any time you're power-washing, don't wear anything you don't mind getting wet/dirty.

I had to redrill those two.  The garage door is F ing awful.  The man door sliders suck.  I will be replacing those two soon.  Over all the garage seems good after going through the hell of building it.  I gave it 3 stars because of what I already mentioned.

My next option is to move it closer to the places we most frequently enter and exit out house, which is by the garage and the back door. If you're buying this to reduce a large bug problem outside, it may not be a great option. I'll come back and update if things change after the move.

Patio_Lawn_and_Garden.reviewText: Still deciding on this grass seed.  Seed was planted in a topcoat layer of 2 inches of fresh topsoil laid down over existing topsoil.  Have sown many yards before and have followed standard protocol of watering/feeding the lawn. It came up nicely in February, but quickly started to struggle when the southern (TN) heat ramped up in May/June.  Isn't that the exact weather this seed is supposed to be tolerant of?  Have needed to spend lots of extra money treating the lawn since and it still struggles during hot cycles of more than a few days without excessive watering.  It's been months since sowing, when will it stop struggling and settle in?

I repainted the deck afterwards and then coated the deck and grass shoot as directed. Grass stuck to the shoot the first time using and you wouldn't know I put anything on the deck itself after mowing a few times. I have tried several different brands of this stuff along with rubberized truck undercoating and nothing really holds up for long. I guess I need to make sure I drop the deck every year or so, clean it and repaint to make it last longer. BTW I mow three personal acres every week and some of it is pretty rough (small rocks, debris, etc) so I use my mower more than most general home users.

BUT... the mechanism for loading and feeding the line is TERRIBLE.  It's a huge pain to load new line and while in the use the line often retreats back into the head. Patio_Lawn_and_Garden.reviewText:
Doesn't hold as much as I thought it would - we will have both sides full with only a few weeks of kitchen/food scraps.  Door is also not the easiest to slide back and forth - it's not a smooth glide and could be difficult to manage for those with limited hand strength.

Pretty sturdy though and I like the spinning action.

Patio_Lawn_and_Garden.reviewText:
The product arrived damaged. A piece had been broken out of the orange blade housing near the right rear wheel. The plastic mount on the right side where the handle attached to the deck was also cracked. This mower appears to have been returned and the resold. The shipping box was not the original - two plain cardboard boxes had been taped together to create one large box for the mower. Part of the original Black & Decker box had been used inside to create some internal box packing. Interestingly, included in the shipping container was 3/4 of a pint plastic bottle of 4 cycle lawnmower oil!

The mower is considered hazardous material, soit could not be returned. Amazon was very prompt about refunding the purchase price.

In spite of the shipping damage, the mower was sufficiently functional to test out before it totally breaks down.

I have 4000-5000 sq ft of St. Augustine grass. The lawn was fairly high since my old mower broke down a few weeks ago, but not particularly thick due to shade. After an initial overnight charge, the mower handled the hour of work without any apparent loss of power. The high grass was not a problem either - the motor slowed a bit where the grass was thickest, but did not bog down.

The single lever height adjustment is really a nice feature, working very smoothly and easily. The light weight, low noise level, and instant start are welcome changes from the old gas machine.

The battery does not have any power indicator - a desirable feature that is missing.

The mower seems somewhat flimsy (note shipping damage above). You feel the need to be extra careful when maneuvering around trees, fences and landscape timbers so as not to damage a wheel or crack something. The wheels are fairly small and narrow, allowing the mover to sink into any turf that is soft or spongy. Was not a big problem on my test mow, but when I have to use the bag during leaf season (that is spring for us in Florida), the extra weight will make it more noticeable. Wider wheels would distribute the weight better and roll easier.
Patio_Lawn_and_Garden.summary: Major shipping issues plus a bonus gift.

Patio_Lawn_and_Garden.reviewText:
It's a great idea but is built too poorly to be worth investing in. I bought the kit that includes timer, 4 way splitter and 2 valves. One of the two valves failed within 90 days; i disassembled it, there is nothing visibly broken, and the filter and washer are clean.
The second valve lasted almost a full year before it did the same thing - no broken parts or wires or anything, just stops working and emits a high-pitched whine as water struggles to go through a closed valve.
The rub here is, you get used to not having to water and don't realize the valve has failed until you notice your dead plants or hear the whine. That ticks me off; if I water daily, I know when I missed a day. If I let Orbit do the job it may cause a disaster when it decides to not work. Buyer Beware - as noted elsewhere, the quality is wildly inconsistent.
UPDATE AUGUST 2008: NOW the "brass" 4 way splitter has disintegrated, within 1 year. It isn't all brass - the neck isn't, it's some thin composite, it just wore away, and my spigot has a cover to protect it from rain and sun. As for valve, I'm a sucker; tried a second one now that Vigoro is distributing the brand. It failed within 10 days. I took it back to the store and took a hammer to the rest of the useless system, and went with a Melnor 2-valve timer. Much simpler operation and reliability so far.
Patio_Lawn_and_Garden.summary: poor quality control, beware

Patio_Lawn_and_Garden.reviewText: I bought three different pop-up canopy tents at the same time and compared them. They were: $66: Tangkula 10'X10' EZ POP UP Canopy Tent Gazebo Wedding Party Shelter Carry Bag (Green) $90: AmazonBasics Pop-Up Canopy Tent - 10 x 10 ft $150: CORE 10' x 10' Instant Shelter Pop-Up Canopy Tent with Wheeled Carry Bag, Gray The bottom line is that the much cheaper Tangkula tent was better quality in every way than the AmazonBasics tent with the exception that the AmazonBasics tent had wheels on the bottom of the bag. If you really want the bells and whistles then buy the $150 CORE tent which I think is worth it IF you really like the bells and whistles and don't mind spending two and a half times as much. I wouldn't spend the $150 again myself - I'd definitely buy the $66 tent or one of the many similar ones on sale here - but if you can't bring yourself to believe that the $66 tent is almost exactly as good as the $150 version, go ahead and spend the $150 - you get a much nicer bag and it's the only one of the three with air vents in the top. Don't buy the $90 AmazonBasics thinking it's better made because quite the reverse is true: the $66 tent is a lot better. I took photographs of the main features of the three tents and I put them side by side in three columns, cheapest (Tangkula) on the left, then AmazonBasics in the middle and the most expensive, Core, on the right. To reiterate: for value or price, buy the Tangkula. For quality, buy the Core. Don't buy the AmazonBasics, it is the worst of the three and not the cheapest.
Patio_Lawn_and_Garden.summary: Poor value. Buy either the cheaper one or the more expensive one (see review).

Patio_Lawn_and_Garden.reviewText:
Been using my Weedeater One now for about 3 years - I've found it to be a fairly well designed minimalist riding mower, but with increasing negatives. The round plastic gear at the top of the steering column under the steering wheel did round off the first mowing season, but the replacement part is metal & won't round off. More horsepower would be nice, but I've had no real problems climbing shallow gradients; if you have steep hills, you need a more powerful mower.

I added the bagger kit during the 2nd mowing season (ordered through Amazon); directions are simple & accurate & I had no problem installing it. Except for the small bags, the bagger works ok. Note: the rubber seal that fits around the edge of the bagger cover hole is purposely not round (neither is the hole) - just rotate it to fit the hole when installing and it should stay in place when lifting the cover to empty the bags. Also, be sure to use the replacement blade in the kit - it creates more suction and gets the grass/leaves up into the bags better than the original blade.

Finally, to the point of this review: the small original bags only have a total capacity of 3 bushels & thus must be emptied often. After some research online, I found the exact same design bags available from Sears with double the capacity (6 bushels). The longer bags have Sears part number 400226, description is "bag soft" or "container"; cost is $46.71 per bag (plus shipping) and can be ordered from Sears Parts Direct at 1-800-252-1698. The online price is higher ($52.50), so save some money & order by phone. The replacement bags are pricey, but they transform the Weedeater One bagger into a truly usable tool for sucking up those grass clippings & leaves.

SEE 3RD MOWING SEASON UPDATE BELOW & DON'T BUY A WEEDEATER ONE!
Patio_Lawn_and_Garden.summary: Bigger bags available

Patio_Lawn_and_Garden.reviewText:
The box had arrived damage where the spool head was sticking out. But no damage to it that I can see. I had to wait for a couple of days due to heavy rain storms here. Yesterday was the very first time using this unit. As it's the 4th 40v 4amp Greenworks garden tool I've purchased on Amazon this year. I had purchased RYOBI from Home Depot their version of the 40v cordless lithium ion string trimmer and edger. Well that one and this one seems to share a lot. Like they don't advance the line when they should and suffer from the glitch that causes it. Greenworks model is better, it allows you to get a deep trench edging right deep into the dirt. Keeping that steady is a challenge! But the line feed is the major selling point here. These units are suppose to automatically advance the line for you. I need such a feature. But after getting 3/4 of the line stool down, sure enough I could see that the line never advanced out. Just like the RYOBI model from Home Depot did on me. I had said oh no not again!

Not even tightly rounded like it should be. Strange how both models are doing the same thing. These are made by Homelite then since that's how makes the RYOBI but Greenwise has multi-head adjustments instead of the 90' degree turning head it has flex pole angles giving you all sorts of ranges to trim and edge. I find that a very neat feature to have. My edge of my lawn looks better than it did using the RYOBI RY40210 93WH where has the Greenworks model this one has 146WH and it's more powerful than the RYOBI one. The only other difference is the line advancement one has 13" on RY40210 and the Greenworks has 12". But you only get 6" on both models. When you buy the units you get the full length but something odd happens when you use it. I guess the one reviewer was right it cuts the line in half.

Also the spool of line when it gets to 1/2 or 3/4 it won't spool out any more. I have to stop it and then do a manually feed of line through the hole then it continues on. Best not even bother with that line notch to hold the line as either that feature is defective or it just doesn't cut the water. I had order that 3x pack of line spool here off Amazon just in case. So now I know this model going to end up being replaced or exchanged. There just not enough choices in this market for such a unit and not at the full battery DC 146WH. You don't want the 93WH not going to last too long an power dies too fast on the RYOBI model.

I've given this just 3 stars because the button layout is poor on the Greenworks model. My fingers hurt after pushing and pressing the control buttons. They could have made it better. Then it's top heavy with the fat battery on top. Same design as the RYOBI 40v but that one is more balanced and ligher. But RYOBI the wheel use on the edger is weakest feature it wears out too fast. The one on the Greenworks is more heavy duty and can be easy to change out in parts. They need to tighten the knot at the factory. I had to do it. The controls on both models are the weakest areas too. RYOBI it could break off as you got to grabs to long rods as with the Greenworks you and push and grab. The push part hurts your finger after a long time.

Greenworks did a better job with how the unit flexes and center loop holder has better flex feature as well. I did see a hole on the top to hang the unit on the wall. There is also a strap clip holder but that feature didn't come with this model. Same with the RYOBI.

Sending this one back to Amazon to get one that does have Auto Advancement in Line going to be interesting to see what I get back? One more defect I've notice was the battery charger unit when you push in the battery it still shows red and green on a dead battery. That's because you have to use a rubber mallet to tap the battery into the charger for it to work right. I did see that the one pin was bent. Un-bending it didn't seem to do the trick. That means it off alignment.

I best get this ready to go back to them tomorrow... 6.1.12 for a replacement!

I'll keep you updated on my progress..

6.7.12
Replacement had arrived. This one was much better. Less than 10 minutes I had assemble it. I did the flip around for the cutter put so the length will be longer than shorter. If you find yours defective just let Amazon know and they'll take good care of you. The battery charger was easy to use this time slide and lock. Not slide and bend like prior one did!

**6.14.12***
This is just keeping worst and worst. I see others are complaining about the weight yep I have too join club on that one. But biggest issue right now is that the auto-line head is not working as advertise. It won't advance! I have to stop open the cover and feed in the line. Now the 90 degree head won't lock into place either. No I didn't use my foot. I had stopped and did this manual with my hand. Both adjustments are not working like the spring or hinge inside is broken. This is a shame it has full power off the bat. But Edging is awful. Not balance and no auto-line feed. To me when I first got the second replacement it work with a full line as the line gets down then there is issues. I had even ordered replacement lines. This one going back and I'll looking at Toro 24V for a replacement off Amazon.

Pros
Power of 40V 4amp 146WH

Cons
Edging doesn't mean auto-line feed
Line is only less than 6-inches never 10-13 inches as the box reads the the label on the unit
Battery seems to drain much more on the model
90 degree adjustment head can stick or not lock into position
Adjustable head from the pole can also not lock into angle positions
Weight Balance is off
Hold the trigger button and the other grabber button for advancements doesn't always work out right
Quality on this one is not up to par
Patio_Lawn_and_Garden.summary: Line Didn't Advance on my Second Replacement

Home_and_Kitchen.reviewText: Many of the things I'll say have been mentioned by other reviewers. Some slices were uneven. It sometimes jammed. They say to turn the holder 1/4 inch on every other slice according to the only English speaking video I could find on YouTube about this mandolin. Better if you julienne then cut into cubes with a knife. You must trim the vegetable to no wider than 2 1/2 inches in diameter to fit inside the dome of the holder and be penetrated by the prongs; long items like carrots have to be cut into short lengths. But I'm happy to have it, I'll might eat more vegetables because of it; it's fast to use. I don't know if all mandolins share these problems. I've read the other reviews about how it doesn't work with really soft or hard items or items that are really small or large. I also own a food processor with the optional slicing and julienne blades which I much recommend more than using this mandoline.

to the other reviews. It's ok - I haven't returned it, but that's largely because of the PITA of boxing it up, getting an RMA and sending it back. It works, but I'm disappointed.

As far as the complaint about the top tier being ticky-tacky and the floor of the top falling through too easily, it seemed that way to me at first but I found that if you have it properly seated, it doesn't slip out, unless you accidentally poke it with your fingers from the bottom. However, I find that I am unlikely to use the feature of needing to remove the bottom of the second tier and would instead be more happy with a second tier with a solid bottom.

Yes, initially it seems not well put together - ticky tacky. but so far it has stood up for me.

The biggest thing I don't like about this is the reservoir is built in. You can't refill it during the cooking and although it might not be a problem for others, the fact that I have to unplug it to empty out the reservoir is a real pita in my kitchen.

Having said that, it's been growing on me over the months I've had it. I've used it to cook rice, quinoa, chicken and of course vegetables. There was some issue with the quinoa because 2 cups was WAY too much for the little bowl they give you, but it cooked up fine. I am in love with how steamers hardboil eggs. 20 minutes makes them just perfect. The first time I cooked chicken it was way overdone at 20 minutes, another time (when the chicken was about 1% still frozen) it took closer to 25 minutes, so it's definitely not a set it and forget it for something sensitive like chicken. And of course it depends big the breasts are.

Technically, I haven't run out of steam while cooking, though when I did the quinoa, that's because I had to stop and reorganize everything halfway through the cooking. Just the same, it's terribly inconvenient and a poor design.

I definitely recommend getting a steamer and the timer is what makes this super practical, but maybe not this one. Look for a reservoir that can be filled while you cook.

I purchased this because it is described as having wheels.  I thought it would allow me to slide both the drawer and the Keurig machine that would sit on top of it forward and away from my cabinets.  Unfortunately, you have to lift it up to slide it forwards.  That doesn't work well with the coffee maker on top of it, so it is being returned unused.  Too bad.  Would work fine for someone with slightly different needs.

The product arrived in a timely manner, which was good. As for the performance, I am generally satisfied. However, it does leave some room to be desired. I selected this product for the price. Since it is designed similarly to the more expensive, leading model, made by The Pampered Chef, I figured that it would be a pretty decent product. It is pretty decent for a rough cut. Yet, it does not  dice as crisply as I would like it to.
Home_and_Kitchen.summary: which was good. As for the performance

Home_and_Kitchen.reviewText: These clothespins are very light weight and seem to be fairly cheaply made.  They'll work fine for most clothes I think, but heavy duty items like blankets, rugs, and jeans seem to be too heavy for them.  They have a tendancy to come apart if opened too and not pulled vertically off the clothes line.  For the price, they are a decent set of clothespins.  I'll probably buy some more heavy duty clothes pins and continue to use these also.

These are great little boxes for organizing my bathroom vanity. Perfect size and seem quite sturdy.

That being said, they still use the horribly sticky labels that many reviewers have mentioned. It's not a deal-breaker for me, but it will be time consuming to remove. I forgot about the reviews I had read, and when they arrived I quickly pulled off the labels on the first box. Big mistake, as you can see in the photos. They use several extremely adhesive circles per label. My hubby threw it into hot soapy water and was able to scrub it off cleanly in about 5 minutes.

On the second box I took my ever-loving time peeling each circle from the corners of the label. SLOWLY. Like snail pace. And I was able to remove the adhesive cleanly. Too bad I have 4 more boxes to go!  I will save the rest of the peeling for later tonight while I binge-watch Fixer Upper haha.

 I wouldn't use Goo Gone or any acetone product as I think it would cloud the plastic, as other reviewers have mentioned.  UPDATE: I tried a 1:1 mix of vegetable oil and baking soda to remove a particularly sticky spot. It worked like a charm, but the abrasive nature of the baking soda did in fact scratch the plastic and left it a bit cloudy. See photos- clouded side vs unclouded side. Still better than the sticky spot!

Anyway as I said, not a deal-breaker for me.  Yes I paid money for them, and I still feel it was a fair price despite the extra work. I mean honestly, I clicked a magic button on my phone and these arrived on my doorstep two days later. That's pretty amazing. I don't want to lose sight of that!  Yay Amazon!
Home_and_Kitchen.summary: Yes they still use horrible stickers for labels

Home_and_Kitchen.reviewText: Not a bad fragrance although a little strong.  Perhaps starting with not bad makes it sound worse than it is.  It is a pleasant aroma, but it can be a bit much without some ventilation.  But that's just an opinion.  You might think it's not strong enough, in which case I would wonder whats wrong with your nose.  If Cherry Vanilla sounds good to you then it probably would be good for you.  Besides you've got the money, right?

I think the flowers are cute but I purchased them because I thought they were perpetual motion flowers with their solar panels and they certainly are not. They don't move very long before I need to bump them. I have seen other ones that are perpetual, even in a room with no windows and that is what I was expecting. They are cute!

Purchased along with the Harp Earring rack so my bracelets & necklaces could be organized. The earring section works great for studs & some shorter hook style earrings, but the distance between each rack is only 2 & 1/4" long so dangle earrings hang over the next row making it a little clumsy when selecting earrings. Reason 1 for the lower rating.

I was quite disappointed when I hung the first necklace on the hook provided and it touched the shelf the organizer was sitting on. I tried two others & the same thing happened, so I measured the length where the bend is in the hook to the base of the organizer & it was only 9" long. Since all my necklaces, except one, average 10" in length, none of them could be hung on this side of the organizer, so it is now being used as a bracelet organizer which does work efficiently. Reason 2 for the lower rating.

I do have some heavy linked bracelets that do not work with the hooks since they don't hang loosely, not to mention there isn't a lot of distance between the hooks themselves. The hooks are more suited for 'fine' jewelry pieces versus chunky styles. So those bracelets have been hooked over the rungs for earrings & do display the beauty of the bracelets in grand style & they are easy to remove at a moments notice with no effort at all.

I used the curved pieces at the top of the organizer for a couple of stretch style chunky bracelets & that worked well.

The organizer can also be used for any type of lapel pin, tie tack & watch. It's sturdy, well made & worth the price paid.

I do recommend as long as you don't have a lot of chunky, clunky jewelry. If you do, you might want to look for a different style organizer.

I bought this model Ninja because it was the most highly rated in Consumer Reports.  The motor is very powerful, and the blades sharp and numerous, so smoothies are completed within seconds.  However, there are some drawbacks.  Because there is more than one set of blades on the vertical shaft of each of the bowls, it's difficult to put ingredients down into the bottom of the bowls.  This contrasts negatively to a standard blender.  In addition, the splash guard enables some of the food to escape onto the motor head, which is very difficult to clean, since it can't be immersed.  I understand that there needs to be room around the drive shaft so that the motor can make the blades rotate, but cleanup is not as simple as i would like.  The model I purchased has 12 different parts, and I didn't anticipate having to find so much storage space for a kitchen appliance.
Home_and_Kitchen.summary: Hard to clean, fill and store

Home_and_Kitchen.reviewText: The mirror is as described in so much as dimensions, functionality and aesthetics. However I was disappointed to find minor issues on the mirror sections--there appears to be some type of adhesive on the mirror surfaces that I was not able to clean off with glass cleaner. I've not attempted to use a razor--and likely won't--because I don't need "perfection" for its intended use. If I were using this in my dressing room I would return it, and I do feel that this quality control issue should not have been passed on to a consumer.
Home_and_Kitchen.summary: Not perfect but okay for my use...

Home_and_Kitchen.reviewText:
My wife bought one of these.  My big issue with it is how noisy it is.  And it isn't a simple tick-tock -- it makes a rattling noise that is hard to ignore.

My wife dropped it, and one of the eyes came off its pins.  I was able to pop it back together.  I don't think that incident has anything to do with how noisy it is.  I wish it did, then I might be able to fix it.

She loves the kitschy thing.  I do get to turn it off when we're watching TV.  I just wish it was quieter.
Home_and_Kitchen.summary: She Loves It, But It's Noisy

Home_and_Kitchen.reviewText: These were for my son's room at cheap storage for massive amounts of toys. They are working okay and I recommendGood two people to put them together, one to hold the previous attached ones together while the other add the new cubes. I also suggest not moving them, they will fall apart. They are okay, they look good.

Had a damaged part on receipt but they replaced it immediately ... real nice folks ...  Unfortunately, the original shipment came with TWO headboards ( no way to tell by looking at them ) instead of a headboard and a foot-board ... so when I had them replace the damaged "Headboard"  That's exactly what they did and now I have a Bed with two perfectly good headboards and, of course, no way to assemble the damned thing at all .... BUT the parts are well made and DO look real nice.

I wanted a Pizza Peel (big spatula) for taking Pizza out of the oven.  This one is big and works fine -- except it is hard to find a place to store it when not in use.  There isn't a hole in the handle, so it can't be hung and it's too big to fit in any of my drawers or cabinets.  I suppose I could stick it in the entry closet--as long as I remember where I put it the next time I need to pull a pizza from the oven.  Think I'll try drilling a hole in the handle and hanging it behind my aprons on the door between my kitchen and dining room.
Home_and_Kitchen.summary: Great to use--but a pain to store

Home_and_Kitchen.reviewText:
I don't know how many stars to give here as I did not open the package. What you get is not the knives shown in the picture. Instead the knives are solid stainless end to end -- there is no black material in the handle. Also, the large knife is a chef's knife, not the slicer that is shown, and listed in Amazon's description. I particularly wanted the slicer so I am sending these back unopened.
  BTW, nothing on the package indicates that the knives are forged, and the Kitchenaid website did not recognize the model number, so that is an unknown.
Edit: The picture is now correct: WYSIWYG. Good for Amazon -- paying attention.

I like the wide mouth, makes it easy to pour into and to clean.  But, as others have said, the lid doesn't stay on when you have something fermenting. I use duct tape to keep the lid down, and it works OK, but I shouldn't have to tape it.  It also has some "weak/soft spots" in the plastic, but it shouldn't be an issue as long as you don't pour hot wort into it.  Other than that, it does the job it's supposed to do, so I can't complain too much.
Home_and_Kitchen.summary: It's good and does the job, but it does have a couple production flaws.

Home_and_Kitchen.reviewText:
The table looks good, but assembly was a pain until I noticed that one of the leg brackets was welded at an angle.
I found the easiest way to assemble it was to keep the bolts loose until all the bolts were in.
The biggest pain was that mis-welded bracket on one of the legs, this is causing the table to bot be level.

I also had a broken leg "cap" on one of the feet due to shipping, but that is just a corner and is not visible in normal use.
Home_and_Kitchen.summary: Looks good, but has a bad weld

Home_and_Kitchen.reviewText: I own several of these types of muffin cups, from Wilson and others. The wilson ones are a little thin, so they tend to tear. On the other hand they work really well. I always spray mine with cooking spray and this helps keep the muffins or cupcakes from sticking to them once cool. I also turn them inside out to wash them and put them in the dishwasher, they come out just fine, you kind of have to tuck them between dishes so they stay in one place. All in all a good product, if you don't want muffin tins.

I have had this for over 6 months and it has held up well. My one complaint is that some of the squares are empty now. When I first got this, I was very excited to try it out based on so many positive reviews. I keep it with a duvet cover, and every time I take the cover off for washing, a lot of the filling is coming out, hence the empty pockets. Still using for the foreseeable future.

I was expecting a lot more of sheets that cost 65 or more dollars per set. these have a very pretty prints. The bad part is that the sheets are very thin and rough like sandpaper. I doubt they will last past a few washings. I had better luck with a brand-new three dollars that I bought on a discount website. Save your money.

The unit has plenty of power for light duty work. Its induction burner diameter is a too small for use with frying pans at 10 inches or more in diameter. The temperature control is not as linear as it should be, lending to burning delicate items such as fried eggs. The cooling fan for the electronics is somewhat noisy. It is a good entry item, at a good value, to decide whether a complete induction range is something one might invest in for the kitchen. In the end, we bought a top of the line GE model range. We Love it! It will keep your kitchen cooler and save on the air conditioning bill  in hot climates.
Home_and_Kitchen.summary: A good product  light cooking or getting know Induction cooking.

Home_and_Kitchen.reviewText: I was going to return it, but I decided to give it a chance.  I guess I'm alright with that decision, but I have a lot of reservations.  For one thing, I thought, from the description, that I could start it up and leave the house while it did its work.  Wrong.  It sometimes gets stuck under the dining table chairs.  The message on the screen says, "Please clear my path."  I thought it could clear its own path.  The dirt box fills up rather quickly.  I have a cat and it is mostly cat hair in the box, but, again, I can't just leave it to do its work.  Sometimes, it can't find its own way back to the charger and runs out of "juice" before it gets there.  When I use it, I shut the doors of rooms, like bathrooms, where it is more likely to get "stuck."  My overall impression is that the robot isn't as smart as it thinks it is.  I'm glad I kept my regular vacuum cleaner, but this is alright at picking up cat hair.  You just can't leave it to do its job.

For $30, this item is just fine.  It's functional, looks nice enough and has an easy to read face.  It also charges an ipod, which is a nice feature.  If you are looking for high quality sound though, you'll need to look elsewhere.  At higher volumes the sound quality falls off sharply, and even at regular volume you can hear the difference between this item and, for example, a Bose or JBL ipod dock.  Another sign of the lower end quality is that you sometimes have to push buttons two or three times before they do what they are supposed to.

If you are expecting these ornaments to have really sparkly rhinestones (as in the picture) you will be very disappointed. However, these ornaments are on the large side and do make a statement. Black and white ornaments are not easy to find and these are reasonably priced. They do not look cheap, they just do not look nearly as good as the picture would lead you to believe.
Home_and_Kitchen.summary: ... rhinestones (as in the picture) you will be very disappointed. However

Home_and_Kitchen.reviewText: This print should be made a smaller size, it is blurry from up close. It's still a very pretty print, but for the price not so much. It really should be sold as a smaller print and not have the option of a 24x36 print, or they should try to fix the blurriness from this larger print. I like it a lot and when I frame it I know it will look great from afar.

I think the title says it all.  It's pretty, with a modest (not sexy) design and adorable pattern.  Very 50's feminine. It seems to be a good quality cotton fabric, with good craftsmanship. BUT... in my opinion, the fabric is VERY thin for an apron.  Wide waistband is gathered with elastic, which is different - not my favorite feature.  This apron is NOT for the plus-size cook.  I'm a size 12/14 and found this apron just barely fits me (and was not terribly flattering on the curves).  Thankfully, I didn't buy it for myself, or I'd be sending it right back.  I also ordered the little girl's version of this apron... so I'll be reviewing that once it arrives.  I have not laundered this apron, as I am giving it as a gift, so cannot rate that aspect.  Sorry!  Oh, and you'll definitely need an iron for this one.
Home_and_Kitchen.summary: Small, Thin Apron with an Elastic Waist.... but still Pretty.

Home_and_Kitchen.reviewText: The ring at the bottom attached to the handle is a little loose. Be very careful when you wash them as they tend to slip off. Had to make sure and slide them all up as high as I could to get a tighter fit. Other than that they work well. It s a cup and holds coffee so Im not complaining !

I received my Crystal Allies Gallery 3 piece pyramid set of crystals on time and in perfect condition.  The minerals, namely 25mm polished amethyst, rose quartz and Clear quartz pyramids are very smooth and calming to the touch and aesthetically pleasing to the eye.  Each one is different and unique to itself and a conversation starter when your friends see them.  They promote healing energy to promote balance and inner peace, remove negativity and come with a certified stone info card in a velvet draw string bag for their protection and storage.  All three will fit in your hand and they weight about three ounces.

Although I received a discounted/free sample product for my honest, unbiased review, I found this product to be of excellent quality and would recommend it without hesitation.
Home_and_Kitchen.summary: Crystal Allies Gallery 3 piece pyramid mineral set

Home_and_Kitchen.reviewText: I got this as a gift for my 84 year old mom who was complaining of sleeping cold during the winter. I had been turned on to the delight of fleece sheets the year before and thought they would be a perfect solution. She was thrilled! She just kept gushing "it's like sleeping on a cloud!," And "i don't have to wear socks to bed!". She wanted a second set so she didn't have to wait while one set was being washed. They are amazing!

Great microwave! The sensor reheat feature is wonderful! Just start it and it figures out how long to cook automatically. It works wonders for leftovers.
This model has a wonderful door-opening button that uses the entire lower corner of the device. Other microwaves seem to be trending toward these little tiny door-open buttons that are surrounded by the fixed frame, hence making the button nearly impossible to push with anything other than a single finger, which is straining on the finger because it requires too much pressure to push the button and hard to use with wet hands. The door-open button on this Panasonic model is easy to push with wet hands and multiple fingers. Keep the big button on future models, please!
Home_and_Kitchen.summary: Great sensor cooking, and great door-open button

Home_and_Kitchen.reviewText:
I've been using this unit on and off for about a month now. For such a cheap little cook pot, it works great.

Cooks a can of soup boiling hot in a couple minutes. The bottom gets so hot even on the low setting that the food / soup that you're heating up will stick to the bottom and burn. My easy cleanup to the burned stuck on food to the bottom, I boil half a pot of water in the mini cook pot and let it sit for a bit. The stuck on food comes right off.

The extention cord is too short! But this unit uses a standard computer power cord so the easy fix was to dig out an old computer power cord I have and use that instead.

This unit isn't perfect but for $21.99 it's well worth the price. So far I've cooked Japanese Ramen noodles, misc Chefboyardee, chilli, misc Campbell soups, anything strait out the can. Works. I haven't used another mini electric cook pot to really compare but I do really like this one so far and I highly recommend it.

we recently bought an unvented fireplace that recommended this fuel. We get 6 hours of fire from a bottle (3- 2hr fires). Its a lot of fun to have a fireplace that you can move around, and the fuel to burn is so easy to use. No problems with it at all, and a fire just where and when we want it- plus no clean-up. Excellent!

Best bed sheets I've ever had!  We bougth one year ago and now is hard to sleep in my other sheets. It really works for regulating the heat it was a game changer in our hot California summertime.  When is cold it just confortable as well. Super super soft. We wash normal cycle a lot  and I dry with low heat.
Home_and_Kitchen.summary: Best sheets ever, great for heat and cold

Home_and_Kitchen.reviewText: Amazing pillow!  Ive been searching for the perfect type to meet my needs and found that several were either too firm or too soft.  With this one, you can remove or add their stuffing which came with the purchase, to make it perfect!  And if my pillow needs change over time, I still have more of the filling to add (or remove).  Thank you so much!
Home_and_Kitchen.summary: Bad Sleeper Searching for a Perfect Pillow and Found One!

Home_and_Kitchen.reviewText: I move from home to hotels and back again a lot.  This bag is tall enough to keep my Chihuahuas from accessing its contents and it holds heavy items like dog food cans.  Whether you use it for shopping or regular transporting, it's durable and the size of a regular Whole Foods or Trader Joe's paper bag - but better and more environmentally friendly.
Home_and_Kitchen.summary: This bag is tall enough to keep my Chihuahuas from accessing its contents and it holds heavy items like dog food cans

Home_and_Kitchen.reviewText: Arrived very quickly and in perfect condition. This multi-purpose ottoman is so easy to put together - just screw in the four legs which were shipped inside the ottoman. The color varies a bit from what's shown on my monitor - a tad less gold than shown; more grayish without being a true gray. The padded trays have fabric handles which make them easy to flip over. Sturdy enough for me (180 lbs) to sit on. Lots of room inside for my books and a sturdy table for beverages when needed. Very happy with my purchase.
Home_and_Kitchen.summary: The right size, the right look, and the right price

Home_and_Kitchen.reviewText: We love these mugs. They each have a different pattern and color, but they look lovely together. They hold a lot of coffee or tea with a bit extra room. I have used them in the microwave and dishwasher and have been very happy with them. They are ceramic, but aren't easily broken, ours have been dropped into the sink without damage.

I absolutely love this bedding set.  The packaging doesn't give it justice when it arrives but once you take it out it is just adorable.  My daughter told me she wanted something red after I purchased this online but when it arrived and I put it on her bed she feel in love; her face just lite up with delight!  It is super soft and not at all what I would call a heavy comforter.  Very light and airy with just enough weight to keep her warm.  Added bonus is the reversible sides.  She loves to flip them over depending upon which one she wants.
Home_and_Kitchen.summary: Absolutely adorable, super soft and comfortable!

Home_and_Kitchen.reviewText: These are perfectly sized meal containers! It's just me and my husband in the house and when we cook a big pot of soup or stew, these are especially good for freezing the leftovers in single proportions. Whenever we want to grab one out of the freezer for dinner or take one to work for lunch, they're microwaveable so they're so easy to use and it reduces clean-up/dishes later too!

Who knew you would sweat so much post partum, this is great for our bed,  if my daughter spits up or messes on my bed I know my mattress is safe. It fits well, and doesn't move. My sheets on the other hand tend to slip off easier now. But for the next few years my mattress is safe.

The size is small, but the functionality is there. This iron is good for travel. It heats quickly and seems to do a great job. It is useful for travel, but that is not all. It is also useful for quilting and for using heat-fusible stabilizer for embroidery. Being small, it can get into tight places. I would not consider it an adequate substitute for a full-size iron for home use, but for the purposes listed above, it is great.

Had to buy 4 curtain panels to fit across our large living room window. Turns out we love having the four panels so we can separate them for a different look. When the curtains are drawn, you cannot tell that there are multiple panels. The quality seems decent, I have seen better, but I have also seen much worse. If you are looking for some affordable curtains that look good, and will block the light/keep heat in or out depending on the season, these are a great purchase!

Its made to fit that model, and they go together perfectly. The stand arrived to me fully assembled other than the middle shelf has to be put in where you want it, so that was nice. Also, you can't really tell from the picture but the top shelf of the stand, where the tv goes, has a little cut out to slide the tv into so it can't really move side to side or towards the front. Its basically locked into place by the stand, so that's cool

It appears very sturdy and is just the right height. I've only had it for about 2 weeks but I feel pretty good about the purchase

ALOT of other people on here have complained about this model and similar stands being damaged in shipping. I personally had no problems with that, but enough other people have that I believe you should be concerned about it and aware of the possibility if you order this product

On another note, I ordered this stand and the tv at the same time, and the tv got to me a couple days before the stand did. If the stand had arrived damaged and I'd had to send it back, that would have been quite a delay. So maybe you should order the stand first and make sure its fine before you order the tv. Just a suggestion

This bread machine is superior than the other regular bread machines. The convection oven cooks the bread perfectly. I love this machine, it makes delicious breads and I wouldn't trade it for any other. Buy The bread lovers Bread Machine cookbook by Beth Hensperger,  Her book has wonderful recipes. She is an expert baker and so far everything Ive tried is so good. This lady outshines everybody else. This book is also sold on Amazon.
Home_and_Kitchen.summary: The Best of the Best in its price range !!

Home_and_Kitchen.reviewText:
Make awsome white rice every time.  One day i forgot to take out the rice i made and 16 hours later the rice was still good.  2 feature i really like are
* - cooker plays a little song when you push the start button and after rice is done.
* - after rice is done, the cooker will start a timer and tell you how long the rice has been warming.
Another awsome Japanese Product.
Thank you Japanese Company. ;)

I really love the pattern of this rug and the color was true to the picture.  It goes great with our patio set.  We had it for about a month now; no issues to report.  So far, the rug has should up to the elements; we had some very bad storms (strong winds) and some very hot days. The only negative is that the ends are still curling up a little.  However, I expect that to resolve itself in time.

I Love this fan.  It's super super quite and provides a high volume of air flow even on low.
It has a nice heavy stand base to keep it solidly in place.  It is over priced, but I've never had a pedestal fan that comes close in build quality or quietness.

One negative is that it beeps every rather loudly every time you turn it on/off or change the fan speed.  I personally find that very annoying. I normally will lower areview by one star for unnecessary beeps.  But I like this fan too much.

The remote could be 1/2 the size it is.  Plus you can only change the speed or turn on/off.  Oscillation is still a manual pull pin on the back of the fan motor.  For this price I expected oscillation to be managed by remote as well.  A bit of a disappointment.

I received these plates the other day.  They are an off white/egg shell/ivory color.  They are very lite and a little under 1/4 inch thick.  Upon receiving them I immediately washed them and placed 1/2 of a butternut squash on it.  With the plate cover on it I cooked the squash for 7 minutes in a 1200 watt microwave oven and it came out perfect.

The plate was warm because the squash was HOT.  There was no discoloration of the plate.  Although the plate was very warm, it did not show any signs of melting.  I'm very satisfied with them and did not see any of the problems that other people talk about.  They seem almost indestructible unless you use them for skeet shooting.

UPDATE:  I've had these plates about a week now.  I use them for lunch and dinner. I have two knife blocks containing professional knives that are RAZOR SHARP.  I use them to cut my sandwiches and also dinner items like chicken, pork chops and beef while they are on these plates.  I have NO CUT MARKS on these plates yet but in time they will be there just from daily use.

I think that when people complain about the cut marks they are doing a couple of things incorrectly.  1. These plates were not designed to be cutting boards or chopping blocks.  2. When I use my super sharp knives I don't need to BARE DOWN with a lot of force.  I simply slice and LET UP before you make contact with the plate and then gently finish the cut.  I don't attack my food like a samurai warrior.

I wasn't sure which one of the 3 colanders pictured I was going to get, but since the title said LEAF I was hoping for the big one (the one with the leafs on the desing). I wish somebody would have wrotten a review before my purchase and save me the anxious wait for the Amazon package: Will I get a small unuseful (strawberry) one, a medium (grapes) not so nice, or what I has hopping for? And YES!!. It was the big one, I belive 5 quarts (hard to mesure how much water a colander holds, it keep draining out!), very nice desing, and excelent price. Love it.

Used this to replace some frosted spray that a renter put on the windows.  The spray was flaking off and the windows looked terrible.  After cleaning the spray frost off with a razor blade, I just trimmed each piece of this static cling privacy film to size with scissors, sprayed with soapy water, and squeegeed the water out.  It looks very high end, in fact several people have commented on how nice it makes the windows look without blocking out the light.  I picked this pattern because it allows you to see just enough between the rectangles without the person outside being able to see in.  Love this product!
Home_and_Kitchen.summary: Privacy without blocking the light! And easy to install.

Home_and_Kitchen.reviewText: We've been using these every day for 7 months now and they still look new after repeated use and washing at high heat in our dishwasher (top rack).  I've washed them a few times on the bottom rack too and they came through just fine. I  love these bowls because they are a thick plastic that I'm not worried about breaking if my daughter drops them.  She loves the bright colors.  They match the Ikea plates, utensils, etc. that we also have.  Although I haven't tried I wouldn't recommend cutting anything with a knife in the bowl because I am sure it would score like the plates do.
