Automotive.reviewText:
NO....

I have 4 5gal and 2 2.5gal tanks with the 2-prong filler adapters (NOT the actual screw adapters from WWII). I have a few motorcycles and a REALLY old truck that likes to sit in my driveway and start once in awhile...

Going to be honest, these things suck. They leak at the o-ring and you get to play the "too much....OH DANG IT...not enough pressure!" game. They REALLY leak at the metal to rubber adapter, but leak at the o-ring area as well. The other half of the leak - that's the part half-way up the tube in the picture (where the green goes to black). DON'T rely on this - I even hate putting fuel into my lawn mower with this adapter. I have two of these and even tried to mush RTV into the rubber. It failed within the second or third fueling session.

Find the 100% metal flex adapter. I've been using ONE for 8 months and it's PERFECT. I use it for the lawn mower, 2 motorcycles and a car. Not ONE drop of fuel anywhere other than the tank. Note: I rotate around 30'ish gallons of fuel a year for various means (soon to include a generator) - the crappy half-metal half-rubber adapters are the worst thing in my garage. They spill everywhere. I literally just fueled 2 motorcycles with the fully metal flex adapter and not one drip.

USE THE METAL FLEX ADAPTER.
Automotive.summary: OMG NO!!!! Stay away from this "filler"

The saddest Bilstein shocks I have ever experienced...

As a long time motorcycle and performance car enthusiast, I am very familiar with what suspension should and should not do. These shocks have a MAJOR lack of rebound dampening, they feel as if they have 300,000 miles on them and do not control the car at all. It will require a revalving with about 30-40% more rebound dampening, for a stock 1992 Caprice wagon. I do not load my car, it is a commuter, it stays clean and empty at all times besides the fuel tank.

While these shocks may be okay on a sedan with 140-160 lb/inch springs, the wagon has a 211lb/inch rear springs, and is not controlled sufficiently with these shocks despite all claims that they are "stiff" and or "performance oriented."  Do not believe the hype on the forums, these WILL require a revalve to match the feel of their front Bilstein shock counterparts on a wagon. The compression dampening however is nearly perfect.
Automotive.summary: Significant lack of rebound dampening

In its resting position, the wiper blade is approximately a 45-degree angle to the surface. The wiper arm for the SUV was made to hold the wiper at a higher elevation off the glass surface based off of older wiper blade designs (the ones with finger springs not single metal strip spring).

Automotive.reviewText:
The good: nice to have a screen, full featured, looks good in my car, plays music :)

The bad: the volume is quiet, even on full.  The screen is small and things like track numbers are even smaller and a poor color choice, so it's difficult/impossible to read while you're driving.  It does not have an input jack, so only works as a standalone player.  Worst of all, the instructions are worthless and the controls are not intuitive.  I discovered the following by trial and error over 2 months of frustration:

(>/=)
- tap once to pause/play
- hold down two seconds to turn off
- tap twice to turn on

(VOL)
- tap once to adjust the volume with the up/down arrows
- tap again to adjust the frequency with the up/down arrows

(M)
- While playing, tap once to get to the repeat/equalizer menu
- While paused, tap once to go to the folder menu
- hold down two seconds to select music/movie/jpg mode

(|<<)
- while playing, tap to skip back a song
- hold to rewind while playing
- while paused, tap to skip back a folder

(>>|)
- while playing, tap to skip fwd a song
- hold to rewind while playing
- while paused, tap to skip ahead a folder

If you unplug it (or remove power) while a track is playing, it will start over at the start of the track when power is restored.
If you turn it off by holding the play button, and then remove/depower it, it will start over in the middle of the track.
If you enter a track # with the remote, it will skip right to that track.
Automotive.summary: Great player, lousy instructions

I'm not impressed with this at all.
I purchased this exact same cabin air filter from my local auto parts store for my 2006 Toyota 4Runner.

I don't remember the last time I changed my filter, it must have been years ago because my old one looks like I've been using it to pan for gold and was full of dirt--but no gold.

The picture doesn't match exactly what the filter looks like.  The picture shows a plastic "ridge" that runs the entire perimeter of the filter (which is what my original filter looked like) but my new one doesn't have it.  The new filter has a cardboard type edge only on two opposing sides, and the other two sides are merely the filter element.  This can cause a less than perfect seal and allow air to pass thru these edge of the filter.  Now don't get me wrong, I don't believe a cabin air filter does much more than catch acorns and grasshoppers anyway, but the sealing properties of this one are not as good as the one I had.

As far as the fit is concerned, the dimensions are correct to fit my car and it does fit well--minus the issue I describe above.  If Purolator would put the same type of stiff edge around the entire filter assembly instead of just on two sides, this would be a much better filter.

Automotive.reviewText:
So first of all some product specifcations:

Battery life = 600 mAh (fills my iphone 3Gs which is about 1200 mAh half way)

There is one mini usb port on it that acts as both a power in and power out. The device comes with a bunch of mini-usb adapters to allow you to connect various other devices to the charger's mini usb.

There is a single button on the device, if you press it once, the green light will blink indicating that it will output power to anything you connect, and if you press the button twice, the flashlight will turn on.

Review:

I had intended to use this to be a little bit greener and allow me to run my Iphone 3Gs off of solar energy. The first day, I had it sit in the sun for a while and when it was in the sun, the little red light would turn on indicating that it was charging. When it got dark, i decided to charge my dead iphone battery, and it got to 50% charge and then the charger ran out of juice.

That night, I placed the device in my window intending to have it charge all the next day. When I woke up, the device's red light was blinking, and the flashlight was on, but not very bright. I tried pushing the button, but nothing was happening. So I decided to give it a little wall charge for a second. After that the device behaved normally. So I placed it back in the sun, and saw the red light come back on.

At the end of the day, I checked up on it, and yet again, the device had the blinking red light and the flashlight was on. The charger battery was basically completely empty, and could not charge my iphone at all.

The bottom line:

When you connect the device to the wall, the charger works fine and as it should (however, the battery does not last very long). However when you try to use the sun to charge.. just forget it. I wouldn't recommend buying this product.
Automotive.summary: Good Idea... Doesn't work with Solar

Thankfully I was able to modify the mount on my bike to make it fit, and I found out I needed to do so by the stator wires being shoved so hard into the frame they were worn bare and grounding out on the frame. Kinda a pain in my ass. But she's charging properly a week later so I can't hitch too much.
Automotive.summary: Meh but works. Horrible shipping time.

Automotive.reviewText:
It does match the dash color and should fit well with a successful install but its just a piece of plastic. It hardly seems worth the price.

Mounting is by pre-bent metal tabs with adhesive and Velcro. I found getting a good, tight, professional looking fit impossible. No matter how hard I tried, it ended up looking like something stuck on the dash with Velcro. It also isn't canted at all so its hard to read.

On the other hand, though I've never had much luck with vacuum windshield brackets, the one that came with the Edge is solid. I may try to install again or I may just forget it and stick with the vacuum mount.
Automotive.summary: Not worth it. Hard to install correctly.

Automotive.reviewText: I do not recommend you buy this. The studs are not long enough to easily thread the nuts even when completely flush. The template is terrible. Template must be taped to snorkel to properly mark holes.  The rubber hose that connects the plastic snorkel to the air filter housing is not at the correct bend at all; it will fight you and be nearly impossible to not have a slight kink in it.
Automotive.summary: Not recommended

Automotive.reviewText: The first one they sent was completely warped. It was impossible to install correctly. The second one was better. Once we got it correctly fitted, we were happy with the product. But in terms of quality control, this is not what you expect from a reputable brand. Very disappointing, and it caused us a huge headache because we were in a time crunch to haul our stuff across the country.
Automotive.summary: First one was warped

Automotive.reviewText: The 2-star rating is not because of the product quality but rather it's not as described. The description says it is fit for installation in a 2010 Honda Pilot but in actuality this product does not fit for the said vehicle. Other than that, I have always been pleased with FRAM products.
Automotive.summary: I have always been pleased with FRAM products

Automotive.reviewText: I was disappointed when I received these.  The size it indicated was not what I was excepting.  When I measured them they were off by several inches.  I think the tires would have been great if they were truly the size that were posted.  To send them back and get a different set would have cost me more to upgrade to the size I truly wanted.  I couldn't take a chance of being disappointed again.
Automotive.summary: not true to size

Automotive.reviewText: buyer beware. this product goes down well but be careful about putting it over anything other than a bare metal surface. I put it on top of black VHT Epoxy paint and it attacked the finish.  no amount of prep work for painting prevented this. When it dries it looks good but the areas that were attacked need to be re sprayed. 2 stars for lack of a warning on this reaction.
Automotive.summary: buyer beware

Automotive.reviewText:
For now I'll leave four stars due to my scepticism on have an LED controller running at 84+ degrees Celsius (184F) without expect that will fail.
I'm definitely satisfied with the results on change a pair of HID for these LEDs. Measured brightness before and after shows that this LEDs are far more bright.
However I also took several temperature measurements which scares me and you can see on my attached pictures.
The main controller reached that temperature in just 10 minutes. Reading some other customers reviews I decided to stick an aluminum heat sink in order to try to cool this module and may have some extra lifetime. I also noted that the LED bulb itself don't rise the temperature above 60 degrees Celsius (140F) due to the cooling fan "till it fail lol"..
There are two possibilities: I come back here in six months and rise this review to 5 stars or near between come here with my failure analysis.
Just for comparison, one image shows my fog light from Syrius (LED) and the head light slight more blue.
The last thermal image is an interesting comparison of heat signature of my Prius engine and on left side the bright led controller..

UPDATED:
Well, a little more than 6 months as I promised I rose to 5 stars. I'm definitely very satisfied with this Led Light and the electronic controller didn't fail. Just want to reinforce that the usage here is about 4 hous/day mean, and often used for more than 2 hours uninterrupted.
One thing I noted (and expected) is that the fans where gone, both fans died but this is not affecting the lights neither the max temperature. Probably there is a thermistor on the LED to slight reduce the current to lower the temperature "my guess".

UPDATED2:
Less than 1000hrs of life one unit surprisingly had its LED module burned despite of my efforts on maintain the driver cool. Attached the dead module side which caused the entire unit to fail as well a tear down picture. I did some tests on the driver (simple swap) and it's still working, as well I did a test on the internal fan which is also working. So, after tear down I was surprised to see that the module don't have ANY temperature management on its LED boards or the entire heatsink block. Of course, lack of temperature management or current management is the root cause of 90% of premature death of high power LED devices. I'm taking 3 stars out, one for my disappointment, one for the lack of temperature management and another for the lie on their advertises which states "monitor the fan speed to get the best temperature protection", the fan installed is a simple unmanaged 6v fan, there is no sensor to reduce the power on the LED when the fan is manually blocked making the unit reach incredible high temperatures in just a few minutes.
Automotive.summary: Ops, read the update2...

Appliances.reviewText:
This is a great idea that I have used before to good effect.

UNFORTUNATELY...

This PARTICULAR device - essentially an air valve - is so poorly manufactured that it required repair BEFORE it could be used.  The plastic shell is a flimsy, two-piece, snap-together affair that didn't snap together well at all, thus leaving the interior valve flap in a warped shell that did not allow the valve flap to seat properly in either position.

I repaired and modified mine so that it now works properly, but I remain annoyed that this product required pre-installation repair straight out of the box it came in.

Clamps provided are actually just plastic wire ties that are inadequate to hold dryer hoses under pressure.  Buy a real set of hose clamps to install this item and/or use duct tape to keep the vent hoses in place.

Screen is small and will rapidly become clogged with lint that gets through your dryer lint screen.  Install this device so that you can easily access its screen for removal and cleaning.

I strongly suggest you purchase a different brand of this device.

NOTE:  USE ONLY ON ELECTRIC DRYERS!
Appliances.summary: Good idea, inadequate design, very poorly manufactured

Appliances.reviewText:
I purchased this to fix a dryer for a family member. This is the part number that a popular appliance repair site specified.  However, this dryer is very old and has "donut" type insulators which are too small for this coil to fit through (the original coil is smaller).  Evidently this dryer requires a full assembly at $85+

Now I'm stuck with a $20 part that I can't use and presumably can't return since I have already stretched it out.
Appliances.summary: Make sure your insulators fit before ordering!

Appliances.reviewText:
These roller wheels seem to take a set after a load is done. They thump and thump until they get warm every time I turn on the dryer. The oem wheels did not do this. I changed these as preventative when I had to change the motor. The whole dryer has to come apart to change them. Very disappointed.
1-29-18 update: Still thumping after all this time.....
Appliances.summary: Wheels thump and thump when cold.

Appliances.reviewText: This ridiculously priced part is another one of G.E.'s big ripoffs.  At least here it costs half what it does if purchased from G.E. (double this crazy price!) Someone is still making a bundle off of these cheaply made, easily broken, nothing-but-a-dial, a knob for crying out loud, pieces of fragile plastic.  It was galling to pay so much for this crummy thing but there isn't much of an alternative.  I searched all over the world wide web and found nothing more reasonable.  The seller was honest and shipped it quickly and I don't blame the parts dealer at all.  It's just that there is no way in Hades that this knob (a KNOB) should cost this much.  Consumers should unite in protest!  There was even an article online aptly titled "The Case of the Mysterious Breaking G.E. Dryer Knob" that pointed out the profits that G.E. rakes in by selling outrageously priced knobs.  Still, I'm relieved that I was able to get one for much less than what the original manufacturer website charges the people they take advantage of.  It does make one wonder what a missing bolt from a G.E. jet engine must cost to replace.  However, that is a matter of life and death and worth the cost.  When it comes to a plastic dryer knob, well, it's a complete and utter outrage of absolutely stunning proportions and the public shouldn't stand for it anymore!  It's robbery, plain and simple!  There should be a law passed that prevents this kind of flim-flam consumer abuse by blood-sucking Giant Corporations that crush the common individual in the name of Almighty Profits!
Appliances.summary: Fragile and Overpriced Piece of Unexceptional Plastic Worth Ten Dollars At Most

Appliances.reviewText:
Very bad quality and item has broken after 4 month of usage. It just stopped working one day and it doesn't switch on when I press on/off button. I have tried to return it but the brush can only be returned in US and conair can send a replacement to US address only so 3 years warranty is worthless if you live outside US. They said the voltage and hertz in the UK are not compatible with the requirements of this unit and may cause the unit to fail if used outside of north American current so be aware if you don't live in US.
However, the brush itself can help to make quite stylish look very quickly and the hair really shy afterwards.
Appliances.summary: Very bad quality, but when works can make quite stylish look

Appliances.reviewText: I entered the part number that I needed and was informed that GE WE4M519 would fit my dryer. When I received it in the mail, I knew by the size of the box that it would not fit. And indeed it did not. I had to send it back. Dissappointed, because I really wanted to dry my clothes again in the dryer.

Didn't much care for these.  Usually when I put a new filter on the refrigerator, the pressure and flow rate of the through-the-door water is substantially increased, but when I installed this filter the water flow was about the same as the dirty filter I'd just replaced.  I won't buy these again.  They are cheaper than the OEM filters, but not worth the savings.
Appliances.summary: but when I installed this filter the water flow was about the same as the dirty filter I'd just replaced

Appliances.reviewText: I like this product and believe it has a useful purpose and despite the fact that the packaging lists that you keep it turning 'right' even when extracting the brush, my natural instincts kicked in when extracting this from a 'very long' dryer vent pipe and yep, you guessed it, the head unscrewed from the rod and now I cannot extract the brush which is 'stuck' somewhere in the pipe.  I'm afraid this could end up being a very costly repair as this occurred in a condo rental unit I own and I cannot access the vent pipe inside the condo without tearing out drywall.  I subsequently purchased additional rods from my local big box store in an attempt to fish the stuck head out (with various attachments) and noticed their product has an ingenious design that this kit is missing....a hex screw which firmly attaches the brush head to the threads once it has been screwed onto the rod!!  WHY DOESN'T THIS PRODUCT DO THE SAME??  I would return this product but I don't have the brush head available and personally, I'd like to send them the bill for whatever it ends up costing me to get this problem resolved!!  Again, with the right safe guards in place I would have no problem recommending this product, but as is I cannot.  Be sure to look for a kit that includes a screw that will firmly attach the brush head to the threads so that a forward or reverse spin will not leave you in the situation I'm in at the moment!!  BTW...big box = Lowes Home Improvement...their product is more expensive but well worth it not to be left with the headache I'm experiencing!!

Valve looks and hook up like the old one, but the output is terrible. The water barely comes out, and it took over an hour to finish washing clothes. It used to take about 35 minutes with the old valve. I ended up getting an OEM valve and the difference was amazing. The wash is done in 35 minutes again.
Appliances.summary: Valve looks and hook up like the old one

Appliances.reviewText: Fit, Finish all good. After install water came out BLACK. Okay charcoal filter, no big deal after I run about a gallon of water through. The thing that really grinds me though is that it lasted LESS THAN A MONTH. I've had this frig ~2-3 years and before this a filter lasted ~6 month's pretty consistently.
Appliances.summary: Finish all good. After install water came out BLACK

Appliances.reviewText:
Worked great for about 2 months, then it stopped cycling. Got stuck in the drain position and burned out the drain solenoid (which was also purchased and replaced at the same time as this timer) melting the solenoid housing and seizing the solenoid. At this point I'm stuck replacing the whole dishwasher anyway. I guess that's what I get for repairing instead of replacing from the start.

I don't recommend purchasing a used dishwasher timer
Appliances.summary: Might buy you a little time, but most probably not a permanent fix

Appliances.reviewText: The plastic tube that attaches the sprayer arm to the basket broke on my current sprayer.  I purchased this arm kit as replacement. This kit is not complete as they do not include the piece of tubing that is needed to attach the sprayer to the basket.  I had to still go to the hardware store and no one sells just this piece that was broken.  I instead found a dishwasher parts/repair store open on Sunday and bought the piece needed.  This was a useless purchase and is going back.

This product does what it's designed to. make ice;however, the main reason I bought it was that there is no drain required. That's true, but if you don't have a drain, this thing has to be manually drained by you, and very often. The lower pan fills up, sometimes several times per hour and when it does you get an ear piercing alarm that doesn't go off until you manually drain the lower pan. This to me defeats the purpose of having it. Not to mention you must drain the ice bin at least twice per day and sometimes more often. If you really want a ice maker I suggest you have a drain nearby for this one, otherwise try another model/brand.

I found this to be one of the largest single layered dish racks on the market which was what I required and it's space and looks were quite appealing. However, similar to previous comments, the rust does set in quite quickly. For me it was about 4 months after I had started to use it. As I thought it may have been the way I looked after and used it, I purchased my second one which I took better care of (such as removing dishes as soon as they were dry). To my horror, the rust set in even quicker at just a little over 2 months.

The cutlery caddy does not drain very well and I find that there is constantly a little puddle of water just around the drainage hole. As a result, wooden utensils cannot be dried in the middle two sections as the ends constantly stay wet. Metal utensils are ok, but they do need to be wiped after removal. Bear in mind, that the water gathered in the middle causes a bit of grime and anything placed in the caddy comes in contact with it. It is hard to scrub off even with a bottle brush because of the size of each section.

There is always water in the bottom drainage tray that never seems to disappear and even with the back of my dish tray elevated on a 2 inch foam block, the water is still there.

The 2 knobs holding the cutlery caddy also rust and unfortunately, there is no way to allow them to dry unless you move the caddy to the other side of the rack.

I will definitely not be purchasing my third one and the price I paid would have been equivalent to buying about 10 polycoated ones which would have been a lot cheaper to throw out if any problems occurred.
Appliances.summary: Great dishrack although too much rust

Appliances.reviewText: I now realize i mostly just bought this for the sensors. The app is profoundly frustrating and does not deliver a simple temperature monitoring system and instead confuses you with bells and whistles. Luckily i have a smaller Acurite brand weather station in my kitchen and i just now just the temp sensors for that device's A,B and C channels. So for the price, if you need 3 sensors this is an ok deal.

I THINK I GOT A USED OR DEFECTIVE MOTOR, IT WOULDN'T RUN UNTIL I OILED THE SHAFT BUSHING AND TURNED THE BLADES BY HAND. AFTER ABOUT 25 ROTATIONS OF THE BLADES BY HAND IT SLOWLY STARTED RUNNING ON ITS OWN. BOX HAD BEEN OPENED AND RE-SEALED SO I MAY HAVE GOTTEN A MOTOR THAT HAD BEEN RETURNED BECAUSE IT DIDN'T WORK AND AMAZON RESOLD IT WITHOUT VERIFYING THAT IT WORKED.
Appliances.summary: IT WOULDN'T RUN UNTIL I OILED THE SHAFT BUSHING AND TURNED THE BLADES BY HAND ABOUT 25 ROTATIONS

Appliances.reviewText:
Excruciating experience with the Bertazzoni service. We bought a Bertazzoni gas range Master 30" a year ago. The week before Easter of this year the oven ignition broke down. It is now mid-May and it has yet to be fixed! They kept saying that the needed part will be mailed overnight to the company servicing the range and that we'll have it fixed over the next couple of days. I just talked to them and was told that the part is back-ordered and they can not do anything about it! Really? It will be 6 weeks by then! After insisting that they get it fixed asap and after being put on hold I am told that they "found" the part. It remains to be seen if indeed we will have a working oven soon...

Now about the performance of this range: first, the range looks good! Second, the top burners are fine especially when you need high heat. My only complaint is that the simmering is not performing well. Even with the simmering ring there is way too much heat for a slow cooking stew in a Dutch oven. My solution: I pile two grates such that the Dutch oven stays high enough. The downside: it looks ridiculous and I can not use the other burners! The oven: works fine for cooking/braising meat which requires more moisture but not so well for baking which can not be turned and therefore gets burnt on the bottom. My solution for this was to place a metal tray underneath such that the heat gets diffused and circulates better (this happens even with the fan on). Bottom line: first, appliances sometimes break down and that is fine but then the service should be of quality and prompt; second, for the price this range should work without these rather embarrassing adjustments! I have made an effort to like this range, hence the adjustments, but the service I have received so far really sealed my thoughts on the Bertazzoni, and they are not positive!
Appliances.summary: probably it is better to stay away!

Appliances.reviewText: Wife purchased one of these recently and I am not thrilled with it. It does make ice and I like the shape and sizes but the ice is soft and doesn't hold up very well in a less than very cold drink. My main complaint is that the ice begins to melt as soon as it drops from the freezing posts and makes for rather wet ice.  Not too much of a problem if you use the ice as soon as it is made but if you transfer the ice to your freezer, as I do, you end up with a frozen mass of ice that is made of individual "cubes" frozen together into a useless chunk.
Appliances.summary: Not good if you store ice

Appliances.reviewText: I bought this because there was a review that showed the top (nozzle) of the filter to be the same was the OEM Samsung filter. I received the filter today and was really surprised that it did not match! This one has a larger opening and looks unrefined when compared to the Samsung ones.  Installed it just to see if it mattered. Yes it does. There is a much louder and distracting sound coming the new one as we run the water. I bought two, but after installing this, will return the second one.  I've learned my lesson in penny pinching.  For me,  $45 for 6 months (just over $7 a month) is worth the piece of mind of having to second guess a third party manufacturer.  Most people spend more in 1 trip to Starbucks.

It's difficult to tell that there's much of a difference after using "Scratch-B-Gone" vs. using only Weiman's (or another) cooktop cleaner by itself. I have done both several times now, and I can detect a small difference after using this "Cooktop Seasoning Treatment." If I use it, the "polish" lasts for a while on my glass cooktop after a cleaning session. I was also disappointed about how poorly the protectant works when I'm cooking meals (boiling water drips, food spills, etc.). Most times I clean my cooktop these days, I don't bother using the "seasoning" anymore because I feel it doesn't really do that much to protect it and it's a pain to have to put it on and buff it out a few times. This product also claims that if you use it once or twice, the protectant will last for a while, i.e., you won't have to re-apply it every time you clean the cooktop. However, I've found that I have to use it every time for the protective aspect to hold up at all. All in all, this product is way too expensive considering that it doesn't really work.
Appliances.summary: Expensive product that doesn't work as advertised

Appliances.reviewText: Unfortunately, this was the only one I could find to fit my disposal (including "universal" fit, which isn't).  It's better than nothing, but not much.  Unless you have really strong water pressure, you have to use a utensil to push food through it, and it seems to act like a plug, causing water to back up.
Appliances.summary: Slightly better than nothing if you need this size

Appliances.reviewText: The RCA RIC102 Ice Maker does produce a ready supply of ice quickly, but the machine is too noisy! (And I've been fitted for a hearing aid!) At first, after setting up the machine in my kitchen, every few minutes I kept being frightened when it sounded like someone was breaking into my house as the newly frozen ice is pushed into the hamper. I hear the machine throughout my cottage and have taken to shutting off the machine to stop the racket unless it is a very hot day and I need the ice more than I hate the noise. Also, I should have researched more carefully and wouldn't have bought this machine which is not insulated; the ice already made eventually melts, causing the noise machine to keep up making its annoying noise even after it's full since that ice melts!
Appliances.summary: As Much a Noise Maker as an Ice Maker

Appliances.reviewText:
Definitely not built to last. Considering this has an evaporative cooler like a refrigerator or air-conditioner, which are permanently sealed from the atmosphere with no possibility of leakage or contamination, this thing should last a very long time. However, the manufacturer seems to have used so many other cheep throw-a-way components (such as for the control mechanism) that this unit is likely to be taking up space in the land fill way ahead of it's time. Mine has not been shutting off when then ice basket is full since it was new, and more recently it only produced tiny little beads instead of ice cubes, hence useless.

Hello Global Corporations - if you want to do the so called "sustainability" thing, built it to last!

Does not do anything as far as filtration when checked with a calibrated TDS meter.  The reading directly out of my faucet was 165.  The waterlines servicing the refrigerator are tapped off of the same sample point. The "Filtered "water was reading TDS  at 155.  Needless to say, there is barely any difference. I doubt that I will be buying these filters again
Appliances.summary: Does not do anything as far as filtration when checked ...

Appliances.reviewText: I purchased this model in black a little over a year ago. Keep in mind we had a GE refrigerator in white for 15 years before this one. The finish on it was very durable and did not have a scratch or dent. The GE refrigerator gshf5kgxww in BLACK scratches and dents easily!!!! The finish is not durable. The interior works well and is spacious. It is disappointing that the exterior functions the way it does.
Appliances.summary: Worst Exterior Finish Ever! Model in Black.

Appliances.reviewText:
My wife and I use both the stove top and the oven quite a lot. We generally like the way the stove looks, and the stove top works well after a couple of service visits to get the high power middle burner working properly. But the oven heats very unevenly and it's a huge pain to light the oven without having the flame go out.

The stove top burners generally work well, but we had trouble from the beginning with the dual-burner in the middle. We could generally get the outer ring started, and the inner ring would ignite but then would go out as soon as we let go of its ignition knob. It took two visits from the service company to get the burner adjusted to work properly. The high power burner is great for getting a big pot of water boiling quickly for pasta.

The oven, however, is a problem. The first thing we realized is that there was no temperature read-out. We already had our own thermometer, which we hung on the back wall of the oven, but it is obviously much less convenient to read this than if Bertazzoni had installed an LED readout somewhere on the front panel. Obviously the oven knows what the temperature is, because the oven is good at maintaining a steady level; why couldn't Bertazzoni figure out a nice way to display this?

The next thing we noticed (and the manual warns of this) is that after lighting the oven burner, you have to close the oven door very slowly to keep the flame from blowing out. When the flame blows out without our noticing it, we get natural gas leaking into the kitchen, not a nice thing at all. And it's not easy to close the oven door slowly, because, as with most ranges, there is a spring built into the door close mechanism.

Finally, the "convection" feature is kind of a joke. I had really looked forward to this feature, as we do a moderate amount of baking. But cookies, bread, and Thanksgiving turkey all get cooked extremely unevenly. We pulled our turkey out of the oven prematurely because one side read 170 degrees. The other side was bloody. We're admittedly rookies at cooking big birds (this was 13 pounds) but this was pretty unbelievable.

We like the stove top quite a lot, but wish we could have a different oven, ideally an electric one. Unfortunately, we're in a building with an old electrical system and it would have cost a fortune to bring more power to our 11th floor apartment.  So we've learned to watch our cookies closely, rotate them frequently, and remove individual cookies before they burn. Next time we cook a turkey we'll cut it into pieces ahead of time, rotate it frequently, and hope for better results.
Appliances.summary: Good looks, but terrible oven ignition and uneven heating

Appliances.reviewText:
Purchased this product about 6 months ago for my Whirlpool (it normally used to take Whirlpool Pur filter #4396701), and had no problems with this generic replacement. When the indicator light recently went off, I did not hesitate to order another one. I did see the negative reviews about it breaking under the fridge and ruining people's floors and wondered about that... Upon receiving my newest one, I totally understand why. At first I couldn't get the filter to go in correctly and decided to put the two side by side.  They both said they were the same model (RWF1021), but they were not the same.  The newer one is longer and the way it screws in is not the same.  I took a picture and will try to attach it to this review -- The one on the right is the newer one.  You can see by the plastic tip it won't screw in the same and it is longer.  Also, the newer one looks like it could easily leak from the nozzle to where it attaches to the tube part.  It is not "sealed" -- or doesn't look fully sealed like my other one.  I am totally disgusted. What a waste.
3/18/16 UPDATE: DiscountFilterStore promptly contacted me and were concerned about my negative experience. They kindly refunded me the cost of the filter (extra star added for their good customer service) - Unfortunately, I do think people who are looking for a replacement filter for 4396701 need to know that the filter they receive may not be the best fit for their refrigerator. I am not sure what to think as the first one I received (back in October) was perfect, but this new one is not the same and won't fit right and looks like it could break and flood.
Appliances.summary: Newer version of RWF1021 (to replace 4396701) is not how it used to be.

Appliances.reviewText:
The kit seemed like a great way to rejuvenate my dryer. It installed easily and, for a time, seemed OK. The belt and the idler worked well. HOWEVER, the rubber rollers failed in short order due to heat. Fortunately, I hadn't tossed out the old ones and was able to reinstall them.

This kit disappointed in that the rubber used for the roller wheels is a substandard material and turned to goo in a short while.
Appliances.summary: The rubber rollers failed from heat after a short time in service

Appliances.reviewText: The product description says this filter inhibits the growth of bacteria, mold and mildew. After 2 months of use, it is full of black mold and fuzzy white mildew. I've ordered another, but this time I'll try using a water treatment with it as well. I'm ordering the BestAir 3BT-6 Original BT Humidifier Bacteriostatic Water Treatment - hopefully that will help. If not, next year the Holmes goes in favor of a different model.

Two stars because I am on a second digital control panel screen that is separating at the corners (Like others have reviewed).  For you keyboard warriors out there, no it is not the same plastic wrap that protects the finish from minor abrasion during shipping.  Think of a screen protector for your phone but attached with industrial adhesive. It starts to peel away taking chunks of plastic and paint below along for the ride.  It was replaced the first time at nearly 90 dollars shipped to my house and another arm and leg for installation (outside of warranty obviously...because this junk doesn't break during the first 12 months of ownership)  but now the new one with less than 6 months in service is starting to come apart the same way the first did.  The rest of the fridge is decent and I would have given it a good review, except when this part fails your fridge is done.  Should have listened to the misses and steered clear of LG and Samsung products.
Appliances.summary: The rest of the fridge is decent and I would have given it a good review, except when this part fails your fridge ...

Appliances.reviewText: filters work very well in my Samsung refrigerator, and price is significantly better than OEM.  Only issue is sometimes the small tube of silicon lubricant that comes with each filter is dried out and unusable.  When this happens I use the lubricant from other partially used tubes I've kept.  I'm not sure how essential using this lube is anyway.
Appliances.summary: Works well as a Samsung OEM replacement

Appliances.reviewText: I bought this to replace my kitchen fridge.  I have three freezers, so I just needed a little space for small items.  This one works really well, everything is the tempeture that it should be.  Besides a bit of condensation( why it gets a 4 instead of 5) on the back wall. I have no complaints.

Pros: Light weight, easy to install, relatively quiet, & inexpensive. Great for simple things like reheating coffee or heating frozen vegetables. I'm a 5'1" female & was able to remove the old unit & install this one in 40 minutes.

Cons: The exhaust fan is pretty weak (but I guess that's par for the course with OTR microwaves), the touch pad isn't as responsive as it should be, & the cooking light is rather dim.

Great for a condo or rental unit.

Love this fan hood. Good price.
The down side is the military clock and poor instructions. I have worked with foreign markets in the past and had to correct their English translation and here is the same problem. Easy to install if you know what you are doing.
Too bad they used blue led and not the more natural yellow tone.
Another plus are the lights are to the front of the hood so it illuminates the front of the stove. (Other styles just washed the back wall due to the position in the back of the hood and creates shadows in the front.)
Appliances.summary: Great fan and hood. Some missteps

Appliances.reviewText: This ice maker was more a expensive than many but I like being able to dispense ice directly into a glass so that is why I chose this one. Seems to work well. My only slightly negative comment is that, since the bullet shaped cubes are hollow, they melt quite quickly in the glass. For this reason I have it set to make the large size cubes.if the cubes were solid they would not freeze as quickly of course. So you trade off speed for ice that melts fast. Still, with greater surface area it cools your drinks quickly. Be sure to let it sit for a while before setting it up. It came packed sideways in another box the said to keep upright! So even kept upright it would have been on its side.

We have used these filters since our GE refrigerator was purchased new 6 years ago.  They have provided us with clean, odor-free water.  We change them when the "replace filter" light comes on. We usually get 9 - 10 months of use from each one.

I've always considered the filters to be expensive, so when I run out I always buy a 3-pack to lower the cost/filter, and I shop Amazon to get the best price possible.

This thing is pretty cool.  The water doesn't come out as fast as I'd hoped but I like the fact that its not one of those huge water dispensers that stick out like a sore thumb.  It fit's nicely on my little table in the corner of my kitchen/dining room.  My husband wanted and ice machine and I needed a watee dispenser so on that note im pleased we could agree on one item that fits both our needs.  I love it so far!

I have had this dishwasher installed for 3 loads now. Runs excellent. Extremely quiet. Manages to get dishes cleaned without pre-washing. Drying is typical of a Bosch from other reviews I have read, but works well for me. THE ONLY ISSUE IS BEST BUY / PACIFIC KITCHENS AND THEIR INSTALLERS!
Starting with the pre-measure procedure. There didn't seem to be any communication from the start. The installers got there ready to measure for an electric range, not a dishwasher. That got fixed. Then the day for install came. Appliance came in damaged, delivery was refused and the new dishwasher was taken away but the old one left in place. This was on a Saturday and a new delivery day was made for the following Wednesday. Saturday night I received an email with an Installation Control Form attached, basically saying that the old dishwasher was hauled away and the new one was installed and I knew about the damage, but accepted it anyway. On this form, someone printed my name on all of the appropriate lines, as if to forge my signature. I know it wasn't me because I was out of town for Army Reserves training and it wasn't my mother on my behalf (she was the one to refuse delivery). Monday came and I received another email stating they were coming Wednesday to haul away the old dishwasher but made no mention of the new dishwasher. I called and was told it was on backorder. After a lot of back and forth I managed to get a new delivery day of the following Monday. That Monday came and I finally received my dishwasher.
I will never buy from Pacific Kitchens again.....and I'm truly contemplating not ever going back into Best Buy for any reason. As I said in the title....You should definitely buy this dishwasher, but I would get it from a company that will not lie to you or try forging your signature on documents.
Appliances.summary: Get this dishwasher....But don't go to Best Buy

Appliances.reviewText:
Quick delivery from prime allowed us to miss only a couple of dishwasher cycles. Used for our Kitchen Aid dishwasher which is 2 years old exactly.

Installation was very quick.  Instructions used B&W photos that made it difficult to see whether the clips was upside down or right side up. Removing the old Adjuster was much more difficult than installing this. Came with a special screw that you attached to your screwdriver to finish off the unit.

Putting the unit back was easy enough... we're taking it easy for now.

I've had it about a week now.  Been making ice non-stop and my deep freezer is half full with bagged ice.
I cleaned it initially with vinegar and ran several cycles through it.
The ice has the consistency of hard packed snow, not rock hard ice like from an ice tray... Which is better, more like from a pop machine at a resteraunt.
I wish it kept the ice cold once it's made, but it doesn't.  It doesn't melt very fast, but when it does, it drips back into the bottom where it gets made into new cubes.  I don't think the size selector does a damn thing.  Regardless of what I select it all comes out the same size or so close you can't tell.
It makes almost no noise except for when it drops the cubes.
I look forward to using this on boat trips. :-)

Bought this for my husband to use at work. So far we've only used it once when we got it in the mail, but it seems to work as it should. Easy to put together and it comes with an extra wick, which is nice. my only complaint is that the top does not screw on at all. it's is just a tight fit. While this makes it compatible for it to fit other bottles, if it falls over or is knocked down hard enough, the top will most undoubtedly come off. Another con is that the wick is to short to use with most standard water bottles. We tried it out with a regular sized bottle and it only went about half way down.
Appliances.summary: Easy to put together and it comes with an extra ...

Appliances.reviewText: This product installed quite easily and saved several hundred dollars in not having to call a service tech.  The original element on the dryer started to smell like burnt plastic and all the clothes coming out had that smell.  This fit perfectly and also solved another problem that had existed for over a year on the dryer. The heating option with a cool down feature did not work anymore.  The thermostat replacement fixed that problem.

All in all we are very happy with the range hood. I the control panel is easy to use with the exception of setting the time. That takes either a manual or some fiddling around with the touch screen. I am rating it 4 stars because, as many others have mentioned, it came with a couple of small dents right out of the box. The way it was packed and the condition of the box indicates that they were there when the hood was boxed. I will say they are not really noticeable and the installer was able to smooth the worst one out a bit. I figure if you look at the suggested retail price and then what they are selling for you have the reason why the price is so cheap. Most of them are probably graced with very minor dents and scratches.

The fan while not real quiet is noticeably quieter than the one it replaced. The lights are a little dim but not so much that I will make on issue of them. This unit looks very nice in our newly remodeled kitchen and I would recommend it.
Appliances.summary: All in all we are very happy with the range hood

Appliances.reviewText: We just installed our kit yesterday. Our Maytag duet models are about 7 years old. The screws are really difficult to put in and require quite a bit of manpower. The bracket has a "lip" at the top that seems to hold onto the dryer, which made me feel a little better than just stacking them up there. You could probably find these brackets at a hardware store for a lot less, so even though I paid $13, that's a lot of money for two brackets, 4 bolts, and two pad strips. Unfortunately, no one sells the kits for less than that so I guess they're all overpriced. Here are pictures of the brackets and our washer and dryer. Please ignore the two different colors. It's what happens when you send your husband to a wholesale appliance store by himself.
Appliances.summary: Works great for older duet models but overpriced.

Appliances.reviewText: worked perfectly however there is one design flaw. the bracket you attach last, requires you to drive screws in from the side. so if you are putting the washer and dryer next to a wall you would have to have them stacked but away from the wall then attach the screws then slide the whole beast as one unit. I have a rubber floor so I could not slide it so unfortunately i have to leave that one screw un-screwed.
Appliances.summary: worked perfectly however there is one design flaw. the ...

Appliances.reviewText:
Installation a bit tricky, but it looks nice. Bottom panel could fasten in an easier way (tabs vs. screws perhaps), but once it's assembled it looks slick. Only problem is filter (Broan BPQTF non-ducted charcoal filter) bumps into the fan, causing noise. Especially a problem when fan is on high and sucks filter toward itself. Seems fan should be set deeper into the hood to avoid this. Or perhaps have a bar across bottom of fan to avoid the problem. Have rigged it so that filter sits on supports against the back wall (front end of filter still slotted into range hood), so that there's enough clearance. Is the fan depth adjustable?

Runs pretty quietly (when it's not hitting the filter). Don't know yet how well it works - only had it in for one day. Went with halogen lights to avoid problems with buzzing with LEDs and inability to use both high and low settings (reported in other reviews). Love how bright they are. All in all, am happy with my purchase except for the fan problem.

So I bought this dishwasher from my local appliance store's "floor model" section. I was without a dishwasher, had a house full of dirty dishes, and was about to be snowed in so I took a chance. I hadn't checked the Amazon reviews, maybe I would have decided on something else if I had.

First of all, my thoughts on price - this is NOT a $1000 dishwasher. I would never have paid that much for it. It is a perfectly good $500 dishwasher, which is what I paid. I could really see people being disgruntled if they had paid a lot for this unit.

This is, in spite of its price tag and appearance, a pretty mid-grade dishwasher in terms of features and performance - hence me being happy with the $500 price tag.

I want to address some of the common complaints I've seen on here:

Complaint: The handle hits the floor.
My Take: No, it doesn't. Where did you mount this? You would have to shove the front door all the way past fully open. Huh? The door doesn't hard-stop at horizontal, is that what you mean?

Complaint: Racks are unwieldy/fall out/come off the rails/etc.
My Take: Top rack has been rock solid. Bottom rack isn't actually ON rails, and the door does go past horizontal so ... but seriously? I haven't ever had a problem.

Complaint: No heating element.
My Take: It pretty much says in BIG BOLD LETTERS that it doesn't have a heating element. Really? You bought a Ford and you're complaining it doesn't have a twin turbo in it? Umm... yeah.

Complaint: Funny smell.
My Take: The first few washes I ran there was a "new dishwasher, hot plastic/rubber/metal" smell. It got better and better with each load until it went away. Occasional stink is handled with DISHWASHER CLEANER. You do know they make that, right? Of course you do.

Complaint: It's slow.
My Take: As compared to...?

Complaint: Fills with water.
My Take: It's a dish... washer. It fills with water. That's what it does.

But seriously now, here's my thoughts.

Cons:

1. No heated dry. This is also a pro, so it really evens out. But if you were looking for heated dry, this isn't going to make you happy. The dishes evaporatively dry. Everything on the lower rack is good and dry, everything on the upper rack that faces downward is dry. Anything with a concave top on the upper rack will be a little damp. That's pretty much to be expected with a unit like this.

2. A limited number of fancy features. You get delicate/normal/heavy wash, rinse only, top rack wash (that's a pro, though) and child lock. That's ... pretty ... much ... it.

3. The flatware rack is a little ... limiting. Not the worst I've seen, but not even as good as my old Whirlpool.

4. No steam. It has "sani-rinse" but it's unclear exactly what that does since there's no heating element. I suspect it just makes the water VERY HOT.

Neither Pro nor Con:

1. It's slow. This is to be expected from an ultra-quiet, ultra-efficient unit. A full wash SAYS it will take 2 hours but quickly senses load and dirt levels. With normal loading in my experience it takes about 85 minutes. Not too bad, but not a speed demon.

Pro:

1. Stainless tub. Really nice.

2. Super quiet. I feel the vibration in the floor more than I hear the noise of operation. And neither is pronounced.

3. "Top rack only" option. This is the one feature I was delighted to have because I really missed it in my old Fisher/Paykel - the ability to JUST wash glasses after you've had people over for drinks or snacks... or after your teenagers have wandered in and out and made every glass you own dirty.

4. High efficiency. Limited water use.

5. No heating element. Yeah, that means no heated dry. But it also mean no melted tupperware.

6. Load and soil sensing. The unit starts with a guesstimate for time and water needed, and adjusts from there. I'm pretty impressed, actually. A heavily soiled load took 95+ minutes, more lightly soiled loads as little as 70, the average has been around 80-85.
Appliances.summary: had a house full of dirty dishes, and was about to be snowed in ...

Appliances.reviewText: It's too hot/humid to use the bucket in our apartment right now, so we just attached the bucket cover to the free end of the hose and vented it out a window! No problems, and beats hanging things up to dry. In the colder weather, we will use the bucket and hopefully it will work out well. The quality of the product is fine for the price, and it arrived in a timely manner.

Perfect for my decor however I wished they also sold it individually. I purchased 2 pairs and they are used up by the 2 door refrigerator and the freezer and the microwave oven. I wished I could make individual purchase for the conventional oven which doesn't have a handle cover. However the product is good and reading other reviews I decided not to machine wash it. Since the color is black and white you it will get stained very easily and all I do is hand wash it to avoid any damage to the cover.
Appliances.summary: Perfect for my decor however I wished they also sold ...

Appliances.reviewText: Good product at a great price. It's hard to find a dual temp wine cooler at this price, but this one works well. The shelves are cheap (but who cares?) but have enough depth to fit most bottles. I've yet to try a large Burgundy bottle, I assume it would not fit without taking out a shelf. My only complaint is that the bright blue LED lights that show the temp cannot be turned off or dimmed. At night it stands out like a sore thumb. If that isn't a big deal to you, then I would highly recommend it.
Appliances.summary: Good product at a great price

Appliances.reviewText: Purchased several units of these and all of them fit very well in my refrigerator.  Quite happy with this product.  One challenge is, I am not sure why they make these bins with brittle plastic!  I can understand Whirlpool's poor design of the doors and placement of these bins make them bump into each other and eventually break!  ( I believe this is by design to make you buy accessories eventually).  Hence 4 stars.

As with most items that come with instructions, it is very important to read the instructions.  The instructions clearly state that the user should flush the filters upon installation to prepare them for use.  The water coming out through the filters is tasteless and odorless as water should be.  Very glad I found these filters at the price I found them.

I got this to replace an icemaker in a 14 year old Kenmore refrigerator.  I like it.  The cubes are bigger, and it cycles faster than the old one.  In fact, I have had to turn it off because my bin was filled, which never happened with the original.

The only thing to watch for (as mentioned by others) is that the instructions are rather poor.  If I hadn't read these reviews, I would have had a heck of a time finding the place to plug the cord into the icemaker itself.

We've suffered trying to find filters that fit without leaking, and the Water Sentinel has delivered for us twice now. We use this filter in our Samsung RS2630SH refrigerator and so far it has worked well. This one feels a little tighter than other brands we've tried that leak, perhaps an indication of a good seal?

My only complaint with this purchase is the most recent one I ordered - it did not come with o-ring lubricant.
Appliances.summary: No leaks, but did not include lubricant

Appliances.reviewText: Filter is direct replacement, instructions weren't totally clear.  They recommend to soak the filter for 15 minutes before installing (can't remember if this is in the pamphlet, but not on the packaging, or the other way around).  Now when I get water out of the door, the stream is strong, but there is also a little bit of dribble toward the front of the dispenser.  There's a joke there, but it's not intentional.  Overall it's good, and cheaper than the original.
Appliances.summary: Good with a couple sticking points.

Appliances.reviewText:
Everyone,

My wife bought me this kegerator for a birthday present and I was super excited.  I ordered a keg of Stone IPA, and after some searching, I found a local place that exchanges 5 lbs beverage-quality CO2 canisters.  I went ahead and swapped the empty that came with this setup for one of their exchange canisters because in the end, I think it will make my life easier not having to worry about refilling it.

I put it all together, let everything chill down inside the fridge to the coldest setting of 7 (this is important because the CO2 loses pressure when it gets cold).  When I went to pour the beer, it was super foamy.  I thought it was just the new keg so I let it sit for another day, and I tried it again only to end up with the same result.  I wasn't sure what to do, so I did some research and found that for my elevation, my regulator was out-of-the-box set to 25 PSI - way too high.  I found a PSI kegerator chart, and realized that I needed to be at a much, much lower PSI of around 5.  I got a wrench and twisted the +/- nob on the regulator until I got it down to 5 PSI and that solved the foam problem - I did not need a new hose like some of the reviews stated.

My next issue.  Once I adjusted the pressure the pour was fine, but I noticed the beer had a really strong plastic/rubber/metallic/chemical smell/taste.  I did more research and convinced myself I had oxidized my beer by having it exposed to too much CO2 PSI -  this later turned out to be false and I learned that beer can easily withstand up to 30 PSI without being ruined.  I was ready to call it a wasted-keg-day, but out of denial I continued to do research on the problem.

Finally, I found an article on a beer brewing forum that talked about how the synthetic washer between the keg and the tap hose could be to blame.  I disconnected the keg from the hose that connects it to the pourer, and I could smell the problem at once.  There is this white ring/washer/gasket thing that comes with this kegerator that is known to give the beer this horrible taste/smell as it passes over it and/or sits in the tube, and it reeked of that chemical smell.  I truly did not know one little washer could stink and foul up beer so badly, but it sure can.  My fingers still smelled like that chemical a day after I washed them, and I have a terrible sense of smell.  I yanked that thing out, replaced it with a rubber o-ring, and the problem was 90% solved.  I ordered a keg cleaning kit to flush the remainder of the smell out of the tap tube, and a set of black synthetic washers that has been reported not to have that problem.

The only reason I gave it a 4/5 is because of the research I had to do, and the emotional toll it took on me thinking I ruined 5 gallons of expensive beer.  I can tell you right now with 100% honesty that I am enjoying a beer, straight from my keg, and it is delicious.  This thing is going to turn me into a beer snob for sure.

I emailed the people at Smart+ and hopefully soon they will stop shipping those bad-news white washers.

Make sure you adjust your regulator, make sure you don't use one of those white washers, and you will love this thing.

-R

I have fine hair that is in a medium bob. After getting this I wished I'd bought the 1 1/2" brush head instead of the 2". It would also have been nice if I could have interchanged the two sizes without having to buy an entirely different brush to get the correct size or even to use the larger size on top and the smaller size on my bottom layer.

Honestly, I have used a round brush and blow dryer for years and I still think I can get my hair better if I do it manually myself. This is pretty good for my bangs especially if I just want to do them and not shampoo my entire head.

I think it's pretty easy to work and handle. I don't find it overly heavy or difficult to use. Just takes a little getting used to but nothing that I'd complain about.

I won't be buying the smaller size though. I'll just use my smaller brush to do it myself as I always have.

It's an ice maker, it either makes ice or it doesn't. The first one I got worked for about a week and then quit. Had to remove all the parts, which is a rather involved job, and return it. Amazon is really great with returns so that part was easy. Got the second one and it has been running great for about 2 months. This ice maker only makes about 8-9 cubes at a time but makes a surprising amount of ice per day, enough for a family of 4 in Florida in the summertime.
Appliances.summary: Amazon is really great with returns so that part was easy

Appliances.reviewText:
I've been using this machine for a week now, everyday. It works as expected, clean my clothes properly and the spin dry gets them about 90% dry before I hang them on a rack to finish drying. My issues with this product however are the following:

- leaks a little during use (I've laid a towel down before use and now I'm fine)
- spin dry starting and stopping shakes the machine voilently, once it's in the middle of spin dry it runs fine but starting up/cooling down I need to hold it
- fill hose was EU without adapter
- instruction booklet is useless (just look up a tutorial on YouTube if this is your first time using a machine like this)

i tried the replacement part for this but did not work! i order this one because it is exactly like the one that i have in the frig and it worked. I looked up the mo no. for my fridge on the ge site and several others sites and it gave me the replacement part no. for my fridge and ordered it but would not work.

I really liked my first non-digital Danby until the drain pump failed after a year.  I coudln't get any response from Danby customer service (I needed a new drain pump) and stupidly ignored that and bought this digital Danby.  Well, now it's spin-spray arm stopped rotating reliably after only a month!  I don't like the fact that it's digital interface won't let you alter the cycle at all.  A real pain.  And I still can't get Danby customer service on the telephone (after waiting 30 minutes on hold) and they don't answer emails.  I won't buy another Danby, especially due to the customer service problem.
Appliances.summary: Failing (again) and still no customer service

Appliances.reviewText:
This motor does not fit all WA6500 series range hoods. If your hood has a variable speed control or an extra letter after WA6500, or if your output shaft is not on the same end as the mounting studs, it will not work, and you will be shopping for a different motor plus a new speed control because you will fry your speed control.  My motor has the same connector but the red wire is green and connects to ground, thereby shorting the speed control output to ground.

And another warning: if you purchase the $11 filter which is "frequently purchased together" so that you can get free shipping by having a total order over $49, Amazon will still aggressively push you into subscribing to Amazon Prime at the checkout by promising you free shipping only if you go for the membership.

So, my total cost to date, including return shipping, is about $180, and I now have a fried control and no working motor, and an Amazon Prime membership that I have absolutely no plans to use.  BTW I am usually very good at ordering parts and fixing things.
Appliances.summary: Does not fit all WA6500 series range hoods.

Appliances.reviewText:
We bought this 6 months ago along with the LG refridgerator 28CF French Door.
THe fridge is awesome - but the dishwasher just looks nice.

It won't remove wet cereal from bowls - you just wipe goo off with your finger of the still wet dishes after a full 2 hour cycle.
It is quiet, plays a little jingle when done and looks pretty = but the dog licking your dishes will get them cleaner.  LG makes nice TV's and Fridges but they make a pitiful dishwasher

Less than half the price of the official Bosch part but an exact fit replacement. I have little polite to say about Bosch engineering (4th igniter replacement in 4 years) or their use of 3 different kinds of fasteners, including a star drive, to make it as hard as possible for the homeowner to do his own replacement. Next time, I won't buy a Bosch, but until then, Supco supplies an excellent part, promptly delivered at a most excellent price.
ON the other hand: purchased in February, failed in May = 3 month lifetime. That's no bargain. The real problem is Bosch's abysmal engineering, but Supco is adding insult to injury with this replacement part.
Appliances.summary: Exact fit replacement that lasted 3 months

Appliances.reviewText: This is the second time I have had to replace this part on a high end KitchenAid Dishwasher. The first replacement lasted five years - this one lasted less than one week. Always saw the same issues as other reviews with very loud squeak and very tight rope. Contacted seller but no reply. Don't buy this part from Senaca River Trading Company.

Aqua-Pure filters are made in the US under license from the patent holder. This is a cheap Chinese knock-off of uncertain quality. Do not buy this POS if you want a real Aqua-Pure filter.

UPDATE: After seller insisted in Questions that this filter is made in the USA and only assembled in China, I decided to test it to see if his additional claim that it works as well as any other filter is true. I tested it with the TDS meter I use to monitor the RO/DI water purifier I use for my saltwater aquarium. First, I ran 5 gallons of water through this filter installed in my Samsung fridge. The water was black for a while, but it cleared up by gallon 3. Instructions say run it for 5 minutes to flush carbon dust, and it took about 7 minutes to pull 5 G.

Measured TDS for the "Aqua-Pure compatible" was 138 PPM. Then I measured unfiltered tap water, and once again got 138 PPM. I repeated the test three times on each water source and got the same figures, +/- 1 PPM.

Consequently, I know that this device does not filter water at all and is certainly not compatible with Aqua Pure. It works no better than having no filter at all in the fridge.

UPDATE 2: The genuine Aqua Pure doesn't reduce TDS either, so it appears that fridge filters are a waste of money even when they're not falsely promoted.
Appliances.summary: Does not filter water in a measurable way.

Appliances.reviewText: Just want everyone to be aware that when you buy a modern GE refrigerator your now stuck with their mobster practice water filters.  Their modern filters are now equipped with a radio frequency device so ONLY their filters will work.  This is a cheap charcoal filter that they get $50 each for.  They tell you six months but check online forums and the max anyone is getting is four months.  I live in Phoenix with pretty bad water and I get two months before the fridge starts going crazy with warnings.  Simple math is $600 extra each year for filters.  Sorry GE, the Gambino crime family never had it so good.

I bought two, mainly for the humidity reading. I tried using both side by side in the same room. The temperature readings were almost identical,  but there was such a wide range of difference in the humidity readings,  that I couldn't trust either to be correct. When I went online to print a return label I was given a message saying that I could not return the product! I will not purchase this product again, nor will I ever purchase anything from this seller.

I don't understand why people will recommend this product. It is even worse than any $100.00-$300.00 Home depot kitchen hood! Every time when I cook, the smoke is not gong out from the Range Hood but everywhere in my house!! I had had to open all of the window in my house every time before I cook!

Skip this one! I have owned this cooktop for 3 years. It has a serious design flaw. Cooking on the front 2 burners will melt the control knobs. I contacted Electrolux for replacements knobs and was told to cook on the back burners. They "offered" a 10% discount for me to buy new knobs. Or I can buy new grates for $575.....REALLY???!! That won't even help!!! If you buy , it will be great for cooking, but it will look like s-h-i-t.

This wick doesn't work well in my MA12010 humidifier. When wet it has no structural strength so it flops over. It is thinner than the original wick. It is packaged folded even though the humidifier installation is circular. The creases from the folds make the structural defects even worse. I strongly recommended looking elsewhere even if it costs a little more.

Be warned. You're not getting a fine piece of German engineering.
Build quality would rate a zero if allowed.
Little bits of plastic started falling off this unit almost immediately. Broken shelf pegs, broken door flap holders and so forth.
Worst of all is it is impossible to dispatch the FILTRCHNG warning even after replacing the filter.
Technicians are useless.
The units runs way to cold and since you can't dispose of the alarms it's impossible to change the temperature.
The menu controller button is flimsy plastic in a flimsy housing that requires tons of force to actuate. Essentially it's broken inside.
Stay away. Bosch has lost it. No quality control at all.

The Rack was in perfect condition. Right, now, I'm thinking about using them as a plant shelf between two milk crates on my patio...

Anyways, my "one star" rating is only because of the above.  If you've ordered oven racks before and know what you're doing (obviously unlike me),
I would recommend this very highly.  It looked brand new!
Appliances.summary: The Rack was in perfect condition.

Appliances.reviewText: This was my secind time trying this brand. Both times it would not work in my fridge. Great price for a bad product. Only gave a one star due to i have to put something. Before i bought this i read to ensure it work with ge gswf, double checked my cureent filter of different brnad. Yup uses gswf...but not this brands verison. I would go elsewhere even of it costs a little more

These shelves are POS. We bought our fridge brand new four years ago. The deli drawer busted years ago and now I have three broken shelves. New fridge cost us about as much as these replacement shelves and drawer. Hate to buy a new fridge when this one works fine, but investing this much money into these crappy shelves that won't last is just money down the drain.

Have had this dishwasher for 3.5 years and this is my first problem with it.  However, it is the same 03 error code (wash pump not working) that many of the prior reviewers have experienced on this website and as noted on other sites, and upon calling Electrolux for warranty (or defective part) coverage, of course, there is nothing covering this type of issue.  It is incredibly frustrating that with my very low usage (travel much of the time and typically do one to two loads a week, if that) that essentially after a typical 1.5 years of usage, the wash pump has to be replaced.  Obviously, they don't stand behind the equality of the product.  Although customer service was relatively helpful in pricing out the potential part replacement costs and recognized local appliance repair people, when asking me at the end of the call, if I wanted to participate in customer service survey, and I said, "You Betcha" ready to blast Electrolux, I was amazingly transferred into oblivion, which has NEVER happened in a survery situation before.  I think it was a matter of selective disconnection for survey manipulation...I think Kelly Ripa needs to attach her name to another brand!!  Would not buy another product from this company, which is so disappointing as I like so many aspects of this dishwasher.

I Purchase this unit a year and half ago with moderate use, you always have to shake it back and forth when it shows need water and there is plenty in there, something to do with a switch and no fix.
Now all of sudden it is done compute no longer worky, seems the gears in the tub have stripped out likely from ice build up as the tub is cracked as well.
I used epoxy to seal up the tub and the gears will not hold it in place.

Cheap Junk.

For what it is worth... I bought this new a little over 2 years ago.  I had a few issues with tearing up cotton t-shirts, but ran them separately on delicate and that seemed to work.  The clothes came out pretty clean.  Every so often there would be what looked like a grease stain on clothes which wasn't there prior to washing.  Overall, at this point I was happy with the washer.  Now however, the washer spins and drains, but the clothes come out soaking wet.  Repairman can't find the problem and suggested replacing the electronic panel and part of the motor for about $600.  I am in the market to buy a new machine all together.  I am very upset about spending a lot of money for a washer which only lasted 2 years.  Please buy something else.

It's actually difficult to truly rate this item because I ordered (and was charged for by Seneca River Trading) a genuine Maytag replacement part #27001007 washer belt and received the ERP (generic) replacement belt. I could have purchased the generic belt locally for about $7.00. I chose the Maytag brand name for it's durability. I'm sure this belt would have worked, but I ordered a genuine Maytag belt for it's quality for a high-use commercial washer. If you are looking to order this belt, you will probably do better to find the generic (37820) belt for a lot less cost. Again, the generic belt should work for basic use but, I still recommend the genuine Maytag belt for quality and longevity. Overall, I'm just not happy having been deceived with this purchase. Don't be duped!

The smart hub stopped working after 6 months.  It was great when it worked but the outdoor sensors are useless without the ability to access the data by the app.

Update 10/09:
I called the company and the customer service person was awesome.  They had me go through a number of steps and everything worked again.  They even helped me update my MyAcuRite account while on the phone.  Back to tracking temps around my house and garden
Appliances.summary: The smart hub stopped working after 6 months

Appliances.reviewText: We bought this dishwasher 8 months ago. In the last 2 months we have had 3 companies come out 5 different times to try to repair this. Nothing on the top rack comes clean. In fact the dishes on the top actually come out dirtier than when they were put in. Because it was within the warranty period, Whirlpool paid for the service repairs. However, when I called Whirlpool for the last repair on 10/7/2013, I was told that it already had 5 repairs and so if this repair didn't fix the problem, they would replace the dishwasher.( Their policy is that it has to have 3 service calls done before they can deem it unrepairable.) Well 6 days later all of the dishes on the top rack were dirty again. When I called to report that the problem wasn't fixed, I was told that I would need to have another repairman come out to make a call to their technical services. I was also told that the last repairman should have done this as it was on his service ticket. Not my problem that he doesn't follow their instructions. Now Whirlpool would like me to rearrange me schedule, and sit around for another 5 hour window for another repairman, the 6th service call since August 6, 2013. I told them it was completely unacceptable. I have gotten no where with their customer service. I am pretty sure that they make up their policies as they go along, as every person I have talked to has given me a different story or version. I was referred to the customer care center and was told I would be contacted the same day. I was called the next day and when I wasn't available, they left a message with a number to the managers direct line. I have called for 2 days, left multiple messages and have had no success in talking to the customer care manager. Whirlpool's customer service is non existent. They do not care about selling crap in a shiny package. They have no intention on helping their consumers. I will never buy another Whirlpool product.

A little over 2 1/2 years ago, I purchased a brand new front loading Whirlpool washing machine (Whirlpool LHW0050PQ) with stacking dryer. About a month ago, it stopped working (the warranty for the machine was 1 year, so it is no longer covered). The power would come on - but the machine would no longer begin wash cycles (the Start button did nothing). I had a repair person in who took several visits to diagnose the problem. In the end, it was determined that the machine required a new control panel. The control panel cost over $500. With labour, I have spent approximately $800 now. When the part was replaced, as soon as the repair person left, I did a load of laundry, only to discover that the problem still existed *exactly* as it had before. I called the repair company - who wanted to take the machine to their shop to diagnose it. What they found was that the new part had almost instantly shorted out as soon as the machine was used for the first time after replacing it. They contacted Whirlpool technical support who told them that something in the machine must be causing the short. According to the person at the repair shop that I spoke to, Whirlpool offered to give them a door latching mechanism for free for the washing machine so that they could perhaps see if it was causing the short (my repair people did install this part).
