In addition, Whirlpool gave me a new control panel (a new $500 part to replace the one that I bought that had burnt out - because it was still under warranty as a new part purchase). I now have the washing machine back and it seems to be working, but I have no faith whatsoever that it will continue to work for any length of time.

Here are my concerns:
- obviously, it positively sickens me that I would have to spend $800 to repair a washing machine that is only 2 1/2 years old. The washing machine was not cheap. I thought I was buying quality. This obviously wasn't the case.
- upon learning that the replacement part would cost so much, I would have just bought a new washing machine (not from Whirlpool!). However, the repair shop explained to me that my stackable Whirlpool dryer was only going to fit on top of a Whirlpool washing machine. So, to replace the washing machine would mean that I would also have to sell my dryer. Weighing the pros and cons of the situation, I decided to fix the washing machine even though it positively sickened me to give Whirlpool another cent. I find it equally repulsive that, when one buys a stackable unit, they're basically stuck if one part of it fails (this would be more acceptable, of course, if the machines lasted considerably longer than 2 1/2 years).
- when the repair person first brought the replacement part to my house, he mentioned that the replacement part was now being sold as part of a kit (control board with motor board - that's how they had purchased it from Whirlpool). He mentioned that, when parts come in a kit, it usually means the company has had problems with the part (so they sell the parts in a way that makes the many repair jobs easier). If Whirlpool has been having problems with this part, I have to wonder why they wouldn't instead compensate customers who'd bought the part in the first place. The fact that the replacement part had *exactly* the same problems as the original part makes me wonder the exact same thing.
- I have to wonder how much Whirlpool is making off of these replacement parts. It is absurd to me that any washing machine part should cost $500 - unless, of course, the company selling the part is marking up its value considerably. I really have to wonder if this isn't part of the company's business model: selling units that fail shortly after the warranty expires and then selling the parts required to fix the units at a jacked up price.
- related to the above point, the $500 replacement part has a guarantee of 3 months. Three months for something that cost over $500! In other words, if the part goes again in 4 months (and the machine's history tells me that this is a great possibility), I am completely out of luck again. I have never - ever - spent $500 on something that didn't come with a guarantee that wasn't at least a year long. You can buy a $30 toaster anywhere and it comes with at least a 1 year warranty! But I guess, considering what I believe to be their business model (see above), I'm not really that surprised by this.
- I am extremely confused by Whirlpool technical support's involvement in this. You would think that the nature of their involvement was an admission that something in the machine had caused the $500 part to go in the first place. This is especially suspect since they offered another part for free to try to make that determination. I just have to wonder why I should have had to pay $800 to replace a part that was caused by a fault with the machine in the first place.
- I have spent $800 and been without a working washing machine for over a month now. That alone is ridiculous. But, to add potential injury to insult, I now have a washing machine with parts that have proven to short out because of a deficiency with the machine. In other words, I now have to wonder if my washing machine is going to catch fire every time I use it!

I have written to Whirlpool 3 times now about this situation. All they really told me in return was that they appreciate my business and that they have added my concerns to their database. I don't think I need to explain to anyone what little consolation that has given me...

This range is a disaster. Negative five stars.
Ours has been on fire twice, all burners and burner controls have been replaced twice.
We are afraid to leave it plugged in because the lower oven will go on by itself and won't shut off unless it is unplugged.  The control board and lower oven temperature sensor are bad.
Left alone this thing would have burned our house down at least twice.
I am done with repairs,  this thing is going in the trash where it belongs.
This thing is not even a good boat anchor.
I will never buy another Maytag and suggest you do the same.

This range appears excellent; it works well (when it works), appears to be efficient, and could be really impressive, BUT it is completely dependent on digital technology, technology that clearly isn't ready for wide release.  Right now, our 6 month old range is incapacitated--the gas works, the electricity is fine, but the control panel has crapped out, so the oven can't be used.  Now if our gas were turned off, or we had a power outage, I could handle this, but to have an oven that doesn't work without properly functioning microchips is insane.  It's stupid, it's inexcusable, and it flat out makes no sense.  Why would any responsible company take an elegant, simple technology that works--the gas oven--with a long history of efficient functioning, and then screw it up by making it dependent on crummy, unreliable microchips and printed circuit boards?

Beats me.

Electrolux says they'll have someone here within the week.

I have intended on writing a review for the past 8 years that I have owned this range.  The only thing I like is the style.  The oven is worse than your cheapest range.  Oven temps are not consistent.  I know that few ovens will keep a consistent temp. but this is the worst that I have ever owned.  It takes forever to get a pot of water to boil on the burner.  The burners keep cycling on and off.  The over door has a fan that runs whenever the oven is on.  I talked to the company about it and they said that it was a fan on the door to keep the door cool.  Thus I can't use my oven when I have guests during warm months because the kitchen is too hot.  I had rather have a warm oven door than warm guests..

I have a neighbor/friend and she has the Dacor gas range and has same problem with the oven and hates it.

This is a $300 range with a 3000 style.
Appliances.summary: The only thing I like is the style

Appliances.reviewText: So disappointed in this spin brush!  When I purchased the 2" barrel I expected the dryer to be 2".  Instead, the barrel may be 2" but the brush is huge.  I have medium length hair and this thing is useless to me.  I didn't bother with all the return hassle so will give it to one of my girls with long hair.
Appliances.summary: Only for LONG hair otherwise useless

Appliances.reviewText:
I bought this for my ferret, but neither I nor she will be handling it. Ferrets are already so prone to cancer and this duct contains carcinogens.  It was not stated in the description, but was stated on the box that this tunnel is made of carcinogenic materials.

Sent to return as soon as I read the packaging.
Appliances.summary: Danger Contains Carcinogens! Not safe for human or ferret handling.

Appliances.reviewText:
This was ordered via Amazon Prime from "PrimeCo Supply" and fulfilled by Amazon. I specifically ordered this version because it was advertised as the OEM part. I was fairly confident I would get the correct part because the vendor had 100% feedback and the listing stated to report to Amazon if an aftermarket part was received.

When i opened the part, I immediately knew it was not the original LG part. It came in a plain box with a printed bar code taped on and the pump assembly had no markings for motor rating, etc. However, my washer had already been down a few days and laundry piles up fast with three kids, so I decided I would install it anyway.

After disassembling the washer and removing the old pump, i tried to put the new pump in the plastic housing, but it would not fit right. The pump looked similar, but was not the same size and the slots to slide into the housing were not in the right spot. You can see the attached picture of the difference. I could have forced it in the housing and probably made it work, but this was clearly not a very good copy of the part, so decided to just return it and get a replacement.

I ordered another one, this time directly from Amazon for a few dollars more and it was clearly the correct part. It had LG printed on the box with a part number sticker the correct printing on the unit. It fit perfectly and the washer now works great.

For future customers, the second picture shows what the box should look like. If not, you probably received some cheap knock-off like i did.

This is the second time i have received a machine the leaks. The box was banged up again with the first load it leaked alover my floor. The machine also is banged up. I have a 7.5 load machine and have never had a problem with it. Its very upsetting because ive paid alot for something that i reall need.

When I read the part i the Samsung manual that they did not cover leaks due to using non-Smasung brand water filters I figured it was just a way to sell more filters. Well, I was wrong! Although this filter looks just like the Samsung one it slowly leaked, filling the bin below with water. What a mess! When I replaced it with the Samsung brand filter: no leak.

I wouldn't do without this dishwasher basket.  All my small items can be washed in this basket without bouncing all over the dishwasher.  I'm a grandma with 5 grands, and I told my daughter about this so she could put the baby bottle caps and nipples in the dishwasher, also after the baby became a toddler, the sippy cup lids could be washed in this basket.  It's the greatest.  And the shipping was reasonable in price, and arrived in a very timely manner.  Thanks!

Excellent product and the supplier delivered it on time and I like the fact that it does a min/max for both.  I am using it to try and understand where moisture may be coming from in my home which is creating frost in my attic and causing dampening of my home ceilings when warm weather first starts to return in winters
Appliances.summary: Excellent product and the supplier delivered it on time and ...

Appliances.reviewText:
My fridge was included when I bought my house a few months ago, and the filtering power ran out a couple of weeks ago. I was unsure what to do, where to buy-everything. I used the owner's manual to get the part number and went to Amazon to search. These were cheaper, I read the
reviews and it seemed that they were mostly recommended positively. I bought them and it was a quick installation and I saved money by buying
these instead of the brand name. Work great, cheaper price, easy installation. Highly recommended.

I bought this particular Water Filter because it was the one for our refigerator.  I bought the 3-pack so that I would have some on hand.  The installation was a breeze.  I followed the directions that came with the filter and had no problems.  Removal was a simple CCW twist of the canister.  Likewise, installation was a simple clock-wise twist of the new canister into the holder.  I prefilled the new canister with tap water, per instructions, and ran about a gallon through before drinking.  I have had no problems and the water tastes great.  I would buy from Amazon again, since they had a good price for the brand I wanted.

I can always trust that I will find the best price through the amazon.com network.  After making several calls to whirlpool dealerships, I found this part.  I was significantly cheaper than what I had expected and showed up ahead of schedule.  It was supplied by laundrydoc.com.  Those guys are amazing.  I have to credit amazon for always hooking me up with the best suppliers.  Online shopping doesn't get any better than this.
Appliances.summary: Best Price, Excellent delivery, great condition.

Appliances.reviewText: It worked great! The reason for me giving 5 stars and not only the part but the company has great costumer service. I had ordered silver but needed black. Spoke with someone at the company and the response was awesome. It's hard to find company's now a days that are on your side. Will order from them again for sure!

Fit perfect. You have to reuse the bottom cover/mount from your old unit. My old unit had different size screws holding it on. For this unit I used Qty 2,  M3-.5 X 10 philips pan head screws and a washers to install it. Other than that, no problems. We're quietly making ice now. No more banging noises!

I always try to keep one of these silly contraptions in my disposal unit. It has saved many, many pieces of cutlery thru the years!
Also, keeps your hands from coming in contact with all the garbage that is being pushed into that little hole in the sink! I leave it in the disposal at all times and rarely need to use the 'stopper' feature, since I have a double sink.

I don't know what the other reviewer is talking about with regards to the holes.  These bags have the cut out holes in them, they are just difficult to see.  I had to look really hard to find them but they are there.  These bags worked just fine and are cheaper than the regular compactor bags that I usually get on Amazon.  I have ordered a bunch more.

This product works as expected, and is the correct model for my fridge.  It is possible however, that I did not need it.  My water dispenser made a strange noise, and dispensed almost no water.  The same was likely true for the ice maker.  I was not able to remove the upper panel, which is what I needed to do in order to replace the part (I was afraid of breaking something), so I called whirlpool for service.  The tech was at my house for about 10 minutes, and it cost me $230 for a service call and labor.  The tech asked if I had the bypass cap, which I was not sure where I placed it, since I had remodeled my kitchen after getting the fridge.  Long story short.  He took the (1 week old) filter out, put in a new one, and it worked.  For one day...  The next day I tried ordering a bypass cap, and then found that I stored mine in the door.  I took out the filter, and put in the cap, ran the water a little, replaced the filter, and now everything works better than ever.
Appliances.summary: Something to check before buying a new valve inlet.

Appliances.reviewText: Bought this for a friend and walked him through the install. These igniters are used in many different appliances and are very brittle. When they break they either shatter or crack. In the dryer there were small pieces everywhere so it's easy to see when it broke. Their symptom was that it would run but just not heat. You can download the PDF online to see where it's located and how to take the panel(s) off.

I live solo in a studio with stone floors and no washer/dryer hookups. This little washer is awesome! I still go tp the laundromat for big items like comforters, etc. But for regular weekly washing for me and any friends staying over, it is perfect. One load fits about a week's worth of undies, socks, a few outfits, and maybe a towel and a pillow case. And the spin dryer works great to get the excess water out - I hang dry my clothes on a folding rack indoors and they are dry overnight usually. If I set out on a sunny day it's dry in an hour or two.

One thing that took some getting used to versus a big automatic clothes washer is that you have to be conscious and aware for the water fill up process - otherwise it will overflow and pour out. This happened once when I was not paying attention while on the phone. So be sure to set a timer! Mine fills in 5 minutes from my kitchen sink.

The other thing to get used to is multiple cycles. I work outdoors so my clothes get really dirty, so I do two cycles with soap, and two to three cycles to rinse until the water is close to completely clear. So it's a relatively involved process compared to an automatic washer. But the results are comparable, and no need to install washer/dryer hookups!

I highly recommend using this machine at a sink with a non-carpeted, sealed or stone floor below it - maybe I'm just a messy user, but seems like I always get some water on the floor when I do laundry with it.
Appliances.summary: Great washer and spinner for apartments!

Appliances.reviewText: This was delivered via UPS and there was no damage to the box on the outside, and the fridge was double boxed so it arrived perfectly. It is about 70 lbs. so you may need someone to help with bringing it in the house. I have the unit in my basement and it is a lot quieter than my kegerator. I haven't heard any loud pops like some fridges have, and it seems to run quietly. It is a small unit but capable of holding a lot of cans. If you have a lot of tall bottles, your space will be greatly reduced though. As for the wire shelves, they are sturdy and spaced about like others I've seen, but if you have small cans (8 oz.) you will have trouble standing them up. 12 oz. cans require a little positioning but generally stand up well. The fridge gets in the low 40's which is cold enough for sodas and beer, and perfect for me, but if you're looking to get them practically frozen for some reason, it won't do the trick. The light in the top is nice and you have the option of allowing it to stay on permanently or just when the door opens, but it's not real bright and only lights up the first couple rows when filled with cans. I paid less than two hundred with free shipping and can't imagine having gotten a better deal. This is an attractive fridge and I would highly recommend it. I will update my review if I experience any problems.

Works great. I used it and an extension kit with extra rods to to clean a 21 foot long vent with a two right angle turns and it did a fantastic job with the adapter that lets you put the rod through and attach a shop vac. Got a TON of lint out, about a 5 gallon bucket full. Inside of the vent was left shiny and clean. Good for safety especially with such a long vent and to my surprise the dryer actually works quite a bit better now. On the auto cycle I used to have to run it again if I was drying heavy things like jeans or blankets/comforters etc... to fully dry things. Now it does it in one cycle and take about 25% less time to go through the auto dry cycle.

I was just wanting to clean out a potential fire hazard but it really does make a big difference running through a dirty vent vs. a clean one. Might be due to the long length of my vent but very happy with this product.

I'll admit it. I'm a huge water snob! I mean huge. We bought a new refrigerator and it uses this filter. I am going to cancel my decades-long delivery of bottled water, because the water from my new refrigerator dispenser is just THAT GOOD with this filter. I can continue to be snobby and save money! Win! Win!

This is my first countertop ice maker this is great machine choice of 3 different sizes of ice to make pretty quiet except when ice drops I use filtered water only in my ice so much better than any ice I have bought before in stores I just use gallon size bags to store ice in easy open and close I make  2 bags at time for our family during warmer weather our kids get ice in their filtered water. This is large size if your countertops are limited you might want a smaller one but for our family its worth the trade-off.  The machine packaged well arrived on time

We have 24 foot of solid dryer vent pipe ending in 3 right-angles before going through the floor into the flexible dryer-vent hose coming from the dryer.  I can't get behind the dryer without moving both the washer and dryer and they are HEAVY.  So being lazy I decided to clean the vent from the outside of the house inward.  I didn't use a vacuum cleaner or a blower or suction of any kind.  I did tighten each section of tubing with pliers and taped them.  I threaded all 24 foot of tubing with the brush on the end into the outside vent and then backed it out.  I got a good amount of lint clods out.  Then I turned on the dryer to blow everything out.  I got no air coming out at all.  My fear had come true, I had forced gobs of lint into the right-angles at the end of the run.  I still didn't want to move that washer and dryer so I figured I'd try one other thing, use the clodbuster attachment.  Now I'm really getting lazy so I tightened each tubing section by hand (no pliers) and didn't use tape.  I pushed all 24 foot of tubing into the vent until I hit some resistance and then turned the tubing by hand (too lazy to hook the drill up).  Then I pulled it all out and there wasn't any lint at all that came out. So now I'm resigned to having to move the washer and dryer, but before I do I figured I might as well turn the dryer on and see what happens.  Lots of lint clods blew out and kept coming out for about 20 seconds.  I've attached pictures of it.  I'm really happy with this product and if it worked for me with all the shortcuts I took it will probably work great for you.  As a point of reference we built this house five years ago and this is the first time I ever cleaned the vent.  A load of ten bath towels used to take 45 minutes to dry, lately it's been taking 3 to 4 hours, so I knew I couldn't put cleaning the pipe off any longer.
Appliances.summary: This really worked well even taking shortcuts

Appliances.reviewText:
We've used these filters for over one year now and they work/install perfectly.  We taste no difference between these and the OEM Samsung Product.  Product offers pefect fit and function and significantly reduces the yearly cost.  I highly recommend this product.

However, product is less expensive to purchase on Ebay due to the shipping charges at Amazon.

The  appearance is very similar to the GE units.  The unit screwed right into position with no issues.  The functionality appears to be the same as the GE unit after one month of use.  The water continues to taste just fine.  A fair amount of money was saved with this cartridge compared to purchasing the GE brand.
Appliances.summary: No issues noted with this replacement cartridge

Appliances.reviewText: Spent sixty bucks a year ago and another sixty this year on relay and capacitor for refrigerator. After the second one went out in a week I watched some you tube videos on the Supco start kit. Ordered and installed . Working great . Cold refrigerator ! I noticed on a forum a guy saying the start kit would ruin your compressor. Hey . If the stock relay won't work it's worth the risk if the other choice is a new refrigerator.

Perfect fit in a 2007 Maytag Epic Z. Watch youtube videos on how to change. You don't need to lift the washer to replace this pump. Just lift the rubber tab with a flat head screwdriver and slide the pump back and out after draining the pump with a deep dish plate to catch the water and unplugging the washer power, unplugging the power clip to the old pump, and disconnection of the two hoses. Drains quick and quiet now. Biggest challenge are the spring clamps. I suggest replacing with stainless steel screw clamps.
Appliances.summary: Perfect fit in a 2007 Maytag Epic Z

Appliances.reviewText: I love it! The ice maker is making ice like there's no tommorow.  We figured it was the filter we had that need to be replace because we were barely getting any ice or water.  We went to Lowes to pickup one filter, but wanted they wanted $49.00 for one.  This filter is doing the job for practically nothing.
Appliances.summary: I love it! The ice maker is making ice like ...

Appliances.reviewText: Part arrived quickly., good price. My 16 year old Kenmore gas dryer (made by Whirlpool) developed a slight gas smell. It was this valve. Not too diffident to install, plus I also thoroughly cleaned the dryer inside and vent of old lint. Now my dryer works great and I saved $$$. Hint, take off the rear exhaust vent and replace the foam seals, they dissolve after years of use. This will keep lint from leaking into the inside cabinet.

Parts bag labeled  " Whirlpool Corporation Factory Certified Parts". All parts were perfect replacements for our Whirlpool Duet 27 inch dryer. Came with 4 drum support wheels, which is required for the duet dryer. Belt and idler pulley fit like the factory parts they replaced. YouTube video's very helpful in this somewhat time consuming, but easy job. Took extra time to fully vacuum the internal components of the dryer. Surprising how much lint accumulated over it's 8 year life span.
Squealing/clunking sound has disappeared. Runs like new again.
Highly recommend product.
Appliances.summary: All parts were perfect replacements for our Whirlpool Duet 27 inch dryer

Appliances.reviewText: Works extremely well and it quiet. It did come with a small dent but the seller was quick with a response and very pleasant. It gets my clothes super clean and The washer is easy to use. I did have to get another adaptor piece from Lowe's. I haven't experience any leaks at all. It's a bit hard to move even with wheels on the bottom. But overall It's a great deal

This was a bit tricky to install as some of the screws are obscured from view, but once you know where everything is, you pull out the old one, set up the cable harness, plug it in and put the 3 set screws back in. After 3 hours or so this thing was cranking ice like you would not believe. Great product for the price. I would buy again. Your fridge will know when it is cold enough to send a signal for the water to fill and you are in business.

Great cook top.  Have only had it a few days but seems to be working very well.  It was well packaged and received it in good shape.  We looked at local stores in our area and price from Amazon was considerably less expensive.  And, it included the Lodge griddle.  The local stores told us that would cost us $60 extra.  We were told the LP conversion would cost extra saying we would have to buy a propane conversion kit.  If you will be connecting this cook top to propane, all of the LP orifices are included and the regulator can be converted as well.  No need to purchase anything else.  I would recommend the Cerama Bryte stainless steel cleaner that GE recommends.

Bought these rollers to replace rollers on my LG dryer. they were an exact match. installed them on my dryer about 8 months ago using a little white lithium grease, So far dryer is running smoothly and should keep going just fine and this dryer gets a lot of use as I live in a townhome and you're not aloud to have clothe lines.
Appliances.summary: So far dryer is running smoothly and should keep going just fine and this dryer gets a lot of use as ...

Appliances.reviewText:
These things have changed my life. I got these instead of the Boveda packs because I read a comparison study somewhere between the two and the Bovedas tested positive for the potential to seep hazardous chemicals. Not sure if that's true or not, but hey. Better safe than sorry I suppose.

I live in Phoenix where herb dries out stupid fast. Even just after a week of using these things I saw drastic change in the quality and longevity of my herbs. Also from my experience thus far, these packs last quite a long time. I have been using the same ones for well over a month now and the indicators say they're still going strong. I swear by these Integra boost packs, now, and tell any of my friends about them when I get the chance.

Came much sooner than expected and very easy to install (under 10 minutes) with a power screwdriver. Just a few wires to exchange, one tube (I'd suggest blowing it out to ensure it's unobstructed) and one screw. Of course you have to also remove the back panel which is about five screws. Seems to do the job. No complaints here.

first thing first: it works. the kit is great in what it consists of and the price is just right i think. to call someone to clean my dryer vents i got quoted from 80 all the way up to 200 bucks. so if you were able to do it yourself you will need to invest a bit more in a "construction" vacuum that cost about 80-100 bucks and start the savings basically from the second time you do it.

so whats with the 3*? my brush broke inside my vent!!!! while i was pulling it out, and yes i was using a drill, all the pieces came out except the round brush. i had to climb to my attic and push it from the other side to come out... what was supposed to be an easy task ended up with me spending over an hour extra in climbing in my attic, disassembling the HVAC pipe so that i can get in there and push down on the brush...

another minus for this kit is that while it is fairly bendy, it will not go very smoothly through your flexible insulated pipes and most likely push the pipe out from its connector.

with all that said, if your vent duct doesnt have to many bends, and you want to take the risk (maybe i had a defective kit that the brush broke), you might save a lot of money doing it yourself!

From the reviews I watched, it looked like a great product. I ended up caving to my curiosity and purchasing the Wonderwash.

First impressions, the base is extremely flismy / flexible. I wish they made it with higher quality plastics. I am not sure if it will be prone to cracking / snapping in the future, but the flexing is annoying if only because the tank wobbles while spinning.

Unfortunately, once I filled it up with water, the bottom started leaking. Given that it "has a patented pressure system that forces detergent into the fabric at high speed for a fast, efficient, economic and very easy wash", if it leaks, it means the pressure isn't being maintained.  I ignored it and proceeded to do a trial wash. The only complain I have then is that it is wobbly. Water was being flung into my face due to the leak, but I am assuming that it is a defect and it does not normally leak (and thus, water will not be flung into your face).

If what I received wasn't defective, I would likely give this 4 stars - pending durability assessments.

I will be contacting Laundry Alternative to see what can be done, and I will update this review accordingly.

Update 1:

Received a replacement tub. I haven't gotten a chance to do a wash yet, but I did fill it with some water to check for leaks - no leaks yet, yay!

Update 2:

The tub seems to work fine now. Did a load of wash and worked out as intended. My only concern is that the metal (the rod that holds the handle) will eventually corrode due to friction and exposure to water.

I also have another quality issue. The metal rings (in the base - used to support the actual tub) are flaking. I noticed little gray flakes scattered on the surface I was using to do the washing. Upon closer inspection, it was coming off the metal rings. Only time can tell what issues this will cause in the future.

I am fairly in between whether or not I would recommend this product. Quality is up in the air, but it definitely works as long as it holds up. If you live in an apartment and pay per load in the basement/in the laundromat, this will pay itself off in about 30 loads. Question is, would it last 30 loads (30 loads in laundromat terms is really like 60-80 wonderwash terms due to difference in size).

While the box looks like they printed millions, the duct itself appears very home-made, fashioned out of cut and bent pieces of  rigid dryer pipe riveted together. With enough TLC and aluminum tape it can be made to work without blowing lint everywhere but it's no quick fix. I would certainly pay more for a version that was ready to install.
Appliances.summary: Frees up space but craftsmanship needs work

Appliances.reviewText: This thermostat came with white wires when the original had to different colored wires. I contacted the support people as I wanted to make sure I had the correct replacement part. I gave the support person my refrigerator model number for them to research. They said they did not have my model number on file and could not confirm this was the correct replacement part. I therefore searched the internet on my own and confirmed that this was the correct replacement part as well as the white wires worked fine. It did not matter which white wire were connected to which colored wire. It would have saved time if the support desk was able to confirm my concerns but other than that all worked well.

It works but doesn't come calibrated. I didn't know this and briefly turned my refrigerator into a second freezer. A few minutes of adjusting it the next day and it worked just fine.
The tube gauge is smaller than the OEM part and it was a little longer. Was very careful straightening out the sensor. Mine came with the plastic tube already installed so you don't need to remove your old one.

Replaced 3 ge reveal 40w in a kenmore elite side-by-side.  Color is very blue and not as bright as ge reveal despite being same marked lumens.  Kind of odd too, since higher color temps at same lumens should be perceived by the eye as brighter and not dimmer.  Would be better if tuned to 4000k, since it makes the fridge a look more like a vending machine now.  Bulbs are instant on, so they don't show typical small lag of cheap led bulbs.  Complete waste of money for these bulbs unless your fridge is killing bulbs every few months like mine.
Appliances.summary: Would be better as a 4000k bulb

Appliances.reviewText: As a few others have complained, mine does not get as cold as I would like it. Plus, the design has changed, apparently in a way that the Danby technical support is not aware. The internal light is now a dim blue LED that stays on 24/7 -- the switch that used to operate the light by opening and closing the door is gone. My complaint is that the light is so dim that I really can't see much inside the refrigerator; I guess eventually I'll look into replacing the LED with something brighter. The door does not close on its own; I have to make sure to physically push the door tightly closed.

The hose is to small to fit any of my faucets so have to use buckets to fill, does a good job with cleaning and the spin is absolutely amazing doesnt take long for the clothes to dry, however the pump needs some help every now and then to drain. all in all I am satisfied with this purchase looking into finding a portable dryer next
Appliances.summary: does a good job with cleaning and the spin is absolutely amazing ...

Appliances.reviewText: It's a nice freezer, and we are enjoying it. Only disappointment is that it has a lot of restrictions - cannot be in garage, do not use with extension cords, etc. that I have not encountered in the past with other freezers. But once we managed to find it a spot in the house, it works very well.

I have only used one about a week and a half. So far, the only difference I see over the original is the price. Will update if need be.

Update:  The original filters that came with the humidifier lasted about a month. These lasted me about two weeks and then fell apart. Will try something else in the future.

Is okay product and the price was not so bad taking into consideration that I got it from Amazon (lowest price I could find). But, water still have some chlorine taste after we changed it and run the water as advised. Fridge filters should really last longer. These are only good for 6 months. I got a fridge that came with it by June 2011. The warning light for filter change came on since November 2011, so it lasted only 5 months. It is also hard to replace because of the water pressure. To make it easy, you have to shut down the water from the back which is a real hassle in my case since the fridge fits very tight in the kitchen fridge space.

A good braided hose for ice maker hookup. Concerned about the wording used as certified. This is only the suppliers name of the product. It does not indicate the hose is certified for an appliance. Since I needed the 15 foot size, it fits the bill. Hope it holds up and doesnt have leak issues. Also doesnt seem to give off a poor taste as some hoses can. Also note hose is made in China as most are today. Overall for cost hose fits the bill. Recommend monitoring of hose yearly to check for leaks. Very common failure found with ice makers.
Appliances.summary: Need extra length.....this will do it

Appliances.reviewText:
At first this contraption was a little confusing. I read the directions about 3 times before I felt okay about going through with the project - was not fully confident as there were a lot of warnings about making sure the drill was going the right way/you turned it the right way so you wouldn't lose rods in the dryer vent. Scared me a little. However, the project turned out really well. We didn't lose any rods (thankfully) and we got out the birds nest that had taken residence in our dryer vent!!
The part that was for the lint catcher was convenient as well and is actually recommended to be used at least once a month in order to clean out the lint catcher. I do need to keep up with this but it isn't convenient to have to put together and tape the rods each time when you only really use it for a couple of minutes. However, if you have a handy space to keep it already together, I can see how this would be even better for keeping up with cleaning the lint out.

Although this belt is a correct (length & style) sized belt,  I feel slighted having received a generic 27001007/37820 belt rather than a specific 271001007 belt. I found the generic listing for about $3.00 cheaper. EDGEWATER PARTS did rectify this situation.

I am using this belt for now and it is working properly; I just feel its longevity may be in question.

These door hinges match exactly the ones we are replacing on our 9 year old Kenmore/Frigidaire oven/range.  Unfortunately we are having to purchase these replacement parts because the part is inherently underdesigned and can fail catastrophically, as ours did. Appliance repair folks said these are not available and no substitution is available, leaving me with the option of buying another stove.  Not so, as Amazon proves yet again. Incidentally, before installing the replacement part, I reinforced them by welding a metal tab at the head of the spring to help prevent blowout.
Appliances.summary: Underdesigned, but if you need these, you know that already.

Appliances.reviewText: I expected/assumed it would have the same slider in the front to adjust the humidity as the drawer I was replacing. In retrospect you can't really tell from the photo. But the new one didn't have it. Which really surprised me since in seemed like part of the drawer and I'm not sure my old one could be transferred, and I had already discarded the broken part. So, if fit fine but I did not get what I thought I'd ordered.
Appliances.summary: What you get (the complete shelf/bin holder) may not be what your receive

Appliances.reviewText: This belt measures 72" My dryer had a longer belt, 8182481, and is 73 5/8 " long. I only found this out after ordering the belt and disassembling the entire unit, extracting the old belt remnants and trying to fit the replacement belt. It came nowhere close to the drive pulley. Amazon has been very quick and helpful in the return and replacement process. Before ordering make sure to measure your old belt. Whirlpool Part Number 8182481: Belt, Drive
Appliances.summary: Did not work with my WED7500VW

Appliances.reviewText:
These are good for protecting the tips of your dishwasher rack to prevent corrosion and rusting.  They fit very, very tightly on my Whirlpool Dishwasher.  They were a little hard to put on, and I think they would be impossible to put on if the tips were already damaged or corroded.

For tips that were already damaged, corroded or rusted, I used UberGoop and the tips which came with it, which are a little larger and thicker, and easier to put on even with the "Goop" applied to the tip.  These have held up well, too, through many washings.

Even without using any kind of adhesive underneath, I have only had one come off, and then just once.  I'm not sure if it came of in the dish washing cycle or if I did something to loosen it.  The price was great.

Big Bearing: 35mm x 75mm x 17mm
Small  25mm x 62mm x 17mm
Rubber Part: 75mm x 50mm x 10mm

Bearings Fit Maytag WHWE950WW02 Front load washer, but the rubber part off 3 mm in depth. I ended up returning the set and buying the good quality Japanese ones and reusing the rubber booth with lots of grease.
Appliances.summary: Big Bearing: 35mm x 75mm x 17mm  Small: 25mm x 62mm x 17mm

Appliances.reviewText: Hmm... I don't know really what to say about this filter.  I opted for the original Samsung filter as a replacement, but the filtering and ice performance has significantly changed.  The water from the door dispenses way more slowly, and it takes about twice the time to fill up the ice bin.  I followed the Samsung support instructions on resetting the ice and door dispensing features, but without any improvement back to "normal."  I think next time I will go with a generic replacement at half the cost.
Appliances.summary: Next Time I'll Go With A Generic Replacement

Appliances.reviewText:
I purchased this because of the good reviews on a number of sites and a low price.
The claim was that it cleaned as good or better than more expensive machines.
If this is true then machines are not very good today.
It does clean but I put a coffee cup in that had not been scrubbed and the stains were still there after the run.
Thats the other thing too, its a long run.
You add to this that the silverware basket is just open baskets so everything just sits in the box sections loose
and the dish baskets are of very light construction.
The wheels on the lower basket just clip on and can pop off when it is loaded.
My old unit was the same name brand and also a budget model.
It was cheaper but we are talking 10 years so it should be.
This unit does not come with a insulation blanket.
The one from my old unit was in good shape and fit this perfectly so while its fairly quiet I cannot comment on this because I did not hear it
without the blanket.
Also my old silverware basket was heavier, well divided, and in good shape with a perfect fit so Im keeping it too.

the essick humidifier I have is great, these wicks are another story though. They do a great job to start with but I guess I have a lot of minerals, and I have to replace mine every 3 weeks! Towards the end, they just get stiff and encrusted with mineral deposits. Since these are cellulose, if you try to get the deposits out so you can stretch out usage, you'll just end up turning the wick into pulp. Overall, pretty good, wish I got more use out of them though.
Appliances.summary: the essick humidifier I have is great, these wicks are another story though

Appliances.reviewText:
This is a small lightweight washer alternative, unfortunately..while yes, it sort of manages to wash clothes...it's not all that effective. You can essentially accomplish the same level of clean by swirling your clothes in a bucket for 5 mins. Which, would be cheaper than this system. The clothes don't come out that clean(as I said, it's the same as swirling clothes in a bucket) and in fact you get cleaner clothes by washing the clothes by hand. In fact, I think I prefer the level of cleanliness from hand washing than I do from this washer.

The unit it's self is fairly sturdy, but the clips used to hold the system on it's "Stand" come out rather easily which can be annoying. especially if you are using the washer in sink or tub, and the clip goes down the drain.

The hole for your clothes also is fairly small. Not too much of an issue for light clothes, but stiff clothing like jeans are a bit tough to get in and out..and even when you get the clothes out? There's a good chance water will be everywhere! So make sure you use this outside, or in a sink or tub..some place where having water pool out everywhere isn't an issue.

Another thing that irked me, was the thing didn't include any kind of assembly manual. Sure, it's not too difficult to figure out how it's put together, but it still would be handy to have that little bit of help along the way.

All in all, I wouldn't really recommend this to anyone, since there are better washing machine alternatives out there (Including hand washing) but it does SLIGHTLY work, so it doesn't get a completely failing mark in my book....I may still use it on occasion, but most likely I will stick with hand washing.
Appliances.summary: Not as good as hand washing.

Vent arrived in a timely fashion but as I wasn't prepared to install it at the time, I didn't open it.  Several weeks later when I did open the box, I notice it had a weird ping on the upper left edge.  It also had a couple of bent prongs that hold in the filter.  The prongs I straightened out but I couldn't do anything about the ping.  I installed it anyway thinking it wouldnt be noticeable but it is.  It is very noticeable.  Other than that, it works fine.

So, all in all, product arrived timely but had some slight damage.  I did not contact Amazon because it was such a long span from when I received it to when I opened/installed it.  I should have opened it and returned it when I got it.

Poor calibration:
Even when the remote sensor is sitting right next to the base station, the indoor and outdoor temperatures are off by a degree or two.

Uninspired support:
I called support to ask if I could recalibrate. I was 17th in line. After five minutes or so, I'd only gotten down to #10 in line, so I opted to have them call me back. "without losing my place in line!"  They didn't call back. Approx 2 hours later, I remembered, and called them again. They'd already closed. (Support til 5pm Central) No option to leave a message. Lame. ...To their credit, they did eventually call back that same day. Support was friendly but not helpful.

Poor documentation:
Support told me that my degree or so of discrepancy was within the +/-2 degree calibration present in "all thermometers".
Neither the manual nor product listing mentions this. I call BS, anyhow. There are plenty of more diligently calibrated thermometers out there.

Poor readability:
If the lighting is not perfect, it's difficult to read both temperatures from some angles when only a few feet away.
I would not purchase this item again. I use one other AcuRite item and while it's nothing to write home about, it's okay, so I'm not totally severing consumer/company ties ;)

...But, after living with it for a few months, I added a couple more stars. Why? I got over the fact that it's poorly calibrated. I don't even remember which one is colder/hotter than the other. I've just resolved to be okay knowing I'm somewhere in the ballpark when I look at the AcuRite 00611A3.
Appliances.summary: Poor calibration: Even when the remote sensor is sitting ...

Appliances.reviewText: It does make ice, which I guess is all you really need. I do wish it made more ice per batch and didn't take so long, but I figure there are practical limitations to a small device. We generally will leave it run for a while so it makes enough ice to fill a small bin, otherwise it only makes enough for 1-2 drinks per cycle. Also somewhat noisy. But overall an acceptable product.
Appliances.summary: Does its job, which is all you can ask for

Appliances.reviewText: The output hose connection for the dirty water should have a washer to help prevent leaking.  Our machine works well except for that we've had it for less than a week and have had to clean up some major leaking from the back of the machine which floods the counter.  it seems to clean the dishes fairly well though.
Appliances.summary: The output hose connection for the dirty water should have a washer to help prevent leaking

Appliances.reviewText:
Obviously much laughter ensues when a package is sold. The knobs in no way fit on the Jennair item it is supposed to refresh
 The off mark is exactly aligned to appear as if it is on another setting. The joke is on America. A 3 rating was given to ensure food is on the table for any innocent children involved.

Office_Products.reviewText: Simple device that has made my family's life easier.  Like most Americans, due to building codes, I have a a spring-loaded self closing door that passes from house to garage.  I am between the garage and house a lot, carrying tools, taking out garbage and of course this is where all the groceries have to pass through.  This little thing has simplified all those times we have our hands full coming through this door.  It is quality made and operates flawlessly with your foot.
Office_Products.summary: Made Life Easier

Office_Products.reviewText:
I've been wanting to pick up some colored pens for a while to liven up my sketchbook and decided to get these!
They do their job and have a nice fine tip for detail work. They don't bleed through my sketchbooks either, but they aren't waterproof (which is fine for me)
Overall I like them a lot! Might expand my collection soon :)
Office_Products.summary: Great for sketches & doodling

Office_Products.reviewText: Purchased exactly one year ago --still looks nice and functions perfectly. No slip, no lifting of the edges, no noticeable wear.  For grins, I just now lifted a corner to see how the backing might've affected my desk.  The sticky back is barely on the wood and easily wiped off dry without bothering the wood finish.  Laid right back down with good grip.
Office_Products.summary: for my Apple Magic Mouse

Office_Products.reviewText:
We have a great, yet strange cat. He loves playing with rubber bands, we found he sees the blue ones that come on produce better than other colors, but the grocery store said they didn't have any. We saw this and got them.

The rubber bands stand up well to our shooting them and the cat playing with them, they don't get hard, or gummy.
Office_Products.summary: our cat loves these

Office_Products.reviewText: This ink is fun. Also bough the Vansky UV Black Light flashlight to be able to read my writing. I use it in my journal to write down stuff I don't want anybody to see but for me to remember. Ha, it is so much cheeky fun to be the only one who knows. I also hire inhome-care providers. When I take my notes they won't be able to read anything about themselves or somebody else, should they stumble over my notebook. Great invention!!!
Office_Products.summary: This ink is fun. Also bough the Vansky UV Black Light flashlight ...

Office_Products.reviewText: Currently, yes, these cartridges don't work...but this is b/c HP created a firmware update that caused ALL non-HP cartridges to be recognized as malfunctioning. We have bought several sets of cartridges from this and other companies and have had no problems. Additionally, when we approached Valuetoner for replacement or refund, they responded promptly and provided a return label with no questions asked. They even refunded a cartridge that was half used. We are waiting for cartridges that can be used post-firmware update.
Office_Products.summary: Cartridges work, HP firmware is the problem.

Office_Products.reviewText: I read all of the other reviews before purchasing, but the item was exactly what I needed so I went ahead and ordered despite the complaints.  The people who mention the difficulty in changing positions are not wrong:  if you try to adjust it without a plan, it's tricky.  BUT there are instructions that come with it that explain the positions in terms of degrees, which have to be the same on each side, and which are on the mechanism itself.  Once it's in position, it's terrific.
Office_Products.summary: Perfect but a bit tricky

Office_Products.reviewText:
It's like my wrist are resting in the bosom of...well Deadpool! I love looking down and my wrist is just lovingly resting between his generous pecks of squishy yes-ness. I have no regrets with buying this; in my opinion? Worth every penny.

I don't know what else to say it's a mouse pad I never knew I wanted with the added bonus of cradling my wrist while fulfilling both my inner immature kid who snickers every time I look down at it along with my not so inner perv who likes the fact that i get to rest my oh so heavy wrist on his BULGING-MANLY-PEX.

Is it necessary? It could be argued no but for me I dint know how i was living without it.
Office_Products.summary: Cradle My Wrist to Oblivion My Little Pool Party

Office_Products.reviewText: So far, I really like this scanner with the dock.  Set up was easy and the image quality seems very good.  It is a good way to get rid of paper clutter.  I want to start putting old photographs on my computer as a way of preserving them.  Receipts of different sizes and thicknesses seem to feed ok.  The cost was much less than some other more expensive models that had mixed reviews and had  trouble with receipts.
Office_Products.summary: I really like this scanner with the dock

Office_Products.reviewText:
If you read the following review & find it helpful in any way, please select "I found this review helpful"... I received this item at a discounted price in exchange for my honest review. Anytime I review an item, I personally test & use it myself in order to give honest & fair feedback, whether it be positive or negative. In this case I was pleasantly surprised.
I use a lot of ink in my home for personal & business reasons, and have been buying ink cartridges that average around $60, so when I saw this brand for a fraction of the cost I was skeptical at first. When I received the product, I was impressed that all three cartridges were individually wrapped. Sometimes ink cartridges can leak, so that was a positive for me. Not only are they wrapped separately, but each wrapping is sealed. This package includes Yellow, Magenta & Cyan colored ink. So when I received the ink, it just so happened the current cartridge of Magenta in my printer needed replaced, so I opened the Magenta package & inserted it into my printer, easy installation, no issues there. After I put it in, my printer asked if I wanted to print a "test page" so I did, and everything looked good. The ink looked normal, it didn't run or look too light. Within a few days my blue & yellow cartridge also needed replaced and again, the cartridges installed easily, no issues, no force needed to insert them, and the color was perfect when it printed. I was really skeptic about these, just because ink cartridges are something that, up until this point, I thought it was always worth it to go with the more expensive brand to get better quality. But there is no doubt in my mind, with as much printed as I do for personal & business, I will continue to buy this brand. You are getting exactly the same quality as the expensive brands at a fraction of the cost. Anyone would be nuts to not try them! Again, I received this item at a discounted rate in exchange for my honest review. This review is MY opinion, I was not asked to give a positive or biased opinion, the views are mine and fairly & honestly written. Please rate my review as helpful if you believe it was!
Office_Products.summary: Less price, same quality

Office_Products.reviewText:
As someone who does a ton of hand scribing, I really love the feel of these gel pens and the resulting look of the ink. They do occasionally smudge, but it isn't very often. Generally you can scribble out pages of stuff without a problem.

The point is smooth and glides nicely across the paper and looks great. Even works decent for cartooning (goofing around).
Office_Products.summary: What other gel pens strive to be

Office_Products.reviewText: I Absolutly love them. I've heard reviews that they are scratchy but i hope heartedly disagree, I even ordered extra fine nibs for it and it is super smooth and nice to write with! I do have to say though, the grease used on the piston mechanisms really threw me for a loop, I wasn't expecting it to be whitish, I thought that the piston son my two new TWSBIS arrived scratched, after emailing the seller though and taking them apart to confirm it turned out to just be lubrication they use. It would have been nice if there was some kind of warning or note to tell me that, I was so upset at first untill I realized it was just grease and not scratches. You gotta admit, it does look like scratches. I was advised NOT to clean it off but I will be replacing it with a clear grease asap. Other than that these pens are beautiful and awesome writers with good flow and smooth nibs!
Office_Products.summary: The pens are beautuful!

Office_Products.reviewText: I've been on the look out for a good folio, and even have a collection of about 10 from company swag giveaways. I wanted a leather one to last the ages, one I would have years later. I have that in my Saddleback Leather tobacco notepad holder. It is a gem. I look forward to passing it on to my grandkids (sorry kids).
Office_Products.summary: A Gem

Office_Products.reviewText: I think this is my 10th year in a row buying engagement calendars from Ziga. The art is cute, but more importantly the build is sturdy.  The double metal coils don't bend too easily and the pages aren't prone to ripping out.  I think the paper is acid free, as there hasn't been any discoloring or fading on my older calendars. (I treat them as a hiking and travel journal and keep every one.) The pages are easy to write on, and I think Ziga has pretty much hit the mark on their design.
Office_Products.summary: Sturdy build, thoughtful design, plus with pretty pictures!

Office_Products.reviewText: This mouse pad is HUGE. If you play at low sensitivity like I do, then It's perfect. There is enough room to move your mouse across without worrying about missing your mark. I have a full size keyboard that sits on top and the mouse pad does not move so you don't need to keep readjusting the pad while playing or worry about over extending your mouse while playing. Would buy again once I wear this one out.
Office_Products.summary: If you play at low sensitivity like I do

Office_Products.reviewText: Love, love, love these ACME PENS. I would buy more of them if they weren't so expensive. They are nice and heavy in the hand and the designs are very nice. I have duplicates of some pens just because I want to use them all the time. They write beautifully! If you like nice, expensive looking and heavy weight writing instruments--this is the one.
Office_Products.summary: AWESOME PEN

Office_Products.reviewText: I have layers of rugs over a tile floor and have tried a couple other methods for sticking them in place. So far, the dogs haven't been able to move the rugs around during our indoor ball playing time! I got it on a lightning deal and was a bit wary but it's been over a month now and nothing has shifted at all! Make sure that your surfaces are dry. I had one spot that was still wet and had to wipe it and let it and the tape dry before getting it to stick. Also, I 'start' removing the backing just slightly at the corners before measuring out what I need so it's not as frustrating as trying to do it while it's on the floor.
Office_Products.summary: Works perfectly so far!

Office_Products.reviewText:
I've been in IT, and a high-tech management consultant, for pushing 40 years.  I've installed almost literally every non-mainframe computer printer -- and at least one printer from literally every brand, family and/or generation of non-mainframe printers (and, don't get me wrong, I've installed no small number of mainframe printers, too) -- ever made.  No, really... I'm that both old and experienced. I've really paid my dues, and I really know what I'm talking about...

...and so if you'll just bother to really read and understand what I'm here writing (and that to which I link), you'll learn why this printer's good, and why you should buy it, as well as how to get the biggest bang for your buck from it.

This really is a first-rate printer, have no doubts about that. However, there are things the user needs to know in order to fully leverage it to its greatest advantage and benefit. If one buys this printer and expects it to behave like an HP (or even an Epson), for example, then one will be disappointed. Most of the negative reviews, here, are from people who thought it would all be just plug-and-play, and who weren't willing to figure it all out (or, more accurately, to just bother to read the various documentation, and watch a video or two); and so they come here and embarrass themselves with ridiculous comments. In what I'm here writing, I refer you to my comment beneath Canon's official Pixma MX922 video, over on Youtube: be sure, if you go there, to read the even *MORE* ridiculous comments by the, I'm sorry, idiots who so embarrass themselves with their ignorance and its revelation of their having not bothered to pick-up and read the printer's excellent documentation.

One must learn the nuances of this device; must set it up properly and then properly configure both it and the "printers" area of one's copy of Windows or iOS; and then one must know a little something about inks and the best ways to both buy and use them.  Fail to read the manual, or try to set-up the device without using the "Quick Start" guide (and follow it, exactly); or fail to download and use the most-up-to-date software from the Canon site; or fail to ensure that the printer's using the most current firmware -- all of that sort of thing -- and it will, I can virtually guarantee, disappoint you.

It's not that this printer is "high maintenance": it is not. And it's not that this printer is persnickety, or sensitive, or fragile or anything like that: it is none of those things.  But it's a classic Canon product, which means, to we who've been installing them for many years, that the manufacturer bothers to provide all the information that the user could possibly need to know in order to properly use and enjoy the product via videos, manuals, bulletins, help files, etc...

...but if the user won't bother to read about and truly learn it, then said user gets exactly what s/he deserves.  Simple as that.

For a lousy hundred bucks (or, more accurately these days, for even less) this is, hands down, one of the best little printers you could buy... especially if you take halfway-serious photographs in life, and want to be able to print them out really nicely.  For me, the fact that I can print directly onto CDs and DVDs is yet another reason why I finally decided to buy one of these.  Yes, I still have my much higher-end HP printer for serious (and seriously-fast) office-style mostly-just-text printing; and the truth is that that HP can print a little bit sharper and better quality text -- especially by comparison when in draft mode; and also using a tiny bit less ink -- than can this Canon...

...but, all that notwithstanding, I'm now using this MX922 as my basic personal printer, scanner, fax machine; and, especially, as my photo printer and that which I use for CD/DVD labeling (because I no longer have to buy labels; I can print directly onto CDs and DVDs which are made to be printed on) instead of the HP, now.  It's a plenty-fast scanner/copier; it faxes well; and for 99% of the text documents that I could ever need to print, it's perfectly clear and sharp and fine. Only if I had to print super-high-quality text, on super-high-quality bond paper, at fairly high speed, might I switch-over to the HP...

...but, that said, honestly, I've learned that the paper one uses has almost more to do with that than anything else.  The Canon ink is different from HP inks; sadly, Canon inks tend to bleed into cotton bond papers more than HP inks; and so it gives the impression to the inexperienced user that HP printers print more sharp text than do Canon printers.  But if you just make sure the paper on which you're printing is "hard" enough, and has a lower fiber content, then even the Canon printer, when doing super-high quality printing, is razor sharp. So don't be fooled by those who insist that HP printers are always sharper. They *can* be, but they're not always: it depends, in large measure, on the paper used.

At any rate, this printer, once everything is just right (and that's the operative phrase, here), is really nice. No, really. I love it. Is it my favorite device of its type, ever?  Of COURSE not... but then, again, I'm old; and I've seen, in my life, some of the best equipment ever made by any manufacturer, anywhere.  But this little device -- once it's properly set-up and everything's configured right, and everything's tested and works; and once you've got the latest firmware, and the latest printer software and utilities (and it, too, is properly configured), and ONCE YOU BOTHER TO REALLY-AND-TRULY LEARN HOW TO USE IT ALL -- is really quite nice.  Be careful believing the negative reviews, here: this device -- like most Canon products -- requires no small investment on the part of the user to first get things just right, and to then actually learn how to use it.  Fail to make that investment, and you'll be unhappy.

Beneath the official Canon Pixma MX922 video, over on YouTube, I wrote a long comment which is probably the best and most useful thing that anyone either owning or considering owning this device could ever read. Though it covers several areas, it mostly covers inks... the single highest ongoing cost of owning any printer; and Canon printers, unlike HP printers (though very similar to Epson printers), tend to use a lot of ink, and to "pile on" ink, in order to achieve even only black colors.  Remember that with ink, unlike with light, the presence of all colors makes black; whereas with light, the presence of all colors makes white.  Canon leverages that to create excellent blacks and dazzling shades of both gray and all colors...

...but, boy-oh-boy, does Canon ever use a lot of ink.  Fortunately, there are ways to configure both the printer and the "printers" area of one's copy of Windows or iOS to default everything to "draft" mode, using only black ink, for everyday printing; and then if you want high-quality mode, then all you have to do is go into printer settings, just before sending a job to the printer, right on your computer screen, and set everything, just for that print job, to high-quality using all colors of ink.  Just doing that will save you a ton of money on ink in the long run...

...and then, beyond that, if you're willing to consider the admittedly risky business of purchasing aftermarket inks and refillable ink cartridges, then you can lower your ink costs by quite literally a factor of around 8... or even more.  But don't underestimate my use of the word "risky" in that immediately-previous sentence: In my comment over on YouTube to which I herein earlier refer (and to which I'll link you in a moment), I cover exactly why some -- not all, mind you, but at least some; maybe even most -- aftermarket inks are a really bad idea. If they're not made to the same high-quality standards as Canon inks, then they will clog-up the print-head nozzles in this printer, but fast; and once that happens, you're done, because print heads for all ink jet printers, regardless of brand, tend to be very expensive... so expensive that by the time you replace the print heads, you've probably paid for most of a whole new printer.  An example: a typical HP OfficeJet-Pro printer might cost two- to three-hundred bucks; and a pair of print heads for most of them will run maybe $60 to $90 per head, for a total of $120 to $180 for the pair. At that point, once you factor-in all the other wear-and-tear variables, it can start to make more sense to just buy a whole new printer, believe it or not.

Printer manufacturers, you must understand, are not really in the business, anymore, of selling the printers, themselves. Rather, it's all that expensive ink, over the life of the printer, in which they're so interested in selling you. Consequently, most printer manufacturers now practically give away their printers; and so that's why a pair of print heads for most printers costs almost as much as an entirely new printer. It's also why most printers, anymore, aren't really repairable. They're so cheap, now, that it's almost as inexpensive to just replace them as it is to repair them, or to purchase new print heads for them.  Even replacing the little illuminating light tube used by the scanner, on most of these printers, today, is cost-prohibitive; and can cost nearly as much as just replacing the whole printer. It's kinda' silly, if you think about it; but it's just the things are, today.

At any rate, make sure your eyes are wide open about using aftermarket inks.  I use them, but then, again, I know how to determine if they're really high quality; and I know where and how to buy them.  And so my (as well as my clients'... at least if they listen to me) printers still last, without damage to their print heads from aftermarket inks. However, if you cannot ensure that you, too, can get the really good aftermarket inks, then, trust me, you'll  end-up regretting using them.  That said, if you can, then... well... all I can say is: WOW!  What a savings!  Where Canon-branded inks, almost no matter how you buy them, cost from maybe 3 to 5 cents per page, give or take, a good set of aftermarket high-capacity refillable ink cartridges (with the auto-reset chips in them), along with the syringe-type thingies used to inject ink into said cartridges, plus if you buy your both pigment and dye ink in big 17- to 20-oz bottles made especially for the Canon Pixma MX-series, it can lower your per-page cost to just a fraction of a penny... in fact, seriously, it can be a fraction of a fraction per page.  I kid you not: the savings from aftermarket inks can be quite stunning!

In fact, the aftermarket ink savings can be *SO* unbelievable that even if you purchase cheap inks which end-up shortening the life of the printer, the cost of the printer is so low, anymore, that it can almost still be cheaper to use even the crappy aftermarket inks; and then when they finally kill the printer (and, trust me, they will), just buy a whole new printer and do it all over again.  Seriously: do the math, and you'll see.

Anyway, it's now time to tell you how to go read that long comment of mine beneath the official Canon Pixma MX-922 video over on YouTube from which you'll learn so much... especially about ink cartridges.  I'll go ahead and link to it, here, but Amazon censors are fairly notorious for deleting such links (even though, in this case, it will just help Amazon to sell the MX922 printer, here) and so I humbly request that the following link be allowed.

SEE | http://youtu.be/JJJRDkSlzww  (mine is the "LINKED COMMENT" there)

If Amazon censors it, then you may also type EXACTLY this (quotation marks and all) into the Google search page box...

"Canon PIXMA Printer: PIXMA MX922" "Gregg DesElms"

...and it should be the second (after the ad, if there is one) search result (or if you use an ad-blocker, then maybe it'll be the first -- and possibly only, after all duplicates have been removed -- search result).  Once you're on the YouTube page, then just scroll down to (or search for) my name "Gregg DesElms" to find my comment with the words "THE ONE COMMENT, HERE, THAT EVERYONE SHOULD READ!" at the very top.  Then click on the "Read more (369 lines)" link to expand it.  Yes, it's long, but it's so worth it that I promise you won't mind.

If you can't find it, let me know in a comment, here, after which maybe I'll just copy-and-paste it into a comment to this review or something.  One way or another I'll somehow make sure you can all read it, by hook or by crook.

And... oh, yeah... two more things...

First, some here (and elsewhere) complain that this printer is slow; that the first copy of anything printed or scanned/copied takes a long time to come out of the printer because of some kind of initialization or warm-up necessary because the printer sort of "sleeps" if not used for a while.  Well, the printer can be configured so that it never sleeps; and, believe me, so doing doesn't use a lot of electricity or suddenly make the printer ecologically unsound.  In fact, I think some of the newest models, with the newest firmware (which can be downloaded and installed into the older models), default to not sleeping because of those complaints early in this model's life. So don't worry about that one: it's configurable.

Second, as with all printers of this printer's type, this one needs to be used.  If you tend to never print, such that the printer just sits there, for days upon days, never printing anything, then it will eventually fail in various ways -- including and especially, getting clogged-up print head nozzles -- just when you really need it. Yes, it'll technically be a waste of both ink and paper, but try to run a little something through the printer every day, if possible.  Just three to five pages per day, of something -- anything -- will help keep it in decent condition.  High-capacity, high-speed HP printers are even worse about that than are Canons: if you don't use those HPs every day, then, wow!, they really go bad fast. Epsons, too, but not quite as much.  Canons are a little bit better about it, but you still need to use them a little... if not every single day, then at least three or four times per week. Print or copy something every now and then just to keep the MX922 printer in decent shape, ready for use whenever you need it.  And if you default the printer to draft mode and using just black ink (as I herein earlier recommended), then go out of your way to print at least a page or two, every now and then (once or twice weekly, I recommend), in full -- maybe even high-quality (which, yes, uses a lot of ink) -- color, just to keep the color inkjet nozzles clear and working well, too.

Hope that helps!

_________________________
Gregg L. DesElms
Napa, California USA

Office_Products.reviewText:
I'm not a habitual reviewer, at least in part because I've got lots else to do. But I've just set up and tried out my new Brother 2270DW, and I do want to comment on 2 aspects.

1. It was far easier to set up on my network than I had expected. It took less than 10 minutes to get it running on my first computer, then another couple of minutes for the second computer to pick it up. I was worried about network settings and so forth, but it self-detected and installed without a single misstep. Functions beautifully with no wires save the power cable.

2. The duplex printing is just plain fun to watch. And, any edge curl is so slight that I wouldn't even have noticed has other people not mentioned it.

After my first afternoon with it, this appears to be a great product. I've owned or operated 20+ printers over the past 3 decades, and so far, this appears to be the one to beat.

James Morrison

Office_Products.reviewText: I've purchased several of these now for my trusty Brother printer.  I use the same toner for both my personal printer and the one at work. My only gripe is more with the printer than with the cartridge itself.  I hate having to reset my printer to allow more pages to be printed - I get a lot more out of the cartridge than my printer thinks I'll get.  I can't say how many pages of printing I get, but it's an awful lot.  I go through many, many reams of paper between refills.  As a teacher, I am constantly printing and both the printer and the cartridge work perfectly for my purposes.  I find that removing the cartridge and shaking it (gently, side to side) helps to get more mileage out of it.  With all the cheap printers/expensive cartridges out there, this one's worth the money.

Office_Products.reviewText: I must say I was pleased with the price and packaging of this product, but was disappointed to find that my Brother Printer would not accept the Black Cartridge. With great difficulty, I found the Skype phone number for IKUTEN and made contact. I was told that Brother had made a code change in the printer to prevent using any cartridge not sold by Brother, but was very pleased to be told that IKUTEN had redesigned the cartridge chip on all current versions of the product and that they will send me a new full set of 5 cartridges. Office_Products.reviewText:
This printer has been great so far. I was a little leary at first, because I had a negative experience with low-cost color laser printer in the past, and because several users were getting very dark prints.

Set-up was a breeze, and I had no problems printing right away.
Don't bother with the CD. Just download the latest driver right off the HP website.

I too, found my initial prints way too dark. (Mac OS X 10.7, Adobe Illustrator CS5)
After some fiddling with the settings, and a lot of trial and error, I am now getting almost perfect results. Here's what I did:

Connect to the printer's IP address using a browser.
In the System tab, go to Print Density:
Leave everything at 0, except for the Midtones. Make all the Midtones at -4.

In the "Printer..." options contained in the Print panel:
ColorMatching: ColorSync: Automatic (hp color LaserJet CYMK V402)
Color/Quality Options: HP EasyColor: ON

The color is best when I leave my Document Color Mode in RBG.

Overall, this is a great printer for the price. If it weren't for the difficulty in finding the correct color settings, I'd give it a 5 star rating. The default color densities are way way off, but fortunately you can fix this with some effort.

EDIT:
Over a year later, I finally had to change the black toner that came with the printer, and I print quite a variety of material, from simple text to full pages of color. Still running on the original color toner, although it has said it's been empty for at least 6 months. Don't listen to it. Eventually you may notice that the color starts to change slightly as the toner gets lower, but it's still plenty usable.

This printer has turned out to be an excellent purchase.
Office_Products.summary: How to fix dark prints.

Office_Products.reviewText:
Nothing bad to say about the printer itself. Double sided and quick printing speed. Perhaps a  bit too loud. A small tip to anyone interested in printing envelopes. A note about the packaging I feel is needed as it was just awful. It took me some effort to carry this home as both handles on the box broke. I'd advise to bring some scotch tape if you need to carry this somewhere.
