Office_Products.reviewText:
Updated 2/4/18--  Good phone--  except I had a problem with programming the memory--  I noticed that I could successfully program a 7-digit local number, but attempts to enter memory with an 11-digit long-distance number were unsuccessful.  Other than that--  great phone... loud/clear sound, pleasant ringer, and LOW cost.  This would be a five-star if it weren't for the memory problem with 11-digits.

The difficulty in adding a long number into memory is apparently due to my local telephone exchange interrupting with a recorded message: "If you would like to make a call....".  This happens because they sensed the phone was "off the hook" with no dialing while attempting to add to the memory.  This interruption causes the intended number to not be put into memory correctly.  No problem with a local 7-digit number because you have enough time before the interruption.  The solution--  place the numbers into memory as fast as you can doing the seven
steps required, and repeat until you have done it without getting the interruption (the time varies--  15 or 20 seconds).
Office_Products.summary: Entering Numbers into Memory.

Office_Products.reviewText: I work for the federal government, and use this to carry my PIV card. I have purchased other card holders in the past. This product is made of a pliable frosted plastic, which has a little bit of give making it harder for the plastic to snap. The card is held in place by a plastic tab that "pushes" on the card to keep it in place. I would have given this a 5 star, but my only issue is that the side loader is on the left side, and I'm a righty. Not a big deal at the end of the day.
Office_Products.summary: Great product for those who carry badges

Office_Products.reviewText: To be fair, I had hoped to get a different calendar that was no longer available, and settled for this one. There is a full page drawing opposite each calendar page, but it alternates from left side to right, making half the pages inconvenient for writing by a right-handed person. There are remarks superimposed in script on each drawing; thankfully, the writing is very light so they are easy to ignore, as I have found them uninteresting and overly personal. There is wasted space at the bottom of each page, where they have  inserted a small overview of the whole month, squeezed to one side and leaving the rest of the space blank, with isn't visually pleasing; I think it would have been better to leave that off and allow more space for each day's notes. The calendar that this replaced was set up perfectly in my view, so I am noticing the inadequacies in this one more than I might if I didn't have the comparison. The strong point with this calendar are the drawings, which are typically lovely. I wouldn't buy this one again, and will start earlier next year looking for a replacement for the Lang planner I used to buy.
Office_Products.summary: Pleasant drawings, layout not the best

Office_Products.reviewText:
This is a great mouse pad.  I purchased 1 for my office and one for my home.  They do what they are supposed to do and are comfortable on my wrists.  It is well made and the company shipped fast and genuinely cares about the products and customers.
If you are looking for a anice mousepad with ergonomic support you can't go wrong here.

There is one negative I noticed about both mouse pads and I removed a star because of it.  They have a really strong smell that has lasted several weeks.  It off gasses for a long time.  At first it was really strong.  I purchased this and it was delivered on 1/22/16.  I was prompted to write this review when I got to work today 2/9/16 as I still smell the mouse pad.  It is not nearly as strong, but the smell is definitely there on both mouse pads.  I am not super sensitive to smells in any way so this caught me by surprise.  Overall this is a nice mouse pad but the smell could be an issue if you have sensitivity to smell or would be bothered by the smell.
Office_Products.summary: Great mousepad but it does have a chemical/rubber smell

Office_Products.reviewText:
The first one I got was riddled with problems. Eventually gave up and sent it back to Amazon for a replacement. The replacement is working as expected. My favorite feature is the AirPrint function, which is a lot more convenient than the wireless printing features on various older model printers that also require a specific app to be installed before things can be printed.

I still haven't gotten scan to computer to work though...
Office_Products.summary: My new favorite printer

Office_Products.reviewText:
I have been using this assorted color set for a few weeks now, and I am pretty pleased with the combination of colored and balck inks. The blue/black combination is excellent, but I am only giving 4 stars becuase the other combinations really just turn out looking like dark red, green or brown rather than the near-black quality of the blue.

The micro points are all right, but I would prefer if this set was offered in a medium or bold point (maybe just not available here). Overall, these pens are nice, but not exceptional and I like the darker colors.
Office_Products.summary: BLX is pretty cool

Office_Products.reviewText:
The PIXMA MG5720 is a wireless print/scan/copy device with outstanding output quality. A lot of thought went into making it easy to set up and use, although we managed to defeat some of that in the early going. I really liked the way it presented out of the box with the instruction sheets on top. They are actually easy to follow, so most people will have the physical setup done very quickly. The ink tanks load into their rack very positively: it would be very hard to get it wrong.

Getting wireless connectivity and cloud functions set up requires getting to the settings menu, which requires actually noticing that the front panel display scrolls up and down (circularly), with a press of the up and down buttons. I did not, however, catch on to that until my kid asked if there was more to print because the display said "1/3."

LAN and Cloud setup are straightforward after that. The aforementioned instruction sheets have flowcharts so that you are told exactly what to do to set up the device on wireless only, or also have a USB connection to a computer.

It's very satisfying to be able to save something on your phone and send it to Google Cloud Print, or even just share something from an app. Futuristic!

The other caution you must observe when printing letter size pages is to pull out the center tab on the paper catcher; if you don't, it will look like cats got your output. This is, however, pretty normal for this kind of printer.

Canon has a Creative Park website with a number of templates for greeting cards, scrapbook pages, calendars, you name it. Some is premium, but a lot is free, and it's quick to use.

One of my favorite features is two-sided printing,. I do a lot of handouts and mini-reports that just look a ton more professional when printed on both sides. I also experienced a moment of techno-rapture watching it suck the paper back in to print the second side for the first time.

I'm knocking off one star, though, for the fact that the printer is ungraceful about printing (at least from a PC) when it's turned off. I should be able to just go turn it on and have it start printing, but instead I have to click this and poke that. It doesn't always weather Wi-fi glitches well, either, but so far that has only required entering and leaving setup. Still, more time wasted at the keyboard or the control panel that could have been productive.

I'm waiting to see what my ink budget needs to be. It's very nice that ink tank levels are available right on the device, so you won't be caught by surprise. Also, the black tank is the largest, which was clever.

Overall, it's a great device. Glad to have it in my "SOHO" environment (aka the desk in the dining room).
Office_Products.summary: Very Nice Home and Small Business Multifunction device

Office_Products.reviewText:
Good range, excellent sound quality, loaded with features.  In the Fisk Mansion we needed a way to have a bunch of phones without ripping out the walls and this worked great for us.

Cons :

Hard to get to line 2 from remote handsets.

SpeakerPhone is not loud enough.

No flash switchhook feature on remotes for call waiting (that I know of).
Office_Products.summary: This set has been really great for me

Office_Products.reviewText:
The pen is great --- just as described, very smooth, no worries about not writing immediately. It is also very small, easily fits into my pocket (a woman's pocket!), and I have been carrying it everywhere with me since I got it. Love it.

What I do not love --- hence the 4 star for an otherwise 6-star pen -- is the clip. It fell off about a week after I started using it (I was using the clip regularly, but not abusing it). It is now just loosely on the pen (falling off every day or so; I keep putting it back, but not sure why). Anyway, it is completely unreliable, I cannot use it at all any  more. Maybe I will try to glue it back, but not sure if it can be done nicely.

Anyway, buy it for the pen, and don't rely on the clip.
Office_Products.summary: Love the pen, hate the clip

Office_Products.reviewText: I like that they were packaged in a sealed bag.  It made me feel like they would last longer unused.  It prints well too.  Every time I turn my printer on it tries to print the test page first.  It didn't do that before so I don't know if it's an issue with the cartridge or my printer.  I know how to manage it now though.
Office_Products.summary: Just what I needed

Office_Products.reviewText: I used this refill on this product: HHI Dual Purpose Capacitive Stylus Pen which turned a mediocre stylus/pen combo into a very nice writing instrument/stylus. As far as the refill itself goes, the pro is the same as the con: it makes a lasting impression. What I mean is, it's a great pen for signing a document printed on nice paper stock (such as checks and the like), but it will bleed through most thin cheap copier paper stock so it's not good for everyday writing. That said, if you want a bold stroke when you write on nice paper stock and you have a pen that will take a Pelikan 338 refill, you really can't beat this.
Office_Products.summary: It's thick, it's bold, it's smooth

Office_Products.reviewText:
My Epson died after only 1 year. Love this Canon.
Pros: PRICE, PRICE, PRICE, ease of set-up and use, quite good print quality.
Cons: printouts fall onto floor (no tray), print quality a little washed out (compensate by setting intensity higher, then looks excellent).
I had no trouble locating inktanks, and they weren't any more expensive than the ones for my Epson.
Office_Products.summary: Excellent value for the price

Office_Products.reviewText:
The paper is what you'd expect.  It's a heavy parchment paper with a nice border.  Our organization has an embosser, which I used on the gold seals for a very professional finish.  This is exactly what I was expecting.

The Click-n-print online design system is terrible.  Just get a word template or even make your own.  All you really need for a template is the margins since there's nothing preprinted or prestuck on the forms.  It was nice being able to view the form as it would look while designing it.  But, it's painfully slow, it no longer opens the documents I saved from last month, new prints don't fit on the paper anymore (despite all measurements and templates being the same) and the print quality is abysmal.  All of my text from a laser printer comes out with fuzzy edges.  I created my own template in LibreWriter and downloaded some free fonts.  The output text has nice crisp lines and looks great on the paper.

Summary:
Great paper, Click-n-print is terrible.
Office_Products.summary: Good paper product, but don't use Click-n-print

Office_Products.reviewText: This mouse pad looks and feels great, the material feels sturdy and long-lasting. It came just as pictured. I bought this smaller version because I wanted something portable for my laptop when I play at my friend's place. However, it took me a while to get used to the smaller size since I have the larger size at home. If it was a little bit wider it would be perfect.
Office_Products.summary: Great material, size is good for casual laptop gaming.

Office_Products.reviewText: They were a little smaller than I expected but the bigger issue I had like many others was the colors. Based on the reviews I knew the colors might be different than the picture, but in my case I got almost all pink and purple and other feminine colors - the only reason I ordered was because I was hoping at least one of them would be blue, green or clear so I don't get funny looks wearing it outside the house! (I already have a pink one I got at Wal Mart because that was the only color they had and when I forget to take it off I get some funny looks!)
Office_Products.summary: Colors totally unpredictable - If you don't care then they are OK

Office_Products.reviewText:
I admit to having seen the positive and negative reviews of this product before purchasing it recently.  I may return it - we'll see.

So far, in my limited one-weeks' analysis of this item (and from a non-technical person), I will first mention the things about it that bug me.

1.) Using the stylus.  You end up having to go back and forth trying to handprint the darn letter.  The screen is not sensitive enough (or is too sensitive and perhaps there's another adjustment I can make in preferences that I have not yet tried).  It annoys me that I have to fix "typos" because the screen thought I wrote and "l" and a "c" when I wrote a "k", for example.  There's a handful of letters that this happens with.

2.) The option of using the "keypad" is there, but have you tried to see that keyboard and actually "type" with the stylus?  If you have and love it, you have better eyesight than I do.  The font is TINY to me.  (Though I admit, I need reading glasses.)

3.) There really does exist a high-pitch sound when the unit is on.  I would not have noticed it, though, if someone here didn't mention it.  It's surely there.

4.) I live in fear of the screen smashing by dropping it, since the insurance is just plain stupid to carry on a system that was only $200.00.

Anyway, the good points so far:

1.) I've had no trouble syncing my data to Outlook.
2.) Having the "tasks" features, the calendar, and even the calculator is nice.  There's still much more to be discovered, as mentioned, I've had it only a week.
3.) Seems nice to not have paperwork (bits of paper all around with notes on it).  I even keep my grocery list items in it...I jot them in when I run out of something.  I plan to sync it up and print it from Outlook for this weekend shop.

I still am on the fence if this was the right system for me.  My sister keeps telling me it seems to be more of an aggravation in some ways (having to back it up daily and charge it daily, etc, and that the font is too small, and then theres the issues with the stylus whereby it's just not doing it's job all the time. Oh, and the delay of WHEN you type in the letter to when it actually appears on your screen can be like watching paint dry.

Having said ALL that, maybe if I get my eyes checked, I'd just get used to the small font and avoid the stylus OR double check that I've got Mr Pointy properly set up.
Office_Products.summary: Some pleasures and some disappointments

Office_Products.reviewText: I just received my under desk keyboard tray, started to unwrap the plastic wrap so my maintenance staffer in our building could install it and the tray where the mouse should sit is all broken in pieces.  I'm sure you're thinking "Just return it for a new one"..except this keyboard tray one took a few days to get and I am using it for my pregnancy-induced carpal tunnel, so I don't have the time to return it and wait for a new one. I go out on maternity leave in 1 month. There fore the keyboard tray is installed, sans mouse pad tray ..but be aware, it arrived defective.
Office_Products.summary: I just received my under desk keyboard tray, started ...

Office_Products.reviewText: I needed a new phone with an answering machine. I charged the phone and started programming it for usage. Two problems, I could not get the answering machine to pick up and it would not ring properly. I tried to troubleshoot but nothing worked. Several days later, the answering machine started to pick up calls and ringing more than once. Overall it is a good phone.
Office_Products.summary: I can hear you now

Office_Products.reviewText:
This product would be nicer if it were a bit thicker. As it is, it fits nicely inside my closed MacBook Pro 15", so it does act as a screen protector of sorts. It covers the keuboard, so maybe it protects the screen from keyboard oils, but it is too small to cover the whole screen, so this function is not as advantageous as it could be. The material is a microfiber synthetic (just like what I might use to clean my eyglasses, but) with a thin rubber backing. The problem is, unless you are using this on a perfectly flat and smooth surface, the mouse does not glide well. I have tried to use this on a kitchen counter that has grouted tile, and it does not work well there. However, on my desk at work, it is OK. It has more friction than other brands like the Fellowes, which I like a lot a better, as it works just like it is supposed to- as a mousepad.
It seems that the product manufacturers are trying too hard to make this a multifunctional item, which, in my opinion, does not work well for either.
Office_Products.summary: Nice idea, but falls short of its primary purpose

Office_Products.reviewText: I purchased this in November 2014 and started using it in December. By the end of January it was tilting toward the edge of the shelf. Small things started rolling off the shelf. I have tried numerous adjustments in attaching it to the cubicle wall in different places and it still has the tilt issue. I only have a tissue box and a small hand sanitizer on it.  I do not recommend it for fabric cubicle walls because the fabric does not hold the pins very snugly. The pins holding it into the fabric stretch out as well. They need to be stronger.
Office_Products.summary: Not For Fabric Cubicle Walls

Office_Products.reviewText:
I was looking for a simple refillable address book that had an individual/separator tab for each letter. That is exactly what this address book is.  Each tab has one letter (with the exception of the "Mc" tab). The pages are simple, name, Address, zip code, phone number, area code and extension.  The pages remind me of the address books from my childhood (pre-cell phone and e-mail).

Also included at no additional charge is crappy lettering on the tabs, spine and front, (gold lettering is already coming off) and the map of the U.S. with time zones and area codes (which need to be updated). I am assuming that the pages were printed before or around 1997 since the 760 and many more area codes are not on this map.

I would not suggest this for people who do not have nice, neat penmanship.  The spacing between the lines is what I consider to be narrow.  So my penmanship looks even more messy.
Office_Products.summary: Simple, refillable and outdated

Office_Products.reviewText:
My previous wrist rest was the Grifiti Fat Wrist Pad 17 with cloth top.  I had picked it out to go with my Rosewill RK-9000 mechanical keyboard because they're almost exactly the same length (17" vs 17.3") and height (0.5").  It worked pretty well except some color fading and cloth fraying at the edges.
I recently purchased a Rosewill RK-9000V2 mechanical keyboard and decided to go wrist rest shopping again.  When I saw that my wrist rest came in a new "skinless" edition, I was super excited.  I already knew it would fit my keyboard length and height perfectly and the "skinless" would fix the issue with color fading and edge fraying.
When it showed up, I was a bit disappointed.  It looks very nice and it feels very nice... but it's too short.  It's supposed to be a full 17", but mine is just barely over 16" (16.25" to be exact).  Instead of matching the length of my keyboard, it's noticeably shorter.  Given some of the other reviews, it appears I'm not the only one having that issue.

Overall, 4 star for quality, -1 star for misleading length.

Attached pictures:
1) overall wrist rest length versus 17.3" Rosewill RK-9000V2 keyboard
2) current skinless wrist wrest (16.25") on top of previous cloth topped version (full 17")
Office_Products.summary: Feels very nice but actual length is almost 1" short.

Office_Products.reviewText:
I am homeschooling my son for Kindergarten this year and I wanted this chart to help him see how to count by 5's and 10's. The description says it's layered with plastic so that you can write and wipe-away.

In reality, this product comes wrinkled, ripped, and in my particular case, some of the ink rubbed off of the word "Counting". While the chart does as it says in regards to the numbers, it is very poorly made.

I could have probably had a similar chart printed up at a professional printers for cheaper and with better material if I wasn't so busy. This item should be priced at half of what they are charging (it is currently $9 and some odd cents).

The back of this thin chart says "Printed in China" so I guess that explains the poor quality. I'm not usually one to spout off about "Made in America" but this is one product that has no reason to be made in China. I'm pretty sure we have the capabilities to produce this right here in our own country...

If you plan to purchase this, I recommend you prepare yourself for the sorry state it will arrive in. Maybe taking it to a place that can laminate it with the proper plastic would be best if you care to spend more money.
Office_Products.summary: Flimsy, Wrinkled, Ripped - But Does The Job

Office_Products.reviewText:
I bought this and returned it when I discovered that the AC cord does not come with the unit. The AC "adaptor" will set you back about $25.00. Too bad, because this seemed like a nice unit when I took it out of the box, with its angled keys and clean face.

For $59.00, you can get a PT-1950, which has a cord and can be used with your computer USB.
Office_Products.summary: Overpriced because it has no AC Cord

Office_Products.reviewText: I love the economical aspects for saving on printing cost. That feature is really great. However, my biggest complaint, its a huge complaint, is that photos are terrible. They use up  a lot of ink, they come out of the printer wet, and the picture is very blurred. Very disappointed with the quality of photos but more than happy on saving on everyday document printing.
Office_Products.summary: Big savings on document printing costs, but quality of photos is terrible!!!

Office_Products.reviewText: I was not very careful when I ordered these, wanting to get to work on my project.  When they arrived I was disappointed to find that the 1 inch-ish spaced you see in the picture are actually separate compartments.  Not sure exactly why this bothered me -- I think I just expected something simpler, cleaner (and more versatile).
Office_Products.summary: When they arrived I was disappointed to find that the 1 inch-ish spaced you see ...

style.Color:: Black Carbon Fiber Palmrest Sticker+semi-black Keyboard Skin

Office_Products.reviewText: this was not very easy to apply. i could not access the video to watch how to do it. I have small breaks in the skin where the pieces don't line up exactly. i won't buy this one again because i could not make it fit like a glove. maybe if i could make it fit better i would buy it again. i like the feel of it on my laptop.
Office_Products.summary: this was not very easy to apply

Office_Products.reviewText:
I am still fooling around with this combo printer/scanner/copier.  First impressions:

Setup was easy, wi-fi connectivity works pretty well for me on my desktop (I have macs) but the laptop seems to have an issue with finding the printer in the preferences.  It prints fairly well.  The first inks that came with printer lasted a long time.  If you get a sign that says "low ink", keep using it until it forces you to change - the inks will last a long time.  The copier works okay, although the buttons on this printer are confusing (no "copy" in English, just symbols - annoying).  I had to put labels next to the icons to remind me of which is copy, etc.  The screen is fairly easy to read.  Speaking of copying, the glass is long, and if you put down a 8.5 X 11 document to copy, and put it at the intuitively correct end, it cuts off the document.  So you have to place it opposite of where you think it should go.  (same with scan position, described below). poor design in that regard.

I am extremely disappointed in the scanner part of this printer. The Epson scanning software is pretty bad.  You cannot edit a document (crop, rotate, etc) before you scan it.....(?). It insists on putting a number 1 after whatever you title the resulting document.  Canon's scanner software is far superior in this regard.  Plus, to scan a document, you put the document down on the plate in the position that it would be to copy straight up, but it's upside down in the scan.... ?  Don't know who thought that up!  And remember, you can't pre-edit it before the scan.  Annoying. It's super complicated to do anything than just scan one page.  Scanning multiple pages in one PDF document takes forever - because you have to keep "adding" a page and previewing it) - it all takes a lot of time.

You also have to set up the scan settings to recognize the wifi before you can use the scanner part.  I had to have Epson walk me through this (they were very nice and helpful).  but the software itself gets a D grade for its lack of editing features pre-scan and unnecessary complications scanning a multiple page document.  I haven't tried scanning photographs yet, so don't know if you can put down 4 photos on the glass and have the scanner distinguish that they're 4 separate images (has anyone done that yet?)
Office_Products.summary: Fair performance, poor scanning program

Office_Products.reviewText:
I make a ton of canvas prints with my large format inject printer. Premier Art Eco Shield is the best quality liquid laminate for canvas  inject prints available. There is just no substitute for this stuff, I love it. It gives your prints that much needed extra boost of professionalism in both looks and functionality.

That being said, this stuff is really expensive and very hard to find. I was all but forced to go through Amazon, which normally wouldn't have been a problem since I'm a Prime member. However, this company does not cater to Prime customers so they force you to pay for shipping.

This stuff is expensive enough without tacking on an additional $12 for shipping a small jar (quart) of liquid. Are you serious? Unfortunately I don't have a choice and must buy from here. The folks are pleasant enough and package their items well, but there's no reason to gouge your customers with an inflated shipping price, especially if you are selling on Amazon and not a third party website. Apply for Prime or at least reduce the shipping cost and I'll edit my rating to 5 stars.
Office_Products.summary: Used on my Canvas Prints (rating is directed to seller not product)

Office_Products.reviewText:
My old paper shredder died and I wanted a new one that could handle me stuffing more paper in it at once. Ordered the Amazon Basics 12-Sheet Cross-Cut Paper/CD/Credit Card Shredder. When I tried 6 pieces of paper, it did OK, but still seemed to stress it. 12 sheets almost stopped it. Yes it will do 12, but I would expect the life of the unit to drop VERY fast with that stress.

It will probably do fine as long as I keep the paper count down to 6 or less.. It's OK, but don't expect it to be happy with large volumes stuffed in it!
Office_Products.summary: Works... but 12 sheets of paper really punishes it

Office_Products.reviewText: These definitely don't show up very dark on my white board. I barely use them because of this; they are barely visible. And some colors like orange and light green are completely useless because they barely show up. The only one that really worked well and that I use often is the black marker. Please invest in better quality markers if you want to write on a large white board.
Office_Products.summary: Not worth it

Office_Products.reviewText: I received this printer free, I had no expectations. I was very excited about it's scanning and it not being too bulky. The quality of B&W document printing and scanning is decent but ink cartridge lifespan in the printer is terrible. I was also not impressed with the printer quality of graphics and colored fonts; ink didn't fill out parts of my graphics with text. The machine itself is quiet, easy to setup, and use. I would only recommend this Printer if you are planning on scanning and printing basic documents.
Office_Products.summary: Good for scanning and document Printing

Office_Products.reviewText: I like the phone- some of the ring tones are horrible, but it is sharp looking and very functional. One annoying part is that there is a red light that really does not stop flashing ever! It is supposed to indicate a call came in, but it really doesn't go away. So we put a piece of electrical tape over it and now the phone is perfect! Great sound, good speaker. I like it.
Office_Products.summary: Not a bad phone

Office_Products.reviewText: I like brother products, I have a larger all in one brother printer. I purchased this one to handle some of my color printing and to be portable. The printer is made of very thin plastic that flexes easily. Set up was easy and all the functions worked as expected.  Except for some difficulty with air print however a firmware update seems to have resolved this issue. compared to my other brother printer, this one is very cheaply made.
Office_Products.summary: Printer works well but it's not very sturdy.

Office_Products.reviewText: We purchased this to lock up medications from children but the problem is that it can't really be set up somewhere on a shelf.  It has to be attached to a wall, which is an issue for us.  The cabinet is just too front heavy without it being attached to the wall so when you open the door, it tips forward.  As a result, we have not used this very much.  We have been trying to come up with a solution but as we are renting this house, we don't want to damage the walls putting in a medicine cabinet - so we must find some kind of alternative solution.
Office_Products.summary: Security hides medicine - but MUST be mounted on a wall to work properly

Office_Products.reviewText: I have a love hate relationship with Dymo. When these work they work great. When they fail they are absolutely annoying. If the software we use didn't have to use these I would buy something else. We have gone through 4 or 5 of these that have simply gone crazy after about 8 months of use. Randomly prints garbage and you have to completely unplug the printer to get it to stop....
Office_Products.summary: Great when it works. Terrible when it doesn't

Office_Products.reviewText:
I see more than a few people have had problems with setting up this printer on their networks. I think I know why.

Personally, it took me about 1 minute to install this printer via my wired network. And it worked flawlessly... for two weeks. Then the network card appears to have spontaneously died - while sitting on the floor, unmolested, happily printing a document. It will work with usb cable, but will no longer be recognized by the network, despite performing a clean reinstall of the drivers. Both of my computers stopped recognizing the printer at the same time. I suspect that those with problems setting up the printer probably had a dead ethernet card in theirs.

I owned the 2070N before this one, and other than longevity (lasting only 1 year) I had no complaints about it. Same goes for this one. But a 2 week lifespan is plenty to complain about.

** edit:
Found a fix! After speaking with support, I found a way to revive my wonky printer. Turn off the printer. Press and hold the blue button while turning it on. Then press it seven (?) times, IIRC. I had to do this a few times over the years, and it always worked. Then I killed my printer by putting something through that I shouldn't. My fault.

For some reason, I decided to buy another one of these. I guess the main reason I went back is the printer install is very, very easy. My latest 2170W has been working fine for over a year, now. No networking issues. Considering my experience with alternatives, I'm more than happy with this printer.
Office_Products.summary: Broken Network Card

Office_Products.reviewText:
I liked this little piece of art. The quality of the bottom part it wasn't good but the top was unique. I cannot hide it that I was a little disappointed.
I wish it was bigger and actually the dimensions are specified but I did not pay attention to it also because it looked like a convincing size from the picture.
I'd like to ad that the box/package was dirty and I did not like the Amazon's gift wrap and the "smile logo" on top of the card (especially the type of font they used for my personalized greeting). I wouldn't like to send a gift to someone and "force" the receiver to see Amazon advertising. Too cheap.
Office_Products.summary: Beautiful but small!

Office_Products.reviewText: this phone is.. fine. The big complaint is the digital answering part. My voice sounds like a crazy robot on playback, and when people leave messages they are all kind of shrill sounding (or maybe that's just my friends). The volume for the answering playback on my phone seems to be a bit touchy as well. It seems to go from quiet to loud with nothing in between. we don't use the caller id features, so I can't really comment about that.
Office_Products.summary: Perfect for when you need to talk on the phone

Office_Products.reviewText: These haven't been my favorite laminating pouches. They are a bit too thick and glossy for my taste. The quality is very good though, but I just prefer a bit less gloss cause it's hard to see what's laminated sometimes when it hits the light just right. Overall they get the job done, but I've used some laminating pouches that were cheaper and were to more of my preference as far as thickness and glossiness.
Office_Products.summary: Not my favorite, but they are good quality.

Office_Products.reviewText: Very cute, but cannot find a rubber doorstop to fit underneath.  They do not work on their own and need a rubber stopper to make them stay, which is fine considering I bought them for their looks.  But, the depth is so shallow that a regular doorstop is too big.  Going to have to find or invent a solution because I really want to use them.  They are super cute.
Office_Products.summary: Very cute, but does not work well

Office_Products.reviewText: I bought this for my classroom, and really liked it at first. However, the time gets increasingly faster at an increment my students and I have not yet been able to figure out. It's currently 16 minutes fast after about two months. We have bets on what time it will be when school ends in June... But I do like the temperature function (we have heating issues) and it holds my whiteboard pens nicely (it fits on the tray under the board).
Office_Products.summary: fast clock

Office_Products.reviewText:
I thought the ink would be wonderful to the eyes given its color.
And it is.

Except, when you write with it, it's a little painful to read.
You eyes strain a bit.  You won't feel it consciously, but you will notice it enough to want to change the color.

The texture and quality is of course phenomenal.
I would recommend to go for one shade darker in this blue from other brands if you want something that is readable and comfortable.
Office_Products.summary: Lighter than expected

Office_Products.reviewText: Recently, this unit was damaged during an interoffice move.  The keyboard tray split where it was screwed to the bracket and came clean off, revealing the material that the product is constructed off.  It really is  just a dense paperboard that is covered in a plastic material.  I'm sure they do this to reduce the weight as it is quite a heavy unit.  I sent an email inquiry to customer service asking if I could purchase a new keyboard tray to replace the broken one and they responded that they needed my original order number, which I don't have.  When I responded questioning why they needed the original order number ( I wasn't looking for a free-bee under warranty), they ceased corresponding with me.  Beware if you need any repairs in the distant future as you won't get customer service support without the original order number.  Otherwise, the unit does what it is supposed to do.  Over time, I will say that some of the screws do start to come lose which again, is difficult to repair because the paperboard material that it is made from easily loosens over time.  For the price, I'm not sure the longevity of the product, especially if you do plan on frequently moving it up and down, as designed.  Probably will last longer if you keep it in one position
Office_Products.summary: Keep your original order number...Or no customer service support for you!

Office_Products.reviewText: I have ordered Lexmark X73 ink cartriges twice from AMAZON, both times the color was 60 not 20 and would not work properly in my printer. I ordered the cartridges  being previewed but got  a valusmile 2-pack for compatible lexmark 60 and lexmark 70. I don't know for sure if a 60 will work in a Lexmark X73 or not but both times the color was unacceptable and the black was faded. I think next time I will buy it off the shelf.
Office_Products.summary: a bummer

Office_Products.reviewText:
Item arrived today and it looks very dark Brown - almost Black.  There is a huge difference between Tan, Dark Tan, and Dark Brown/Black.
I'm attempting to get back into my old habits of using Franklin Covey planner.
The item is genuine Franklin Covey but I expected my item to look like the picture and not almost black.

1 star for poor representation of the product!!!
Office_Products.summary: Wrong picture

Office_Products.reviewText:
I was looking for an answering machine with multiple mailboxes and there don't seem to be many to choose from, so I bought this one as the specs sounded promising. It was small, which was good. It needed 24 hours to charge the phone before I could event attempt to program it.

The user guide was missing lots of details, and customer service didn't know much about the product. Many other issues, but the most relevant one was that messages left on the machine could hardly be heard, which negates the whole purpose of an answering machine.  One customer service person suggested that for the messages to be recorded louder I should crank up the volume on the answering machine and leave it at maximum. I've owned lots of answering machines. The volume control is for listening to messages, not recording incoming messages.

I returned the machine and recommended to amazon that they stop selling it.
Office_Products.summary: Terrible answering machine

Office_Products.reviewText: I hate to give a bad review to a product,  however,  this is a  generic, which by default, it supposed to be less quality,  however I wasn't expecting it to be this bad,  do not buy this product,  it will ruin your printer, and it may ruin even more than a few days of your life,  when you need to print, you are expected to print,  not run out trying to find out what the heck happened to kinkos!

Office_Products.reviewText: These pens are terrible!  I have only had them for a couple of weeks.  The caps fall off or crack.  The tops of the pens fall out leaving the gel exposed.  Most of the pens would not write right out of the box.  The black one was in my pen hold cup with the point down and all the ink drained out of it.  It is now totally empty of ink and worthless.  They are cheap, badly made gel pens.  Do NOT buy these.  Don't waste your money!!!

Office_Products.reviewText:
I don't know about this product, but I ordered from a vendor, and this package that I received... nowhere did it say it was DUCK BRAND, which appears to be a good name brand.

What I got is Bubble Wrap that is popped.  It is on a roll, but so many of the bubbles are popped.  What is that about?

When you order this, Duck Brand, make sure you get Duck Brand on the labeling.

To this day, I cannot guarantee I received Duck Brand....Rizzo
Office_Products.summary: The Bubbles were 50% popped already

Office_Products.reviewText: Every time I attempted to print, the message screen indicated that this cartridge was either missing or defective, and to get it to function I'd have to take out the cartridge, clean the electrodes with pure alcohol, re-insert the cartridge, and wait for the machine to decide if it was okay or I needed to take it back out and re-insert, until it finally accepted the cartridge, and printed.  The wasted time, wasted paper, and wasted aggravation hasn't been worth the cost savings.  Except for the fact that this cartridge was a tinny bit smaller than original HP cartridges, I don't understand why it causes so much trouble, because I had such good results with prior re-manufactured color cartridges like this one.

Office_Products.reviewText:
Terrible stickers.  I bought these static stickers thinking it would save me some trouble with occasionally removing residue of actual stickers.  Well, they don't leave any residue, which is what earns them the 1 star, otherwise would be a zero star item.  Product regularly crinkles up and falls off the windshield.  I own 5 vehicles and it has happened in every vehicle.  If they manage to stay on more than 2 days, they seem to hold for the remainder of the oil change, but it's the frustration of having to try another sticker 2-3 times per oil change that is just too frustrating.

If you have the patience to try multiple stickers, these may work for you, the price is right.  But for me they aren't worth the hassle

Office_Products.reviewText: Maybe I received a defective pen but writing with it was like nails on a chalkboard. The tip was like writing with a marker that is starting to dry out and had a 'squeak' noise to it. I would have never paid $5 for this pen if I had been able to test it out first. It ended up in my kids art box instead.

Office_Products.reviewText: One phone after another ceased to work.  When you answered on #4 phone - none of the other phones would connect with the caller. This was a thoroughly frustrating set of phones. They would drop calls or cut off after the first ring.  I was replacing Panasonic phones with these new ones.  The old ones with their problems are far better than the new ones.  Will buy another brand.
Office_Products.summary: DO NOT RECOMMEND!

Office_Products.reviewText: What the heck happened to these pencils?  Use to love them (even when they were made in Mexico they were good)  not now.  The quality of these pencils have SERIOUSLY went down hill since they went to China.  The lead is different and not centered,  the paint is different and comes off after minimal use,  the wood is different and no longer has the cedar smell.  They don't sharpen smooth....  These pencils are horrible now.  Sad,  they were always my favorite.  Grrff
Office_Products.summary: What happened to this pencil?  Horrible!

Office_Products.reviewText: Deserves zero stars. Came damaged! Was told that it would take 6-8 weeks to replace. Attempted to fix it myself, and use. The product is so cheaply made that the entire cabinet tipped forward, all of the draws opened, and it fell on top of me. Thankfully others were around in the office when it happened, so I wasn't completely crushed. Just a few bruises and cuts-still recovering.

Office_Products.reviewText:
It says it's Linux compatible, but unless you're a super Linux geek, don't assume that means you can install the driver for it! I will have to do some research and learning and keep trying, but so far it isn't working for me on Linux Ubuntu. The lack of a printer to computer cable is a minor problem compared to this.

Bad Canon!

Office_Products.reviewText:
Received it and blue ink leaked out immediately and stained my carpet and hands.

Installed into the printer and everything it printed was smeared in blue. Red didn't show up at all. I cleaned the head several times, same results (actually got worse the more I printed). I installed my original Lexmark cartridges (they were low but still had a little) and it worked fine. Messed around several times just using one of each color with the Lexmark cartridges and could never get it to print correctly no matter what cobination or how many times I installed and uninstalled them.

They don't quite click into place correctly either.

Ink drips out of them (all colors did, but the blue REALLY LEAKED). The Lexmarks don't leak at all and I've gone through several sets.

Seems to be hit or miss with these.

Returned and got a refund (Ya Amazon!)

Found some OEM Lexmark caridges on Amazon for a steal and have been happy ever sense.

I bought this printer as part of a computer purchase and it has never worked right.  It won't recognize the 124 ink cartridges that came with it.  When Epson sent me the replacement 125 cartridges with won't recognize magenta.  Unless it recognizes all ink cartridges it won't work.  No even black and white printer.  This means it won't copy either.  It's a worthless piece of junk.  I have to add here that I've been dealing with computers and printers for many years and I've had the most difficulty with Epson printers.  I'll NEVER buy one again.  I recommend Canon printers.  I've had the least trouble and best reliability with them (e.g., they last me for several years without incident).

Office_Products.reviewText: This is a great idea in theory, but it's very hard to use in practice. We ended up wasting the whole roll because of one mis-application. I regret not getting the paint, which may be a hassle but at least it's cost-effective because you can mess up applying it once and not ruin your whole purchase.

Office_Products.reviewText:
- I am not able to get it to work on Windows XP.

Office_Products.reviewText:
Honey Can Do is the worst company I have ever experienced in my life.  I received the cart with missing parts (2 cotters clips) and becuase I need the cart. Office_Products.reviewText: Awful. I dislike leaving bad reviews but this is a waste of money. I'd return it but already threw away the product package it came in. And it's not worth the return shipping. The pencils sharpen well enough IF you can get the pencil out. Every pencil I sharpen gets stuck and I have to move my desk away from the wall and unplug this sharpener otherwise it just keeps running and the pencil really needs to be forcefully pulled from the sharpener.  The pencil is also difficult to insert and you really have to give it quit a push. Then it won't come out. At first I thought it was me until several others tired to use this sharpener. Office_Products.summary: I dislike leaving bad reviews but this is a waste of ...

Office_Products.reviewText:
I have owned this printer for three years, and I can't count the times I have been extraordinarily frustrated by this printer in that period. One would think that, with 20 years of experience as a software engineer, I would be accustomed to dealing with buggy system software. But there are simply too many problems.

The most obnoxious problem is that, in many circumstances, it is IMPOSSIBLE to print B&W if one of your colors is truly totally gone. The manual and the printer tell you that you can but it fails every single time, despite all new driver downloads etc.

The printer faces many other system failures, some of which involve numerous failures at updating firmware. Enraging, truly, the amount of time you spend trying to get this to work properly. Next to it, my Brother and my Canon printers have practically 100% up time.

There is a lesson in there. I got seduced by the nice colors of that printer. I should have remained focused on the reliability data. Epson, as a printer brand, is simply unreliable, and outright fraudulent when dealing with printing B&W. So don't do what I did -- stick with Brother and Canon, don't waste your time with Epson.
Office_Products.summary: Do not believe anyone who says you can print B&W when one color ink is out

Office_Products.reviewText:

However, nearly 25% of the calls I make or receive the caller cannot hear me.  Nothing.  Nada.  It is VERY frustrating.  The number pad on the phone will not work in those instances either.  For instance, if I am dialing the pharmacy and trying to enter an Rx number to order a refill absolutely nothing registers from the phone.  It's completely unreliable and has been a waste of money.

Do like the feel of the paper and the darkness of the dots. Just need to provide a better binding and stronger cover .
Office_Products.summary: Do like the feel of the paper and the darkness of ...

Office_Products.reviewText:
This isn't card stock, or even particularly rigid paper.  It's just regular glossy photo paper with pre-cut areas that let you pop the "cards" out after you print them.

In order to use this paper properly, you have to create an account on the Avery web site and load the corresponding template from the website.  If you don't, you have to carefully calibrate your printer and  your design to get them to match up with the pre-cut regions, which is more trouble than it's worth because all you get, IF you are successful, is a floppy little piece of photo paper.  You'd be better off just buying regular glossy photo paper, printing multiple cards on one page, and then cutting them out with a paper cutter, because it's less trouble and expense to do it that way and you get the same result.
Office_Products.summary: Don't waste your money or time on these.  Just use regular glossy photo paper and a paper cutter.

Office_Products.reviewText: This is the second one I BOUGHT also, and I too only gotten 30 pages per ink cartridge,... Office_Products.reviewText: I was ordered a pink pen for my bday and couldn't wait to recieve since I have been looking for a pink pen like this forever.......however, to my dismay, I opened the box to find a black pen instead. Not a happy birthday girl. :-( Even worse than the color, I tried putting the pen in my purse and the rinestones started falling off. It's not cute to take out and use now. I recommend getting this pen to sit at your desk, not to carry around in your purse.

Office_Products.reviewText:
I've read some current reviews about this phone system and decided to add my review late in case anyone thinks about purchasing this discontinued system (refurb, ebay or where ever).  Take heed in the negative reviews.  I purchased the base unit plus 3 additional phones a few years back from Circuit City when it was still the top of the line.  It worked great for 9 months, then like other reviews here, the system tanked without a single thing changing in our house.  All of a sudden the sound quality fluctuated from serviceable to horrible, handsets could no longer lock onto the base unit even from the next room or feet away from the base unit.  The answering system becomes frustrating over time because it seemed to have problems of it's own picking up, recorded message/greeting.  Customer support was a bad experience, online support is nill.  We still have the phone system sitting in a closet and I was looking for the manual, yet up to par with the rest of their support, you cannot find it on their support web site...I found it here on Amazon where I guess some kind soul submitted it and brought me to write this review.

In France, Siemens phone systems are the rage my wife just returned from her trip...but it must be something with the Euro models.  In the US, they are junk.

Replaced the Siemens system with a Panasonic 5.8ghz KX-TG5100M system for about 2 years now and have had nothing but fantastic success.  The only negative/problem we encountered was the system used the NiCd 850mAh batteries and a year ago during a week long power outage (hurricane) the $25 batteries drained and would not recharge no matter what.  On a hunch, I called Panasonic customer support and explained my situation and they sent me new 1000mAh NiMH batteries for all my phones at no charge.  To this day I have yet to experience 1 real problem.

Panasonic makes great phones, better to spend your money on something other than Siemens

Office_Products.reviewText: It's a nice size and has a nice feel, at first.  Besides the strong chemical odor when it arrived it seemed to be the perfect solution.  The problem is, my wrist made a permanent depression in the middle within a day or two of use.  So then I rotate it to alternate what part I rest my wrist on. I don't believe that this was worth the price that I paid.

Office_Products.reviewText:
The sharpener worked fine, until it broke after two months: the pencil indicator stopped indicating. Contacted the seller, ACE PHOTO DIGITAL, and was referred to PaperMate customer service. Easy enough, I thought, until I spoke with Sanford L.P., the owner of PaperMate trademark, and was informed that they do not manufacture, nor perform warranty work for this particular model. Rather, the PM-400S is made under license by World Office Products.

I called the two numbers provided. The toll-free 800 number appears to be disconnected, and the regular number is picked up by a digital voice mail dump. I then went to the company's web site and found that it contains only a page full of external links. In fact, it appears that World Office Products does not exist.

I contacted ACE PHOTO DIGITAL once again and asked them to attempt to resolve this matter. They have not responded.

I fully blame the vendor, ACE PHOTO DIGITAL, for selling a discontinued product, made by a company that no longer exists, without stating anything to that effect. A warranty is very much an integral part of a product and inability to obtain warranty drastically diminishes its value. This blatant omission of a key piece of information constitutes an egregious violation of a vendor's responsibility. Combined with the fact that ACE PHOTO DIGITAL refuses to even as much as respond to my request, I will make sure to specifically avoid buying anything from this operation and recommend that anyone reading this review do the same.
Office_Products.summary: Broke after two months, impossible to get customer support

Office_Products.reviewText:

Office_Products.reviewText: The logo is not even close to being centered on the fabric, it's way to high and part of it got chopped off at the top. Office_Products.reviewText:
This is a typical mousepad, but if you are expecting a realisticly colored and crisp picture - this is not the one for you.  The colors on this tiger are orange and blue and are slighly blurry.  It may be appreciated by fans of Auburn University since their colors are blue and orange and their mascott is a tiger.
Don't waste your money on this one.
Office_Products.summary: Orange and Blue

Office_Products.reviewText: Pencils do not fall easily into the mechanism to be dispensed. I used #2 regular size Ticonderoga pencils exclusively in my first grade classroom. I have come to the point of just leaving the top open so I can manhandle the pencils into an accepted formation to make mechanics work. The acrylic knob comes unscrewed as students try to retrieve a pencil as there's a need to rock the turn knob back and forth. I now leave two or three pencils resting on the delivery tray to avoid frustration on the part of all involved. The concept is nice; but, the reality is very flawed.
Office_Products.summary: Doesn't Deliver As Promised

Office_Products.reviewText:
I like the pen itself.  The violet ink color is bright, legible, and unusual but not too candylike (at least for me).  The pen writes smoothly and precisely.  It is slenderer than the average pen, but is comfortable if you grip it lightly.  Because it is so slender, it is nice and unobtrusive in the pocket.

Why two stars then?  I bought a box, and every pen in the box had not one, but two bar code stickers on the cap.  So now I have to spend an hour scraping the stickers off and cleaning the gummy residue so that I can have a newish pen instead of a sticky, grimy one.  I don't think most people buying a box of pens are planning to resell them, so I don't understand why they need stickers.  Next time I'll buy somewhere else.
Office_Products.summary: Plastered with stickers.

Office_Products.reviewText: I am a preschool teacher and was looking for something to cover the back of a shelf. I wanted a magnetic sheet that was strong enough to hold magnetic letters, allowing the kids to play. This is not strong enough to hold even the lightest magnetic. The sheet itselfs IS the magnet (meaning it sticks to a fridge or a metal surface). Not what I was wanting it for.
Office_Products.summary: I am a preschool teacher and was looking for something ...

Office_Products.reviewText: Sometimes it prints fast and other times, like now, it prints really slow. I have looked online for fixes and it seems to be a common problem with these printers and there is no fix that has worked so far. It also goes through the maintenance boxes (which cost about $20 each) fairly quickly so I have had to buy a reusable one. I guess going through maintenance boxes quickly means it also wastes a lot of ink. Talking about wasting a lot of ink. When my other printers have run out of ink, they finish the page and then tell me. No, not this one. It always seems to stop 7/8ths of the way through printing a two sided piece that I have to then throw away. It just seems that Epson has to get their finger out of their ... and fix the many software issues and it would be a decent printer.
Office_Products.summary: It could be great - but it's not.

Office_Products.reviewText: I purchased this new drum for my Sharp AL1631 copier that gets light usage, less than 30 copies per week.  It worked fine for a week then started leaving blank areas on copes down the center of the page.  In addition to that, the end of the unit fell off and two gears fell out.  It took me a while to figure out how to reinstall the gears to make the drum work, but the blank spots continued.  I thought that it may be the new toner cartridge that I had installed at the same time, but even after purchasing a second new toner cartridge, the blank spots are still there.  The first 2 or 3 copies are fine, then the blank gets wider and wider.  I finally decided to just buy a new copier and stop spending money on new parts and supplies.  Of course, this was what I was trying to avoid in the first place.
Office_Products.summary: Poor quality product

Office_Products.reviewText: I have the older version of this phone with 2 more handsets purchased in 2010.  I began having trouble with my line and assumed (unfortunately) that it was the phone.  I ordered this newer version of the Panasonic so I wouldn't have a big learning curve in programming, etc.  I set it up and then discovered I still had the problem.  After the cable company solved it, I hooked up my old phone again.  This new version is a real cheapie.  The readput lettering is so dim  that I had to bend down to read it before answering.  That was my main beef with it.  Mine also arrived with a faulty set of batteries.  I'll keep it for emergencies, but certainly not recommend it.
Office_Products.summary: Buy something else...

Office_Products.reviewText: Don't buy the calendar this year!  This is the third year that I have bought this calendar and I am very disappointed.  The actual calendar section with the days and dates has been significantly reduced in size while the pocket has been significantly increased in size.  This means that there isn't enough space to write all the activities for the whole family every day.  Also, it is printed on different paper and it is really difficult to write on.  The pen's ink does not seem to stick even though I tried different types of pens.  The calendar isn't even on the wall yet, so I was writing on a flat surface.  It is going to be even more difficult once it's up on the wall!
Office_Products.summary: This is the third year that I have bought this calendar and I am very disappointed. The actual calendar section with the days an

Office_Products.reviewText: I knew buying this board was a gamble, as many of the reviews indicated boards that arrived bent out of shape. I hoped I would skate by with a perfect board, but I found that to not be the case. The board has a decent bend in one of the metal sidings and a break that is clearly visible in the back of the board. Additionally, you can tell there has been a break from the cork side as well.
Office_Products.summary: I hoped I would skate by with a perfect board, but I found that to not be ...

Office_Products.reviewText: I got the Epson V33 Scanner and had a lot of trouble with the EPSON SCAN Software. I installed it and the buttons wouldn't work right. I kept getting a message telling me to re-install the program. I even loaded it from the file on the disc, and still got the error message. When I click on the Epson Scan Icon on the desktop, it works great, and the pictures come out great, but it won't work with the button. I haven't had time to contact Epson yet.
Office_Products.summary: Disappointed

Office_Products.reviewText:
It is an absolutely gorgeous portfolio.  Unlike other reviewers, the pen holder is a perfect size for me.  I use a conventional Gel Pen most of the time, and a much more elegant pen wood-carved very "fat" pen that fits ok. but is a little too tight.  My favorite fountain pen (a little fatter than my conventional gel pen) fits perfectly.

Why only 4 Stars?  The portfolio arrived and an inch or so of the stitching inside the portfolio was frayed and out of the holes.

I am returning it, but also immediately ordering another one.

UPDATE

The new portfolio is perfect with no damage and, as usual, Amazon was perfect in accepting the return and getting a new one to me fast.

I so want to love this portfolio.  The leather is gorgeous, soft and, I'm sure, durable.  The stitching is extremely well done.  But, for me at least, it fails to "function" test.  In addition to holding an 8-1/2 X 11 pad, I use my portfolios to hold loose paper.  I always put a few sheets in the pockets on the inside opposite the pad.  There are two pockets like that on this portfolio.  Unfortunately, both are way too tight.  It is impossible to slide a couple of 8-1/2 X 11 pages into them.  For an otherwise extremely well made and aesthetically beautiful product, it simply isn't practical for me.

If using the inside pockets to hold a few sheets of loose paper doesn't matter to you, or you are willing to fold up your loose paper before sliding it into one of the pockets, this is a fabulous folder.  I wish it worked for me.
Office_Products.summary: the pen holder is a perfect size for me

Office_Products.reviewText: Honestly it looks great without the scratches and used looking marks on it :/ it came fairly fast but it just looks like they didn't care enough to properly package it to avoid scratches..its supposed to be a christmas present for my 61 yr old mom but really I wouldve never bought it if I knew it was extremely hard to open. And I'm 22. Gunna have to help my arthritic mom open it even though it shouldve been perfect.. Smh.
Office_Products.summary: used?

Office_Products.reviewText: I have owned several Lexmark printers over the years and have always felt they were very dependable. However this model E260DN is one I wish I never purchased.  The printer doesn't communicate with my computer (windows xp)all the time. Every week I have to first remove the printer drivers then reload my printer drivers from the CD. Maybe I just got a lemon this time.  Still think I would give Lexmark another chance in the future.
Office_Products.summary: Disappointed with Lexmark on this one.

Office_Products.reviewText: I'm actually going out of my way to write this review for some cheap pens, in the face of all of these positive comments, so that I can put down 2/5 stars here, so I hope you will at least appreciate my earnest review. I am not sure what all of these raving comments are all about and where they are coming from, but from my personal experience, these pens do not measure up to the competition. The ink, when it does run, runs smoothly, I will give it that, but it does not run consistently. You will be writing out a sentence and out of the blue, the ink runs dry on you momentarily. When you are writing in a journal, as I do, and it does this to you mid-sentence, and you are having to try to re-write what you want over and over until the ink starts to flow again, it looks blotchy and uneven on paper. Better then Pentel's EnerGel by 3 more stars would be the simple G2 pens from Pilot. They are available everywhere, and just as affordable. Ink runs much more consistently.  The only reason I bought these Pentel EnerGels was for the violet hue, actually, as that is my favorite color, but the pens are so sub-par that I am ditching these pens altogether. I went out of the way to write this review because I strongly believe in principle that criticisms should be dished out when due.
Office_Products.summary: Better then Pentel's EnerGel by 3 more stars would be ...

Office_Products.reviewText:
This chair is definitely made for an extra large person. For them, it is probably wonderful, except the directions for putting it together are puny, to say the least. My husband is an expert at such things, and he said the directions didn't help him any. The entire directions were just a few lines.
I am 5'2' and weight 115 lbs. My problem with the chair is that I needed a back that would adjust backward and forward. It is confusing because this chair will do that. But, after your lean it backward, it will only adjust forward to where it came from. It will not adjust forward any more than that. For me, that was still leaning back. I needed the chair for my home Internet work and for word processing, not to relax, or lean it back and sleep in.
It would be great for that. Also, the chair seat is 4" longer than an ordinary office chair so the edge of the chair dug into the back of my knee bend.
The seller was no help because he didn't understand my problem, after all, just pull the handle and it will go back to the original position, so it will, indeed, adjust forward. Amazon dealt with it well, which they always do.
Office_Products.summary: The back and forth of it.

Office_Products.reviewText: Seems well made but 2 beefs --- has an annoying blue lights which I could not find described on the website - and its really not aluminum.  Instead its plastic with a piece of aluminum wrap on top of the plastic.  That doesn't bother me as much as the lights do (and I took this in daylight), and the white with the alum cladding looks a little too out there for me (my taste) - see picture for the lights.
Office_Products.summary: Looks well built but not quite as described

Office_Products.reviewText: I'm very disappointed with this stapler.  I use it in a very busy tax office, and this time of the year every minute equals $$.  More than half the time I use this stapler, the staple itself ends up a bent mess that doesn't make it through even 10 sheets, and I have to pull it back out with a staple remover.  If the stapler is laying flat on the desk, it works better than if I hold it in my hand and attempt to staple sheets together.  9 time out of 10 when I try that, it is a disaster.  I would return it, but don't even have the time right now to package it back up for mailing.  I'll definitely NOT be buying this brand again.
Office_Products.summary: BIG DISAPPOINTMENT

Musical_Instruments.reviewText:
The Tascam DR-07 might not be a big boy in the world of digital recorders, but the audio quality is amazing.  I use it mainly for recording voice, but a trip outside with all the noises of the city yielded great results.  However, not all is perfect.

The case is made of plastic, which the recorder picks up much too well.  Using a external microphone solves that, but what use are the built-in mics if you can't use them without picking up case noise.  I've learned to use the DR-07 without it making much noise.

Unless you live in a region where wind doesn't exist, using the included wind screen is necessary to make recordings, even while speaking in a room (if you like to speak close to the microphone).

really good start up guitar. got it for my girlfriend for chirstmas. she loves it. she also has fairly small hands. she can't do bar chords yet, but i think its possible.
really good guitar for what its worth.
it takes a while for the strings to stretch to stay in tune, which is understandable for any new guitar strings placed on.
had a wierd industrial smell when it was opened im guessing from the staining process.

overall, id recommend this to anyone just starting out.

I like the ability to "dial in" the exact tempo. I like being able to subdivide a measure. I like the sound, and I like the size. It gives enough volume for working with my practice pad and/or snare. I like it. Some things that would improve it?

1) I REALLY wish the line out was stereo. It's not mentioned anywhere, so I contacted Korg. "It this a mono output? Seems a little dated to me." They confirmed to me is was mono, "like most other metronomes." I would prefer stereo so when I used headphones, I'd get the click in both ears. I supposed if you're running a mono mixing board for a band, and want to feed a click to the monitors or something, it's fine. But if you intend to use it with 'phones, get a 1/8" mono plug to stereo jack adapter.
2) The wheel IS difficult to manipulate, but it's not a huge deal.
3) The sounds aren't all that pleasing. I was hoping for a shaker sound. Instead, I just leave it on the default.
Musical_Instruments.summary: I like the ability to "dial in" the exact tempo

Musical_Instruments.reviewText: I bought a single B212A several years ago to use as a powered monitor with a small single amp Yamaha powered mixer.  I used it for solo and duo acoustic performances and the Behringer powered speaker probably had more power and better sound than the PA I was using. I now find myself wishing I had two of these so I could ditch the powered mixer and just go with a small, unpowered, Behringer 4 channel mixer.  I'm pretty sure that would make for a rock solid small PA.  Pros - Crystal clear amp, great sound and lots of power.  Cons - Its a heavy beast for its size.  Also, you can't daisy chain two of these together or use the amp to power other speakers and you can't use without the power on.  I've had extremely good luck with behringer equipment over the past 10 years.  I know some think its second rate but I've got no complaints.  Hope this helps you.  Rock on!
Musical_Instruments.summary: Lot of power in a medium sized package

Musical_Instruments.reviewText:
Just got this in, played it once and love it so far with its bright sound, smooth decay; the perfect addition. Wuhan's are all handmade and you do gamble somewhat with the results, based on their customization. However, the ones I have (ride, crash, HH and now the splash) have been impressive, especially considering their price. The HH are a bit tinty and will need replacing, but I look forward to getting the 8" splash and 14" China Crash next.

Peace,

Seems like a pretty solid little guitar. Construction is sturdy. It doesn't feel thrown together. It actually looks and sounds like a beginner's guitar. Comes with little guides you can slot into the fret board to help learn basic chords. It also comes with an extra set of strings. A strap and a pick would have been a nice addition and wouldn't have added to the overall cost that much, but really, not a bad deal.

Bought these for Karaoke and small family gatherings.  Connected to a small amp and they work just fine.  Rated only 4 stars because I don't know how long they will last.  The system is easy to set up and provides nice clean sound.  Voice comes through clear without any noticeable distortion.  This is a great system for the price as I use these only on occasion.  Thus, I could not justify a big investment in this type of equipment and the Pyle system provides good quality, excellent value and function.  These worked out great for my purposes.

My 10 year old has been playing trumpet for two years now. The first year, we rented one, but last year we decided he was responsible enough to use my Dad's. The case was old though, and we worried it would get destroyed in an Elementary School environment, so we decided to get one that could get knocked around a little and not worry about. After a school year, it still looks great and the trumpet does too :-).Never popped open and my son never complained about it being to heavy, or about any other aspects. The only thing that could make it a little better would be an internal compartment for valve oil/slide grease, but they fit inside OK loose.
Musical_Instruments.summary: Good case for Elementary School child

Musical_Instruments.reviewText: The tuner itself is fine.  It appears to be accurate and the metronome function is handy.  It is large, though.  However, the clip on contact mic is practically useless for clipping on the headstock of a guitar and I don't want to clip to the sound hole as it could mar the finish of the rosette..  The wire that connects it to the tuner is waaaaaay too short.  Buy the tuner without the contact mic and then buy a contact mic separately with a long enough cord.
Musical_Instruments.summary: The tuner itself is fine. It appears to be accurate and the metronome ...

style.Style:: Manhasset M48 Symphony Music Stand AC48S

Musical_Instruments.reviewText: A good solid stand with a good base. It works well and I have a sizable ring binder that I use to hold my music and this stand holds it just fine. I originally had a concern that the adjustable height would slip under heavy weight since it does not have any type of adjustment for clamping the post. It has enough resistance to adjust the height up and down and so far, no issues even with my heavy binder. Not sure if these loosen up over time but time will tell.

The guitar it's self is awesome and well worth the price of the whole package.

Don't count on the extras on the other hand. The video is done by a right handed guitar player so you have to do the exact opposite of everything he does and for a new guitar player he moves incredibly fast. The tuner is a whistle which an experienced guitar player might be able to use, but is practically useless for a first time player. I would recommend buying an electronic one. The bag doesn't look very good. It will protect your guitar from scratches but not from bigger things. If you're not picky about color and size the picks are fine, the strap is also fine.

As to the guitar. There are several youtube videos of people playing this guitar. I feel that none of these reflect the beautiful sound this guitar is capable of making. It is a beautiful guitar with a beautiful sound. I've seen guitars like it sell for twice as much. The price is great even without the extras.

Would I buy this guitar again? Yes! Every time!
Musical_Instruments.summary: The guitar is great! Everything else not so much...

Musical_Instruments.reviewText:
Okay, first things first:
This kit includes everything shown (INCLUDING CYMBALS)

Includes: frame, snare pad (dual zone for rimshots), 3 tom pads, 3 cymbals, hardware for mounting everything, module, kick pedal, kick drum, hi-hat pedal (module has different sensors for open/closed hi-hat so both register), even drum sticks, all cables needed to hook up the kit.

Not included: Throne, cables to hook into a speaker/PA/amp, etc. (but those usually come with your amp anyway).
THAT'S IT. Everything you need to actually get sound out of all the components is there.

That's the main reason I would rate this kit high.
Most other kits I looked at prior to purchase wouldn't correctly advertise if it includes cymbals or not. HUGE ISSUE, but have no fear for this kit.

Okay about the product:
Haven't gotten to play it much since the Holidays just passed, but the sound is nice. Customization of the kit sounds, recording, trial to some software... (All this is is the product specs I think.)
Got to play it more since (*This is an update*) then and things work well in general. See the cons for the bad stuff.

All in all, a good product. Probably not the best you can get but for the price, a good entry level kit and you can get some good use from it before you move to a more expansive kit.
I'd recommend this kit to anyone who is beginning or has more use for an electric kit than an acoustic kit. If you're more experienced, I'd say this would work, but I know I'd like something more high-end.

Some cons:
FIRMWARE ISSUE. Easy patch if you google the kit and firmware update. All you need is to unzip the folder and have a cable to connect the module to your computer. (This is the reason why I'd rate it 4 stars.)

So far, I have had my kit a bit off balance, but I'm sure I can get it adjusted the more I play it. Just haven't gotten that far yet. Careful you don't tip the kit and break something (I don't think this is really a problem with all kits, but I'm letting you know that it's possible for it to want to tip over)
Its difficult to keep balanced sometimes because the frame is loose on mine. I figure I can tighten the frame a bit. But I'll probably just strip the screws in the plastic mounters. So try adjusting the feet position a bit.

That's about it. Hope this was helpful for you.

I got this for using on my sitar, I had no idea if it would work at all. But! Am I glad I did, because it works perfectly on my Sitar and also my acoustic guitars!

I use it on my sitar so I can hook it up through an effects pedal, and that is just such great fun.

I highly recommend it if you are on a tight budget like I am.

Con: The only this that I am not greatly satisfied with is the suction cup stick on, It holds good almost all the time but if I where to play live I would have to tape it on, would much rather have  had a Velcro fastener for live applications.

But for use at home it is excellent!

I am disabled so lifting heavy powered speakers over my head is a major problem. These stands, though a bit hefty in weight are a relief for me. I simply set the legs and then drop the speaker onto the top of it, loosen the lock knob and then pull the retractable release and they go up effortlessly.

However, taking them back down takes a bit of care. The retractable release/lock is fixed on the stands upright arm. The holes in the shaft holding the speaker is NOT indexed to stay in one position. It easily turns when you rotate the speaker. When it does you can not lower the speaker and easily lock it in the down position as the holes do not line up with the locking mechanism. If the shaft holding the speaker was indexed to prevent it from turning with the speaker I would gladly give this a 5 star rating.

Just got it today, haven't used it in performance yet, but I tried it out with my mute collection.
