Video_Games.summary: One Of The More P.O.ing Games Of This Year

Video_Games.reviewText:
Has some improvements over the original EQ, but falls short in the story and plot dept. One of the nice things in EQ 1 was that each race and class were unique from the beginning. Each race started in its own city, which fit that race. Dark elves in an underground city, were no non-evil visitors were allowed. Halflings in their shire-like setting. Wood elves in their treehouses, etc. Each class got its own abilities and spells from the beginning. Each race and class felt unique.

Now, everyone starts in one of two cities, depending on their alignment. Everyone starts as the same class, specializing as they go along. The game has lost a lot of its magic because of that.

And why did SOE have to rehash the EQ1 story? The game is not different enough to warrant a brand new release. Couldn't they come up with a better, different story line?

Also, forget about going solo. First, you gain experience MUCH faster if you are in a group. In addition, you can't really do anything in the dungeons unless you are grouped. Grouping is fine, but sometimes you just want to go around on your own. Also, there are certain things in the game that you cannot do unless you are in a guild. This game is not designed for the lone adventurer.

Another problem: You have to be logged in and in your room if you want to sell your items through the player merchant system. Now, since you can't do anything in your room, you can't play the game while you are selling.

EQ 2 is a simplified version of EQ 1. While it addresses some of EQ 1's problems, it seems to have lost something in the process.

Where to begin...

I've been playing EA's Fifa series for 10 years on various platforms/consoles(PC, Playstation, Xbox, Xbox 360), and I am always at the store the day the game comes out. I purchased Fifa 07 for Xbox when it came out, and I loved it. I thought the manager mode had some great touches, and the game was just a fun soccer game. But, that's a different review entirely. As for Fifa 07 on Xbox 360:

Positives:

Corner kicks. I like the fact that the players no longer just stand stationary in the box until the ball is played in. Anyone who has ever played the game in real life knows that you don't just stand around hoping the ball hits you on the head. You move to get open. EA finally added some life into the offense in this regard.

Commentary is very good. I like the random side conversations, and the nice references to particular players. I play with Newcastle, and it's cool to hear them mention Owen's WC injury, etc.

Personally, I think the graphics look pretty good. Some of the players are way off as far as looks go, but during the gameplay, the game looks great. That's pretty much where I end my positives.

Oh, and I do enjoy being able to kick the ball around with Ronaldinho during the game load. It's nice to have something better to do during load times. Unfortunately, there are no moves, so it does get old pretty quickly.

Negatives:

Player creation lost some of it's fun. First of all, you can't turn your player when you are creating physical attributes. You can't turn the head to get an accurate depiction of what the player looks like. This isn't important to some people, but I enjoy creating a team of my friends, and it's fun when the people look fairly similar to their real-life counterparts. Also, you can't stack a player's skills. This is good and bad. The main issue I have is that you can't create a real phenom player that you can use as a future backbone of a team. I haven't played enough to see how long it takes to get a player up to a Ronaldinho level of skill, but I can't imagine it being possible with the talent attribute system that EA used this time around.

The  interface is horrid...I repeat...horrid. As an interface designer myself, I can't believe this game got away with this. I noticed that all of the EA games are using this new horizontal expansion menu, but it's garbage. Go back to using the simple stuff...please. Some of the stuff that I was looking for is so deep and annoying to get to, that it makes me not even want to complete certain tasks. Player creation took so long that I made one player, and didn't feel like going through the process again. The fonts are hard to read (granted, I don't have a huge HDTV), and the black is heavy and sets a very drab tone for the game. The regular Xbox version is so much nicer to look at.

Game play leaves a lot to be desired. Is it just me, or does the computer try to dribble non-stop? I can't even get the ball half of the time. It takes a double or triple-team approach to disrupt the computer's player on the dribble. Annoying.

Then there's the obvious lack of trick moves. How do you make a game this involved, a game that strives for realism, and leave out a major aspect of the game. The worst part seems to be this: EA made the defense easier to dribble around instead of adding trick moves. Very lame, and very frustrating, as it's hard to defend the dribble as well (mentioned previously).

The amazing offering of teams and players!!! Okay, okay, you know that's sarcasm. 6 leagues? What? Seriously? If I'm lucky enough to get to the "ECC" or "EFA", I can't wait to see the teams in the tournament(s). I guess you go straight to the group games even if you finish in 4th in the Premiership. Looking forward to that! Ha.

With all of that said, I will continue to play this game and hope that they improve some of the gameplay issues via updates, but I'm still highly bummed about this offering, and I'm so tempted to just go back to Fifa 07 on Xbox, because I had a lot of fun playing that...and thankfully, I didn't trade it in.

THE SHORT: Improved and deeper character distinction, better socializing, town "aging", and no loading between lots make this a funner, more "alive" Sims game. But items and options have obviously been left out for you to have to buy from the EA website later, no ultra speed means sleeping and working (in-game) will leave you with nothing to do for 5-10 straight minutes, and worst of all, the game crashes. I mean, for pretty much everybody who plays it.

THE LONG: A pre-release copy of the game made it online, but it was buggy and those who played it wondered if it was unfinished. EA themselves confirmed that the leaked copy was a "beta", in other words incomplete, and was prone to crashing. I played this early copy and was satisfied with what I saw, so I awaited the retail release for a full, great game.

I bought it and was shocked to see that apparently EA was lying to curb piracy: The official release is the same as the pre-release one they had been calling buggy and unfinished. They simply released a buggy game. As I write this, it's the game's first week of release and with 200 reviews it has a 2 and a half star score. I feel this is accurate. The fun of the game is brought down by the fact that it literally feels unfinished.

First, the game itself. The concept with this entry in the series seems to be an emphasis on deeper characterization. Now when you play a family, the neighborhood around you is "turned on" at the same time. This means that while you play your character, the other houses in the neighborhood are still aging, having relationships, and so on. Time moves for the whole neighborhood now, not just you. Of course you're supposed to be able to turn this off but that doesn't work, which I'll address later. Personally I love this feature- it will keep your game fresh as new faces and families will come and go furthering the random aspect of the game. I can see where there are problems as well- you don't want to lose a family you made because you're playing as a secondary one, for example.

Pretty much every item can be color customized to your liking. You can make the mailbox outside your Sims' house bright yellow and purple if you so desire. This works for clothes, the house, your character's hair, almost everything. It's nice to finally, after 9 years of Simming, be able to color things how we want instead of having the same few choices for the best, most need-fulfilling objects. While it's easy to the point of boring to be able to coat your walls with the same cheapest, plainest wallpaper and then color it however you want, it's nice to have the option. The color customization is a handy feature and runs very deep- you can choose not only the style (metallic, wooden, etc.) but also choose individual parts like the fridge handle in addition to the fridge itself.

But this concept brings up my first big complaint with this game. When we saw that pre-release game leak, we dismissed the lack of items as something they'd fix in the retail release. Not so. Perhaps due to this color customization feature, they have greatly reduced the number of items you can choose from in some categories. While it doesn't matter much to only have a few couches or whatever, it's inexcusable to have as few as about a dozen hairstyles to pick from. I haven't checked the females yet, but when I made my male character, I was upset with the very limited hairstyle set. Let's put it this way- I always make myself in every Sims game, and this is the first one where I wasn't able to make a character that looked a whole lot like me, with hair being a big reason. They still have a relatively similar slider system to adjust size and angle for mouths, eyes, etc. You can now also adjust body shape. But the fact that there are fewer choices than before is just a letdown. Some reviewers have complained that the characters look plastic and out of proportion, but I didn't think so myself.

A feature of create-a-sim that I really dig is the new personality system. Instead of giving points between extremes like "messy" and "neat", you now get several slots to permanently choose from 50 or 60 "traits" such as messy, evil, dislikes children, couch potato, etc. This makes characters more unique and affects them more noticeably than the other games. For example adding a cooking trait to your Sim will make him happier with a chef's career and faster at gaining points in the cooking skill. A hydrophobic Sim will never get in the water by herself and get negative moodlets when you force her to. It's a feature you can ignore- just add the common traits of "neat, friendly, lazy", etc. if you want. But if you want to never have the same kind of Sim twice, this feature will really come in handy and give you much to explore.

Now the neighborhood- the game comes with one, and there's a second one you can get from the EA website if you want to pay, which I think is a problem that speaks for itself. Anyway It contains around a dozen families already and EASILY room for dozens more. There are several "community lots" as well- scroll around the map and you'll see a military base, arena, central park, and small businesses. One of the nicest things in this game is that now everything is part of just one giant landscape. Going anywhere in the game takes no loading or seperate screens. Say you want your character to go from her house to the grocery store across town. Just go to the map, which zooms out really far instead of changing to a different screen or menu. Every place has an icon in this view. Click one, tell your Sim to go there, and out they go. Watch them go there from far above or zoom back in and watch as they get a quick car ride to the location you chose. In the map view you can even choose a lot to edit, and hovering over a location tells you info like who's home, where they are, where you work, and so on. Pretty useful.

You can even just make your Sim walk the whole way there. No more hitting an invisible barrier at the end of your property. Walk your Sim across the street to ring the neighbor's doorbell or walk them through the hills and forests to the ocean on the other side of town. No loading screens. You'll even see other Sims walking around, going about their day the same as you. This is an awesome, much-needed feature that brings a real sense of life to the Sims. They seem to have done well with the game engine as well- I've seen as many as 14 other characters walking around on my screen at once with no performance hit, and I play on a capable but not notably powerful laptop.

Other new features are things like "moodlets" which are indicators of how your Sim is feeling. Cook good food for example, and your Sim will get a moodlet that shows he'll be 40 points happier for the next afternoon because of the tasty meal. Neglect cleaning the dishes, and the dirtiness will lower your Sim's happiness 10 points until you do something about it. The new feature is quick to understand and if you don't like it, don't pay attention to it- the classic green/yellow/red needs meter is still there. There are a couple less needs, and now you only have to go to the bathroom only a couple times a day. Slightly more emphasis has been placed on interacting and exploring your character and your neighborhood than maintaining needs, though you still have to do so.

Socializing, or rather getting to know people, is funner than ever. Gossiping will now tell you specific info such as who's mad at who or who is rich. If a sim is romantically involved they'll tell you who it's with. And as you learn a sim's traits, the game keeps track of them. Find out that someone is flirty for example, and that statistic is filled in on their profile. Getting to know sims is now less generic and more personalized. Instead of chatting repeatedly to fill a bar next to another face in the relationship menu, you now have reason to actually get to know the character more deeply because their personalities and status in life will be kept track of for you. It's fun to discover new things about new characters. And now, talking with people is easier as well because the game tells you what the character is thinking about the conversation.

Going to work is now more involved as well. You can choose whether you want to work extra hard or suck up to the boss and so on with occasional repercussions and benefits. You'll get career opportunities as well- as a chef, you can be invited to have a cookout at the park or enter a cooking contest among many other possibilities. The PROBLEM I have with jobs is one of the biggest problems I have with the game- the speed system.

The speed system SUCKS. At regular speed, it's fine. At double speed, it's okay for briefly skipping through showers or paying the bills. But in what I can only believe is a massive bug, there is no third speed option. It's there, click it if you want. But it does nothing. What this means is that when your character sleeps or goes to work, you get to walk around your own real-life house for a good five minutes because that's how long it's going to take for your Sims to be done. This is a major irritation that will get old fast, and while it's true that you can use this time to go play another family, you shouldn't have to. So, uh, patch then, EA?

Another bug is the aforementioned lack of ability to stop town aging. If you don't want the rest of the neighborhood to age and have kids while you play, too bad- like ultra speed, clicking that option does nothing. If I had the choice, I myself prefer having the neighborhood evolve and change. But not everybody agrees, and it's realistic to expect the option to, well, WORK.

But the biggest issue I have with the game is by far its instability. It crashes, and crashes hard- shutting down my computer at least once almost every time I play for a half hour or more. This has seemed to happen to me most while my character is doing the long, slow task of sleeping, so that's 5 minutes of sitting vulnerable (though the crashes could be random, who knows). Moving the mouse around and doing things in-game seemed to curb this a bit, but nothing works regularly. I panicked, thinking something was wrong with my system, but lo and behold, minimal research reveals that people with system specs that blow Sims 3 away suffer the crashing too. No one seems to be exempt and no cure has yet been found. Your game will probably crash, so take my advice and save often, and make a copy of the Sims 3 save folder every so often. This kind of crap doesn't ruin the game for me, but it haunts play with anxiety. To have to live with a game crashing and possibly shutting off your system every time is utterly inexcusable and potentially dangerous.

So there you go. The game has even more features I haven't tapped into- subtle things like fishing, the wish system, hidden rewards and skills, and more- like the Sims 2, it's my opinion that the game was not greatly revolutionized but pleasantly updated to feel more natural, deep, and fun to play. Personally, I love the game myself. The average score of 3 that I give it is due to the couple massive bugs and the greedily shrewd nature of withholding basic things so they can charge you for them after you've already bought the game. If these concerns are addressed and fixed, the game would get a 5 from me. As it stands, it's a fun game that has to played with patience and frustration, and will hopefully be fixed so it can live up to its high potential.
Video_Games.summary: A great and deeper Sims experience with some welcome additions but also some extremely frustrating bugs.

Video_Games.reviewText:
Initially these worked great, however, the charge they held gradually diminished to nothing.  A year later they won't recharge or hold a charge anymore.  I tried to see if I could get replacement batteries from Dreamgear, but they don't sell them.  It's useless now.  (For what it's worth, I always tried to discharge the batteries fully and recharge fully and didn't let the kids trash them, to no avail)

The induction charging feature is a big plus though.  You can simply lay the controller (even with the silicon covers on) or just the batteries themselves.  I've since purchased the Nyko model and was very frustrated by how clumsy it was to mount.  No such problems with this model.

I would give this product 4 or 5 stars if it were possible to buy replacement batteries, as it stands, this is a throwaway once the batteries burn out.

As a high end PC gamer I sometimes like to catch up on games I missed at launch in the sales, NFS The Run is a typical example of a game not worth the RRP but is certainly worth the price in a sale. The game is pretty fun but at the time time can be very infuriating as some of the stages in the run mode are deliberately geared up with AI that cheats to win even when it would seem out of the race the named rival characters can zoom in to lead when they had no means to do so. That said I played the game for a few days to completion and the multiplayer modes seem quite varied. One word of advice though, even though the game supports using wheels, joypads are better, as the dashboard cam view makes the game look pretty low rez compared to outside cam default. I was playing the game at 90-120fps in Ultra settings @1080p while playing this, and noticed Vsync on locks the game to just 30fps, so best to play Vsync off guys. [...]

I bought this package more as a joke for myself because I knew how uh... great... it was going to be.

No, these are not top notch games, and if you are looking for those this pack is not for you. They are extremely glitchy and vague and the physics are wonky, but if you're a internet conossieur like myself and like things for the shock value then buying 20 games for such a cheap price is totally worth it.

There is a reason "simulator games" are revered by YouTube. You will have the time of your life when your vehicles suddenly turn upside down or people and animals start rotating on their axis at top speed for no reason. Or when your car gets hit by something else and manages to re-balance itself with no problem as if held by a buoy. Or maybe you load up the game and end up helplessly falling into a void and have to restart. All of this with a complete lack of instructions in most games, so it's one big adventure (and learning curve). It's wonderful!

It is a pretty small size for any computer. If you have problems with performance you can adjust the settings in the games themselves and it usually fixes everything. Also if you have Windows 10 you have to manually select the disc  in My Computer and install the programs one by one in their corresponding folders.

All in all it depends on what you want this game for. But it can be fun when you try to play it seriously as well.

... but Requital, while making a decent showing on several fronts, also shows they still have a fair way to go. On the plus side, the hidden-object portions are pleasantly rational. You're not just picking up the usual random junk from someone's storage room but in each case assembling a discrete set of objects for a particular task. The designers do a similarly nice job of tracking the player's tasks, location and a fairly ornate story. On the other hand, it's very short -- a determined player could finish it inside three hours -- and has very little replay value. (The major puzzles are rejiggered with each game, but the objects can always be found in the same locations.) The game ends with unseemly haste. Under Windows 7, a couple of features appear to break (including the tutorial). And some of the character artwork is, well, odd. The cop looks like a monster (and moves like a robot) and the male protagonist sometimes appears to have breasts -- as though the character's gender was changed in the late going.
Video_Games.summary: I'm glad to see hidden-object games are becoming more like rudimentary adventures, but ...

Video_Games.reviewText:
Capcom's Dead Rising is an amazing game.  Amazing in the fact there's incredible possibilities.  The concept is highly original and engaging - but there's a problem!  Capcom didn't "go the extra mile" if you will.  Don't get the wrong idea, the game is very detailed; my only complaint relates to the game-play (or lack thereof).  In a realm of endless potential (the game's concept), I feel Dead Rising could have been so much more.  Regardless of my high standard, Dead Rising still ends on a solid note, and therefore, I'd suggest it's worthy of its price tag.

The graphics are first-rate, no question.  The controls are a little sloppy, but when you're engaged in an environment of slaying zombies doggedly, you really can't complain.  The game is challenging and frustrating at times.  When you're attempting to rescue a survivor, it's almost impossible to get them back to "base" without them being ripped apart.  The storyline is the wildcard.  The compelling plot increases the value of the game.  Not to mention, there's creative and witty humor along the way (remember the crazy clown?).

Bottom line - there's other XBox 360 titles that outshine Dead Rising.  However, your system wouldn't be complete without your very own copy!  You could rent Dead Rising and defeat this monster in a few days if you play 24 / 7.  You'd still miss the side missions, which account for much of the game's longevity.  Completing the side missions is the challenging part of Dead Rising; and it's the only way you're going to get full value from playing it.  In other words - buy the damn thing.

Look, if you love Dead Space, have dedicated your life to the game and think its the best thing since antibiotics, then I apologize for the coming blasphemy.  I liked so many aspects about this game but overall it just didn't resonate with me.  Here's why:

I love the horror/survival horror/action genre, so I came into it with positive expectations.  This had Ridley Scott's "Aliens" movie written all over it.  I was psyched.

Graphically, the game is pretty amazing, possibly one of the best looking games out there in the space-genre.  The atomosphere of Dead Space is remarkable, I've give you that.  They really captured the scale and isolation of space, and will positively creep you out with the strobe-lit rooms with random blood spatter.  There is much detail here, but I appreciate all the effort in that.

Audio-wise, I think this may be one of the most effective uses of surround I've seen so far in a game.  Its so damn eerie at times, I muted the volume.  Random screams, metal grinding and breaking free, whispers (or are they?), things crawling through duct work, out of sight...this game does "ambient" better than some games do their main audio.  Its almost as scary when things ARENT jumping out at you as when they are, and Dead Space uses that Hollywood scare tactic a lot.  A whole lot.

I like many aspects, zero-gravity, the work stations, even the weapons were ok, but why 3 stars for fun?  Because I played several sections into the game and realized not only how massive the amount of time it was going to take to solve it, but also how I was going to be repeating so many tasks so many times, and then backtracking through all the areas I previously passed through, like some kind of masochistic scavenger hunt.  I can take this for a while, but not for an entire game the size of Dead Space.  Even the cool new areas and details weren't enough pay-off to make me want to spend the kind of hours I was going to need on this one.

Its an interesting lesson for game developers:  beauty, atomosphere, storyline may not be enough to make a game "5-Star" fun if it requires a lot of repetitive work.  Many, looking at the ratings, feel differently, but I was surprised enough by this to want to write a "second-opinion" review for those who haven't yet played it.  You may love it, buy the animated DVD and the comics and pledged your life to it, but you may not, so before you buy, you may want to try (rent).

The product does live up to its capabilities yet it does not have such a fastened grip to the xbox one when plugged in. The hub has to be placed correctly or else it'll slip right off eventually causing it to break. The LED light isn't much of a nuisance to me but the way it's designed was not actually ment to be locked in tightly. Even when the hub is plugged in correctly, it's still not leveled with the xbox one if you place the it on a flat surface like on a coffee table or desk.

For story mode..1 player..i enjoyed the game..over all its a great zombie game...BUT..i do have a few negatives....first thing that stands out is the last boards, it seems like valve had 1 idea for the final of every chapter...hold the fort while tons of zombies attack while you wait 10 to 15 minutes to be saved by someone..that got alittle boring by the third time around. The pipe bombs and malatov cocktails i pretty much never used,it always seemed like the only time you need to use it would be when the hulk zombie (tank) comes running at you. 3rd would be the short boards..they seemed so short...15 to 20 mintues..you can beat the game in a few hours...although the replay value is high...i still felt like i was getting jipped..i know the games they make these days are for on and offline play..i thought the single player lacked a bit...the game is fun and i couldn't stop playing...but there seems to be something missing..no cut scenes..no great occurences that happened that i will take with me when i move on to the next game...nothing memorable except tons of zombies running at you...the game also is not scary..no spookyness to it...this game could have been way better(the 1 player story mode anyway)..but it still had me in zombie heaven...great animations when you shoot them, good graphics..old school zombie flick music that was perfect...good zombie game that could have been better.

"Front End" Addendum: GUNNAR Optiks is aware that the plastic used for the frames of the original Intercept glasses breaks easily, so they have switched to a (hopefully) more resilient plastic. GUNNAR customer service bent over backwards to make things right. Thanks, GUNNAR!

________________

The glasses do help with eye fatigue, but the original onyx frames are made from extremely poor materials. I am very careful with anything that costs as much as these glasses, but I've gone through two pairs in about two years. The frames broke in the exact same spot both times, at the juncture where the top of the frames meets the nose piece. This would seem to indicate a structural weakness as well as brittle, breakable plastic.

The current pair broke either while they were on my face or while I was removing them!

The lenses smudge easily, but I did what someone recommended upthread and bought some pre-moistened Zeiss Lens Cleaning Wipes. They clean the lenses better than anything else I've tried. I'm using them on my current Intercept glasses (temporarily "fixed" with duct tape) while I wait for the upgrade GUNNAR so graciously offered to me. I guess I'll be reviewing the MLG Phantom glasses within the next month or so. :)

The Intercept model does not play well with my Steelseries Siberia V2 headset. They are uncomfortable to the point of being painful.
Video_Games.summary: They do help with eye fatigue, but there are some drawbacks.

Video_Games.reviewText:
When I first seen this mouse, I thought it would go well with my Alienware desktop.  I also like the interchangeable sides with custom weights. The things I didn't like about the mouse are that there is no grips on either side of the mouse.  When playing FPS or any game for that matter that requires a quick lift of the mouse, your hand will slip or you will grip so tight that you click the buttons on the side.  If you use the claw for your mouse position, do not get this mouse ( to clarify, I do not use claw, but I attempted on this mouse and  it doesn't work.  Another thing wrong with this mouse is that the left mouse button creates a lip of the 6 button side plate in a manner that makes it very difficult to push the button that sits directly under that left mouse button. The other 5 buttons are pretty easy to press.  your hand has to be in a slant to push the most forward buttons as well.  The design is flawed a little.  I might hold onto this mouse or I may return it.  I will decide over the next few days.
My word of advice to Alienware is redesign the six button side plate to bring the buttons back a quarter inch and down a few cm. as well as get rid of the lip that the top mouse buttons create.  The last change would be to never make a mouse without grips.  Probably your biggest design flaw!
Video_Games.summary: I also like the interchangeable sides with custom weights

Video_Games.reviewText: First of all let me say that I am a 2d game aficionado. I have collections of 2d games that I cherish.  This game I had high hopes for, but it is really an adventure game disguised as a platformer.  Most platform games do not have you looking for objects in order to open up other levels.  I enjoyed the platforming aspects, but I hate that if I finished a level and did not pick up a hidden treasure, I had to go back in the level to find the object.  I am still waiting to get a new Super Mario Bros for the Wii.  I really enjoyed the one on the DS.

The second complilation of Sonic games, the other being the Mega Collection, this one offers the 3 classics that the other missed: Sonic CD, Sonic R and Sonic the Fighters.  Let me say this now:  Sonic R and Sonic the Fighters are crap.  I've beaten R in less than an hour, with all hidden characters and Chaos Emeralds, each track taking me no more or less than two attempts:  One for the hidden character, one for the Emeralds.

The Game Gear games can be unlocked in Sonic Adventure: DX, so if you're getting this for those, it's much more fun to get them in Sonic Adventure, which is still a fun game, though a bit dated (but if you're getting this collection, you shouldn't be complaining about 'dated').  Sonic CD is definitelly a fun romp.  I still haven't beaten it, I'm sorry to admit.  The other games you unlock are fun as well...  But you have to unlock them.  Sorry, I can't recommend this game PURELY for Sonic CD, which is what rides the 'Fun' rating of this game.  Hardcore Sonic fans ONLY need apply.  And even *I* have seen the light and have tried other ways of feeling nostalgic for the old days.
Video_Games.summary: Its fun, but nothing we haven't seen before

Video_Games.reviewText:
I started off thinking this was going to be a great game.  The graphics are great.  The story line seems pretty good.
But.
The game is pretty much the same thing over and over and over just repackaged slightly.  As you go up in strength, the creatures you fight get correspondingly harder.  You add some more players but after the first extra player, the strategies stay pretty much the same the rest of the way.  It's just as hard to get through the first few screens as it is to get through screens much further down the line.  (Except for the "Boss" screens, some of which are pretty damn nasty.)
And when I say "further down the line", I mean line.  This game isn't like Morrowind where you can pretty much go wherever you want and do what you what.  You are locked into a world with very few options except for the occasional semi-hidden sidetrack.
There is no roleplaying in this game.  Character development is just about gathering up as much stuff as you can get.  And after you've got a gazillion dollars, what's the point?
There are a ton of other games I'd prefer to play.
Watson Davis
Video_Games.summary: You Vill Go Vere Ve Vant

I wish I could give this 0 stars. This by far the worst video game I have ever played. It is completely unrealistic to the point it is unplayable. Passing is horrendous. Half of my passes do not go to the player I had intended, thus leading to turnovers. I can't count the number of times I have tried to make a short pass while brining the ball up the court, but instead, it throws a full court pass out-of-bounds. There was one time where I wanted to pass it to a player cutting to the basket, but instead it passed it to a guy standing out-of-bounds.  In another case, I was running a set play, and when it prompted me to press X to pass to the guy coming off the screen for the three, I hit X, and it throw down low and was intercepted. The defense is also terrible. My defense can never find the guy the are supposed to guard, leading to wide open three's for the opponent. Also, on screens, my defenders get so confused on who they are supposed to guard. Sometimes they switch, other times they don't. Good luck guessing what they will do! Finally, it is impossible to make a contested shot (unless you are Curry).  You have to have at least 5 feet of space to make anything.  Even a perfectly timed release won't help you make it. Oh and by the way, good luck driving with anyone. The AI defense won't let you get by. (Even if you are Westbrook)

Video_Games.reviewText:
This isn't a Silent Hill game. Everything that made the original's(1-4) great i.e. 1. Original, meaningful monsters. 2. Great atmosphere. 3. Survival horror. 4. Good story. And 5. Horror! Just aren't here.
Most of the monster's are reused from Silent Hill 2. They were supposed to be based on James own person demons. So it didn't make any sense and was just lazy to have them in Homecoming. Only the boss fights had any meaning. But most of the game your fighting James's demons.
The atmosphere is too dark and dull. It seems like they where trying to make the game scarier by making it so dark that you can't see but it doesn't work.
This game is way to combat-oriented for a survival horror game. It has this awful up and close combat system that wants you to fight almost every enemy. The older game wanted you to try to escape the enemy's. This one you can't even run! This isn't a survival horror game, its a really bad action horror game.
 The story tries to hard to be like the movie. In the original most of the cult members were dead. It makes no sense for them to be alive, why would Silent Hill let the other cult live?
Almost all the scares are predictable jump scares.
The only good thing I can say about this game is the soundtrack is amazing, and there were a few good boss fights.
Homecoming is not a Silent Hill game. It contradicts all the elements of the good Silent Hills. If you want a boring, action horror game, Homecoming delivers But if you want a Silent Hill game play 1-4.

Sometimes, I wonder how certain ideas and concepts for games come to reality. I mean, who would ever say "Hey, you know what the public needs? A one-on-one fighting game on Game Boy Color featuring Shrek characters"? Somehow, that's not the craziest thing the fictional ogre has been involved with, but Shrek: Fairy Tale Freakdown is an absolute bust anyway.

The sprites are super-small, and the fights don't last at all, meaning you can plow through this thing in a dozen minutes or less, counting the times you would lose to the opponent. Even if the length was altered for the better, though, the control is still as wretched as the arcade/NES game, The Legend of Kage. If you jump, you can't move while in the air. And you can only jump straight up, or in awkward diagonal angles. There are supposedly secondary attacks you can use via button combinations, but God knows what could actually activate them. If the control didn't suck enough, certain arenas have holes for you to fall into, which drives the control problems home considering how many times you could accidentally fall into a hole.

You know what fighting game made in 2001 you should be playing or purchasing instead of this? SUPER SMASH BROS. MELEE! After looking at this shovelware, it's hard to even think that it would ever be made in the same year, because this takes the industry back to around twenty years prior!

I love video games and I really like the BOF series, this trash is the exception. This game forces you to lose and start new games over & over & over again, each time while carrying stats over, in order to progress through the story. Aside from already being forced into constant new games, when you use one of your powerful special abilities in a fight, it kills you and your forced to start a new game..... think about that for a minute. This last part is minor compared to the other awful aspects, but the footstep sound effects are very annoying. This is literally the worst RPG I've ever played.

Pros:
Literally none.

Cons:
Everything!

Play any of the other Breath of Fire games instead, especially BOF3 and BOF4. In addition, there are plenty of other amazing PS1 RPG's you can play instead of Dragon Quarter. My favorites are: Legend of Legaia, Legend of Mana, Suikoden 1 & 2, Grandia, Final Fantasy 7, 8, and FF Tactics, Wild Arms, Star Ocean, Guardian's Crusade, Legend of Dragoon, etc.

For the past year my Xbox One has been shut down for the most part, because I simply haven't found anything interesting to do on it.. I regret giving up my Xbox 360 with a decent collection of games (including Kinect-enabled ones) - because there is still a huge gap between the games available for the One and 360. As an example, Limbo debited 3+ years ago on Xbox 360, and it just came out on Xbox One. I enjoyed Fruit Ninja over 2 years ago, and it's still not available for Xbox One!! Such a let-down.

Please explain why they made a new console that won't play Xbox 360 games? That's really stupid, and I have only myself to blame because I trusted Microsoft to port existing games quickly, since they've decided to break compatibility on purpose.

I would also like to point out that Xbox One games/apps are sluggish despite the up-to-date hardware. For example, Xbox Fitness is absolutely painful to use, as it loads a full minute (which feels like an eternity) and all animations and transitions are horribly rough.

Another source of frustration is the dashboard UI. Browsing for games (which I do frequently, hoping to find something interesting) is very confusing?! It's either one flat list of all games, or poorly defined categories with very limited number of titles. And I can't still figure out how to rate and review games/apps...

Finally, the prices for games for purchase on the console (downloadable) are regularly ~2 times higher than same titles on a disc (e.g. Amazon). That's just a shameless rip-off. They are definitely not passing the savings (media/distribution/commissions) on to consumers.
Video_Games.summary: For crying out loud.. Get an Xbox 360 instead!!!

Video_Games.reviewText:
This game has so many problems it's not even funny. First of all, the game is terribly optimized. I have an excellent graphics card yet I have to run the game on medium settings just to navigate the menus without a huge delay. Second, the colors are completely bugged. I can't even play a quick game without the colors going neon green or just totally black. You're also forced to watch the cut-scenes of the MyPlayer mode, which would be fine except that the colors are completely screwed up making it difficult to see anything at all. Not only that, but certain menus are actually not fully displayed on my screen, instead it's as if they're being pulled down into a corner.

Perhaps this game will be decent after they release a patch (or ten patches) but right now, you DEFINITELY should NOT buy it.

I am still in shock that I was so excited for this game to come out only to be so disappointed.  As others have said, a good description of how I felt after a few hours of playing is "heartbroken."  I hadn't been keeping up with any of the development, I just overheard someone saying it was coming out the next day and got excited and bought it.  I expected this game to be a well-refined version of the Sims 3 with more emotions and new hobbies and things to craft.  But this game plays like it was written for a tablet.  I've tried to summarize my experience.

The first thing that disappointed me was CAS.  I realized you have to change the appearance of your Sim by clicking and dragging, which can introduce a lot of variance into what you are trying to do.  The hairstyles don't look as real as they did in the Sims 3.  It is like they are all wearing plastic wigs like the Wiggles.  Then I noticed there are only a few preset colors for the outfits which leaves no room for customization.  Why wouldn't something as simple as a colorpicker be implemented in a large scale simulation game?  Even Microsoft Access has a color picker and it's for databases!  But CAS isn't why I play the Sims so I just kind of grumbled and brushed these things off.  Nothing a few good mods can't fix.

Next, I'm seeing a 2-D image with the outlines of clusters of buildings.  Slightly confused, I picked one of them to buy.  (I didn't find out until later that was actually the map.)  So now I'm feeling a little skeptical, but my house loads up and I start trying to play.  Woohoo!  The first thing I did was try to cook some eggs, but I can't quite see and I can't get the camera angle to move vertical.  It only moves left and right and zooms.  Great.  So my sims are eating eggs and I also can't figure out where the hell the Needs are, or any other info about them.  Instead of everything being in a cluster in the lower left hand corner, things are split on each side of the screen.  This is absolute hell with my Eyefinity setup.  Half of my Sims stats are 6000 pixels in the other direction.  But this isn't the first game to not support Eyefinity so again I keep trying to like what I am experiencing.

After eating I go try running around and came across some harvestables, and some rocks, Awesome!  But I get to some water with fish and the cursor is crossed out.  You have to click on a sign with a fish on it that is on land in front of the jumping fish to make your Sim fish.  Why does there need to be a sign instead of just clicking on the fish?  Then it gets really upsetting.  My camera won't move so I zoom out wondering why can't I scroll past here?  Then it hit me that this was a border so I moved all around the neighborhood and yep it was basically a giant rectangle limiting me to three houses and their yards.  What the hell?  I press 'M' to bring up the map and BAM! the 2D picture with the clusters of buildings.  All the pieces come together.  I click on one that looks like a Park... LOADING SCREEN.  So..  No more jogs down to the library?  No sending my Sim out in the woods on a 3 day fishing trip?  What is the point?  Just to walk around a flat rectangle until I have to pee and shower again?

Then without even thinking, as kind of a reaction you would have to seeing something horrible, I closed it out and went straight to Origin and got a refund.  At the time I couldn't even believe I was actually going to ask for my money back.  But to me it was like opening a box of Monopoly, and only finding Chinese Checkers.  The few little perks, emotions, and the eye candy that this game adds only pale in comparison to the functionality and freedom that has been lost when compared to the Sims 3.

If you are thinking about getting this game, I ENCOURAGE YOU TO DO SO.  Go to Origin right now, buy the Sims 4, and play it.  Then you will see for yourself, and you have a 24 hour window to get your money back.
Video_Games.summary: It's like opening a box of Monopoly only to find Chinese Checkers...

Video_Games.reviewText:
How would you like it if you went to a local grocery store for a bag of Doritos but the store would not sell it to you unless you bought a whole case of salsa in addition? It looks like Microsoft has done just that.
I have been a loyal NFS fan since the 1990s. This is the only game I play every 2-3 years. A new release out? I buy it and let the good times roll for a week or two.
This time it turned into a nightmare. I insert the disk into my XBOX360 Slim. The game wants to download a 1.6GB update. No problem. I have 3 drives. Internal memory (3GB free), an XBOX360 fat edition harddrive connected by cable (10GB free) and a 4GB USB drive, empty. The game notifies me that none of these are acceptable and it wants me to buy an additional Microsoft drive. Frustrated, I restart the game and try again without the update but it doesnt let me skip the update. It definitely is determined that I spend another $135 for the harddrive I don't need since I have plenty of available storage. Buying a 320GB drive to install a one time 1.6GB update doesnt make any sense to me.
May be I am missing something? I chat with Microsoft support. After an hour of reiterating the same point, the support rep finally understood and presented me with two choices. Either buy the new harddrive or use somebody else's to start the game. I patiently explain that this is the only game I play. I cannot possibly justify spending $200 for it and then wait another 3 years until a new NFS release is out. I don't have any local friend that play this game to borrow the harddrive from either. She apologizes profusely, but offers no help at all.
At this point I drive to the same local BestBuy store I purchased the game from. I have no receipt anymore (it never occurred to me that I would ever need it, I didn't expect to be shaken down). No problem. They find the purchase and hear me out. The store manager issues a full refund - in violation of their own return policy for open games.
I wish Microsoft understood what BestBuy learned a very long time ago. Customers want to be treated with respect. They don't like being extorted. They vote with their dollars by taking their business elsewhere. That is what I am doing. This Need for Greed release was the last one I ever bought. You know what? Make it the last XBOX game I ever bought, even a console.

Should have known better to NEVER download any game from EA.  I just want to play the game, I don't want to have to give my information over to EA Games and have them in complete control of my gaming experience.  Glad I only payed less than $20 for this download, the installer quits each time it gets to the actual install screen and amazon just points you to EA games and there you have to register and answer tons of questions and STILL don't get any phone number or help whatsoever.  LESSON LEARNED...don't buy this download, go get the actual cd of the game so you aren't at the mercy of online NON support.

*UPdate: Amazon.com was awesome and refunded my money for this download.  Now they have a great Amazon downloader which gave me zero problems in recent purchased downloads, so Amazon rocks! (EA still doesn't!)
Video_Games.summary: UGH! No support available from Amazon OR EA games

Video_Games.reviewText: I bought a Playstation 4 in September of 2014, and here it is 14 months later and its broken. Your only solution is for me to pay 149 + taxes and shipping to repair what is a know defect from launch day. This is supposed to be a 10 year cycle for this system and here we are 2 years in, and people are having the same issues they were on launch day. This as a consumer is unacceptable, and I don't understand how Sony can feel good about charging an additional fee to fix a problem they knew about before launching this product back in 2013. You have just turned a happy Playstation customer into a soon to be Xbox customer. I don't know if you remember the red ring of death issue Xbox had several years ago with their 360. Well, about 2 years into owning a 360 (1 year OUTSIDE of the warranty), I got the red rings and my 360 was dead. You know what XBox did? Sent me a brand new one free of charge and a box to send my damaged one back, also free of charge. That is customer service and pride in your product. Sony has demonstrated to me that they don't care about their customers and are ok with shipping defective products AND charging them 3/4 of the price of a new product to fix it. Thanks for nothing Sony.
Video_Games.summary: and I don't understand how Sony can feel good about charging an additional fee to fix a problem ...

I'd just completed Crysis and Warhead, couldn't get the original FarCry, but figured that FarCry2 would be just as good, right? Wrong. Dead wrong.
Quite apart from the movie scenes that you can't click through, the dreadful weaponry (the degrade feature is a nice touch, granted, but it's not suited to a shoot-em-up like this - maybe in something like Call of Duty it would better), the cloning of the opposition (in the guardposts? Oh please), and the oddball  effects (if you firebomb a wooden hut with a briefcase in it, the hut burns to the ground but the briefcase remains unscathed. Wow.) the Load feature of this game frankly stunk. If you have a lot of saved games it takes forever to bring up the list - faster to kill yourself and then Load Last Save. I'm running a 3.2ghz dual-processor, nothing should be slow on it. But this game is. As far as empathy with characters goes, there isn't any. After the 5th mission or so the only reason to play it is to complete it, you couldn't give a damn about the player, the Jackal, or anything else. There's some nice features in this game but it's not worth playing for these.
If you liked FarCry go and buy Crysis - it will blow you away. In a more enlightened age, Ubisoft's butchering of Crytek's franchise would have been grounds for hanging, drawing, and quartering Ubisoft's executives and display their heads on spikes at the city gates as a warning to others.

That's precisely what this title was for me---literally---and I honestly and sincerely believe that it will be for other fans of Acclaim's line of wrestling games for the Sony PlayStation as well, mostly because of various elements in its gameplay. Whereas the gameplay found in three other PSX wrestling titles by Acclaim---namely, WWF Warzone, WWF Attitude, and ECW Hardcore Revolution---seemed complex at first with its multi-button commands for each move in a given athlete's arsenal, most players eventually got the hang of it after a few matches, which made it that much easier for them to win with preexisting grapplers. Creating their own characters with the games' Create-A-Wrestler feature also became a more enjoyable experience because of this system. Instead of keeping such a set-up, however, the company's development team tried to facilitate matters in Anarchy Rulz by simplifying the controls for certain moves to only one or two buttons apiece. Unfortunately, this complicated matters instead, as certain maneuvers only become available when a player's wrestler stands in front of a dizzied opponent or has two or three stripes in the little box besides his/her name that indicates his/her advantage in a tie-up. Likewise, reversing particular moves (e.g., a hip toss, a hammerlock, an Irish whip, or a hurricanrana) is still pretty tough to pull off---for human-controlled competitors, that is. CPU-operated wrestlers, on the other hand have a jolly time reversing such moves whenever they have the opportunity, regardless of the game's initial difficulty setting. This makes it all the more frustrating for beginners. Of course, how about trying to trap another wrestler within the turnbuckle? Though it was a breeze in HR and Attitude---and even in Warzone---trying to do the same in AR is almost impossible, as the other athlete flops out of the corner almost every single time. This consequently renders corner moves highly impractical for both preexisting and customized grapplers.
In examining the other features available in AR, I will admit that I did enjoy the inclusion of those ECW personalities that didn't appear before in Hardcore Revolution and hence made their debut in this game, from the legendary "American Dream" Dusty Rhodes to the lovable yet laughable "loser" named Mikey Whipwreck. I also liked the various "jobbers" that players can unlock---even the foul-mouthed Trainer, who (for some reason I as yet cannot ascertain) is now a heel (bad-guy wrestler) after being a babyface (good-guy wrestler) for three games straight since Warzone. The opportunity to create one's own stable (four-member team) is also pretty fun, but considering that it takes a whole block of memory to save a single custom-made stable, players will ask, "Why bother?" The same goes for the new types of matches that one can participate in---Dumpster, Table, Backlot Brawl, and Brimstone. Sure, they're all very innovative and quite fun to watch, but the aforementioned flaws in control take much of that fun away. Even the Create-a-Wrestler feature---a staple in this line of games from Warzone on---leaves much to be desired, for though players have far more options available to them in selecting the outfit, entrance music, voice, moves, and so forth for each character they make, the nature of AR's gameplay again messes things up by compromising the nature of the moves in use. For example, in the instance that a given CAW uses both a Torture Rack and a Beast Choker, that character can only use one of these two submission holds upon pressing the punch button when grasping an opponent from behind, which varies with the degree of tie-up advantage (s)he has at the moment and accordingly makes the selection of created characters' maneuvers rather useless. This especially holds true for players who might not know what some of the moves are supposed to be in the first place based on their names alone. Speaking of submission holds, I would like to bring up the fact that almost EVERY hold in Anarchy Rulz is now meant to force opponents to "tap out"---even such holds as the Side Headlock, the Leg Grapevine, and the run-of-the-mill Full Nelson.
Sorry to say, but only the most "hardcore" enthusiast (if you'll pardon the bad pun) of Extreme Championship Wrestling would want to purchase Acclaim's ECW Anarchy Rulz, and then only for its nostalgia value. Not only is its gameplay a chore to become accustomed to (as mentioned above), but with its ugly graphics and mediocre sound quality, Joel Gertner's obnoxiously self-serving "color" commentary, and an inappropriately large amount of bloodshed for ANY game with a rating of "T for Teen," this title is not one worth playing. My advice for PSX owners and ECW fans alike is simple: Save your money on both Aspirin and video games by sticking with Hardcore Revolution.

I was really looking forward to this title, but I now have the biggest case of buyer's regret that I think I've ever had with any game.  I play a lot of racing games, and I think this is the biggest ripoff I've ever experienced in a game purchase.  Understand that I'm playing on the "Easy" difficulty setting and "Novice" driver setup with all assists on, and I've still only been able to get through about 8% of the campaign, and unless Atari comes out with major update to either dial back the difficulty and/or fix the really bad, twitchy handling, this is probably about as far as I'll ever get.  I wouldn't mind so much if you were given unlimited access to all the tracks and cars in Arcade and Time Trial modes, but the vast majority of the game's content is locked until you unlock them in the campaign.  So as things stand right now, I only have access to 9 out of 36 tracks (nothing from Nordschleife) and 12 out of 52 cars.

Atari, you are hurting yourselves and gaming in general when you make games this inacessable and frustrating.  I applaud your choice to have selectable difficulty settings in the game (ALL GAMES SHOULD HAVE THIS), but if you're going to have an Easy setting, IT SHOULD ACTUALLY BE EASY.  By all means, have a Difficult setting for hard core gamers who want to spend hundreds or thousands of hours pursuing a near impossible goal if that's what they really want.  But for the rest of us mere mortals who want to have fun, and not another freaking job, please give us (and yourselves) a break.

Where to start.

Cons: This thing is a monster, and not a good one.  The " thick cord is about as fun to manage as a coat hanger.  It occupies 2 USB ports, one for logic the other for power, but they're not labeled.  The software to program it is NOT simple.  Once you do spend the time to program it and save it to the BIOS, it's not permanent.  The keyboard often lost it's saved programs and you have to rerun the utility and reconfigure it.  The caps key broke.  Absolutely the worst keyboard I ever owned.  I gave it away to a friend and they don't even use it.  You want a keyboard that works plan and simple, buy a CM Storm Quickfire TK.  Half the price and works.  Sure you can't macro any of the keys, but what good is that when you have to keep reloading the keyboard utility.  Lastly, white lighting is not white LED.  They're RGB LEDs.  Color bleed between keys can look weird when set to white.

Pros:  Nice RGB lighting effects.

One of the best parts of the original Starcraft that has kept me playing it since the beginning is the ability to play it over the LAN with my friends.  Activision\Blizzard has seen that in their infinite wisdom to not include this style of play.

I'm sure some of you are thinking whats the big deal?  You have an Internet connection, you can play with your friends all in the same room.  Except of course when my Internet connection drops.  Or maybe I'm in place without reliable Internet.  Or my router gets taken out by lightning.

I'm sure Blizzard is trying to play up the supposed benefits to customers but lets face facts this is about piracy.  The irony though is pirates will figure a way to play the way they want and legitimate customers will get the shaft.

No LAN means no purchase and 1 star.

Ranked Match

Casual Match

Battle Lounge

Training

Versus

Survival

Capcom Fighters Network

This is a very pro online only game disc.

Story mode is nothing like arcade & is not good at all. One round fights vs 3 or less (for some fighters like Rashid & F.A.N.G) on very easy mode.

Survival mode. Nobody really care about this at all. Online players and casual alike.

SF5 should have been a download game only for now, then later came out with an disk with more content on it. Right now this is not worth $60. I am tired of companies treating legitimate purchasers of their products as pirates. I hate the fact that:

1. This product phones home to EA to see if I have used my one of 3 (or 5... who knows) installs. If I bought the game, I payed for MY system, I should have control to install this on my system as many times as I please. I frequently re-image and upgrade my pc. I shouldn't have to phone into a sub-par support service to get another chance to install my game that I paid for. Also based on previous EA support changes, They will probably charge you 2-3 years down the line just to talk to their support.

2. Securerom. Anything that adds insecurities to the pc is a no-no for me. Why am I forced to open my system to vulnerabilities to play a game? Google securom security problems, and you will find thousands of posts across many forums. Add the fact that it causes compatibility issues with various system configurations that impair the ability to even start games.

3. These games are cracked and on torrent websites before they are even published. The DRM doesn't doesn't do anything but hurt paying consumers.

Guess what EA, every game I see published by you that I have a pre-order order on, and has Securom gets the pre-order canceled. I canceled my pre-order for this game, and cancled my pre-order for Crysis: Warhead as soon as I saw posts with securom in it. I will save my money for companies that treat their customers with respect like Blizzard, Stardock and Ubisoft.

What were they thinking??  I haven't been able to play more than 15 minutes without my system crashing.  I've tried the patches, my drivers are up to date and all other games play without incident.  There's only one file/solution left to try with these two games and that's using my stand-by file: file 13 aka as "the trash recepticle".  Good luck to those who are able to play this one, for I am returning to a tried and true favorite: Civilization III.  Good luck and good gaming!!

At first, this game was "alright", and I must admit that I enjoyed the prospect of leading the world into global nuclear war.  However, aside from single handedly conquering the world using "unorthodox" dipolmacy and rising China to the most powerful country in the world, this game is not very interesting.  In other words:  after about an hour, you're ready for something else.  Aside from the lack of things to do in this game, it constantly crashes, and every patch brings a new, interesting set of glitches.  At patch 1.3, everytime I tried to run the game, it would ask me to restart to "complete the installation", and I did this several times.  I upgraded to patch 1.4, and I had the same problem, so I threw the game away (literally).

Basically, do not buy this game.  Don't be tempted by the idea of "controlling an entire nation", because by "control", they mean "change a few values, illegalize a few religions/political parties, and that's about it", and by "realism", they mean "tax the people at 100% because they won't mind".  If this is a "realistic geo-political simulator", then we are all doomed.  Do not buy this game.
Video_Games.summary: After patch 1.3, couldn't even run the game

This is the worst game. I guess the first Galaxy Force game was so good it warrented a sequel. I'm not kidding when I say I made games better than this in 10 minutes on my old Commodore 64.

Even if you are in the top right or bottom left firing in the wrong direction, whatever boring weapon you have will eventually kill the non-threatening baddies. There's no story, just shooting.

It is the most underdeveloped part of FIFA in god knows how many instalments in the EA series. The audio commentary.

Current generation CPU's can process 7 billion computations per second.

My goal keeper just threw the ball short to the opposition and they almost scored. This was almost disastrous. Everyone would be furious, "what is he doing!!??!", but instead Martin Tyler is telling me that my goal keeper has just made a stunning save. He is a hero.

Simlarly, a stunning through ball, Messi is one on one with the goal keeper. I take a shot, bahhh it goes wide. Messi just missed a sitter. But Martin Tyler is so impressed with him. "what a great shot! well done messi".

A couple of minutes later, the box is heavily defended, I can barely see a patch of green grass. I manage to create something out of nothing. A half chance at goals at best. Understandably it goes wide. Fair effort. My striker did well to even make something of it. But Martin Tyler doesnt see it that way. "He just squandered an amazing chance" he claims.

These mistakes in audio commentary are due to the archaic algorithms that still exist in the 20th instalment of the FIFA franchise.

The archaic set of commands that determine what Martin Tyler says.

"IF 'player does this' & 'ball does 'this' THEN commentator says ......"

No other variables? You cant spice things up a bit in the 21st century of computer coding?

I could have written this set of codes on my 86' ATARI.

It doesnt factor into the equation where the ball is, what happened a few moments ago, who is around during the sequence? In fact this data is already there for them to use. (You can get this information during half time with detailed map analysis of what was played and where). Just put this data into the audio algorithm for heavens sake!

It would take EA sports a fraction of effort to add and tweak these few extra variables into the equation. A little bit more data entry, a little more man hours, and a few more bits of command. You could drastically improve the commentary of FIFA 14.

If player was outside the box & there was 4 defenders in front of him & player does this & if ball trajectory does this, then commenator says this....

= "wow shot goes wide but messi did so well to make something of that. He had no space. Great shot outside the box"

You get the picture

= "Oh dear he was one on one with the keeper there"
= "Wow what a cool and calm finish, he still had alot to do"
= "Oh my goodness Zlatan! My word. A rocket from outside the box"
= "Oh he squandered the chance, he had Xavi completely free on the right"
= "Ronaldo! wow he just passed all the defenders"

Take into account the position of the ball, the position of players. Why cant Martin Tyler yet differentiate between a one on one and a long distance shot from outside the box.

Instead, EA sports has made the most minimal of efforts to release new titles for the PS4.
Better lighting?!
Better crowd dynamic?!

Are you kidding me. The only thing EA sports has done here is amp up the graphics settings.

The tomb raider franchise used to be great games, but not anymore.  This game really has the feel of a company milking their cash cow for the last time.  It's VERY buggy even though it's been out for quite a while.  Apparently a last ditch game doesn't warrent a patch for the multitude of bugs that it has.  The controls are extremely inconsistent in the PC version.  They are completely wrong in the documentation, don't even bother with it. Directional controls depend on your view and it's anyones guess what a particular control is going to do from a particular angle. Saves actually save some semblance of your game progress about 90 percent of the time.  Other times they do nothing and your progress is lost.  It's just shoddy and the controls and camera control are outdated.  Most games are much better than this now.

Upsides:  Yes there are a few... Hey it's tomb raider so it's got a decent storyline.  The graphics are decent.  It's a pretty good looking game.  If they would have put the time into the controls that went into the graphics, it might be worthwhile.  I've never left a TR game unfinished, but this is a frustrating mess and I'd advise you to pass on Underworld.
