Video_Games.reviewText: Civilization 5 is the last game I ever purchase that uses Steam as a game client.  Whenever I load a saved game (whether an auto-save, cloud save, or regular save) the game crashes to my desktop due to a "runtime error that caused the game to crash in an unusual way."  I've tried everything to fix the problem....2K's support site, Steam community forums, the Internet.....NADA.  No help at all.  I think the latest patch to the game broke it, so good luck with 2K/Firaxis coming out with a new patch anytime soon!  I have now switched to console games permanently, and if I need to play a game on my laptop, I will buy the disc version instead.

I recently purchased Sims 3 and have played it quite a bit over 48 hours.  It feels fairly similar to me compared to Sims 1 and Sims 2.  However, what's really driving me nuts are the bugs.  I immediately patched Sims 3 to the latest version before playing.  Sims 3 has completely crashed on me 5 times, each time erasing several hours of progress.

I have no other stability problems with any other games.  Most of the games I play are significantly more taxing on my hardware and operating system, so I am sure these are bugs in the game and not with my system.

I have to remember to save after every Sim Day in case the game is buggy again, however sometimes I forget.  There are no automatic save options..  Also, I get messages like "error code 12" and "error code 13" when I try to save my game sometimes.  When I see these errors, I have to Google for a workaround which sometimes works, and sometimes backfires and makes me lose all of my work.

There is NO excuse to release a game with save game problems.  There is even less of an excuse for a game that has save problems 6 months, and many patches, after releases.  I truly regret spending any money on this game as it has caused me more frustration than joy, especially when I compare it to how trouble-free Sims 2 played.
Video_Games.summary: It's still a buggy game 6 months after release

Video_Games.reviewText:
There are things I can't stand in this game.  First, I'll say what they have improved on.  The rebounding is so far feels better than 2K13, and you can actually play defense.  Now, let's talk about the huge amount of flaws.

First of all, this game is not beginner friendly on My Career.  Shooting sucks at this game, so you might have a better chance at getting an open shot then actually making them.  True, an open shot doesn't always go in, but a majority of them should have gone in.  It's not the game itself it's hard to shoot the ball, but for whatever reason, 2K decided to remove the Rookie (very easy) and Pro (easy) difficulty setting, thus making the easiest difficulty, All-Star (medium), a nightmare for new-comers or for those not that experienced.  From playing 2K13, I can easily say that all the difficulty does is make your shot worse, and that's it.  Also, the tutorials really don't help.  They don't show you how the move is done, and you get a strange, loud "NO" if you did something wrong, like Lil Jon was teaching you how to play over the internet and just got frustrated.  It might sound goofy, but believe me, the game actually does this.

The AI has to be the dumbest I've ever encountered in any game.  They never take open shots, but instead, pass it back to you, even if you're out of bounds or not open, pass it to someone else, tries to drive it in, or just stand there with the ball.  They'll also make some crazy decisions, for example, Wade run from under the basket to the right side of the court, and going back and forth from there.  The shooting might make not turn you into a ball-hog, but the teammate AI won't turn you into a play-maker anytime soon.

The controls in NBA 2K13 were perfect in my opinion, just a little slippery at times, but in 2K14, controls aren't the best.  The controls really did not need to be "improved" with an "intuitive Pro Stick," the right stick controls, and the right stick should only be for Iso moves.  You can change what the right stick controls, but it's still unnecessary for 2K to change the controls.  I even hated calling for a screen because it's the Circle button and not the R1 button, which I found more comfortable than using the Circle button.  It's still a bit slippery at times, and the controls could be just a matter of getting used to them, but this is one area 2K13 has an advantage on.

Another bad thing about the game is the soundtrack hand-picked by the cover boy, "King James."  I find it hard to enjoy a soundtrack that's filled with top hits like "Blurred Lines," "Who Do We Think We Are," and "Can't Hold Us."  It's not the fact that they're bad songs, but I don't feel like some of these songs belong in a basketball game.  I'm actually surprised Gunman Style, Taylor Swift, and Justin Beiber wasn't in there somewhere, because then the soundtrack will be really out of place.  There are a few songs I like, such as "Now or Never," "In the Air Tonight," "Radioactive," and "Clint Eastwood," but most of the songs are chart topping hits that I don't like, heard a million times, or just don't belong at all.  Please, somebody put Tech N9ne, Rittz, or Yelawolf in a 2K game.  I don't care as long as a song belongs in the game and gets me pumped up, not pumped "faked."  Sure, 2K13 had WAY too much Jay-Z, nobody can argue that since he was the executive producer, but I'll take that soundtrack over 2K14's any day of the week, 24/7.

Now let's talk about the very serious issues with the game.  The servers are horrendous.  It will take you 10-25 minutes for you to save a game to 2K's servers, if you're lucky.  When it doesn't save your game on the servers, you will be forced to play the same My Career game you played before, even if you said to "No, I don't want to quit."  Whoever programmed the game should be replaced, because I noticed that when I changed through the camera settings, it did not save the camera settings, thus making me go through the same menus just to get the angle I want.  (Oh, and I don't why, but 2K loves putting stuff on the right stick, including the some of the menus.)  There's also a bit of a delay when wanting to skip some stuff, like the intro which took a lot of taps of the X button just to skip (and that intro is kinda cheesy, if I do say so myself.)  It just terrible on the programming.

Recommendation: Unless if you're a pro at the game who didn't get a Xbox One or PS4, do not buy!  It's not beginner friendly, the things 2K took out were more important than they thought, and it's really an abysmal game overall.  It's unfortunate since I wanted a basketball game to hold me over until I go next gen, and now, I'm calling the game a skip or a next gen buy, at least next gen has features that matter.

This game was very poplular when I was in my young teenager. That time we had to pay 1 dollars for 1 game. I found this game sold in Amazon. I downloaded from this site. Maybe because I am grown, I ended up being tired of this game. Or I am somewhat an addict to Checker game. If you have a lot of time, and don't mind feeling as if you are being chased all the time, you will enjoy this game. I'm glad to play this game. Now I experienced playing this game knowing how it makes me feel, rather than frustration that I didn't play enough when I was very young.

Batman: Vengeance drops players into the universe from the popular animated shows. While this has been accepted as one of the better Batman-based video games, I found it a really frustrating experience. The game has its moments, but too many control issues killed the experience for me.

The main reason fans will want to pick this up is to hear the voice talent from the cartoon reprise their roles, including Kevin Conroy, Tara Strong, and Mark Hamil. The plot isn't terribly special - it tries to innovate in how it links all the villains together so that Batman can fight them, but it wouldn't be compelling without the voice cast backing it.

In fact, hearing the voice cast became my only incentive to get through the game. Batman is animated reasonably well, and Gotham is accurately (if blandly) modeled in 3D to match the look of the show. The combat system though, stinks. Batman has an arsenal of gadgets, but u have to switch into a clumsy first-person mode to use them. The c-stick isn't very good at precision aiming, making boss fights like Mr. Freeze and a helicoptor overly difficult. Batman is also rather easily beat up in a slugging match, despite his years of training. Thugs will often land the first punch, then punch you again as you get up, or corner you in a wall and keep you from retaliating. The constantly shifting camera doesn't help things either. Whats a good Batman game without a decent combat system?

In the end, I had much more fun with Batman: Rise of Sin Tzu, and even the much-hated Batman: Dark Tomorrow. Fans of the animated shows may want Vengeance just to hear the voice-acting. It's not really fun for anything else.
Video_Games.summary: I want Vengeance - on this game

Video_Games.reviewText:
The good:

This game is a top-down 8-bit MMO city-builder.  The interface is very simple for a city-builder, like Minecraft.  The entire planet is a complete wasteland, but can be rebuilt by purchasing materials from a simple point-and-click interface using gold coins, the game's resource.  More gold coins can be found by killing slugs, catmen, or thugs.  The number of materials number in the dozens, however almost all of these is the same material but rotated 90 degrees.  The game is 8-bit, but somehow manages 3-dimensions of building, which gives a lot to the imagination.  For example, brown blocks look nice as a house floor, but when stacked on top of each other it looks like a tree trunk.  Green blocks make nice grass, but in in the air green blocks looks like tree leaves.  Stone blocks in a cube form four walls in a house, but there can be crenellations for a castle's roof.  There's limited art possibilities possible for cacti and smiley faces, and no doubt can be fun for someone with an imagination.

There's a lot of ingenuity in this game.  For the halloween update, everyone gets the ability to purchase a pumpkin block.  The fact that the player has to painstakingly farming gold from monsters prevents players from building too quickly, meaning that there's always plenty of wide open land in order to create a whole town.  Town stones, which are required for being a mayor, must be purchased with real money.

The cost: Teleport portals must be purchased with real money.  Town banks must be purchased with real money.  Which means that aren't many mayors, and there aren't ghost towns of people whose population is exactly one mayor (here's looking at you, Minecraft.)  Mayors are not gods but simply have the ability to let others share land and housing easily.  I'd like to see one someday.  The total cost of creating a whole town with teleport portals is ten bucks.

What bugs me is the amount of content.  There's almost nothing.  There are three pieces of furniture for the house, and a very limited number of customization options for the character.  The game's pizzaz ends a few hours in.  It would probably be a blast if there were six to eight people working on the same town all at once, at the same hour, but then the game would be over eight times faster. This games looks like it's in alpha stage.

WWF Raw finally bought a wrestling game back to the PC. I WWF title hadn't been seen since Acclaims WWF In Your House in about 1996 or so. However, this game did not live up to the expectation of what it should have been.

I myself have always loved Wrestling games, ever since way back in the days of the original Nintendo, and the games and graphics have come a long way since then, and THQ where able to whip out the best of the best wrestling games of all time for the Nintendo 64, kicking off with WCW titles and working there way up to WWF No Mercy which is still my all time fave.

But I have no idea what THQ have been thinking when they make there Wrestling games for other systems... why change it and develop a new way to play when there is nothing wrong with the way it is loved best? THQ made the classics WCW/NWO Revenge and WWF No Mercy, the two best of the best wrestling games, but then they went and made WCW Nitro which is hands down the worst wrestling game of all time, being too arcade like and no fun.

You would think they learned from there mistake, but no, they did have some success with a similar but better style of game play with the PS games like Smackdown, but every one still agrees that the way they developed it for the 64 games was the easiest to use and preferred way.. but they did not listen to what the fans wanted, and instead combined the awkwardness of Nitro and Smackdown to create there first title for the X-Box, which later was converted to the PC, this game here, WWF Raw.

First off, there is already a few titles called WWF Raw, most fan's call this game WWE Raw now to separate it from the SNES classic. First thing I noticed was THQ screwed with the moment you start the game, they released there first few with the ability to turn the game on, and within 5 seconds you can be playing a match.. unlike this one, they bore you with copyright screens for a minute.

Ok, now onto the game; the graphics look pretty darn good, a big improvement since the N64 games, the wrestlers look cool, much better then the PS titles that looked awful. The moves are executed decently, some are too quick for my standard, but thats just my opinion. The new polygon system is a nice touch, to be able to adjust heads, bodies, and the rest to whatever size you want. The intros look pretty damn good and the pyrotechnic graphics are amazing. The controls are not too bad, you can get used to them, after a while and the music is as close to the real thing as its gonna get.

Now, the cons. There is no where near enough moves to do in this game. The  menus are atrocious to guide through when creating a wrestler, the CAWS take a back step now with an option to make the crotch, upper thigh, lower  leg and feet costume... to make a simple pair of pants you have to go into 3 different menus and select each section to do it. interesting idea, but annoying, they should have kept it the old way or had an option for the preset proper clothing/attire stuff in the one selection. The caws have so  much new stuff to chose from, but not enough attires you actually wanna use.

The matches are a joke; there is nothing in this game but 1 on 1, 2 on 1, 3 on 1, 2 on 2, 3 on 3, 4 on 4 and a so called Battle Royal that is only 4 players. A battle royal is a match where you all start in the ring and try to eliminate everyone else by knocking them over the top rope... not a fatal four way elimination match... what was THQ thinking????

No cage match, no cell, no backstage areas, no HBK, No DX (i'll let the last 2 pass as they weren't around at the time) no LADDER MATCH, no TLC... and whats worse, there IS a ladder in the game, you can pick it up, you can set it up, but you can not climb up it!!! The only decent weapon is the table, which you can set up and break your opponent through, but using hacks on WWF No Mercy show that that game could do better still cause the breaking tables in this game are nothing special.

I may not have done something correctly, but, as far as i know, there is only one arena, Raw. No Mercy was called that and still had all the arenas to choose from.. why was it so hard to develop a few extra pictures and stick them on the background of the arenas?

Now i'll list as a WWF No Mercy fan what I liked about this game and what I hated.

Liked
- Wrestler Intros (pyro, effects, music, crowed)
- Undertakers Motorcycle is a proper 3D model he rides in on.
- Ability to alternate between titan tron video and players entrance during intros.
- Options to change the polygons around.
- option to attack opponent during there intro.
- actually does have some music WWF did not own the copyright to like the Undertaker and HHH's theme that they slacked off on buying the rights to in previous games and had them with old themes or gave them the raw theme song.
- can sustain more then 4 wrestlers during a match at a time.

Hated
- no commentary
- unclimbable ladder
- not enough match types
- not enough moves
- not enough CAW options (every category)
- playing against the computer is too hard even on easy
- Some controls are confusing
- only one arena
- no backstage
- intros show things like motor bikes and ravens trolley, yet there not usable during a match or even seen, they magically disappear.
- Unlockable characters are not worth it.
- nothing special about unlocking hats and sunglasses to pick up and put on during a match.
- can sustain more then 4 wrestlers in a match at a time, but does not have any 4 on 4 or royal rumble match to do that with, there only seen when "interference" is selected.
- during the match music is annoying.
probably more
- No blood
- Cant climb the ladders.

overall; get yaself a rom of No Mercy and hack away with it. This game here is a nice looking game, but a dud to play and no replay value. Fun on two or more players, but frustrating and annoying on one player.
Video_Games.summary: Could Have Been So Much Better, what a let down by THQ.

Well, I squee'd with joy when both this and the other item I bought from a different place arrived at the same time.  Happiness was short lived once I pulled the adapter out however.  I'd heard(Apparently Wrongly) that Wii plugs also work for a Wii U as it uses the same type.  How unfortunate for me that this was NOT the case at all and to rub salt in the wound the plug has "Nintendo" plastered on it as if to mock me for trying to cheaply spend my little money.

Video_Games.reviewText:
Listen to me.  Don't buy this game. If someone wants to give it you, refuse it.  Seriously, I paid $49 for this pathetic excuse for a third person shooter. I was bored after the first 30 minutes. No real storyline, just the repetitive action of shooting bad guys who somehow can shoot YOU while you are standing behind walls. Also, grenades can damage you even if you're nowhere near the explosion. The graphics weren't bad, expecially the jungle scenes.  That's why I rated this game with 2 stars instead of one. I like third person shooters, and was hoping this would be one of those games like Rogue Trooper, which was very good.

Save your money, but if you feel the need to blow 50 bucks, then take the money and flush it down the toilet.  You'll get just as much satisfaction.

This was too quick I beat the easy mode in 3 hours or so.  Your allies you can not cross their borders so if one puts an city by you then you are stuck in your corner until you get a boat or declare war.  I am sure this game is great online where you can play many people for hours but really this is not that cool.  I wanted to get into space race or something better but then I completed the domination side and it forced me to stop so I never got a chance to get past the gunpowder.  I was really let down by this game.  I am taking it back.  I would pay 25 or so for this game but 60 is way to pricey.

The Fallout series is one of my all-time favorites and Fallout New Vegas is a great addition. Yes it does look and feel a LOT like Fallout 3 but I think that is GOOD thing. Why drastically change something that worked so well before? After all, this is just taking place in another area of the country...not another world. Things should look and feel the same in DC as it does anywhere else in the country. I do have some performance gripes though, the lag is bothersome and the graphics could have been smoothed a little. Maybe they should have played the game before they released it. All in all I am very happy with the game so far!

ok.....played the game quite a bit more. This game is a wreck! Crashes, lag and bugs ruin what this game could have been. Also this game is waaaayyy to easy! Haven't tried it on hardcore mode but in the normal mode I couldn't find a challenging fight. I am selling it before I smash it. changing my score from 4 to a 2

Seemed like a nice keyboard.

Pros:
- Nice price for a fairly respected brand, Redragon.
- Solid, quality construction. It weighs a ton and won't accidentally move on your desk.
- Awesome backlighting, though I couldn't care less really. I just need backlighting to be bright yet adjustable, and able to have solid colors, which this can do nicely. There are also lots of random multiple color patterns that can be cool.
- Felt nice for typing fast.

Cons:
- THE KEY NOISE! Warning to all first time mechanical keyboard buyers: Cherry Blue (or blue equivalent) key switches really make a loud click sound, in addition to the loud sound of the keycaps hitting the floor of the keyboard (you'd think that could be combatted somehow in the design of the keyboard -- I read "O rings" for the keys could help alleviate that, but the clicks were still too loud for me).
- While the keys felt nice for typing, they still seem mushy because of the travel distance they have. Sure, the keys contact about halfway pressed, but it still felt long, especially when using game commands. I guess it takes a lot of getting used to, especially coming from a lower profile keyboard with flatter key design.
- The caps/num/scroll-lock indicator lights are obnoxiously bright, like laser beams into your eyes!
- Sorry but the font used for the letters and stuff on the keys is just ugly to me. Guess that's supposed to look "gamey?"

So I had to return this keyboard because I could not take the key noise during gaming (I don't use headphones), which was distracting and broke immersion for me. It seems funny how such mechanical keyboards are sold as gaming keyboards -- I want to hear my game, not my peripherals!

Immediately after purchasing and downloading the newest Sims 3 Stuff pack from Amazon I sensed something was amiss. The file download size was 2 to 3 times smaller then any of the other Sims 3 stuff packs I had purchased before, but I presumed perhaps they had made it more efficient and smaller using different compression techniques, oh boy was I wrong. Opening up the folder for everything from this pack I was immediately disappointed at the general lack of quantity. This is by far the smallest stuff pack to yet come out but it is still the same price as the others. The quality of the items was fine as usual but I just could not get past the fact that I paid $20 for a set of about 24 things. There are bigger collections for download on the Sims 3 site! Honestly, if you want a Sims 3 stuff pack, buy High End Loft or Outdoor Life, they have far more items for about the same price.

Two complaints, one minor, one major.

I ordered the green wireless controller.  The one I received today isn't the same shade of green depicted on the Amazon page, the buttons are a little different, etc.  That's all fine.

The major complaint is that I thought the wireless controller would come with a way to connect to my PC, i.e. a dongle or whatever to plug into a USB port.  No receiver or cable came with the controller so I can't use it until I get one.  I thought it was implied on the Amazon page that a receiver would come with it (but maybe I just assumed that based on my experience with buying a wireless mouse).  Just be aware if you don't already have a wireless receiver.
Video_Games.summary: Be aware you need your own receiver

Video_Games.reviewText:
I did enjoy the open world format of the game and being able to go wherever you would like. The game was buggy, I got stuck in rocks and signs a few times and had to restart. I didn't receive an achievement that I unlocked, to which Ubisoft responded saying that it was a known issue and that I would get said achievement whenever they fix the problem. I also had issues with content that was supposed to be unlocked because I purchased the gold edition, that also has not been resolved. Will be contacting Ubisoft again about this.
Lastly, the ending was terrible. So terrible. And the alternate ending was even worse. I cannot believe I put 92 hours into that game and ended up with that ending.

When I got this game for Christmas by accident (expected Tenkaichi 2) I figured "Well, maybe it is as fun as the second game." then I found out that it was not what I expected. DragonBall Z Budokai Tenkaichi 1's story mode is the worst mode in the game and you have to play it in order to unlock new characters of course. It is basically a mission based story mode and it is very heavy on it's missions, for example: you have to face against Raditz as Goku in the Saiyan Saga but you have to "Survive until time runs out" in Tenkaichi 2 that doesn't matter because you can destroy Raditz all you want but here you actually have to let Raditz survive not you other wise it would show you a cutscene where it shows that you have won the fight but when you get sent back to the mission select screen you did not pass the mission. The game also changes the computer difficulty at random making some missions impossible to beat and you can not continue on until you beat the specific mission. Even though you can change the difficulty in the options menu it won't make a difference when you were doing so well in the last 20 missions and all of a sudden the enemy starts to attack you from every angle so that you can not escape it, why have a difficulty setting when the game chooses it for you. The Z-items are worthless, they are used as power-ups per mission instead of staying on the character in the mode. While that is a pain in the ass, there is training mode where you can freely beat the living snot out of your opponents without any worry of missions although you have to keep going back and forth in selection screens to change say: Goku to Super Saiyan 3 Goku. Overall I give this game 2 stars it would have been four if the game wasn't a cheating bastard all the time.
Video_Games.summary: Fun to play in practice mode, but not in story mode.

Video_Games.reviewText: I only recently got into LOST.  After watching all the episodes I got hooked and got this game to satisfy my LOST-tooth.  I give the developers props for creating a game that is NOT another first person shooter.  They created a beautiful world with a great story, immersive artwork and fitting acting.  Where did they fall short?  Everything else. The game is choppy.  Even in 2008 they could have made it smoother.  When conversing with fellow castaways the screen goes black for a second as it cuts between the different dialogue tracks.  With the most powerful gaming consoles behind this game, that should not be necessary.  Also the game is very exact in what it will accept as the right answer.  In many puzzles you are asked to take pictures of objects, but the program is very specific- if the angle is off by even a little you have to keep repeating it until you get it perfect, without useful feedback as to how to fix the problem. There are long cutscenes between chapters which cannot be skipped. As in "previously on LOST..." IF you want to just shut up and play, you can't.  You need to sit through episode like recounts of what you just did.  This is doubly frustrating when the cutscene is integrated into what you need to do.  Even a slight mistake in the task and you get to sit through 2 minutes of cutscene all over again.  The system of looking at and using items in the environment is also frustrating.  You can be directly in front of the item you are trying to use, but if the game's camera is not set just right you'll end up doing the truffle shuffle trying to get the computer to recognize what you are trying to do. The rules also seem nonsensical.  For instance, if you spend too much time in the darkness you will die and the game over screen will just say "The darkness killed you." WTH?  Many of the puzzles are math problems with fuses and voltage, look for something through caves and go back and forth between locations to get things.  Buy it because you like LOST, but if you play more than a chapter a day you will get frustrated and wish you hadn't.

It must be in style to make games with no story lines these days.  I really don't like deathmatch only games, but this game really didn't say anything about it being like that.  Anyway, this game plays very similar to Unreal Tournament or Quake III.  I'm really not very partial to these games.  I thought maybe Warpath would have a single player story-line, but I was completely wrong.  I'm not saying multiplayer games are bad, it's just not really my thing and I much prefer a story line to get into.  I just wish they would advertise that fact a little better so I know more about what I'm buying!

The single player sequence is very similar to a multiplayer sequence, only you're fighting against bots.  For the amount of time I was playing this game it didn't seem like there were a huge amount of maps.  I really do wish they had a real story mode to go with this game because the character concepts are actually really cool!  Even though they are a bit cliché, I still liked them.  Like Quake III and Unreal Tournament this is a sci-fi based game and you can play as any of the three races, one of which is human, the others are the Ohm, a cybernetic race, and the Kovos who are a warrior race and actually rule the territory.  The single player sequence does seem somewhat unique where you get to choose the battlefield and then you have to defend against the opposing forces depending on which race you are.  This is all mapped out on a small grid and when you control the whole thing you win.  Of course you have to do this multiple times on different maps for that grid.  Unfortunately because this game strictly plays like a multiplayer game that relies solely on "who can get the most kills" and "capture flag" scenarios it gets rather tiring after a while.  Seriously, those are like the only two scenarios they had me go through.  The difficulty level varies and some sections were more difficult than others, but still they were all the same format.

The weapons you get to choose from are a little less than exciting.  When you start out you can only choose one weapon in single player, then you have to beat levels and you can eventually choose a different one.  It appears you can only choose from three main weapons and three secondary weapons.  This was kind of disappointing and it seems like this game was thrown together rather quickly just to cash in on Unreal Tournament fans... without it being Unreal Tournament.  I don't know, I'm pretty disappointed in this purchase.  If you're a really huge fan of multiplayer styled games then this game probably isn't too bad.  I mean it even has vehicles you can drive around, but I didn't play on any maps that were big enough to really take advantage of this.  The one map I was on that did have a vehicle was pretty small and I didn't see the point in having a vehicle.  If you're into Unreal Tournament, you should probably stick with those, because from what I've played that system has a much better design and a bit smoother play.  Also, this is the first review on Amazon for this game and since it came out quite some time ago, I wouldn't expect there to be a lot of people on Xbox live playing this.  So unless you really like being challenged by bots in your multiplayer game, I'd say this is something to skip.
Video_Games.summary: The single player mode is really just multiplayer with bots!

Video_Games.reviewText:
The short - This game is buggy as hell, and lacks polish, I would recommend waiting for patch.

I've clocked about 6hrs total and about 3hrs actual.  Why you ask? Because the game crashes constantly.  The first crash may of been my fault.  Since I let the console go into save state overnight or whenever I put it down (as I do with a lot of games) when I came back and started a quest I got a 1st in two respects.  The 1st time a game has ever crashed, and the 1st time I ever had to submit a bug report directly to Sony as a result.  The 2nd and 3rd crash came from the multi-player portion.  If at anytime a packet gets lost, the game doesn't exit the multi-player it just freezes the game (you can tell from the lady at the counters animation no longer moving (that, and the game stops responding)).

The lack of polish part.  It is glaring in combat.  When you hit an enemy it triggers a spawn event.  What should happen: both enemy and your party should spawn and duke it out until one side wins.  What does happen: sometimes your party doesnt spawn, or they spawn towards the end of the fight.  The enemy group doesn't spawn. Or both groups spawn in incredibly late.

During combat, Hit detection is broken, if you knock an enemy down you can no longer hit them until they stand up.  If you do the Thief's advanced attack the 1st hit lands and all other hits will swing thru the enemy target and not connect leaving you animation locked and unable to move for their retaliation strike. I wasn't able to hit the rabbits with the archer.. I  couldn't target lock them because I wasn't in combat and I couldn't hit them just blind firing in their direction... could be me, dunno.

After combat, you party despawns leaving you to loot everything.  The healer in the group doesn't heal everyone to full (forcing you into the menu).  Debuffs do not go away after combat (Big Issue with this one)

PVP lacks polish (when not crashing).  So they list the game modes but don't explain what they mean.  You get Champion, King, Even, Underdog.  So not knowing what any of that meant I chose even .... I did find a match and was completely outmatched.  2/3's of the pvp selection screen is the useless leaderboards.  They couldn't put one more text box explaining what each setting meant?

Raise/Debuff -  This one really irks me.  It is not based on what is wrong with your character, it is based on the level of your character.  The higher the level the more it costs.  Two of my characters got hit with moneypit which drains your money as you go it was cheaper to kill them off then try and get back to town and run to the priest to fix it.

The light district.  So the big flaw here is the quest turn-in system.  You have to pay to talk to the quest lady to find out she can't accept the turn in or she doesn't have anymore quests to hand out.....REALLY? Also, the first time you talk to a lady she double explains herself... its really strange but they only seem to do it once.

Lastly, the load times are pretty lengthy for what you actually load into.  I think in some area's it is generating random characters.  I base this logic on the times my game crashed and I went back into an area different npcs were in there.

Not to end this on a sour note.

I do like the customization (limited for character creations) but I mean the overall different armor/outfits that reflect on your character.

I do love building my own party, hopefully if I can get farther I can ditch the forced members for the ones I really want.

So if they do patch the game and improve the stability I will update my review and score.  Until then, buyer beware!
Video_Games.summary: Buggy, lacks polish, wait for patch.

Video_Games.reviewText:
I bought this game a few years ago... It was better a few years ago.

This game would probably be great for younger girls. Basically you run the horse around the barrel, no skill involved. The pattern for the competitions never change, just barrel pattern. Although in the practice pen you can go through multiple courses such as the pole pattern (Still with barrels) etc. For the older girls (Over 12) I would recommend the Legacy of Rosemond Hill. It includes jumping, cross country, and steeple chase. With an additional story line (Almost a mystery) added. In addition, you have the option of owning three horses total as you place (Or win) in the various competitions. More challenge=more fun.

This is a very simple game, I like these to just relax and kill time. Some people who prefer more strategy based games and action probably would not enjoy this. The only issue I had was some of the levels will not let you finish, there is a glitch where some blocks are lifted off the ground so the ball will never hit them and you cannot complete the required amount of busted blocks to finish the level. It's not a big deal if you just play a random game here and there but I like to advance through the levels in order and try to use the same "life", thats how I challenge myself with these games. With this glitch its impossible to do that since you can't advance. I emailed the software company customer support asking about a patch for this, they replied once asking about my computer hardware, when I sent them the info I never heard from them again.
Video_Games.summary: Fun to kill time with, but some levels will not let you finish.

Video_Games.reviewText: The only reason I gave this game 2 stars is because of the music. Otherwise, the gameplay is bad- you would need three hands to at least play it correctly. The camera angles are weird and don't rotate, causing issues when targets shoot at you from off-screen leaving you running in circles madly trying to find them before you die. The force power combos work only sometimes, and not effectively. You have to be a dark Jedi/Sith- you can't choose which alignment you play or which character. Lastly, some of the fight sequences are very difficult to pull off, seeing as you need to be using the touchscreen, movement keys, and right/left triggers all at once. So, 2 stars for music and that's about it. I'm sure on the PC, this would be a different and probably better experience, but not for the DS. If you want cool force powers, I'd recommend playing Star Wars The Old Republic on your PC; it's free to play and free to download, and the Jedi Knight abilities and effects are better than those of this game. Plus a better storyline of course. Hope this review helps some of you thinking about this game.

So far I'm about ten hours into this game. Which isn't saying much. Most of the gameplay isn't really gameplay. On average, for every hour you play for about ten or fifteen minutes you can actually control what your party does. Everything else is just drawn out micro-cinemas. I am a big fan of all the other FF games but I think they went a little overboard on the cinematic aspect of this game. The graphics are amazing. That's true. I'm not trying to dispute that. It does however, take more than dazzeling graphics to make a game work. I think square sacrificed some of the finer points of gameplay to accomodate the stunning visuals.
I would recomend this game to anyone because I am loyal to the series and it still may surprise me yet. Just be warned to be patient and be ready to put your controller down often. Also, up until this point the storyline has been relativley flat and dull.

I know I am going to get bashed for this, Just to let everyone know i am not a Sony freak just bashing this system for no reason. This is my second 360. My 1st...Red ring of death, so I bought the HDMI Xbox thinking it would not freeze up from overheating, red ring of death etc.... I enjoyed playing the system for 10 days, treating the xbox 360 like it was my kid, being gentle with it, giving it plenty room to breath and even putting it in the box when it wasn't being used. Then I started getting a E64, E65, and E66 errors and now it doesn't work at all. Don't get me wrong if i had a fully functional system i would love it, but I am not going to accept buying a system that only works some of the time. So off for repairs it goes and we will see how my next one turns out.

Don't believe the hype: "Titanfall" is not a transcendent classic in gaming. Indeed it adds a variety of slight innovations to the traditional FPS format, but none are so groundbreaking and revelatory as this  "Xbox One exclusive" would like you to imagine. Perhaps it is one half of a great game, but there are numerous shortcomings which make one believe this was rushed to launch instead of being properly developed into a full experience.

"Players can scramble anywhere with crazy parkour!" - See "Brink" or "Mirror's Edge"
"Giant mechs are awesome!" - From "Lost Planet" to "Star Wars Battlefield," plenty of others have done it before and with far more personality in the bots.

What's most telling about the weaknesses of this game is how little attention is paid to the superfluous parts of the game beyond the online multiplayer. The campaign is minimal, there's no originality in design, and the "story" is completely forgettable. Future, space, aliens, whatever - "Titanfall" just wants you to plug in and shoot each other into oblivion in their generic and soulless sci-fi world.

There is much praise for the "speed" of the game, but really that just amounts to madcap scrambling and respawning, with hardly any unified strategy or teamwork. The touch and mechanics are identical to "Call of Duty" as well, for better or worse.

I would watch even the most experienced killers try and fail to execute various wall climbing/running maneuvers, making for a frustrating experience when you cannot get the character to do what you want it to.

Why no split-screen either? We have 2 systems even, but 4 players, so only half could play at a time. From other deficient features like the paucity of execution animations, the choppiness of the melee attack, to the dearth of weaponry, there is no doubt room to grow, but this version is half-baked at best.

It doesn't even look that great - The hud is both bland and muddled, while the environments feature little destruction of elemental flair.

This one is only for the most hardcore of FPS junkies. Its online base will predictably vanish soon once the mainstream gamer population realizes they've been duped. When our friends brought over the new "Metal Gear" and "Dark Souls" games, our group was all too eager to abandon this redundant shooter, since 10 minutes of play is the same as 100.
Video_Games.summary: A small and soulless step forward

Video_Games.reviewText: I purchased this game for my 12 year old daughter after she fell in love with a 2 week trial version of this for the PC.  I really wanted to get the DS version so she didn't stay on her computer so much.  So far the game sucks.  She enjoyed the PC version much more because the fish didn't die off as bad.  With the DS version, we did what people recommend and bred fish to a similar type (you only get one of each type).  The baby fish die off non stop.  Any adult fish you sell don't get much money, so it's hard to purchase the items needed.  She is playing on easy too.  This game is NOT for really young kids.  They will get bored with it in no time.  There is little interaction with the game except in short spurts every few hours!

i thought that having a complete set of one of the best games i played since ever is nice so i ordered this one but when i got it i was SHOCKED if you think that you can replay metal gear 1 or even 2 your are wrong.cus there are a big deference in the graphics and sounds and AI etc so if you are thinking about getting this one just to add it to your collection it is maybe nice but if you are buying this to replay the games really save your money.......
Video_Games.summary: I am a big fan BUT .................

Video_Games.reviewText:
I do not recommend this mouse at all. My first gaming mouse, I was thrilled to have when it was working flawlessly, but after about 6 months, the issues started showing.

Logitech sourced the cheapest Shenzhen alleyway bargain-bin microswitches for this mouse. The middle mouse button was the first one to die, merely 6 months after buying. I barely used it for anything other than scrolling web pages, but it died nonetheless. This is a very common problem as I discovered when Googling it. Another six months down the road, the left mouse button started to fail, double-clicking whenever I'd single click something and sometimes not registering clicks at all. This made it impossible to do even basic PC tasks, let alone gaming.

Appearances deceive. It's ranked highly by those that had just bought it. Those that have had it for a year know that it will die long before you get your money's worth.

Wanted to wait until I beat the game before I posted a review. Now that it's over, all I can say is that I'm relieved I don't have to play it again.

I love the Zelda series and I really held out hope that this would be great, but it was just more frustrating and annoying than anything for the following reasons:

1) While Zelda games usually start with a bunch of mundane tasks to get you familiar with the controls, this game didn't seem to stop. Even in trying to get into the next temple to get the a new weapon/beat a boss, you had to run around looking for a key (literally) to get through the front door. It got old and repetitive.

2) The story and characters of Skyloft were kind of lame. Yes, it's basically the same story in all Zelda games, but the writers tried to mix it up with something new and it was boring. Even when I read reviews about how "you'll see at the end how it's considered a prequel to other Zelda games," the ending wasn't anything special. The characters seemed very one dimensional too - they had one purpose to fill in a side quest or as part of the main story and once it was fulfilled, the person rarely said or did anything new. Seemed like a missed opportunity.

3) The game itself seemed too directed towards kids. It is rated Everyone +10, but feels a lot more like an innocent Everyone. Twilight Princess (which I loved) is rated Teen and admittedly pretty dark - maybe that's why they tried to lighten this one up so much? It's a personal preference, but I like Zelda games when there seems to be more danger and when the bad guys really threaten or hurt a character.

4) Speaking of PG, the bosses are far from scary. In the past when a new boss was introduced, it would usually make the hair on the back of my neck stand up and I'd be in awe of how creepy it looked or panic for a second on how to kill it. In this game, the bosses are almost comical looking and it was usually pretty obvious from the get-go where to attack it. For example, in one a part of the game you're on a ship and the boss's tentacles are tearing through it to attack Link. Seems like it could be a menacing boss, but I get to the deck and find out the tentacles belong not just to an octopus, but a Rastafarian-looking octopus. Not very intimidating.

5) I hate Fi, Link's guide, because she has less personality than Apple's Siri. I think I was in the minority, but I loved Midna in Twilight Princess because she had a ton of personality. I think even Navi in Ocarina of Time had more personality. Besides that, Fi really doesn't offer any  help. She repeats the same information that someone else has just given you. She occasionally sings and dances like an ice skater, but even that grates the nerves.

6) Could be the Wii Motion Plus control, but I had a lot of issues of it locking up on me and being unable to control Link once he's start moving in one direction. I'd have to unplug the nunchuck and reattach it to set it straight again. I think I had the problem once or twice throughout the entire game of Twilight Princess, but it seemed to happen once or twice in every play sitting.

I'll stop there. Like I said, I'm sure it's great for a younger kid or for someone who hasn't played another Zelda game before, but I found it too disappointing. So why did I play if I disliked it so much? First, because it was Zelda and I had to know happened; second, because I can't move onto a new game until I finish one that I started (an OCD thing). And now that I've finished it, I am free to move on to another game or play Twilight Princess again. Hooray!

Sacrifice has enough eye candy and interesting gameplay that it could easily merit four or even five stars--IF it were stable and reasonably smooth to play. I realize that my 300 MHz B&W G3 represents the low end of the Apple spectrum these days, but since I have no trouble getting Black & White or MYTH III to run smoothly (and both of these have hefty system requirements), I certainly can't see why Sacrifice should sputter and crash the way it does. Don't bother going for the lowest resolution and detail settings, either--it won't help. You might as well enjoy the nice 1024x840 32bit graphics, as the game's performance will not benefit from turning all the nicer video settings off. Form what hear and read, not even having a nice tricked-out G4 will get Sacrifice off the ground--something must be fishy with the code itself. It's a shame, since Sacrifice is quite an original title with amazing visuals and great sound FX. But it's the first game in a long while that I really wish I hadn't bought.
Video_Games.summary: A game you'll hate to love ...

Video_Games.reviewText:
Why-oh-why you guys did not improve everything? when I read other reviews describing that this looks like an expensive expansion pack of MW2 I didn't believe it. People even called it MW 2.5! Too bad it is true. The game is fun (I only care about Multiplayer) but still, we payed 60$ for new maps!? everything else is the same!
What makes this game even more sad is the fact that some maps look similar to the ones you find on MW2.
We buy games cause of the graphics, game play, etc. You just gave us new maps and recycle everything else! I feel cheated somehow.
Video_Games.summary: Big Fan of CoD:MW and I'm extremely disappointed

Video_Games.reviewText:
I have been attempting to acquire a copy of Suikoden 2 for a while finally got my hands on one when I ordered it from this seller.  The price was good and the item was complete.  I received the item very quickly.  I immediately tried it on my ps1 and it said "please insert a playstation cd-rom." I tried it a few times, tried a few different games in it (other games including FFVII worked) but suikoden still didn't work.  I tried it in both my ps2 and ps3 afterward but it still didn't work (ps2 remained on browser screen and ps3 didn't do anything).  I contacted the seller informing them of the problem and promptly returned the item in its original condition.  I wasn't going to write a review about this initially as the return went very smoothly (so far as I haven't received the full amount back yet) however just now when searching for a complete working copy I came across the description stating that I switched out the case.  I received the item in a shipping envelope wrapped in a washcloth (wasn't dirty or anything but not the most protective means of wrapping).  I can't speak to the condition that it was when it left the sellers residence however I returned the item in the same condition I received it and had the post office mark it fragile so the condition would not worsen.
I would be very cautious purchasing this item.

Toys_and_Games.reviewText:
Great Stadium! I really like how the retractable roof is movable in this 3D stadium. And it slides very easily so however you like it being displayed, opened or closed, you can change it whenever you like. This took me about 2 hours to complete building.

My only issues was that the a piece was mis-numbered and so when I followed the instructions, it made the pieces not fot together correctly. Just pay close attention to how the pieces look like and the pattern/symmetry of some parts. So instead of going 20 -> 21 -> 22 -> 23 -> 24, my pieces actually went 21 -> 22 -> 23 -> 20 -> 24.

This gift was perfect for my 2yo daughter. We've been working in our unfinished backyard and she loves to be out there along with us raking and digging. The bag is constantly swinging from her arm and filled with dirt, rocks and weeds. The bag is sturdy canvas material and the tools are legit. There's no wobble to them at all, they seem as sturdy as any of my hand trowels. None of the paint has chipped off either and she uses them in rocks/gravel. Since the shovels are the favorite I'm glad there are 2 for when we have a friend over.
The only reason I didn't give it 5 stars was because I feel like it needs gloves to be a complete set. We pulled out a pair of knit snow gloves that we don't care about, but not everyone has those lying around. Somehow kids always notice and want the accessories.
Overall this is a great buy. Well worth the money, not like those plastic sand toys you'd find at your local store.
Toys_and_Games.summary: Great quality, just wish it came with gloves.

Toys_and_Games.reviewText: Great deal for the price.  These are adorable little trains that are about 2 inches long and maybe a little over an inch tall.  They seem pretty sturdy.  The grandson LOVES them!  Grandson saw me opened the package and started jumping up and down squeeling, he was so excited.  Grandboy has not put them down since we got them.  I gave grandson a little basket to carry them around in.  They also easily fit in little toddler pockets so he can carry a few with him anywhere.

I liked this toy because there were many ways to play with it besides just pushing it around.  My 3 year old has been enjoying it and is capable of doing all of the activities except unfolding and refolding the trash basket.  We have had it for a month with no issues, but if your kid is a rough player you might want to go with a different model.

I did have one piece missing from my set, the top of the gas station. This set has a large number of plastic pieces. I wish things like this would come in a plastic bin with a snapping shut lid so you could neatly put them away when you are finished playing with them. But it is a very fun set, you can easily snap together the town (some parts don't come apart so easily to put them back in the box). There are instructions. Every piece seems to have a lot of built in areas where you can make imprinted things out of play doh. Fun things like cakes, pizza, etc. There is a town center with a clock and kitchen, a gardening center, a garage, and a car. There are hats and things to make play doh people. You do get play doh in 8 colors with the set, yea! The gas pump allows you to press out play doh, but this set does not focus on extruding fun things like ropy hair for the people. The focus is on playing with the town and pressing out shaped objects. The town would also be fun to play with any small dolls.
Toys_and_Games.summary: A lot of fun, a large number of shapes that you can press out.

Toys_and_Games.reviewText:
I was looking for a pocket-sized RC boat I could run in my moderately-large pool or or take to a small lake.  I found that the UDI Bullet was quite a fast boat for its size.  My first run in the pool, I ended smashing it into the walls a few times blunting the nose a bit.  (I later sanded it back into shape but not without some compromise of aesthetics). For pool runs, I now run the boat at 1/2 to 3/4 throttle. If you're going to take it to the pool, I would recommend first-time users or RC noobs like myself to:
1) watch your speed
2) attach a piece of silly putty or yellow modeling clay to the nose to avoid damage while getting familiar with the controls.

This boat really excels in small lakes or maybe clandestine runs in public fountains with large reflection pools. Lots of fun and full throttle all the way!

The low battery warning signal is an excellent feature that tells you you've got about 30 seconds of run time left so get her back to shore pronto!

A couple minor issues:
1) This boat makes notably better right turns than left turns. I have heard that the slightly larger UDI Venom boat has the same issue since they share the same platform.
2) When testing the self-righting feature, I noticed that sometimes the boat would right itself immediately while other times it took several tries or just didn't happen. I would caution against relying too much on this feature.

Overall, I'm very satisfied with the UDI Bullet. I was initially considering two other boats; the Proboat Impulse 9 or the UDI Venom. I ruled out the Impulse 9 because at $80 it's considerably more expensive.  I ruled out the Venom because the Bullet is slightly smaller and so I thought it would be better for pools.

If you don't have a pool and you plan to run in lakes or larger ponds, consider the UDI Venom or UDI Tempo which share the same platform but are slightly larger. I presume they also have more powerful engines as well. Interestingly, the UDI Venom in the orange paint scheme is actually about 8 bucks *cheaper* on Amazon than the UDI Bullet.

I think this is cute, but costly.  I wouldn't buy this again unless the price was lowered.  I took it out of the package and it worked.  I haven't washed it, so I can't tell if it will die off the first time I do use/wash it.  The price is way over what it should be, but other than that it is ok.

Nice amount of beads, especially for the price - will make LOTS of stuff. I only wish they didn't include quite as many semitransparent colors, especially colors that already have 3-4 solid shades (green and pink for example). I've been supplementing this bucket with the single-color packets of black and white beads but that's only because my designs include a lot of those colors.

This rocket set is a wonderful value for the price. Assembly is simple, though the base could be a bit more sturdy. The pieces come apart easily for storage.

My kids enjoy running and jumping on the launch pad and sending the rockets flying. They like to have competitions to see who can launch them the highest. Adults can send the rockets even higher!

One obvious caveat - if you have lots of trees or a small yard there is a chance that rockets will hang up or get stuck on the roof.

For all the negative reviews, I didn't expect much out of this set.  However, they had buy 1 get 1 half off at a local store so I bought it.  My kids ages 3 and 10 love it, despite its simplicity.  I have owned the blue Tomy trackmaster sets, the tan trackmaster sets, and now this, so I am not new to trackmaster.  My only complaint with this new track is it's harder to snap together, which is why I docked a star.  He can't put it together by himself and be creative as he would with the tan track.

This set goes along with the "Tale of the Brave" movie, and even though this is a very simple track, my 3 year old plays with it for a full hour at a time, rehashing the movie or singing the "Monsters Everywhere" song from the movie while James goes around getting spooked by the attractions on this train set.  Both my Thomas fan kids have enjoyed this set quite a bit so I feel I got my money's worth from it.

I tested the new James on the old tan trackmaster track and he does indeed work.  However, he does not work on the track where the train triggers an action, he just spins.  If you just want him to travel on plain track though, it's fine.  Also, my old trackmaster trains work fine on this set, since the hills on it aren't steep.
Toys_and_Games.summary: Kids like it, especially the movie tie-in aspects

Toys_and_Games.reviewText:
I think the other reviews cover this product pretty well, but I did want to add something from our experience.  We put these up in my son's room, and his bedside lamp at the time had a regular incandescent light bulb.  After a good "charging", the stars would stay bright for maybe 10 or so minutes.  His light bulb burned out and the only replacements we had on hand were CFL.  Not my favorite for a bedroom, but, holy moley, "charging" the stars with a CFL made the stars significantly brighter and longer lasting.

I would say there's a good quantity of stars for a ~16' x 14' bedroom.  Not too overkill.  Obviously, more larger stars would be nice since we wanted to make certain constellations pop out from the tiny the stars you get in the package.  Planets and moons would have been a nice addition to the set too.  The biggest issue was the tiny amount of putty they give you.  Didn't come close to doing all the stars.  We grabbed a package of the un-dyed putty from the local office supplies store and were off to the races.

I bought this for my 3 year old daughter, and she seems to love it. The shapes work better than the pen does (that has always been the case with these), and it seems pretty durable considering how my daughter treats it. Clearing the board takes a few swipes, and it doesn't seem to ever clear it completely, so I'll deduct one star for that.

This looks cool, but I hope my son ends up liking it. It's a Christmas gift so not sure of it's performance yet. What I can say is not to get it off Amazon. I got mine for $37 as a doorbuster price on overstock.com that's including the $2.99 shipping. I got the silver over the yellow cause I just thought it looked nicer. If my son enjoys this toy then I may eventually get the mini one.

This was a hit at our house (I got both the purple Fairytale and the blue Ocean mats).  My only problem with it was that the colors were fairly limited.  Another reviewer had suggested Crayola Pipsqueaks washable markers so I picked those up while waiting for my mat to arrive.  With the addition of the extra colors, the kids had a great time - 2 or 3 at a time at each mat.  The stencils were fun and we had a fun afternoon.

Once folded, the pocket held the markers well and was easy to carry.  I plan on taking these mats to the park the next time we go for a little down-time fun.
Toys_and_Games.summary: Lots of fun but pick up some extra colors to make playtime even more rewarding.

Toys_and_Games.reviewText: My husband and I are both avid readers with large vocabularies and this is our favorite game; we play at least a couple times a week. This is the basic set with no frills. The wooden tiles are well made and clearly stamped, and the board is sturdy and has stood up to being stomped on by our cats when we set the game up on the bed. I subtracted a star for the fact that one of the H tiles was missing when I received it. I didn't bother sending it back, just found an old game at a garage sale and cannibalized it for the letters.
Toys_and_Games.summary: Nerd game par excellence! (I say that with love)

Toys_and_Games.reviewText: Fun for my spawn that likes to get into everything! This is a huge distraction from the everyday normal stuff that she's not supposed to get into. Pretty sturdy in the wear and tear department, as we've had it since Christmas and she's rough on everything... Relatively easy to clean though I'd really prefer to just through it in the wash and be done with it, but I don't think it would survive. Over all a good purchase for a kid that is busy and likes to get into stuff and she thinks she's a princess.

I bought this game for my brother last year for his birthday.  I did that because long ago on his birthday, he actually got this when he was young.  This is one old great game.  I do love this gam, but after too many times of anything; reading a book, watching a movie, or even playing a game; it gets boring, because you actually know what will happen next.  Then I've heard of another 2001 edition.  it  has all up to ruby and sapphire Pokmon.  however, its not the best game.  it is hard and cool thought; but it does remind me of monopoly.  you get poke dollars just like the video game.  the end result has you add up all the money. whoever is richest wins.

I only gave  this game four stars because we are still working on learning how to play this game. We are having a blast with this game and even a child who hasn't played many card games before December wants to play this game even more. My child is the one who will ask to play again because it is fun. Make sure you have plenty of room in case you want to display your cards especially if you're playing with a younger child. When playing we spread our cards out so we can see all the pictures. This game brought tons of laughter, fun and was a great game to enjoy time with the family.
Toys_and_Games.summary: Lots of Fun & Laughter! Fun for the Whole Family!

Toys_and_Games.reviewText: This is a great value of an old classic game. I love that it is compact and small. It takes up less space to store. My daughter loved the colorful plastic player pieces. I love the player pieces too because they will not break or come apart. The board does have a split on it to make it fold-able. The directions were easy to read and follow. I do suggest you read them all before you play though. I didn't catch the whole moving your player up to the next color that you are on if you land on the same square as another person. The thing I wish was a little better were the cards that you draw to move with. Those I am afraid my almost 3 year old will end up tearing in the future because they are very light weight paper. To keep pieces together I do suggest using some snack baggies to hold them. This game is a great value even if my daughter did tear the entire thing up in a few years the price makes it easy for me to replace it with out being upset. Although the game board is pretty sturdy and I don't think that will be an issue.

This is a nice set for any collector.

The set comes with the Super X3 with landing gear, freezer beam, and freezer-missile pod parts, 3 of the ASTOL-MB93 maser jets,  4 MDAW-93 maser tanks, and 4 MBT-92 maser tanks, 1 small building, 1 large building, a display stand, a stage act arm, and a 3-pronged attachment for the display arm to support the jets. The vehicles are all nicely detailed, and perfectly scaled with the monster figures.

The Super X3, the main attraction in the set, is really nicely detailed. The included parts are easy to change out, though they are very small and potentially very easy to lose. The one issue I had is that one of the weapons molded on it's wings, which are very small and thin, was bent out of the blister.

The biggest detractor to this set is the inclusion of only 1 stage act arm. You get the choice to either display  the jets, or display the Super X3 but not both without having an extra display arm sitting around. Luckily I had some extras from a Stage Act 4 set, and the Stage Act 4 set is relatively inexpensive, but it is still disappointing.

Compared to this sets release mate, the Godzilla Effect 2 set, which costs as much as this set but is far bulkier, this set is a bit of a mixed bag. As an avid collector, this was a must have for me, and I am pleased with what is in the set, but they could have included more for the asking price compared to the effect set released alongside it, if at the very least another display arm.

These pins are great! We are planning our first trip to Disney World for our 3 year old. He loves them all. I subtracted one star because we did get a few doubles of the same pins, but that is OK since he can trade those at Disney. As far as I can tell, these are all authentic, and there were quite a few "hidden mickey" pins in our lot. I'd say easily 10. I would definitely order again. We had a lot of "mickey" shaped pins, some Winnie the Pooh pins which my son loves, a couple from "Nightmare Before Christmas" which he also loves, and a few of the original Mickey Mouse characters. Definitely a great lot. I can add photos if anyone would like to see the ones we got.
Toys_and_Games.summary: Perfect for pin trading at Disney with some that we will be keeping!

Toys_and_Games.reviewText:
We were raised to respect critters that got into the house and I learned several ways to fold a piece of paper to safely trap a spider to transport it outside.  About 10 years ago I bought an inexpensive "Bug-Sucker", which made the job easier.

Bought this device a couple of years ago to replace that first one.  It works great, and I like the trap door/magnifier to keep the critter safely inside until I can release it outside.

I've never used it for bug study, and I'm way too old to try to evaluate it from a kid's perspective.  But I have a lot of fun with it, even just as a bug rescue device.

I agree with other reviewers that you REALLY need to put in some "real" batteries to get it to work to its full potential, batteries that come with stuff like this are usually cheap and weak.

I originally discovered this game earlier last year when my friend brought it out for all of us to play. At that time it was two groups of friends being introduced to each other so not all of us were familiar. The game really helped us get out of being shy and before we knew it, we were cracking up on the floor. On a more educational note, I think it provides a great challenge of trying to pull out the right words to describe what was on the card. A lot of us had difficulties at some time, especially the men.
Toys_and_Games.summary: Great Interactive Game to Break the Ice

Toys_and_Games.reviewText: We are the proud grandparents of a 20 month old.  We have 6 horses that she gets to ride when she comes to our house.  She loves horses but lives in the big city of St. Louis, so having a play horse for her Barbie is just grand.  It is her favorite toy to show all guests that come for visits, even the mailman.

I love Wange building blocks. They are 100% compatible with the Lego sets, but have a more modern style as far as the design of the buildings goes. The people are made cheaply and the wheels come off the vehicles too easily when pushed, but these issues don't really affect me since I don't play with the toys. I just build the buildings for my nephew to play with.
Toys_and_Games.summary: Great building designs, 100% compatable with legos, and worth the price!

Toys_and_Games.reviewText:
This is well made.  My kid liked it and plays with a lot. He likes hammering things and using the screw driver.
The only complain is that the nuts are too loose for the holes in the toolbox.  I glued a 2 bolts to the inside of the tool box so that my kid can screw in the nut.  Other than this this was a good buy

Good batteries, half the price of originals. Flew several flights...no issues, voltage was spot on. Charge held up as well as DJI batts. Zero abnormalities. Obviously, this is what DJI should be charging for theirs in the first place. Total scam they have going on with the price of official batteries...knowing that people will want to, dare I say... have to, have more than one battery.

If you guys are wondering why they don't quite make the reassuring "click" sound when you put em in. Look very closely at the tabs on the battery. One tab on the same side on both of mine, is ever so slightly recessed, compared to the DJI batts. Teeny tiny bit. Making it so it doesn't click like it should. Still, seems as secure as the originals, so I'm not worried about it falling out. You almost need to be Popeye to pull these out...or the originals for that matter. Probably a good thing.

Lastly, I'm fairly convinced these have the exact same internals as the DJI batts. Voltage, charge time, flight time...it's all identical. Also, testing the cells manually (holding down the button for 5 seconds) produces the same results as DJI's. Lights lite up for exactly the same amount of time. And all the times of how long each light stays on when you press the button (charge check, powering on, charging)...is exactly the same as the originals. So, these most likely have the very same chip running the "smart" part. Only difference is that tab on one side and the light brightness (one vs three diodes it seems).

What's there to say? These are Fudge dice, specially marked dice for games using the Fate RPG system, such as the Dresden Files RPG and Deadlands Reloaded. The faces don't have your traditional pips or numbers; instead, you get 2 blank sides, 2 sides marked + and two marked -. You roll four Fudge dice, count each + as 1 and each - as -1. Add them up, combine the results with your character's skill value, and you get the result. The dice themselves feel solid, and you get different colored sets of four dice each, enough to spread around the table with your friends. This package is still the best set of Fudge dice I have found for a reasonable price. Most other sets were limited editions (making them currently expensive for dice), or only come in sets of 4 (meaning you'd have to buy multiple sets to get as many as this package). This set is common enough to be affordable, and has plenty of dice for everyone at your table to use.

I got this one for Christmas. I have played it with family and friends. There is a nice balance of trivia between the books and the movies. I tend to dominate in book references, but really stink when it comes to the behind the scenes and actor references.
Game play is pretty much identical to the original Trivial Pursuit game. The nice part about this game is that even kids can play it... I have played with kids as young as 9 and they have been able to answer quite a few of the questions.

This expansion comes with four new board sections, each with a new location that grants a special power. One of the cooler aspects of this expansion is that if you collect a token from both of the new locations on the tile, you get an additional bonus tile that can be used to either perform a powerful additional bonus action (such as building your first mandatory settlement of your turn on a spot that is NOT adjacent to an existing settlement), or a more powerful version of the original extra action (such as building on a mountain terrain!).

There are also a few new Kingdom Builder cards that add more variety to the game, as well as 5 new terrain cards that each include one of the original terrain types, and the new marshland terrain.  So you can use them even if you don't have any of the expansion boards out.

If you're already in love with Kingdom Builder and just want more, this expansion will be right up your alley.  If you aren't a fan, this expansion won't change your mind.

If I had any complaints about the product, it's that the box is a little large for what you get inside it.  They probably could have made it half the depth.  Of course, if you have the Kingdom Builder Big Box to store everything in, that may not be an issue.  Also, the retail price for it is also a bit high for the contents (thank goodness I got it at a steep discount).
Toys_and_Games.summary: A solid expansion for a one of the all-time classic family games

Toys_and_Games.reviewText:
We'll give this 5 stars. It works well, but our son 3 years old was just too old to enjoy this as much as we thought he would. We have it with our other baby toys in a treasure chest end table, and other children who visit (many different children) will love to pull it out and play with it.
We were just disappointed that our son didn't want to play with it as much as we hoped.

We got the truck in perfect condition and my husband and son both love it! Took a little bit of work getting familiar with what to do since it was our first hobby truck but when we got started it was great. The only thing was that the truck stopped responding to the remote one time and went out of control! However, I think that was because there was another frequency controlling it. Anyway we love the truck and would recommend getting it.
Toys_and_Games.summary: My son and husband love this truck!

Toys_and_Games.reviewText: I bought these for my toddler grandson.  We both love them!  The letters are lightweight with a magnetic backing.  They hand wash nicely - a good thing with a toddler.  The magnets are just perfect for the letters - strong enough to stick very well, but not too strong for baby hands.  Very pleased with this purchase.

You know for a split second I actually had to re-check the name of the company that makes these stuffed rabbits for children.  They're called Webkinz.  At first I seriously thought that word was a pun of the famous Elmer Fudd line "Wabbit!" (you know, when he's hunting for Bugs Bunny, haha).  Where was MY mind!!  Anyway, this stuffed rabbit is an adorable toy for any child that has a desire to cuddle up to their animal collection while they sleep.  It's sturdy, adorable, dependable and worth spending your money on.  Of course do NOT let your dog get ahold of this rabbit or it WILL be destroyed!

Once you try these cards, you will never want to use anything else again.
Easy to shuffle, slide great, will not bend during normal use.  If you have some serious card bending poker friends, these cards will more than hold up.  The jumbo index are a little more expensive, but worth it if you have a ten pack.  I have only had them for a couple of weeks and have played about 5 games of hold-em, but they have not become mishapen at all.
Normally I only get one nights use out of a deck of regular cards.  They will pay for themselves in no time!!!
Toys_and_Games.summary: These cards are worth every penny!!!

Toys_and_Games.reviewText: We stayed with a friend at his painstakingly remodeled farm house in Connecticut, we live in Seattle, and thought he needed a tractor.  Since the house was from the late 1800's this one seemed to fit and would be a great addition to all the antiques he had purchased around the area.  We hope he loves it.  We do wish that the seller had a way to send it as a gift, as we have had to send it to ourselves and now have to repackage and mail it.

Quick to put together and easy to operate for even a small child.  The 1 year old only took 3 minutes to figure out how to start the music going and the balls popping, and it's now the first toy he heads for in the morning.  When he gets a little older, he'll start fetching the balls himself.

It needs 4 D-cell batteries, and I'd recommend rechargeables as they'll take quite a beating!  You can tell when they're wearing down because balls won't pop right out of the toy onto the floor.

My only criticism is that it's a little loud, so ours mysteriously "doesn't work" early in the morning.  (He hasn't found the ON switch yet, thankfully...)  But the child loves it!

I bought this for a 28 month old boy for Christmas and he absolutely loves it! Another 14 month old had a lot of fun playing with it as well. The dad of the 28 month old didn't want his son playing with a toy kitchen so a grill was a nice compromise. They placed in on the screened in porch nearby dad's grill so they go outside and grill together. It is great quality for the price and seems to be very weather resistant.

I read mix reviews about this product but it was so inexpensive that I didn't care if they came out bad.  When I received the product it was a bit disappointing but honestly they turned out to be amazing. The flowers are plastic so they come stuck together, you just have to rub them against each other to separate them. What they worked best for was decoration I took one of each color snip them and tied them together to make one long string of flowers and then I decorated the door frame of the restroom, and garage. Made it look really festive, luau pop.

This is a great kitchenthe colors are great, it has a cool vintage look, and our son loves it.  Its a smaller kitchen and best suited for a corner location, but we knew both of those things when we ordered it and its exactly what we wanted.  Assembly was time consuming, but the instructions were clear and the parts were clearly labeled.

I am big collector of Pullip dolls and this is my first time purchasing an Isul doll.  His stock clothing is made extremely well with very elegant details.  His features are very soft and gentle...he looks very similar to his sister Pullip.  This is a delicate doll and not meant for a child to play with but rather for display.
