Toys_and_Games.reviewText: This is a cute Christmas Angel that is one of three. The other two are Ty Beanie Baby - Gift the Bear Love (White Version) (Hallmark Gold Crown Ex... and Ty Beanie Baby - Gift the Bear (Red Version) (Hallmark Gold Crown Exclusive) Christmas. We bought this for our 6 year old daughter. She loved "Clever Castle" but is now bored with it. This is the perfect solution. The "easy" puzzles are challenging for her now, and she can grow into the harder puzzles. I love that all the brightly colored game pieces are contained in the game board ... one less game box for me to mess with.

Bought for my 13 month old. She loves the squeak toy in the alligator's head. The book is soft and has lots of bright colors so my daughter plays with it frequently. We've had to toss it in the wash a few times in the last few months due to spit up and it's held up great! Well worth the price and would purchase again!

Toys_and_Games.reviewText: This puzzle is made by my favorite Ravensburger! I enjoyed making it and then I gave it to my friend. They love it too. I love the colors of the one I got. This is in reply to the other reviews. I don't have any single complain about this one. I enjoyed making it and love the picture!

My teen son verbalized that he wanted a German Shepherd, knowing it can't happen...but I bought this plush to go with a World Wildlife Fund donation (Adopt a Working Dog -German Shepherd) for him, so  it needed to look like a real shepherd dog. Toys_and_Games.reviewText: This is a great puzzle, and it is very well made.  My daughter started playing with it when she was about 18 months old.  Even though she couldn't always put the pieces in the correct spot, she still loved to play with them.  Now that she is 2 yrs old, and able to complete the puzzle with ease, she likes it even more.  I am trying to buy a puzzle rack to accommodate this and a few other Melissa and Doug chunky puzzles.  I hope they will fit.

My son got a train-set and train-table for Christmas, so I got this to go with everything.  The coolest part about this is the fact that it is battery operated.  My son is 19 months old, and he just gets a kick out of watching it chug around the track on its own.  The battery doesn't last too long, but it's just a single AAA.  I love Brio, and I like the fact that it is compatible with other sets.

Bought it the moment it POPped up on Amazon.  Box was in great condition.  Drogon has a very solid build, making him heavy.  Painting is beautifully done on this magnificent dragon.  Dany had a barely noticeable minuscule line across her left eye.  I was able to scratch most of it off, and you can't see it when she's in the box.  One of the best figures Funko POP has ever produced!  The price should be $25.00, but I know it will rise as demand increases.  Therefore get it while it's still below $30.00!
Toys_and_Games.summary: Get it now before the price rises!

Toys_and_Games.reviewText:
With all the negative reviews about third party inflation, most people have forgotten to review the actual figure! Yes, it's only $25 at the Disney Store or on their website, but enough about that.

People have given Disney so much grief about their SW acquisition, it's hard to see the GOOD things people are saying about it, this series being one of those good things. The Elite Series is a collector oriented line of diecast figures that really hits the mark and Captain Phasma illustrates that point very well. I have heard people compare some of the Elite Series figures to the Black Series figures, in this case it's really a moot point. Of all the TFA characters Phasma was the most perfectly suited to the diecast style, even though they didn't really use the properly reflective material for her armor.

All the masked figures in this series look great. As the description of the series says on the back, the makers of these figures have worked very closely with Lucasfilm to make the most faithful reproduction of these characters possible, and for the most part they have. I haven't (and probably won't) collect any of the figures outside of TFA without a helmet or mask. Main reason being if there is one shortcoming with this series it is that the paint and sculpt for the human faces aren't the best (especially if you're familiar with NECA).

All in all these figures are not expensive and fall somewhere in line between looking and feeling like a Sideshow Collectibles type statue and a great action quality figure. If you are a Star Wars fan I would highly recommend this series.
Toys_and_Games.summary: A Review About the Actual Item

Toys_and_Games.reviewText: This game is fun and a bit different than your normal game as you use the box as part of your board! It plays differenlty too and keeps you engaged. Lots of fun to play but it is a game for 3 or more players. It was very easy to figure out how to play the game. (About 40 min to learn and about an 75 min to play.) Def. buy if you are looking for something new and unique. It is out of print on the Days of wonder website but you may be able to find it on amazon or ebay or other websites. I bought mine from a small gameing store in Chicago and I live in CA.

I bought this for a small niece.  If my daughter had one of these when she was small, she'd have LOVED it. As others have said, this is a great toy.  This will inspire imagination. No electronics or flashing lights here.  Simple and timeless and almost every small child will love it.
The log is about a foot tall, not very big.  Each animal is small but plenty big enough.  This is great in that makes for multi-dimensional play.  Kids can play with one animal at a time or all together.  It is also small enough that it won't be met with thoughts of "where am I going to put it" by parents. The animals go back into their log after play, so hopefully no frantic scrambling to find the favorite at bedtime.

My grandson is only 2 but loves this 4 wheeler.  He had a little 6 volt car that he rides but it always gets stuck in the grass and doesn't want to go uphills, even on concrete.  I had to buy a helmet for this ride on toy, as my grandson goes full blast and even at 2.5 mph it's much faster than you think when you're chasing him.  He hits my house will full force so the helmet is a safety precaution to make sure he doesn't get hurt if he gets thrown out.  I know this is for an older child, however, my grandson is enjoying this so much because his little short lets don't stretch out far enough to reach some of the pedals on the other ride on cars/trucks/toys.  With this the vehicle, you move it forward by pressing the pedal down on the floorboard.....so length of legs is not an issue for him because he's just pressing down instead of out in front of himself.  He hasn't mastered turning the handle bars quite yet but has almost mastered the understanding of pressing the button to go backwards if he gets himself in a jam.  The wheels are great in that they have great traction pretty much anywhere, short of wet grass.  All-in-all I am thrilled with this purchase.

I'm a fan of non electric toys that inspire kids to use their imaginations so these were appealing to me. I got them for my oldest kids for Christmas (3 & 4) and they sort of ignored them until my nephew (8) played with them. Now my kids can't get enough!! I guess they just needed to see them in action. I will say that they slip around on the hardwood so they now only use them in carpeted areas only, not an issue here but if you don't have carpet that could be an issue ;-).

I love this kitchen. I did a ton of research before finally ordering this kitchen for my 21 month old daughter for Christmas. I cannot wait to see her face Christmas morning. She and her cousins are going to have so much fun playing with it. It was kind of a headache to assemble but my husband did it fairly simply one weekend. Took him about 6 hours to assemble once he separated all of the parts. We were missing one bolt and I plan to contact Kidkraft to have them send it to us.

I love this thing. I lover purple and so does my daughter and love the princess style of the tent. She had a Frozen tent, but this one is much roomier. Not sure I would put any balls in it like the product displays, but great place for my daughter to let her imagination flow as a princess in her own castle tent! There is enough room to even have a friend in there with her! The tunnel is nice too, but the tent is used more.

I bought this harmonica for my two-year-old grandson for Christmas. He loved it. He played it for most of the day. We had to pry it out of his hands at bedtime. It is well-made for the price, and where else can you find a toy that entertains a toddler for hours! I was so pleased with it that I came back and ordered two more in case he loses or breaks this one.

Everything came as expected. The dice are cheap, both in price and quality, but they get the job done. The colors aren't great (who wants bright orange dice for DnD?) but the numbers are readable on all of them, which is why I bought this cheap set over a similar one. If you just need some cheap, functioning dice, these will suit you just fine.

I received a sample of this FLOATING GLOBE in exchange for an honest review. At about 12 inches high-total, it is smaller than I hoped it would be. Also the cord that it comes with is pretty short and you'll need an extension-cord to put it on a shelf or table, where it looks best. All the same ... it IS a very "interesting" and fascinating conversation piece. Perfect for a Den, boys/girls bedroom or playroom.

The AT-TE is one of my favorite Star Wars, and really deserved to have a new lego set of it. I was glad that lego made this set as one of their Clone Wars sets. The build is long, easily over an hour. The finaly product is well worth the effort; it is bigger than you might expect and full of fun details. When combined with other legos you can really have a fun battle! One of my favorite design elements is a sturdy handle for when you want to move it or put it away.

Wow.  The dimensions show something about 24" and less than a pound.  So I bought it thinking it's small and can be used as a prop for a small child's costume (approx 2 feet in size would be perfect, and light weight).

Instead, it's 7 feet long and heavy.  Where on the site is this disclosed?  The package is over 2lbs, this thing is big.  Please, get your descriptions at least somewhat right.  Awful waste of time, shipping/money, and now my son's costume will be incomplete.  Awful item.
Toys_and_Games.summary: Item is noting like the description - it's 7 ft long!

Toys_and_Games.reviewText: No actual setup guide for DX6e users. I've used the DX6 ,DX7-8 and DX6i set up and it just flies horrible. I've owned a Blade CPX and that flew like a champ on my DX6i (I no longer have). I couldn't bring myself to give it anymore stars due to the lack of proper setup guides for the DX6E transmitter.

the predator sb was falsely advertised as a 4 channel. its is not! will not fly left and right. customer support is a joke. for half the price you can get the wL toys v912 helicopter witch is true 4channel and flys MUCH, MUCH better, parts are cheaper. where the fly bar on the protocol predator sb is plastic and breaks all the time, the wltoys is metal. i've had two of the predator SB helis

I bought these thinking that it would be much better than good polished axles due to the fact that the graphite would last a while on the wheels.  When I installed them the day before the race, I found that the wheels were so snug that they wouldn't spin freely.  I put the axle into my drill and then used the drill to spin them while I held a washcloth tightly against it to remove some of the graphite.  Even after doing this the wheels would still not spin really well.  After a lot of work doing this, I finally got them to the point where they were OK.  Keep in mind that I also bought some of the wheels that were lathed and hollowed out on the inside.  My car actually weighed 5.09 ounces on my scale, but on the derby scale they didn't have hundredths and it weighed 5.0 ounces there and passed inspection.  I put all of the weight in the back of the car which is supposed to be best.  The car was amazing.  So here is how we ended up.

My son's car came in 4th place.  The car that came in first place was made from the same kit as ours.  They put the weight at the bottom in the middle.  His car had good polished axles and he added graphite.  His car was so much faster than ours that it blew me away!  The other two cars that beat us were no where near the quality of car - it came down to the speed of the wheels/axles.  HOWEVER, all this said, my son was proud to come in 4th and had a great time, so I didn't share my frustration with him about these axles.  Next year he will be old enough to help me more and I look forward to that.  I will just buy some good quality polished axles next year.  Hope this helps anyone looking at which axles to buy.

These are really poor tub crayons.  They don't color well.  They are much more fragile than another set of tub crayons that we purchased.  I was excited when we got them due to having more colors than some of the other sets out there, but since none of the crayons color nearly as well as other sets we have purchased, they went in the trash fairly quickly.

My 2 year old got this for Christmas from his brother. He opened the box, my husband blew it up. About 4 hours later, the thing was completely shredded. When he hit it, it came apart at the seams. Which then led to the kids trying to climb inside the deflate broken tiger. So not safe at all. I will not be rebuying it for him because I am certain it would suffer the exact same fate. Very disappointed.

I am very disappointed in this product.  From the picture, the carrying case looks sturdy and well made.  That is not the case.  It is made so cheaply and unattractive that I am embarrassed to give it to my grandson as a Christmas gift.  Wal-mart has a much better quality Ninja Turtle Travel Kit that should last a long time, and the price is better. Don't waste your money on this product.

m very disappointed in this product. From the picture, it looks very nice.  That is not the case.  I'm embarrassed to give the art kit this to my grandson as a Christmas gift.  the

Toys_and_Games.reviewText: My 1 year old got this for his birthday in June. He loved it at first. But it soon stopped moving forward when you press the smokestack. It seems like some wires are crossed. Instead of going forward, the wheels move an inch and then it says whatever level it is on. So annoying. Sounds like this is a common problem with this toy based on what others are saying. I love Fisher Price, but we are so disappointed with this toy. It barely lasted 2 months. :( :(

This mask was split in 2 when it reached me. While it may be been mishandled during shipment, I blame the seller for not packaging it well enough to prevent such breakage. I received 3 other masks from other sellers in pristine condition. Granted they were more expensive than this. I guess you get what you pay for.

I got it and it was defective. A piece on the inside was missing and it could not be put together completely. The biggest problem is that the box was opened (I did not mind that) for inspection I guess and it passed inspection!!! How did it pass?! My son really wanted this, but there were no more available so we ended up getting the Legendary Megazord.

It came open in a drawstring bag was supposed to be a gift for my kid but you look at it and don't know what it is, bag it was in was dirty appeared used. Also small holes in it, I'm not going to waste my time giving a crummy gift. Returning. Dot waste money, looks like it came out of stolen Goods box truck.

Toys_and_Games.reviewText: I wanted to love it and was prepared for the hours of installation based on the other reviews, but I am so disappointed in the QC of the product parts.  The elevator is essentially upside down!  We spent over an hour trying to get it together as described- looked at the color picture on line and everything, but alas- it wasn't to be.  And as a Christmas gift, we have no time to return/exchange it.  We thought we were being good putting it together on the 23rd.  I don't think my daughter will notice although some older cousins and friends might.  I notice and I paid for it so I am highly disappointed!
Toys_and_Games.summary: Parts made wrong!  Upside down (sort-of) elevator!

Toys_and_Games.reviewText:
I bought this truck for my son who LOVED it.  After not even 15 minutes of play time, the mechanism for the trash can...which is the most fun feature for toddlers, BROKE.  I returned and exchange it for another one so that I could tell my son I fixed it.  After a couple weeks of play, the mechanism BROKE AGAIN.  I had to explain to my son that it couldn't be fixed because I'm not going to go through the agony of having it break a 3rd time.

Both two guns are good guns, the colt is a pistol probably my favorite gun, the  strongarm is kinda a revolver I personally think it's good for nerd war its easy to load,cock,and shoot. Toys_and_Games.reviewText:
The ball is a lot of fun to play with. However, there are much cheaper beachballs that achieve this same effect without the disappointment of being geographically inaccurate in more than a couple of places, some of historical significance to at least one continent. There is a patch you get with the set that you could technically mark-up and paste onto the neglected areas of importance to you if you're so inclined... but the patch kit is supposed to be for when the ball tears.

Blowing up the ball is a major invitation to a sugary chemical toxic billow cloud coming out at you. Thank you for that kick in the pants, manufacturer!

I think the two omissions that caused me to write this review both have something to do with the concept of the Asia-centered world map, which places China at the center (China being translated into 'middle country' or 'middle kingdom' originally) splitting the Atlantic Ocean and messes up places like Iceland, the nine Azores archipelago islands, Madeira, Canary Islands, the discoveries of which awakened the crowned heads of Europe to the idea that there's land out there to be settled and found - as opposed to splitting the world map from the internationally-agreed upon date line running down the Pacific. The propaganda mindset shows in the neglected geography - it's just easier not to have to think about lining up these places if you just omit them on your way to totally ignoring what the international community decided on for a world map. And you should see the stretch they did on the land from India to S.E. Asia. Bangladeshis will be very happy to learn their coast has been stretched to more than double what it is in reality. Perhaps they can ship some of the land back to the Azores as a humanitarian donation.

A nice promising ball but ultimately a bit big for road trips with kids and not really your best educational friend for your kid once you actually start getting down to the brass tacks. Speaking of brass tacks...
Toys_and_Games.summary: Get something smaller and less Sino-centric

Toys_and_Games.reviewText: This is a rip-off of Trouble, but not the classic one, the horrible updated one that has terrible pieces that don't stay put. And the packaging is just god-awful. Instead of having a normal board game box with a lid and a base, the box opens on the side. So unless you get a baggie for all the matching cards, they just slide right out of the ends of the box. Do yourself a favor and buy a well-produced board game.

Then the other ear did the same thing. Also, where the brown stripes in back attach to the yellow part, it ripped apart there, and now the stuffing is coming out! The slide is pretty much worthless as my kids don't like the sprinkler spraying water in their face. Without having the water running down the slide, the kids don't move when sitting on the slide, AT ALL. So no going down the slide.

There are 2 water release valves on the bottom of both pools but for some reason I was unable to pull the valves open, which made for many bucket runs to empty the pool.

Toys_and_Games.reviewText: This item has 6 pages. But only the first one (dog with number 1) crinkles. My baby likes the crinkling sound and feature very much, which is from our baby Einstein bouncer. However, he lost it when we took him out for a walk. So I want to buy a new one from baby Einstein to make it up. However, it is disappointing since one one has the feature.

THE BEBOP IS EASILY WORTH 5 STARS, but not in it's current condition - I will explain.

Background:
I am not new to flying drones. My first drone was the DJI Phantom 2 vision plus - a much more delicate and breakable drone when crashed then the Bebop, but it is also bigger, a lot more powerful, takes better video quality, and originally costing about $400 to $500 more then the Bebop with a Skycontroller.

Bebop Pros:
*The Bebop is very durable for a drone and can take a good amount of crashes without breaking parts. This is huge, because as a new drone pilot you will crash, period.- and probably quite a bit too. Where with other drones, like the Phantom 2 Vision plus, parts will break (like the gimbal) and camera and that alone costs, about $600. to replace.

*The Bebop's video is extremely stable and sturdy without a gimbal. This is huge too. No moving parts, less things that will break when you crash. Video quality isn't as good as say the Phantom 2 Vision plus, but it's well worth the trade to have a very smooth video - and I prefer the Bebop's technology for video stabilization then that of a gimbal.

*Drone is pretty small. Some might think this is a downsize, but I found it a lot more convenient then with my Phantom. It's easy to carry from place to place. I have more confidence using this around my smaller kids, then I do with the larger Phantoms. It's less spicuous to use  when out in public and in parks.

*Skycontroller - The Skycontroller really is the only way to use the Bebop. It has decent distance and makes the Drone much easier to use.

Cons - in this order:
*Price - This is the biggest concern.
With the introduction of DJI Phantom 3, they have set a new standard of quality and value for your money - like it or not. The Bebop with Skycontroller currently is $899.00. The Phantom 3 Advance is $999.00 and it is incredibly superior for only a $100.00 more. It's like buying a Moped for $899.00 or buying a Ducati for $999.00. Are you getting it now?

*Skycontroller \ Price.
The Bebop without the Skycontroller is really just a ridiculously over priced $500.00 toy. Sorry it's true. Without the Skycontroller you don't have the range or distance to really use the drone seriously.. Again, think of buying a Corvette but then being told you can never leave the  Cul-de-sac (dead end street) that you live on with the Corvette. Ya, it's exactly like that. And if you want to buy the Skycontorller separately it's $400 and stupendously expensive - so no win here.

*Cheaply made
For $899.00 I'd expect Parrot to make the Bebop drone feel like I was getting a block of gold, yet instead what I got feels very cheaply made as others have stated. 2 rubber landing gear lost on it's maiden flight. People have complained about this from the beginning and Parrot has done nothing to fix the wrong, at least with DJI, they came out with several versions of the Phantom 2 Vision Plus, in trying to correct problems and make a better drone, but not here with the Bebop. The battery connections has to be held on with a $0.25 Velcro strap. REALLY??? A $900.00 package and I am holding the battery to my Drone with a $0.25 Velcro strap. I would of respected Parrot more if they included a role of duct-tape, but then again that cost more then $0.25 and the price of the drone might of gone up another $50 bucks.

*Lastly Flight time.
With the stock batteries you're lucky if get 7 to 11 minutes of flight time. I'm sorry, $900.00 not acceptable for the price when Phantoms are hitting 16 to 20 minute flight times and the Yuneec Q500+ (you can now get at $999.00) can do 25 minutes of flight time. 7 minutes, 10 minutes, really not enough time to set shots you want to take video of and or pictures. It's just ridiculous .

Would I buy this product again? No, I just can't for it's price.
As much I like the Bebop and in many ways prefer it over DJI's Phantoms for everyday flying and want to give it 5 stars, good common sense tells me, no way - just not worth the money. If the whole package, (Bebop and Skycontroller) was $500.00 I'd still think twice in light of the Phantom 3 Advance, but at least it would be at a price point enough to temp me if I really didn't know any better and had no way of getting $1,000 to buy the more expensive drones. Remember, Moped or a Ducati. But then again, sometimes it just might still be worth the save $1000.00 for the Ducati then to buy a $500 Moped.

Personally, I would like to see what Parrot does with the next version of the Bebop. hopefully they will learn some lessons and, they will price more line with what they are offering in compareds to the competition and make the product with more quality so it can feel like a premium product for it's price.
Toys_and_Games.summary: THE BEBOP IS EASILY WORTH 5 STARS

Toys_and_Games.reviewText:
This is not the best for three reasons:  First, it's really hard to put together.  Second, the windshield is dark grey and not see through, so I couldn't even install it or my two year old wouldn't be able to see (he's still short).  Third, it doesn't get traction on most surfaces, and seems to need perfectly level asphalt.

Pros:
- Car is a good size with a good amount of power.  My 37 pound 4 year old could ride it fine.
- Theoretically, you only need a phillips head screw driver to assemble this.
- Battery comes fully charged, so you can get immediate gratification, by putting it together with your child (my two kids were excited about putting it together, and they handed me parts and held the screw driver for me) then driving it.
- Can tip up and rest on the back bumper, so it can store smaller leaned against a wall.  Storage is pretty big, but not as big as if it couldn't get stood up on its back bumper.

Cons:
- To get to the battery, like to be able to charge it, you have to unscrew two screws to take off a plastic battery cover.  Those screws can come all the way out of the battery cover.  You know how some toys, the screws come out of the toy, but the screw stays in the cover when it's all the way loose, so you can't loose the screw.  This is not like that. You loosen it, and you have to keep track of the two screws, for hours, while the battery charges.
- Assembly was awful.  For the front plastic piece under the windshield, there are two holes in it and two holes in the body of the car, and you screw it on there.  But, the holes did not line up.  The holes on the plastic piece under the windshield were too close together.  I had to get out a drill and move them to get them 1/8 inch farther apart.  Such a tiny little amount to widen the holes, and the factory should have had better quality control.
- Assembly was awful.  Each tire has a huge rubber band that you put on it for traction.  This is really hard to get on, and you need to put it on four times for four tires.  Yuck!  You need the rubber band too, or else the car will end up with the single drive tire spinning, digging a hole in your yard.  (It's one wheel drive, but that doesn't seem to affect performance once you have the rubber bands on.)  Instructions for these tires say put the rubber bands in hot water to get them easier to get on, and putting them in hot water did make them stretchy and easy to pop right on.  So now you need a bucket of hot water too along with your drill for the misaligned holes.  I really think they should have put these bands on in the factory, where some machine could just have stretched them and popped them on with no fuss.
- Windshield plastic is dark grey.  The product photo shows it clear, and the pic on the side of the box shows it clear, but really it is very dark grey.  My 4 year old is tall enough his head is over the windshield.  My 2 year old is short and he said he couldn't see through the wind shield, so I just didn't install the windshield.  This makes for a different look and feel to the car, so be aware.
- No traction on most surfaces.  Before putting rubber bands on, no traction anywhere.  After putting rubber bands on, traction only on perfectly flat asphalt.  No traction on grass, and when it gets to the middle of the road, where there is a small curve to the asphalt, it skids and needs to be pushed.

To drive, there is a button for forward and reverse that the child can push.  Then the child pushes a foot pedal to go.  The 4 year old had no problem driving around and liked it.  The 2 year old (maybe 2 years 2 months, so just turned 2 and is 25 pounds) understood how to make it go, but had some trouble.  Partly, he can't really steer.  Partly, he had some trouble pushing the pedal.  Partly, the car doesn't drive on most surfaces and is frustrating even for the 4 year old.  He was excited to sit in the car, though.  He'll grow into it, but be aware if that's your age/weight range, this toy may be old for them.

Instructions say up to 50 pound child.

I feel like this is a toy to where the quality control at the factory is bad and it's hit or miss if you get a dud or not.  Probably, a year from now, I will have forgotten the pain of assembly and maybe at that time I will look back and think how awesome a toy.  But right now, I am so upset about the misaligned screw holes.  If it's a gift, put it together ahead of time, and give yourself a full day.  If you are gifting to someone in another city and you won't visit to assemble it, then maybe look elsewhere if the parents are not too mechanical with a toolbox.  I think if all the holes had lined up perfectly, then I would have given a good review, and really it was just those two holes - other parts lined up fine.

Also, this is really key:  My husband thinks the alignment is off and that's why it's giving trouble driving and can't drive on most surfaces.  That fits with screwholes not lining up and steering column being hard to get in.  The steering column felt like it wanted to be almost an inch to the side and I had to force it into the hole in the dashboard where the steering wheel goes.  I am now thinking that the dashboard for my car was manufactured wrong and am thinking to disassemble and maybe mount it with totally new holes a bit to the side.  I really am good mechanically, and do most household repairs.  I think the way the Jeep I got was made is wrong, but not all the reviews are bad, so maybe the factory has ten production lines and nine are good but one is not and I got off the bad one.

Other reviews about the car not going say to add something to the wheels for more traction.  From googling that, I see that you can get bike tires and take the tread and glue it on the wheels.  Supposedly, according to online forums, this will burn out the motor faster with more friction on gears.  I dunno.  The bottom line is, with this unit I got of this Jeep model, I didn't get a functional toy and instead got some kind of expensive googling things and fixing up this project.

I also got another Power Wheels, the Frozen 2 seater Mustang, and that other one runs great on all kinds of surfaces.  I think skip this Jeep and instead get a different model with better quality control at the factory.
Toys_and_Games.summary: Hard to assemble; doesn't drive well; maybe bad quality control at the factory

Toys_and_Games.reviewText: Purchased  gift purchase  for an upcoming birthday.  Box appeared to have sat on a store shelf for years - still had a layer of dust on top. Original store price sticker still attached with a another sticker covering it.  Box is tattered and not great for gift giving.  See photos.  Actual operation of the toy is still to be discovered.

I bought this tube for a river float trip last weekend.  This tube is very big and seems like it would be very nice IF it did not come with a hole in it.  We noticed the tube was deflating after only five minutes of it being taken out of the box and blown up and we figured maybe the heat had something to do with it. So we transported it down to the river on the shuttle and by the time we got there it was completely flat, besides the cooler.  We then had a worker help us air it up completely with an air pump and then we walked the tube down into the river which was about a two minute process where we carried it all the way in which the tube was completely flat.  At this point we had to scramble to find tubes that other people had accidentally left behind so we did not get left by our group.  This was very stressful and as much as I would like to either patch it up or send it back to Amazon, I was forced to leave the tube on the side of the river so we were able to float with our group.  Not saying this tube is bad, but my experience was not the best.  I would suggest blowing it up beforehand and letting it sit if you need it for an all day float trip like I did just to make sure there are no holes.

Okay so I bought this to give as a Christmas gift to a child that loves things that light up.  The package arrived quickly as expected.  Putting the batteries in this thing is a real pain in the rear it requires a tiny screw driver (included in the package) and and multiple clasps and fasteners etc.  The ball itself once turned on plays a very loud obnoxious snippet of a song that lasts about 10 seconds and repeats it self over and over and over it tries your patience quite quickly.  The lights are colorful and the gyrating motion is strong really making it bounce and roll around the house. SInce the package came with 2 briteballs I let my dog chase one around the house at first she was terrified of it then she loved it chasing it and barking at it and then she killed it in about 3 days.  Now onto  the good stuff.  The way you turn this thing on and off is by depressing a metal pin that is quite small and almost impossible to find when its on and lights are blinding you and the thing is jumping around. So I get a panicked call from my husband.  He had delivered the toy to the child for Christmas and set it up for her but he said as soon as he pushed in the pin to turn it on the pin fell out leaving it stuck on.  He said he couldn't get the batteries out because it was gyrating and blinding him making it impossible to find the tiny screws and use the tiny screwdriver LOL.  He said it had been going off for hours and was so loud and obnoxious it was driving everybody crazy.  And he didn't know what to do so he threw it in his car to try to wait out the batteries.  So the thing is bouncing around his car crashing into things and shooting colored strobe lights out of the window.  HAHA so of course he calls me and is like what do I do?  He finally got it turned off by using the little screwdriver to poke through the hole where the pin had been to get it off.  Needless to say that thing went straight in trash.  Ohh if I could have been a fly on the wall.
Toys_and_Games.summary: Your going to want to read this review!!

Toys_and_Games.reviewText:
Nice, soft football. Serious color shedding after 2 months of indoor use. Makes a mess.

Updated review - this football has only gotten worse after the initial shedding.  Red and blue are all over our apartment and now there are holes in the football body that our son can stick his fingers into (he can' help himself) and made even bigger.

Wouldn't recommend this football and won't buy this brand again.

Super cute high quality doll for a toddler. Much cuter in person and looks to be even better quality than I was expecting.
Edit June 2018: I've had the doll about 6 months now and it hasn't really been used but I had to wash it because one of my cats got a hairball on her. Nothing said to undress before washing so I left her dressed. Now her body is covered in stains from her top. Her hair also got hopelessly tangled despite precautions to prevent such. Had I known the possible issues, I would have just hand washed. Deducted 2 stars.
Keep finding more issues. Tons of shedding from hair as well and I see there was color bleeding from the eye embroidery as well leaving big black/blue splotches above her eyes. This is super disappointing. She should probably be labeled as surface wash only.
Toys_and_Games.summary: Super cute high quality doll for a toddler. DO NOT MACHINE WASH.

Toys_and_Games.reviewText: I was excited to get these but very disappointed with them. The package came with 2 big stars, a couple medium sized, a few small ones and then a ton of TINY little stars. The colors are nice and they look pretty on the walls but I wish there were more big stars. Unlike other reviewers I didn't have a problem with not enough putty, I had just enough to hang them all up. However they are already falling off the walls (my 5 year old is excited to find stars on the floor, atleast). They only glow for a few minutes too, even after spending a day in a ton of sunlight in my girls room.

This kit as a scale model lacks much. Scale wise it is too short (height wise) and not long enough. If you count the gun ports and the cannons you add to the top deck it is only a 78 gun ship (Victory is a 3 decker of 100 guns!) As just a model kit it is not bad, the parts fit well and the engraving is decent. For a beginning modeler it would be a good place to start. It is not overly complex and is a rather straightforward build. The kit I recived has thread for the rigging but no rigging chart (which is referred to in the instructions).

I loved this game when I was a child so I was very excited to give it to my kids at Christmas.  When did they start making it so cheap?!  The whole point of the game is to be banging on the lever to get as many balls as possible (and they give you only a few balls) but when it is made of cheap, thin plastic that snaps together, it breaks everytime.  This is really disappointing.

The train itself is great, runs fast and seems to be sturdy.  The Batman figure is very small and doesn't hook properly to the zip line.  The buildings are sturdy cardboard, but tip over when the zip line is used.  My 4-yr-old grandson is used to the quality of Thomas Trains, so this was a bit of a disappointment because he had to be too careful with the whole set for it to function as described.
Toys_and_Games.summary: The train itself is great, runs fast and seems to be sturdy

Toys_and_Games.reviewText:
This kit ultimately had the parts needed to fix my chopper, the upper main shaft assembly.

However the blades in this kit were all the same, just four 'A' blades, no 'B' blades, so I was only able to replace the worn uppers.

Also the fit of the tail fin buckle was too large, and I had to use the original lug to get it to fit snugly into the new fin.

I got the part I needed to fly, but I spent the extra couple of dollars hoping for a refresh, which I didn't get.

This item is good for the stuff inside the journal, but is horrible for the voice password.  My daughter had to keep resetting it and rerecording her password.  I was with her when she was doing it and it sounded exactly the same, but it wouldn't take it and then she would get upset because it wouldn't open.  Good concept, but not well executed.  It made for a very unhappy child.  There are some out there that are better, but I just don't think the voice password is there yet for child journals.  I would not recommend you buy this, if the excitement is over the password part and not the EAH stuff inside.

This is a popular toy with my adopted grandkids.  The fact that it is Disney's Frozen characters makes it popular right off the bat.  It is an interactive toy with a brief musical interlude about building the snowman which even I find quite cute and intriguing.  This reminds me of toys that I played with (albeit updated version) but the bicycle, the dolls, all can be used for imaginative play.  I recommend this for children old enough not to put the smaller pieces in their mouth (I would say that this is the only draw back to the toy and thus why it has 4 stars vs. 5).

Update - the kids have been playing with this toy for a bit now and unfortunately I am having to resend my initial review.  The durability of this toy is very poor, especially for the bicycle.  First of all, the bike's front wheel does not roll well and the dolls' feet do not stay on the pedals.  The main problem though is that the bike broke at several places within the structure and has since been abandoned.  The kids do like the dolls as they have jointed legs and arms and so they can play with them like they are marionettes.  This toy is a good idea and the girls still like the Frozen theme of the toy but over the long haul, this toy did not hold up well.
Toys_and_Games.summary: Bike broke after only a few days of play

Toys_and_Games.reviewText: It's somewhat difficult to put together and trying to get the Legos to drop into the slots is a huge challenge.  My almost 4-year-old didn't seem to get the concept. So for now we set aside the top layers and have all the Legos stored in the bottom container only.  Maybe it'll come of more use as my child gets older and gets more Legos.  However, I like the product's concept and the design is certainly cute.

When I opened up some of the packages some of the belts had the color scratched off of them. The instructions seemed like google translate was used for them. And as I was practicing how to put them on when I took them off one of the stitchings of the belts snapped. Now I have to buy another set somewhere else. And I wasn't very pleased with how everything fit anyway...

Ill give this kit 3 stars because its an awesome idea and I think with some practice you could accomplish some great papermaking, however I was disappointed in the kits initial performance. The package contains everything you would need to make your own recycled paper including shredded tissue paper (1 big bag of white and several smaller bags with bright colors) to get you started. Unfortunately the directions that come with the package are lacking. The enclosed pamphlet has pictorial directions which offer no recommendations on specific measurements/ratios for your project. Further, it tells the user to look up the Paper Factory Youtube video for more detailed instructions. After viewing this video several times I realized that this video is not for this version of Alex Toys papermaking kit! The tools used in that video do not match what is provided in the Eco Crafts Paper Making Kit and in fact belong to the Paper Factory kit which is different. I was able to locate a review video for the Eco Crafts kit and get an idea the measurements/paper mixture (we used majority white paper and added a little bit of colored paper to tint), and step by step instructions. We mixed our paper and water in a Ninja blender to be sure we got the finest pulp we could. The mesh screen was not tight the way you would need it to be to be able to squeeze all the water out and the plastic sheets provided for squeezing the water out don't fit inside the mesh screen which they should, to be able to adequately expel the water. What we ended up with was a really soggy sheet that had too much water in it. The excess water prevented the pulp from adhering together so the paper broke into pieces once dry. I may cut the plastic sheets to get them to fit the screen as I think this was our biggest problem. Overall my kids (8, 6, & 4) had fun with it and loved the paper once done, but not sure it was worth the effort. Hoping that after we practice a few more times that well get better and be able to produce something they can actually use for scrapbooking or other paper crafts.

Toys_and_Games.reviewText: These four figures run the whole spectrum from bad to good. Simon is pretty solid, and while the articulation isn't great, he still has a wide range of motion and a few neat accessories to get him in some cool poses. Alucard & Dracula aren't anything special, with their clothes limiting movement a great deal. Alucard's sword is also hanging down in front of his crotch for whatever reason... looks really stupid to me. If you really try, a few cool poses can be made, but otherwise they're mediocre at best. The succubus is downright terrible though. Sure, she's sexy and sculpted pretty well, but they went and gave her a couple articulation points at the shoulders so she can move her arms up and down, and I honestly can't figure out why. She'd be fine if they just picked a sexy pose and didn't articulate her at all, or if they had really articulated her like Simon since she could get a wide range of motion thanks to the lack of clothes... but the half assed 2 points of articulation just frustrates more than anything else. There are better, sexier figures out there, so unless you're a die hard Castlevania fan like me, do yourself a favor and pass.

I've read David-Matthew Barnes before and I enjoy his young adult and adult fiction. This is the first poetry I've read of his, and I must say I enjoyed it. Each of the poems in this collection is very personal and tells a story. They're written with different styles, and though they all have similar themes, it's never redundant.

A few of the poems stood out to me and I highlighted them in the book. "Paper Boy" really resonated with me because I was a paper girl when I was younger, and I felt much the same way. The poem really captures that feeling of being alone and free and contemplating the future. I was twelve when I had my first paper route, and I remember biking along dreaming up what my life would be like, especially since I was "sophisticated" and had a job.

"Souvenir Boy," where the title I assume comes from, stood out to me because of the last lines "Although we've come close, there are more than hot white seconds between us - there lies a lost country or two."

"Look for Homer" felt so much like a fantasy to me, I wondered if this really happened. I got lost in the poem and placed myself there on Mylopotas Beach, and at the end I was sorry for the poem to end, and sorry for the poet to leave.

"Dear Mr. Sanchez" might be my favorite. I really loved the style this one was written in. As a letter, it's so effective in getting the meaning across and translating the poets emotions to the readers. I've reread it several times and have started my own poem using this form now.

"Celebrity Skin" felt like another fantasy to me, and I wanted to drop the book and email the poet right away and ask if it was real and if it were, who the person in question was. It was deliciously scandalous, like something you'd read in a novel.
Kindle_Store.summary: A great collection of poetry that stimluates the senses

Sandy Gadow has completely up-dated her book The Complete Guide To Your Real Estate Closing and added information relevant to the times. I was surprised at the amount of information provided in this comprehensive book.  The new dedicated Media Center which is available to purchasers of the book is fantastic! A great bonus is that I was able to print out blank forms which I will be able to use in my own real estate transaction. The money-saving tips are also very helpful.

I found the book to be well-written, with great illustrations and examples. The easy to understand way in which closing is explained made sense and is easy to follow. I have read many real estate books, but never one written by a closing professional. Someone who really knows the subject matter from first hand experience. This book prepared me for what to expect at closing, what fees I was allowed to question and how to negotiate lower closing costs. I realized that settlement errors just don't happen at the mortgage level, they also happen at the title company. This book delivered on it's title. It really is a complete guide and a handy reference book. I went to closing with less worry and more confidence than ever before. I understood what I was doing and what to question. This is the only book I could find that really helps you with the final and most critical part of a real estate purchase (or sale). Thomas and Priscilla Christen
Kindle_Store.summary: New Edition is great. I can recommend it highly

Danielle Jamie has done it again. Yep, if you are thinking that she managed to write one of the most perfectly flawed book boyfriends yet again, then you are correct.
Brody is this ruggedly handsome yet broken man who loves his insanely adorable son Corbin with all his heart. His perfect life was ripped away from him three years ago and his life is still in shambles. His life revolves around his son and work, leaving no time for himself or the chance of love.
Until Callie walks into his door. Callie herself hasn't had it easy. She was abandoned by her father and lost her mother, her best friend to cancer. She is pregnant with her on-again-off again boyfriends child and she has reached her breaking point. She refuses to be his doormat any longer, so she goes to visit her aunt.
Callie and Brodys story touched my heart and turned me into a flustered, blushing mess. One minute I am swooning over Brody and his sweet, sexy self. The next I am crying as he breaks my heart.
You will be rooting for Callie and Brody to have their happily ever after. Trust me on that. Its amazing how one Christmas Wish can change your life.

Digilogue is the digital disruption compass of any company striving to hold onto their legacy while fast tracking to satisfy the needs of the customers of tomorrow. Anders nails it - he eloquently captures our hearts with the truth of his family owned business struggling to find its own path of bricks to the modern day clicks. Will Georg Srman be victorious? I wait with high hopes and positive ambition for this upstart go-getting swede. In my own industry, technology in construction, it rings too true that you will always need a hammer to build - very analogue; but at the same time technology through hardware and software makes every strike of that hammer more efficient. I didn't have a word for this connection of analogue and digital until reading Digilogue. I recommend this book to any CEO trying to connect to new Millennial clients or the year 2 university student trying to connect with the heritage of big business. Well done Anders, more success awaits you and can't wait for the next installment!

Max is an absolutely wonderful and enchanting little boy, unless hes your son!  Actually, its hard not to be delighted by Sally Goulds Max and his brother Charlie.  In fact, the whole family is full of characters, each one with their own quirks and likeable features.  From the father, who bulldozes ahead to give his family memorable vacations, to the mother who is wise, understanding, caring and smitten with mystery novels, to evil Aunt Avril, whos really not so evil and Nanna, the wonderful Grandmother we all wish we had, the entire clan is endearing and exasperating, as all families are.

The Venetian Job is the third installment of The Max Books and each one gets progressively more entertaining, due in part because you come to like these characters more and more with each book.  Even if you don't have small children, or don't generally read childrens books, I would recommend The Max Books.  They are very enjoyable and will bring a smile to your face.  And everyone can relate to the little boy who just never means to get in trouble.

Kindle_Store.reviewText:
Dan Ames, who writes under both his own name and the pen name, Dani Amore, has concocted a delictiously twisted short story "Scale of Justice" with a surprise ending that seems to have come directly from "Tales from the Crypt." And, appropriately for a story involving a chef, author Ames seems to know that the proper recipe for this type of story is to let it simmer just long enough to maximize the flavor.

A chef who made the mistake of trying to rip off a Detroit crime boss is saved from literally becoming a meal for a group of hungry alligators by the big man himself and given a chance to win his and his son's life (the son has also made a drugged out mess of things). I did not use the term "big man" casually here, because the boss, one Diego Villanueva, is literally a huge man, weighing in at some 400+ pounds. Diego has a problem; his boss wants him to lose some weight rather quickly, and Diego knows that with his normal eating regimen that's impossible.

So, Diego informs the chef that if he takes over the preparation of Diego's meals and can create appetizing enough low calorie fare that enables Diego to stay on his diet and lose weight (almost a pound a day over the next month), then the chef's life (and his son's life) will be spared. That proves to be a task easier said than done. The chef has no problem whipping up delectable fare; the problem is that Diego doesn't seem to be losing any weight, and the daily weigh-ins are a grim reminder to the chef of what he's facing in a few more days.

Author Ames describes "Scale of Justice" as a hardboiled thriller, and the hardboiled part is certainly correct. Ames plays a truly bizarre scenario completely straight, and the first couple of chapters in the story (yes, even a 25-page story has chapters) are written in a blunt, matter-of-fact, hard nosed style. The later parts of the story, in which the chef desperately tries to figure out why Diego isn't losing weight, are played just as seriously. Plus, Ames is in no hurry to rush the ending; instead, he takes his time describing the chef's plight and how he tries to do something about it. It's only when Ames reveals the trick ending that the reader appreciates how truly warped (and darkly humorous) the entire scenario has been. And, because Ames has taken his time in telling the story, the impact of the ending packs an even greater punch. The story simply wouldn't have been as effective had Ames, as other writers might well have done, played the entire story for laughs. "Scale of Justice" only works because the chef's predicament seems quite real.

"Scale of Justice" is about as well constructed as a story of this length can be. You won't get much character development in a story this short, but you do get good atmospheric description, an interesting story idea, and a great ending. It's rare that I get through a story that packs a punch and doesn't seem to have a single paragraph that's not effective. Dan Ames has managed to write such a story here. The story actually brought back fond memoriesfor me, both in terms of plot and tone, of those that used to be anthologized in "Alfred Hitchcock's Mystery Magazine" (and often wound up dramatized on his TV show. "Scale of Justice" has exactly the right balance.

Gen revels in her new "engaged" status until an earthquake literally makes her world crumble. After frantically searching for Mack who's gone missing, she finds him buried under debris in a mansion he had no obvious reason visiting. Her relief is short-lived as his cranial injury robs him of a good part of his memories including those he's made with her. Mack is not Mack anymore.

This is the most gripping story in the captivating Gen Delacourt mystery series. Gen's emotional involvement tampers both with her judgement and her responses, forcing her to assign the case to the cool and smooth Devlin, yet he wants her to be more than his sidekick. For Gen, a committed relationship was shaky ground; losing it means she's lost part of herself, and she has to fight for resolve on many fronts. The emotional aspect in this novel is what makes it stand out.

But that doesn't mean that the mystery part is played down. If anything, the addition of a potentially paranormal element makes it even more appealing. Secondary characters pop out strongly, and I was pleased to see Shiloh and Luca returning to help Mack out as did Livvie and Bree to Gen.

If you've enjoyed Gen Delacourt's mysteries so far, Lock the Cellar Door is not one to miss.
Kindle_Store.summary: Gripped both my mind and my heart

Kindle_Store.reviewText:
I really, really love alternative history, and having a fresh read in the "what if" genre makes Legacy a wonderful find for readers lusting after something newer than Man in the High Castle and/or Fatherland. In Sky's divergent novella we are introduced to Peter, the son of Hitler who has been raised in isolation and secrecy. He's brought out of hiding, dusted off, and groomed to follow in his father's footsteps by men who hope to see him pick up the pieces of a shattered nation, and attempt to restore what's left of a fractured ideology. The tone coerces a kind of sympathy that will sit uncomfortable with many readersbut it is in this aspect that I was totally sold on the writing. The moment you start *kind of* understanding an SS officer, my friends, is the same moment you know that the character development has been well executed.

It's generally pretty rare to find a whole lot of depth or dimension in a novella, but Legacy does a great job in the space it's been allotted. The style of writing is consistent with the subject matter, and while others might argue that the ending is predictable, I'd have to insist that the journey to get there is certainly a unique, engrossing commute. It's well worth an afternoon lost to intelligent escapism.

I'd like to thank the publisher, who furnished an ARC of this book.

I first read this book when it was called The Billionaire's Angel and part of A Maine Christmas... or two. When I realized that it was being released alone and with a gorgeous new cover I didn't hesitate to purchase and reread! You fall in love with Grady before the first chapter even begins and Emily as soon as their story starts. It's a beautiful novella written by JS Scott. I find it amazing that she can evoke such strong feelings and make you fall in love with her characters in a short novel. I loved this book and won't hesitate to recommend.

This novel is gripping. I endured at least a week of exhaustion because i could not put this book down at night. The characters are realistic, the story is suspenseful. You never know what is doing to happen next. The dialogue is so realistic. I could really picture the scene, it was written so descriptively. An awesome read, especially if on vacation, and you don't have to go to work the next day! fast-paced thriller based on some mysterious and frightening ideas about religion, power and the supernatural.

The characters are well-drawn,  very interesting and the story-line with its many twists and turns extremely convincing. It left me thinking about it long after the last page was finished.
Kindle_Store.summary: Gripping thriller from beginning to end.

Kindle_Store.reviewText:
During the summer, high school student Nathan Chambers chooses spelunking and advanced summer classes over video games, mall haunting, and movies. When he and his friend Sam decide to break through a collapsed area in a Carlsbad, New Mexico cave, Nathan hopes to find fame, glory, and treasure. When he hears what he thinks is another spelunker trying snatch victory from his hammer, Nathan rushes in headlong.

Nathan describes the creature in the cave:

"It was as if a mad scientist took an octopus and placed it on a human body, in some insane experiment to create an aquatic version of Frankenstein. The creature stood over eight feet tall and the three tentacles sat in a way that made it appear as if the creature had some kind of crazy beard. He continued to fidget with the TV screen, unaware of my presence. The hands working the machinery were human-like, but with three fingers on its hands. The skin of the creature, illuminated by the large spotlight in the center of the room, was a denim-blue color like someone with poor blood circulation."

The creature severs Nathan's rope, his only link to safety and the outside world. The teen's life changes forever.

Using details and excellent characterizations, Mr. Gaydas expertly suspends our disbelief and allows us into the world he has created. Throughout his adventures, Nathan meets "creatures" with thoughts and feelings, an entity with an allergy to humans, a version of an intergalactic bureaucracy (Max Weber would be excited beyond belief), and stumbles onto a computer program which changes his outlook on life. He also learns enemies can be friends, things aren't always as they appear, and "alien" is a relative concept, even on earth.

While the book targets young people, readers of all ages will enjoy this wonderful science fiction adventure.
Kindle_Store.summary: Science Fiction Adventure for All Ages

Short, sweet and sexy!

A few years back Noah told Gwen that they wouldnt make it as a couple because of his career as a SEAL. They moved on, but when they meet again quite by accident, the sparks still fly. Noah realises it may be his last chance with Gwen, and he has to weigh how important she really is to him. A SEALS SACRIFICE is a short but complete story about second chances at love, and Ms. Weber handles the whole situation with much flair. Within the confines of a novelette, the author is able to tell Gwen and Noahs story in full and make us care about them. A SEALS SACRIFICE is a beautifully written story about two people who truly care about each other and really make an effort to deal with their issues and make it work.

Benjamin M. Baldinotti opens his debut book saying, Stress management doesn't have to be that complicated or hard to reduce, first of all, you have to understand stress in order to reduce it or avoid it completely. I know that you think stress isn't a choice and I know that, but I also know that stress can have a massive impact on your health, mood and overall your psychological and physical state.

In a very conversational manner and casual tone (setting the stage for paying attention to someone to whom we can relate) Benjamin divides his book into four sections - CAUSES of Stress, Stress SYMPTOMS, EFFECTS of Stress on your Health and Body, and How to AVOID and MANAGE Stress.

In each of these areas Benjamin makes note of situations to which we all can relate (causes or sources include not only work but home and finances and illness within the family unit, changes in home or job; symptoms include insomnia, chest pain, fatigue, GI problems, anxiety, depression, substance abuse; effects of stress as the cause of 85% of doctor visits; management includes meditation, exercise, positive thinking, breathing deeply, laughing, yoga, reading).

In typical Benjamin style he closes his brief session with us stating, We all think that we can live forever, no one thinks about life being just a short cycle of some ups and downs, so make sure to live it the way you want and the way you need it to be. Dont sweat over the little negative things in life because nothing good can come out of it except some additional completely unnecessary stress and believe me you don't need that in your life. Wake up and grab life by the neck and ride that thing like there is no tomorrow. You will be grateful to yourself later for taking matters in your own hands and don't let others to always look down on you, because in order to get respect you have to respect yourself in the first place.

Nothing terribly new here, but condensed in immediately accessible form that is easy to digest  and likely with allow some introspection. Grady Harp, May 16
Kindle_Store.summary: You must respect yourself so others can follow...and give respect in order to get respect

Wow this book had a lot that I love in it. It was raw and gritty when it came to the passion between Brielle and Hudson. Those two have such a smoking chemistry it just screams off the page. When these two are together, it is not disappointing! I love the mystery aspect to this book too. There is a lot of intriguing moments where you want to scream because you want to know what is going on!

I received an advanced review copy from the author in exchange for an honest review. The Nightingale Rises is a very exciting suspenseful romance by amazing author, Cynthia Dane. Love, love, love this series as I do all Cynthia's books. Nala and Vincent are still trying to find evidence against Xavier Crow to prove he is a murderer. Nala believes he killed her sister, Tasha and Vincent is sure he killed his fiance, Desiree. They join the Aviary, which is a bdsm club, run by Crow to try to get proof. The problem is someone knows something suspicious is going on with them and warns Nala that they should be very careful. During all this Nala and Vincent are growing closer to each other. Can they survive the danger and be able to be happy again? Can't wait to read the next book in this series.

*****I was gifted a copy of this for review*****I am soooo glad I was.  This is an awesome series and even better a new author for me! I simply can't wait for the next set.  This book had me riveted, Angels, Demons, Nephilim, all have order, houses, and a world the writer immediately pulls us into.  This book will have you in it's grip from first word to last. As I am a paranormal junkie to the core, this book had my brain clicking all over the page. As Aiden's friend dies and she learns some secrets he kept, her world is forever changed...You can be too read this book!

This book starts out three years later. A lot as changed since Rhee and Dax last seen each other. When I say a lot, I really mean a lot. There is a few reasons why Rhee ran away in the first place. She thought she knew where her sister, Mickey, was, and, well, she has a secret that will change her life forever. A secret she can't tell anyone, especially not Dax.

Rhee is living a happy life with a few people closest to her. She has a really good job, and does charity for children in need. She has her life on the right track. Everything is going very smoothly for her, everything besides finding love.

Dax is lost and has no idea how to find himself. He's depressed, but would never admit it. Everyone can see it. Ever since Rhee left, Dax's life has been spiraling out of control. He loved the stowaway and misses her more than anything.

Dax goes out of town on some business matters. Little does he know, Rhee is there, and soon they will be brought together. He has always put the club first, but when he finds Rhee, he doesn't know what to do with himself. He starts putting off business. He starts wanting to spend more time with Rhee, and be around her and.... the secret addition.

They both want each other. They both want to wrap their arms around each other, and never let go, but neither of them will strike the first move. They're both confused and don't know what to do next.

Drama unravels and puts all three of their lives in danger. Will Dax and Rhee end up together? Will Dax keep his commitment to the club or to Rhee?

I absolutely loved that there was a book two in this series. I fall more in love with Dax and Rhee as characters. Rhee makes decisions that not everyone has the strength to make. Dax will do whatever is takes to stay with the love of his life. Two people that are destined to be together, no matter what the obstacles that stand in there way.

I give this book 5 stars, and I can't wait to start reading the last book in the series! I recommend this series to all of the people that love MC/ Romance books.

Aurora, a former prostitute, receives a windfall and decides to buy property in Pine City, Montana. She outbids a local rancher for a large home and many acres of land. God calls her to help the prostitutes in the town to leave that life and become independent. She receives opposition from a crooked sheriff, the owners of the brothels, and the men of the town.. This is a very good Christian Fiction book, and I highly recommend it.

Death would be easy, but I feel she would rather be a fighter, and I can't help but respect that. I'm not sure how this story's gonna end, but I'm dying to read what's going to happen now that she has done the unthinkable. There is no way this will end good for anyone. But I'm still rooting for Haley, cause I know if she's going down, she's taking Jude to hell with her.

Okay, let me just get this off my chest. Sienna & Nick... I have an urge to punch things. I had a horrible feeling the first time that bitch showed up. I knew that I would hate her. I knew I would hate Nick. I almost thought that they would end up being connected somehow. I don't even have once ounce of pity for that skank.

Reckless begins just as Effortless left off. Kiera and Kellan had just symbolically married one another on the dance floor at Pete's. She is free of school, Kellan is getting ready to record an album and with nothing stopping them they are getting ready to start this new life...together....on the road.

But nothing seems to ever come easy for them. Joey returns and has her own plans of revenge for Kellan, but this first test of Kiera's trust and faith in him came much too quickly. I was not surprised by her reaction, I expected it. However, while the old Kiera was still there, the new Kiera was really trying to fight to make her way to the surface.

Kiera's character did show some growth in Reckless (finally), but for the first time I wanted her to be less reserved. I wanted the claws to come out. But she really did come into her own in this one, and she really did find that trust that her and Kellan never really had to start with. But as the D-Bags head off on tour, with Kiera along for the ride - for the first time it's not the fans and groupies that challenges their relationship. It's his dream, but so is she - could he throw away his band's dreams to ensure that he can hold onto Kiera? This is where Kiera's new found faith comes into place, she won't allow him to give up on his dream or crush the band's dreams either.

But when Kellan becomes the hot new star and is being tied to one of hottest singers Kiera is struggling to remain by his side, and remain invisible from Kellan's spot light - but that can all backfire as rumors spread and fans show how ugly they can be. Kellan's relationship is pushed along with his will. He has fought his whole life to be loved, to have a family and to mean something to anyone and his love for Kiera has suddenly become his dirty little secret. But some can only be pushed to far before they can't take anymore.

Although there are parts that had me completely twisted, Kellan's love for Kiera did not waiver one bit. They knew what damage could be done without trust and faith in one another. Although there are times when Kiera's private thoughts wander into dangerous territory, she does really try to think things out and there is just no faltering in Kellan's love for her.

This was a wonderful ending to this series. You get to keep all the boys and girls close to your heart and you even have your moments when you rather hug Griffin than slap him. This series was just a brilliant series. Between the ups and downs in the first book, the crazy stress of book two - Reckless for me was just icing on the cake. Yeah it had it's moments of stress and concern but you just felt this was going to be forever. That finally they have learned from their past and that they would make it. I don't want my time with Kellan to end, it was all summed up so perfectly that it just felt so final. Kellan has to be one of my all time favorites, I will miss him.

"I want to save her because..." Even though he was speaking to her, he never took his eyes off mine. "Because I'm a better man with her. Because I can't imagine going back to being who I was before I met her. Because I'm afraid...that I could be that monster again without her here loving me."

In this final installment of the Devoured series we witness a change in Clara and finally a change in Eli. As they fight to stay alive and get the help they need in order to live peacefully Clara learns more about the world of the Devourers. But for these two, nothing will separate them. Consume was an okay wrap up to Eli and Clara's story. We meet new characters and delve a little into ones introduced in book one. It was interesting reading more about the world Eli is from. But at times the book was just bland. The action was bland, the relationship was bland, and the characters were not really memorable. Well except for Enoch, he was interesting. I'm interested in how his story will play out in the next book in this series.

The book had its few good moments and that is why the 3.5 rating, but wasn't a book that I would read over and over again. I felt there was so much potential to Eli and Clara's story if the Devourer world was delved into more and in depth.

All in all, if you want a light, quick read then pick up this series.

The mother/son team that writes under the pen name --- Charles Todd --- have already created the terrific Inspector Ian Rutledge series.  Now, A BITTER TRUTH marks the third entry in their latest series --- the Bess Crawford mysteries.

Bess is a British battlefield nurse who witnesses first-hand the horrors of WWI.  Additionally, she finds herself constantly at the center of various deadly mysteries.  A BITTER TRUTH finds Bess befriending a young woman named Lydia who appears to have been battered by her husband, himself a British serviceman.  Bess decides to accompany Lydia to her home and is quickly thrust into the middle of a murder that may have been committed to protect a deadly family secret.

The difference with this Bess Crawford mystery is that she herself is unwittingly made a subject in the murder investigation --- a fact that makes her involvement in finding out the truth that much more difficult.  Although this is not Charles Todd's finest work, it does feature what they always do best --- create an atmosphere of a bygone era that is so real and gritty you are practically transported there with every line.
Kindle_Store.summary: Another fine entry in the Bess Crawford mystery series.

When Rhoda meets Ben, a farmer and landowner, baby Nashe and Paumina, she encounters a more sinister form of abuse from the town folks of Grand Saline, TX during the 1960's. It's an eye opener page after page!

I plan to read more works  by Julie Roberts Towe and rate this novella at 3.8 stars.

My lifetime involvement in the martial arts, self-defense, combatives and weapon arts has taught me many important life lessons.  In my more than 70 years of searching I have been fortunate to have studied and read hundreds of books on the martial arts and the philosophy of Bushido(Way of he warrior).  Since learning to be meaningful must be an endless search for truth, I have bought and read hundreds of excellent books on the philosophy of the martial arts, this book is NOT one of them.

The author claims in his research that he has come up with the following twenty five principles of martial arts.  The include the following:  (1) Formlessness (2) Yielding  (3) Fast loss, Quick win)  (4) Deflection  (5) Division  (6) Circling  (7) Straight lines  (8) Balance  (9) Avoiding conflict  (10) Retreating (11) Minimal exertion
(12) Self-cultivation  (13) Defeat  (14) Timing  (15) Movement  (16) Mind States  (17) Memory  (18) Concentrated Attacks (19) Total Defensibility  (20) Alliances (21) Shifting power  (22) Hard and soft  (23) Courage
(24)  Apprenticeship  (25) Knowledge.

In conclusion, this book is okay possibly for beginners learning the basic principles of the martial arts; however, there are numerous books available that are better at teaching the philosophy of Bushido (Way of the Warrior).  Buyer beware.

Rating:  3 Stars.  Joseph J. Truncale (Author:  Martial Art Myths)
Kindle_Store.summary: This book is okay, but there are numerous others on martial art principles that are better.

Kindle_Store.reviewText: A good, basic listing, with simple explanations, of the top things one should have on hand in the event of major catastrophe of any sort. Some are evident, others less so, but he makes a good case for them all. Kindle_Store.reviewText:
3 "More Than Your Past" Stars

After his introduction in Raleigh and Mia's book as the best friend, it's Pax's turn to face his past. In high school Pax first saw Gemma on one of the first night's she moved to town. Before the accident that hurt Mia and sent Raleigh to prison, Pax was part of the racing scene. His brief encounter with Gemma led him to wanting more until she turned up again dating his older brother Blake. But when Gemma accused Blake of rape, Pax wanted nothing to do with the girl who cried wolf.

Years later Gemma is back in town to help her dad who's in the hospital. Having been called names and accused of lying, Gemma has tried to run from the accusations. But being back in the small town brings up all the pain and suffering of the past since no one has forgotten and still no one believes her.

Running into Pax was the last thing she wanted but since he's now her dad's partner in opening a raceway, she sees him a lot even though he is still angry. But when the truth comes out, Pax becomes a partner leaving Gemma to wonder if she can heal old wounds and survive in a town that hates her so that she can be with Pax.

I was really excited to see where Pax's story went. He was a really interesting side character in book one. With such a tough subject, I expected more angst and more tension. In reality the book was overly sweet and a bit too easy. I didn't understand Pax's staunch stand behind his family when numerous times he was obviously the odd guy out for no reason and a recipient of his families terrible behavior. Pax was less bad boy and more follower which is fine just not what I was expecting. The story did keep me flipping pages and hoping that Blake got what was coming to him. Plus Gemma and Pax were smoking hot together.
