I clean it and the the filter out, put it back together and get another 60 seconds out of it.  Clearly this wasn't designed to handle normal use. My previous two roombas worked flawlessly on the same surface - low pile carpet.  As much money as iRobot wants for these and the attention they require,  i'd say you'd be much better off using a regular manual vacuum.  I wanted to love it as I have almost everything else in my house automated, but alas, this unit may be destined for the dump.
Industrial_and_Scientific.summary: Expense lesson learned that iRobot has lost their way.

Industrial_and_Scientific.reviewText: This bracket is a piece of junk. It is half the thickness it needs to be to support a 4.5" water filter housing. Look at the video of my filter bouncing. Tried to save time by getting this bracket and now I have to weld a support across the whole thing just to make the install acceptable.

Get what you pay for.  Hassle and not reliable.  I had wixey and was not careful.  It hit router bit.  I thought they would be the same but no.  Wixey is much better....buttons are more definite, it is easier to zero and more sturdy.  This is flimsy and buttons don't always work so have to press again.  I compared to digital calipers and this is not accurate.  I borrowed neighbors igage  and it was right on....with calipers just like wixey was. This is off by about 10% a huge amount in precision sork.  save your money and buy the igage or wixey....you will be much happier
Industrial_and_Scientific.summary: Compared to competitors 1 star....poor quality in any ways.  Not accurate

Industrial_and_Scientific.reviewText:
If you need casters for Gladiator Gear (Garage Storeage) you should check out my experience before you buy. See my comments on these casters at [...]

In summary the product does NOT come with four locking casters as advertised - only two lock.

And, installation is a nightmare.  You have to use a reciprocating saw to cut out the collar that the screw-in feet attach to.  Also, several of the bolts are difficult to install and two are impossible.

Also, the casters mount to low and the rear casters hit on the sidewalls of the base and are prevented from swiveling freely.  They only swivel about 45 degrees (22+ degrees left, 22+ degrees right).  They might as well be fixed.

The document I linked to above outlines my experience and illustrates my installation and modification of the GearBox with photos.

I sent a copy of this document to Whirlpool.  I will post an update if I ever hear back from them.
Industrial_and_Scientific.summary: Installation Nightmare - Does not function as intended.

Industrial_and_Scientific.reviewText: This is a great epoxy glue, specially formulated for jewelry needs (and I will use it to glue stone cabochons to metal frame). Before I bought it, although, I was reading through description and reviews trying to figure out what is the actual amount of tubes that I will get. It is not really clear from the description, because each unit of glue is two tubes (glue and the hardener)  My problem is that amount supplied from the seller is a half from what advertised it the listing :( While seller says :"Epoxy 330 Glue, 1/2 Fluid Ounces, Pack Of 2", you receive one tube of the actual glue and a tube of hardener, which is together obviously one unit, not two, as advertised. This is why only one star review is given.
Industrial_and_Scientific.summary: Great glue, only half of the advertised amount

Industrial_and_Scientific.reviewText: I would like to try it but cannot after repeated attempts get the last part to screw onto sweeper...What happened to Rubbermaid to send out a priduct that people complain is hard to put together,...I will have to pay our buildings handyman to put it on for me...very frustrating, I think it will be a good sweeper but not being to try it is beyond annoying 11
Industrial_and_Scientific.summary: Hard to put a simple screw together handle,

Industrial_and_Scientific.reviewText: I've heard a lot on the internet about Rescue Tape, so I figured I'd give it a shot. I'll save you the long winded details and say that on every attempt to seal leaks on the pressure side of any liquid or gas system... failed spectacularly. I'm sure this stuff would work fine for holding something together, Or even work great on zero pressure plumbing (like drains and vent tubes). But that's not what I needed.

SO many things wrong with this vacuum. Bought it to use on hardwood and tile floors. The suction is minimal. I constantly have to clear the dog hair off of the floor piece and hand feed it into to center suction area. The container is NOT easy to clean - you have to reach in with your fingers and pull the debris out. Because the motor is positioned at the top, it is heavy and unwieldy. The ONLY nice thing that I can say about this vacuum is that it has a long cord. I've used it for more than a year, but it's going in the trash tomorrow. Way too much of a headache.
Industrial_and_Scientific.summary: Awful suction and hard to clean out

Industrial_and_Scientific.reviewText: Way too loud! I believe that these dryers are causing hearing damage and I wouldn't be surprised if someone files a class action. Any restaurant that has one will lose a star or two on Yelp because of them. You can often hear them from the dining room. Do us all a favor and don't buy this thing. If you have to get an air dryer, go with the Dyson. At least it works and doesn't cause tinnitus.

I was very disappointed with the quality of this cart. I  bought it to use to transport my groceries and laundry to and from my apartment on the 2nd floor. It did very well climbing the stairs (the design of the cart is excellent for this), but the quality of the construction is poor. However, the tri-wheeled track type rear wheels and The lack of front caster wheels makes the cart  difficult to turn and maneuver in tight areas such kitchens or through doorways, especially on carpets.
  The light weight construction is my major problem with the cart. The first time I used it for my groceries the fore leg bent. The next time I used it as a laundry cart and both legs bent. I have returned it for a refund and will be looking for a better quality product the next time.
Industrial_and_Scientific.summary: Good idea but poor quality and design.

Industrial_and_Scientific.reviewText:
This seemed like the perfect item to protect my wood floor from muddy paws and snowy boots.
It was supposed to be a barrier.
After a month or so of use I pulled it up...there in the middle, the floor was wet and molded, to the point that it needs to be sanded down.
I could understand if the damage were near the edges. One could then assume that some moisture overflowed or was trapped on the floor. But in the middle, where it is supposed to protect the floor?
To make it even worse, I ordered the Andersen 272 first. It was different from the description so the Amazon rep re-ordered it for me, said to donate the wrong one. Within days I called back, worried that they would send one that was exactly the same since the product description was still wrong.
The rep told me she was going to cancel the order and I could re order myself, a brand new order. So I did, assuming that the original order would be refunded.
It never was, so I called.
This time I was told I would have to return the first one, which I would be happy to do, but after being told to donate, I did.
So, this was a very expensive lesson, not just in paying double, but my floor is ruined.
Industrial_and_Scientific.summary: I purchased a top of the line product to protect my floor

Industrial_and_Scientific.reviewText: This is a very large grain, not powdered as stated.  I use it for bath bombs and have used from 2 other suppliers on Amazon and never had a problem.  Neither of them were powdered but most of their grains would go through my sieve.  None of these grain do.  I've made 4 batches and I'm using the rest of this to clean sinks and toilets because it's useless for bath bombs.  Had it been properly stated as large grain, I would never have made this purchase.

They click on in my pocket a lot the bulb part has become loose and it's not as bright and there's no way to tighten it... it worked well when I first got it but I barley used it and just from being in my lab coat I guess was too much wear and tear for it lol don't waste your money

Industrial_and_Scientific.reviewText:
I've been dealing with quite a few measuring devices that are inaccurate, and this is one of them. The temperature is consistently off by -8 degrees. That's not within the margin of error for just about anything. one or two I can see making sense, but this far off is insane. The humidity is never listed as OK as displayed on screen in that ad even when it's show 45-55% humidity. It always says that it's low or high for some reason. The highs and lows are fine, but when they are as wrong as this one is it doesn't matter.

The upside to this one is it is cheap.

Industrial_and_Scientific.reviewText: I hate this vacuum with a passion. I'm just waiting for the second generation Dyson before getting rid of it. Every day I find another reason to hate it, I just watched it spin around for 20 minutes trying to go home. It should be nicknamed the dump vacuum because I can't imagine it being any dumber. From destroying cables to running out of battery and waking me up in the middle of the night I'm surprised with all the positive reviews.

Total ripoff. This price is literally for ONE pouch. The title says "pouches". The picture shows 3 pouches which I thought was weird. This is such a waste of money. I would definitely appreciate a refund because this was misleading and I'm extremely unhappy. Now I still have no pouches and I'm losing money because I'm going to have to order more and wait to get them. I run a business and needed these. If you're going to sell one pouch (don't understand why anyone would only need 1 pouch) then you should specifically label it as ONE.

After wearing out my third Hoover hard floor/carpet cleaner I was quite happy to try this one.  Unfortunately the squeegie (essential for hard floor cleaning) would not even attach.  A call to Hoover brought a quick response that they would send a new squeegie.  It arrived eight days later and did attach, but not with a "snap" as mentioned in the manual and the Hoover site video.  I began to clean the tile floor; after a few swipes the squeegie came off.  Tried several times with the same outcome.  I had a prolonged call with the Hoover support line; the agent kept indicating I hadn't put the squeegie on correctly.  She suggested that I should take the machine to the service center (70 miles away, I turned that idea down), and then said I could take it to a local appliance dealer to have them show me how to attach the squeegie.  After telling her I had read the manual twice and watched the Hoover how-to video, plus had my engineer husband read the manual and watch the video, and he had no better luck attaching the squeegie so that it would stay on.  She then told me she would transfer me to someone that would give me further assistance.  When the new person got online, she not only did not know anything about the situation but said she asked if I was a dealer because that was who she works with.  She transferred me back to customer assistance and another agent who offered to send a new squeegie.  I did not want to go past the 30 day return period, and did not have any hope that a third squeegie would solve the problem, so declined that offer.  I asked if they had any clips or other means of keeping the squeegie attached and got a negative reply.  I told her I would be giving up and returning the product.
Amazon made it very simple to return the product; they deserve a five star review for that process.
Addendum:  About 30 minutes after completing the customer support phone conversations, the first agent called to let me know Hoover would replace the appliance.  I did not take advantage of their offer, but instead gave up on a hard floor cleaner/carpet cleaner and purchased a different brand vacuum/steam mop....which does work.
Industrial_and_Scientific.summary: not useable on tile; perhaps will work on carpet

Industrial_and_Scientific.reviewText: I receive a " old stack " product , since i was pay 45 $ for 4 tubes of caulk  i was expecting a high quality eco friendly product , but was  impossible to squeeze almost dry product  from a tube ...... stay away from this company if you planing to finish job on time !!!!!!!!!!!!!

I agree with all the one star reviews. This stuff is junk. I thought it would compare to the polyseamseal I've used in the past. I properly cleaned the surfaces. It was more runny (less firm) out of the tube than my previous product. I waited 36 hours (draping the shower area with a plastic sheet to protect it). It looked good & felt OK, until water hit it. I had left for work & came home to a sticky, runny mess in place of my hard work. Avoid this product! Wish I could give it ZERO stars.

I picked it up out of the package and it instantly popped. This is very poorly made. I work in a lab with fragile glassware, so I was extra careful and it still popped from picking it up. The glass must be so thin that a light touch breaks it.

Maybe I got a bad example of the product, and the quality control is just bad, but since there's no returns I won't know.

Industrial_and_Scientific.reviewText:
Wonderful for hard floors, small spaces.
Pros:
  Lightweight, good suction, but best feature is getting a vac with filter bags for this low price. The bags and filters keep the dust in the vac and make it easy to dispose of without having to breathe clouds of dust.
  Works fine on hard floors and rugs without pile (ie. sisal)
Cons:
  Toy attachments. Crevice tool is silly. Save your old ones.
  Not for carpets, usable on some rugs.
  Buttons for power and cord rewind are too alike. Paint or tape one for sanity's sake.
Other:
  The bag light has never come on for me. I have cats and cat litter and choose to remove bag sooner than light comes on to save the motor.

Spot does a good job. I like that the dirt container is located on the top which makes for easy empty plus it is large enough that I only have to dump it a couple of times a week. I don't have pets so those with pets would probably have to dump it daily. I would have rated it 5 stars if it could find its way back to the charging station all the time. Thankfully if I get home in time before the battery is dead it beeps to let me know where it is stuck. Otherwise I have to hunt Spot down to figure out where it has gotten lost. It does a nice job transitioning from area rug to bare floor. I wouldn't hesitate to buy it if you are looking to purchase one. I like it much better than the iRobot that a friend has because it is so easy to clean out. It is a tad noisy but not as loud as a regular vacuum.

As a med student, I used the really nice tuning forks at the clinic before using this one, and while it pales in comparison, it works great for the price. I can't afford a $30 tuning fork, and this one does the job. It works the way it should, and it's great for practicing my technique. I can see this ones being used on patients, not just for practice, because it actually works well.

Coats tools & other surfaces very nicely.  Would have given it 5 stars if the top were a screw on rather than a plastic snap on cover.  I expect that the shelf lift will not be very much with this top.  I tried sealing it with electrical tape around the edges of the snap top and time will tell.

Work very well. I have used this type of wall anchor before. The only thing you will want to remember is to make sure the screw is all the way in when pounding into the wall. You don't need to pound hard but the tip came off that the screw threads into and I had to pull the anchor, repair the wall and start over with a new anchor. First time this ever happened to me and I have used a lot of these.
Industrial_and_Scientific.summary: Very good product, I like them because they are durable and sturdy.

Industrial_and_Scientific.reviewText: This is a really nice scope for the price. The CD for the software was broke in half during boxing by the manufacturer and they were very helpful with getting me a download of the files I needed an the USB driver for the USB connection. I found the menu system to be fairly intuitive so didn't need to read to much of the manual to get started and this is my first scope. I like that it can take a battery for portable cordless work also if I need and I my opt for that upgrade. Owon responded quickly to my support request and was very patient with me when I got a bit confused on where the USB driver files was located.
Industrial_and_Scientific.summary: Good scope and great supprot from Owon.

Industrial_and_Scientific.reviewText: Love this product!  Diaper products and lotions and ointments were all over the changing table and I needed something that would keep it all tucked away neatly and would make it all easy to find.  This product is great!  Has lots of slots and spaces for all baby diaper needs and spins so you have easy access to it all.  Only quirk is the top cover that you place the wipes on.  If it's a new wipe case and is full, the weight keeps it in place.  If you are more than halfway through the wipes in the case, then there is not enough weight to keep the top down and it can pop up in one of the corners.  But i can live with that because it keeps my changing table neat and clutter free!!
Industrial_and_Scientific.summary: Great Product to keep Clutter at Bay!!

Industrial_and_Scientific.reviewText:
Used about 4hours of tv watching and now it just makes a grinding sound. Had to disconnect it and go back to the tv speakers.

Update: Swees sent a replacement unit for testing and I narrowed the problem down to a setting on the TV. Initially, SPDIF setting for audio out was set for Dolby and worked fine for the first 4 hours. After swapping out the unit and cables trying different things I discovered that setting the SPDIF audio out to PCM made it work. Unfortunately, the setting will not stay set to PCM but reverts to Dolby every time the TV is powered off. I can only assume that something happened to the TV after using the Unit for a little while that prevents the setting from being saved since it all worked OK for a while with the SPDIF set to Dolby. Otherwise the Swees Digital Coax and Optical Toslink to Analog RCA Audio Converter Adapter works as advertised.
Industrial_and_Scientific.summary: Updated. Used about 4hours of tv watching and now it just ...

Industrial_and_Scientific.reviewText: First, the shipping was fast!  I received it the day after I ordered it, before my delivery date! Second, it works much better than the Extract 60 of which I have had for several years and the 60 leaks out of the back, this one does not!  The ability to change the brush scrub is much better, as is being able to go from wash to rinse without stopping.  Used it last night and was very happy with the results!

Love it!  I wanted a powerful vacuum to use for my house.  I was looking at $400 vacuums and thought that was a ridiculous amount to spend on a vacuum, so I figured out I could buy this powerful vacuum for 1/3 the cost instead.  I had never thought of buying a shop vac before.  I only learned about them from reading about them on amazon.  I went down to Sears to look at what a traditional shop vac looked like and was mortified by how huge they are.  I love the small size of this shop vac.  Wow, I made a good decision.  I have cats and a dog and needed something that would pick up animal hair - which this does wonderfully!  I have oriental rugs over carpet and it works great on carpeting.  I also like to use it to clean up on my cement patio area - it works great on concrete.  And it works great on my kitchen floor as well.  Wow, what a great vacuum!  The only reason I am giving this great vacuum 4 stars instead of 5 is because it doesn't come with attachments.  I had to pay $29.95 to buy the attachments.  I can't use what it comes with without leaning over to vacuum because it only comes with a hose and a small attachment.  To clean your home you really need to buy the attachment kit.  If shop-vac is listening - you need to sell it with attachments.

With gorilla glue, I glued six 1.5 inch diameter caster soft rubber wheels on the bottom of the vacuum.  Now I can roll it around and it's very stable.  I have also bought a bunch of dyson vacuum attachments to use with the machine (I had to buy a 1.25 inch wand and hose).  I highly recommend this vacuum.

I love this chip clips. I find them unique and useful for me. The colors are fun (pink, blue and green) and they come in set of six. We always have left over chips in different varieties open at the same time and now I use these clips to seal them and still crispy after few days. I use two of them in one chip bag to hold down and close the bag properly. I suggest making them longer because one of these clips is not enough to tightly seal one big chip bag. I received these clips as a complimentary product in exchange of my fair feedback in a form of a review.

It does the work, but the it's not as smart as I thought for the price. It's only smart enough to navigate one room. If I let it clean my whole apartment by itself, it would spend more time on one room without getting to other rooms before it ran out of battery. I had to lock it in one room for a while, move it to the next room, and so forth to make sure it doesn't run out of battery without getting to my entire apartment. Also, it does get stuck in wires, so I need to make sure all cables/wires are off the floor.

It's a little thick and hard to work with, but the color is an almost match for my backsplash grout. In case anyone is looking for a match for StarGlass grout in Aquamarine, the Siroflex in Aztec Blue is pretty close. Not exact, but if you don't want to mess with custom caulk colors it's probably the best "off the shelf" option.
Industrial_and_Scientific.summary: the Siroflex in Aztec Blue is pretty close. Not exact

Industrial_and_Scientific.reviewText:
I wouldn't recommend ordering this if you're going to need it urgently within a week or two. Otherwise, it's definitely worth your money.

I was given this package as a gift, and began to assemble it the day before I planned to brew, only to find that it was missing most of the parts. I had the chiller with welded GHT fittings, one female GHT to 3/8" hose barb fitting, hose clamps, and a single hose (meaning I was missing everything on the left side of the main product image). It was unusable in this state, since the proper fittings are required for you to hook the hose to the chiller.

I let customer service know, and they were happy to ship me out the replacement parts. I was excited to receive the parts, but upon inspection, one of the replacement fittings had a 1/2" barb, meaning it was mismatched with the rest of the kit and wouldn't fit in the hose provided. I contacted them again and they got it right the 3rd time (and threw in some free crown caps at my request).

The product itself is great, especially if you get everything you need in one go. Not having the hoses clamped to the chiller makes it easier to move around, and less likely that you'll damage the hoses by having them dangle over the edge of the pot while you're putting it in for the last couple minutes of the boil. The faucet adapter was key for me as well, since I don't have access to a garden hose. And finally, having two 12' hoses ups your chances of being able to set the kettle where you need it while staying in range of the nearest faucet.
Industrial_and_Scientific.summary: Great product, but was shipped incorrectly TWICE

Industrial_and_Scientific.reviewText:

Comfortable, cool, great pockets and quite a few complements on the look compared to our issued uniform. The fit comes to just above my belt line so doesn't interfere with my tool belt. Couple of small quality issues. I intended to put my microwave on the bottom shelf - The bottom of the middle shelf is only 13.5" above the lower shelf and my microwave is 14" tall so another adjustment I have to make. Industrial_and_Scientific.reviewText: Exactly as described. Great quality at a reasonable price. These are aluminum on the outside and plastic on the inside. They're more than adequate as far as durability for most applications. They look nice too. I use them on a wheelchair speed control potentiometer that takes a beating by the staff at the nursing home where the chair is used. Typically the potentiometer breaks and the shaft of the pot with this peice on it gets lost. The price and the quantity of this product is ideal for these circumstances. I'd recommend these for most control applications.

These are fine. Be careful of trying to power a Pi 3b+ (or similar) using this cable. A single 28AWG connector (appears to be aluminum wire) of this length with 2A load will drop the voltage 0.31V, which gets you into the undervoltage danger zone. (Additionally, 2A is apparently technically too much current for 28AWG wire thermally, though I didn't have any issue with that.) Using both 5V pins as well as multiple grounds may help.

So far, so good after 10 days and being used bunches of times.

I have severe arthritis and cannot use a traditional vacuum cleaner.  I have someone who comes in and cleans for me every other week, but needless, to say, the floors get quite dirty.  We have 2 cats, 1 dog and a large parrot in a house with mostly area rugs.

I had a roomba until it got to the end of its life about 6 months ago.  I chose the Neato over a new Roomba based upon the many reviews here on Amazon, and am pleased with my purchase so far.

1.  First of all, it cleans very well.  I believe the Roomba cleaned a little better in terms of getting every little crumb off of the floor, but the more powerful suction on the Neato means it grabs more deeply on carpets.

2.  Emptying the dustbin on the Neato is much easier, and it's a cinch to lift off of the top, which is easier on arthritic hands.  It just lifts right off of the top - you don't need to pull it off of the side like the Roomba (or at least the one that I had).

3.  This cleaner rocks on carpet.  Even with a bi-weekly Dyson vacuuming, there was still a lot of pet hair in our wall-to-wall bedroom carpet.  I ran the Neato about 4 times to get it all out, and voila, the carpet looks great.

4.  I believe the Neato is quite a bit louder than the Roomba, but this is a question of personal perception.

I am pleased with my Neato, and will wait to see if I run into battery or other issues that reviewers have commented about.  I gave it 4 stars because of its performance on floors.  If a few crumbs here or there don't bother you, than it would be a 5.
Industrial_and_Scientific.summary: I had a Roomba and chose this instead

Bags shrunk to fit around my bath bombs, but were not the correct size for me. Only negative was I could not figure out how to make the open end seal up. Other than that, this product would be very useful to someone who needed that size!

Industrial_and_Scientific.reviewText:
If you are a first-time printer this is the printer for you. This was the first 3d Printer that I have owned. The printer and I went through some growing pains, but let me say the rookie mistakes were mostly mine. This is extremely user-friendly. After this printer stopped working due to constant use, I tried another company's printer. The software that came with this printer was a nightmare! Sometimes when I am sleeping port numbers manifest and haunt me. This is a plug and play machine. You plug it into your computer, click the appropriate file, and you are off and running.

After I sent my second printer back because their software was hot garbage, I bought another one of these. Let me say, I was printing something in less than ten minutes.

2 issues:
1)  is that my shower door had 2 ends that were only 0.39" wide, so obviously these wouldn't fit.
2) is I measured the brackets to see how much filling I'd need to do and 3 of the brackets measure 0.455" wide, and the other measures 0.426" and is visibly more narrow.  They're advertised as 0.4375".

I also noticed that the hole is slightly staggered.  Meaning its off center to the right on one side and the other is off center to the left.  I suppose that's on purpose so the screws don't hit once assembled.

I have some filling to do to get them to fit before I can comment on quality...

This is a decent digital PH meter.  At first it wasn't as easy to use as I hoped.  It does not give you an immediate reading, it takes about 10-30 seconds to adjust to the correct PH reading.  When the tester arrives at a reading, it will fluctuate .05+/- as the liquid moves around the tester.  The only downside I have is that it will need to be recalibrated every few weeks.  When you receive the product, it has two sample packets of PH 4.04 and PH 6.86.  Empty the packets into a glass jar, mix with deionized water, then dip in the tester and adjust the tester till the reading is correct.  I notice that over time the readings will off set and you will need to recalibrate, I personally recalibrate once a month.  I use the tester for my fish aquariums and my hot tub.  This thing works great for hot tubs, because the pool testing kits are very hard to differentiate one shade of yellow versus another shade of yellow (they all look the same lol), but this tester will give you great readings within .05 of your hot tub water.  For aquariums, I still find it easier to use the drops because the aquarium PH testing kits show multiple colors and it is much easier to tell what you PH is with testing drops, but for Hot Tubs and Pools this is a must have.

So I rely a lot on reviews so I wanted to add input.  I really had a lot of hope for this machine.  A self-docking robot that vacuums and mops for around $200 is a crazy good price.  Here is what I discovered from my purchase...
The product did not work.  It kept saying, "check underneath sensor."  I followed the instructions in the manual multiple times and cleaned the sensors.  No luck.  After about 30 minutes, I finally got it to work.
I found the device cleans very well.  It's a bit louder than I expected, but not terrible.  It did a very good job cleaning my tile and laminate flooring for about 20 minutes.  The vacuum picked up a lot of material and the machine is heavy enough to scrub well with the pad.  The pad was filthy when I stopped it and the floor was surprisingly clean in that area.
The machine is very easy to maintain (unlike some comments I read on here.). The pad simply sticks underneath and the vacuum debris pops out quickly for easy disposal.
Once I stopped the machine, I could not get it working again.  The reviews are true that the company is out of business so if you get this device, you better spend the extra $20 for Amazon's service protection plan.
In sum, not a great experience but since I had it such a short time, Amazon is refunding my purchase, no problem.  I was impressed enough with the price and cleaning ability to try buying it again with my refunded money.  I'm hoping I just got a dud and my next experience will be better.  I'm not expecting much.  I figure if I can get this to run a year or two it will be well worth the money.  I just can't bring myself to spent $500-600 on one of these devices that only mops or only vacuums.

UPDATE:  so robot #2 arrived today.  This one seems to work.  It spent about 30 minutes on its initial charge moving about and cleaning the floor.  It cleans and scrubs well and left the floors looking great.  At times it seems confused and moves slow, but you just have to let it do its thing.  One problem is when it finished and tried to find its dock, it couldn't seem to figure it out.  It headed right for the area which was promising, and even ran into the dock, but just kept spinning and moving around the area.  After 10 minutes I couldn't take it anymore and just put it on the charger myself.  I had read that it couldn't seem to self charge in another review and am sad to confirm that...at least so far.

So, if you are looking for a nice little robot that cleans tile, hardwood, etc. well at a very cheap price, this is for you.  If you are looking for a $800 dollar, self docking system that you hardly have to touch, this isn't it.  Just make sure you buy the warranty.

The item description claims that it can handle up to a 25V power supply. I tried running this board with a 24V power supply and one of the bypass capacitors blew up spectacularly. Turns out that although the driver chips can handle the voltage (I think they're rated up to 36V), this board uses bypass capacitors with a 16V maximum working voltage. To be on the safe side you wouldn't want to run right up to the max rating, but you should be fine with a 12V supply or possibly even a 14.8V LiPo battery pack.

If you're feeling adventurous you could desolder the two caps in question (C7 and C8 on the board) and replace them with higher voltage rated caps with the same footprint to beef up the max voltage.

Other than the blowing up issue, the board works fine.
Industrial_and_Scientific.summary: Power supply max voltage lower than claimed

There is about a 1 or 2 second delay from when the power is turned on and when  the light reaches full intensity (BRIGHT).  On the one I received, the AC wire colors were blue and red, which translated to white / black  (neutral / hot) in the U.S..  In the plug, I connected the blue wire to the silver color screw (neutral wire), and the red wire to the brass color screw (hot wire) in the plug.  The ground terminal of the plug was connected to the green / yellow wire.

As reported by others, thought there is a ground wire (green / yellow) on the short (6 inch) pigtail, it isn't connected to the metal housing in the one I received. This wire was too short (inside the housing) to ground directly. It was necessary to  connect it to the base of the rear housing (by removing one of screws), connecting a wire under it and connecting a longer wire to reach the ground wire on the pigtail going into the voltage converter.  I have a soldering iron, solder and used it to insure a good joint to ground (between the longer ground wire and the terminal at the end of the green / yellow wire).  Particularly when you have a metal housing, grounding is necessary for safety. The lights don't appear to be listed (e.g. UL), which isn't surprising when the housing isn't grounded.

As was recommended in other reviews, I removed the glass cover and inner reflector and inspected the mounting of the LED element.  Though there were 4 screws and there was thermal compound on the rear of the LED element, the screws were not down tight. The screws are flat head M3 x 0.5 pitch x 4 mm.  The inner reflector only used 2 screws (same size screw as on the LED element) and got a couple more at the local hardware store.  I made sure the screws were tightened down on the LED, and made sure I had a good (though thin) later of thermal compound.  If you have a LED element that fails and you have a soldering iron, you can replace the LED with one from Amazon or Ebay [currently $9 to $8 for 50W element].  I'm using mine as a plant light operated with a timer, but have also used them for outside illumination.

I prefer the switch below. It is a different idea, not exactly the same.  When I enter the bathroom the light turns on automatically and when I exit the bathroom the light will turn off after one minute, five minutes, 15 minutes, depending on how I program it.  The bathroom fan could turn on and off in the same manner either using the same switch or using a separate switch. Using a separate switch, the fan could turn off after 15 minutes and the light could turn off after just one minute. While you're moving around inside the bathroom  the light will stay on.  Like I said this is not exactly the same but it is more automatic and it is worth thinking about other ideas. This is an occupancy switch but there are also vacancy switches. So I replace the switches in my kitchen with vacancy switches so that when everyone leaves and the lights got left on the lights will turn off automatically after five minutes or whatever you tell it to.  I've installed these  occupancy and vacancy switches all over my house and love them.

https://www.amazon.com/Lutron-required-Single-Pole-Location-MS-OPS5M-WH/dp/B005WM3C42/ref=sr_1_8?ie=UTF8&qid=1475874063&sr=8-8&keywords=Occupancy+switch

I had super high hopes for this vacuum. This is my first roomba. I thought it would have a methodical way of cleaning, but there are several reasons why this vacuum doesn't work like I had expected. Here's the short: the question is vacuum yourself in just minutes or endure loud vacuum background noise all day long by a vacuum that gets confused and dies before going home to recharge itself. I thought this would be something that would simplify my life, but it's more like having a third child...it's noisy and one more thing to watch over.

Cons:
This robot supposedly goes home to recharge before it dies. The very first time I used it, it died and I had to carry it back to home base. Because it died midway through the job, it forgot what it had already done and restarted everything from the beginning when it restarted. After redoing what it had already done, it started to die again and tried to go home  but couldn't attach to home base, making confused circles right in front of it. Again, I had to carry it and manually attach it to home base. So the first 4 hours of cleaning, it only cleaned my dining room. In 4 hours of my own time, I could have hand scrubbed each and every tile and cleaned every inch of grout in the dining room along with polished all the furniture to a high shine.

This thing is loud. Shame on me for thinking it would be something that could run seamlessly in the background. Not so...really loud like a full size dyson and needs to be something that I can run when I'm not home (although I am rarely gone the whole day and it needs the WHOLE day to finish. More on this below).

Short battery life. The roomba starts with a full bettery and runs longest on the full battery. When it dies, it recharges and starts again on it's own, but runs for about 45 minutes before needing to go home to recharge again for another 90 minutes. NINETY MINUTES. Then it restarts the job. This goes on all day long.

Takes the entire day to get the job done. I have about 1000 square feet on the first floor where roomba was working. After EIGHT hours of working and recharging, it was still not done with the job. Finally at 10:30pm and bedtime, I had to simply cancel the job because it's too loud to run in the night (well it can't see well in the night anyways). 8 hours is a long time to endure loud persistent vacuum noise on the main level on and off all day. I'm curious to know how long it would have taken to get the actual job completely "done" had I let it keep going. 12 hours? 15 hours? 1000 sq ft takes me all of 10 minutes to vacuum on my own. The question is truly do it yourself in 5 minutes or endure loud vacuuming noise all day long. Maybe if you leave all day for work this may be the thing for you. If you work from home like I do... maybe not the best choice.

I am not going to bother with replacement/warranty as this is a fairly cheap item, and it will work fine as a caliper, just not in the digital way. But I am quite disappointed.

I purchased six of these and two leaked through the valve stem with a fine spray. They are in an outdoor location so it matters little and I hope they will seal-off eventually. After I set the flow I shouldn't have to readjust them and renew the leaking. They would be a pain to cut out of the system now.

Industrial_and_Scientific.reviewText: With the Schwinn reputation for quality  one would think that "some assembly required" would not be a major stumbling block for your average parent or grandparent. However this trike required some major drilling and re-drilling one of the holes needed to fit the deck assembly to the frame. Once the hole was widened the screw was able to be tightend but...the frame was a not a good fit. The piece was bent....What's a parent or grandparent to do???Send it back? Not have the gift for the birthday? Make do and hope for the best? I believe the integrity of the trike has not been compromised too much and we will keep it. But...Shame on Schwinn for not having better quality control

If you want a painful finger, this is the meter to get. To get a reading requires not only holding the meter in the liquid but at the same time, holding a switch that hates being moved. It wants to spring back and it fights you when you try to push it. It's as if it's screaming, "I don't want to read the pH; I don't want to read the pH." And if you ever wanted to become a contortionist, just trying calibrating it. Now while you're struggling to hold in the liquid and bearing down on that recalcitrant button, you need jam a jeweler's screwdriver into a small hole in the back and twist it. Don't forget to put your best contacts because the display is super tiny.

I really believe Milwaukee Instruments is working in cahoots with hydronium ions to prevent us from counting them.

Seriously, this is a pH meter you want to avoid.

This silicone product Red Devil 826 100% Silicone Sealant Clear Architectural Grade 50 Yr. 10.1 Oz. Cartridgewas prominantly displayed during a search specifically for "aquarium sealant". While it may be a great product, the manufacture directions on the container clearly state that the product is "NOT RECOMMENDED for use on aquariums". A little more information in the product description about usage caveats would have helped me avoid a useless, time consuming purchase. For what it's worth, the extra cost next day shipping was flawless. I received the product as promised he following afternoon.

Maybe...under the perfect conditions...with the moons aligned and the gods smiling down...then, this stuff may stick where you put it.  Mostly not though.  I simply want to warn people that I tried once again to use this stuff and for the third time it just let me down.  I threw it out.  Waste of time and money.

This  made in China metal platform truck is sold under various manufacturer names on Amazon.com.  I doubt if the truck is heavy duty, in that it could stand up to punishment, but it is definitely heavy, weighing about 40 pounds. The only way to get the truck out of the crushed box was to cut away all sides and just pulling it out. You have to attach the four wheels yourself.  This involves pulling out four bolts attached to the bottom of the truck for each wheel, along with their flimsy locking washers. You then have  to attach each 5" wheel to the platform using the bolts and washers. The threaded part of the bolt is only about 3/4" with a hex head, perhaps too short. A socket wrench should do the job, but getting the bolts back into platform both tight and straight is no easy matter. The wheels do not allow for much headroom, so getting the socket to work properly becomes quite a chore. I had to resort to a set of pliers to complete the  tightening, which wasn't always as tight or straight as I would like. With the short bolts there is also a strong possibility the wheels could become loose or fall off after several uses.

Given the weight of this truck, a good deal of the Amazon cost is for additional shipping charges. If you could pick it up at a local store it would cost about $40-$50 plus the sales tax. Also returning this monster to Amazon would be quite a chore. (But I am contemplating  doing it anyway.) Buying  a platform truck at your local home improvement store  may be a more rational choice. Look for a Rubbermaid  brand truck. Their wheels just pop in and lock in place. No bolts necessary; and they weigh far less than this one.
Industrial_and_Scientific.summary: Not worth the trouble of assembly or the cost.

Industrial_and_Scientific.reviewText: Complete Chinese garbage. My project required 22 tacks. Good thing I bought a bigger package because it took 34 tacks to complete. I used a proper tack hammer and have reupolstered plenty of chairs in the past using American made tacks from Jo-Ann fabrics with no troubles. These tacks bend and break very easy no matter how squarely you hit them with the hammer. I now need to do some touch up painting on my piece due to these week azz tacks. The only reason I'm giving them a two star rating instead of a one star rating, is because when I finally did get the tacks in, they do look nice and create the appearance I was looking for.....after plenty of curse words and frustration later. I will drive the hour and a half to buy American made tacks for now on.

I purchased this caliper because it was represented as USA made.  When I got it I discovered it is Chinese made.  The purchase thru Amazon was with Antonline.  To return a product to Antonline, they require a 15% restocking fee. So here's the math:  Cost of caliper thru Antonline = $29.63.  Shipping =  $6.93.  15% of $29.63 = $4.44.  So to return a product after such a discovery will cost me shipping 2x $6.93 plus the 15% restocking fee of $4.44 for a grand total of $18.24.
So I decided to contact General about this. I wrote them a decent e-mail telling them what has happened.  And I got NO REPLY, which is no surprise considering the way large corporations think about their customers these days.  This is the last General tool I will ever buy.  If we consumers get more pro-active in our purchases and respond in this and other ways, maybe, just maybe, we can get a little respect for our hard earned money.

Returning this item. Straight out of the box, there was a small cover on the top of the calipers that was loose and kept falling off. The thumb wheel was loose and wobbled from side to side. Readings were inconsistent--when the tool was closed and zero'd out, it would always show a different reading after it was opened and returned to closed.

shows pan head screws.  What was in the box was 1/4 - 20 flat head screws. The image I see when writing this is of a flat head screw. The image on the returns page is of a flat head screw.  Items look OK but not at all correct.  Am returning the item.

The Erisan EZM2 Aircast is actually one cool little device. You will receive the AirCast, the WiFi and adapter cord and also an instructional pamphlet. Let me share with you step by step how to install and use this unit. First attach the provided cord to the aircast unit. Then attach the aircast unit to your TV. The little aircast device itself has a HDMI plug which you plug into your TV. Then you will need to plug the other cord which is attached to the cord adapter to a USB charging plug. My tv automatically pulled my HDMI screen up once plugged into my tv but you may need to cycle through your TV options to the HDMI setting. You will get a blue screen with info about the aircast on it. You will now need to turn your WiFi on your phone and it will scan picking up the aircast name which is " MiraScreenD2F2784A" Click on this name and enter the password which is located on the right upper screen of your TV. Once you get the little check markon your iPhone meaning your connected, slide your option screen up and press the air drop button. Then you will see the option to turn on the "Mirroring" on the device name " MiraScreenD2F2784A." Once turned on you will then see the screen that is on your phone on your TV. In the pictures provided you can see the many different things I did with my aircast. My daughter and I had a lot of fun going through our pictures and she sat and watched them on the television. I also checked my email, got on to my Facebook page, checked out my tweets on twitter and also watched a few videos I had recorded on my phone. This device is not able to play YouTube videos which is kind of a bummer but still really cool to do other things on. When the aircast displays on the screen it does not fill the whole screen up, it is just a bigger size from your phone size. This device was so easy to set up! I used my iPhone 6 with this aircast! This device is a great way to share pictures with a big group of people on the TV. No more having to pass around your phone. Just use the aircast, sit back and cycle through what you want! I definitely recommend this aircacst! I received this product for free in exchange for an honest and unbiased review.

Electronics.reviewText:
Since I spend a great deal of time flying for work, I decided it was time to upgrade my cheap headphones for a better quality set instead of the cheap pair I usually have or the ones provided by airlines (can never tell if they actually sanitize them).

After a great deal of research reading reviews by audiophiles, I decided to try the MH40's out along with the Beoplay H6, Beoplay H8, MH30. numerous Beats models and what ever model Bose what available at the local Apple Store.

I made sure to listen to the same songs on each pair to determine the sound quality that I liked as well as which offered the best comfort (I wear glasses) and muffled out background sounds. Luckily it was a busy day at the Apple Store so there was a very good amount of background noise created by all the other shoppers.

Out of all of the pairs I tried, I loved the MH40's the best with the H6's a close second. The Bose much like other users have noted had a very bland or muted sound quality no doubt due to the noise cancelling feature. Everything else I tried was too bass heavy which I do not like. The H8's actually produced a certain low frequency that almost immediately cased discomfort in my ears and a headache.

Pro's that made me decide on the MH40's:

* Extremely light, comfortable and does not disturb or effect my glasses
* I love the sound quality, works great with everything I listen to (Classical, Blues, Rock, R&B (non-Hip Hop), and the variety of Electronic music)
* Sounds great with movies as well
* Comes with 2 cables that can be removed in case they are damaged
* Well made with great materials (still have to see how they hold up long term)
* Breath well, no sweating around my ears even after wearing them for an extended period in a warm store
* Has an easy to reach mute button on the right side
* Love the retro look

Con's or things I did not like:

* $399 price (but I prefer quality so expect to pay more)
* Lacks a hard case, only a cloth bag (especially for this price point, a $20 hard case like the Geekria could have been included)

Over all I look forward to enjoying the MH40's on my upcoming flights this year.

One quick note, if you are like me and tend not to read instructions before using devices, make sure to plug the cord into the left side and not the right side otherwise you will notice issues with the sound quality since the right side is meant as an output only connection.

For Mac users, I tested the MH40's on my iMac, 17" Mac Book Pro and 11" Mac Book Air as well as both of my iPhones (6 & 6+) and found that they work great with all of them (including the inline volume controls).

If you are thinking of purchasing a pair of MH40's but also want a hard case to protect them, check out the Greekria case I purchased and wrote a review on as well.
Electronics.summary: Fabulous Headphones - NOT FOR BASS HEADS!!!

I am one of the people who was late onto the iPhone scene, but before I finally got mine I did some extensive research on accessories. Having heard about the short battery life, mostly due to the phone's capabilities, I decided a backup battery/charger was a must. I researched a number of batteries/chargers and finally decided I liked the Kensington Battery Pack and Charger.

I have not been disappointed. Here are the things I have liked about this battery pack and charger:

1. You can charge the iPhone and battery pack at the same time, which is nice if you use the battery pack on a daily basis.
2. You get an extra iPhone data cable (iPhone/iPod hookup on one end and a USB plug on the other). When I'm at work I just use this cable to charge my iPhone from my laptop's USB.
3. Using the supplied accessories you can charge just the iPhone or just the battery. Basically, you are getting another iPhone DC Adapter.
4. The battery charges the phone almost completely while still on. I have had a number of instances where my battery was at 10%-20%. I plugged in the battery pack, while leaving the phone on and I was able to get my charge up to about 90% in about 2-3 hours. If I turned off the phone, I'm sure I would have gotten the full charge, but 90% while still being able to use the phone is great.

I have very few complaints about the battery pack, other than it would be nice if it were smaller. Even so, the battery pack is smaller than the iPhone and a little bit thinner. So, in the grand scheme of things there could be much bigger draw backs.

Overall, I am extremely pleased with the purchase. For the money, you can't go wrong considering all the extras you get for the price. I've seen a lot of other chargers go for more, which didn't even come close to features and accessories.

Here are some tips to help you when your iPhone is low on battery until you get your Kensington Battery Pack and Charger:

- Decrease the brightness of the screen
- Not using Wifi, turn it off under settings
- Not using Bluetooth, turn it off under settings
- Not using GPS (localization services), turn it offer under settings
- Set Fetch New Data option to Manually

Electronics.reviewText:
About me:

I'm a Computer Programmer/Photographer who uses a Laptop for coding, DSLR to take pictures and Good music player to listen to music. Simply put, I use a equipment for what it's meant for (and the manufacturer is good at making it).  I'm not a musician but still have a deep love for any music.

For people who aren't anywhere close to getting a Bose:

So if you're the kind to use a cellphone to take "awesome" pictures, DSLR to take videos and Dock Station to have Alarm and Radio, you rather go for one of those Dock Stations which has the fancy LED Display, Radio and Alarm clocks but sounds distorted when you try bumping it up beyond 60% Volume (basically Jack of All trades, master of none). They're still worth every penny if you need a Multi-purpose gadget. No complaints there. You can stop reading now.

Those who are seriously considering a Bose Sounddock:

Just remember, with Great Quality comes Great Price. :( If your love for music is greater than your desire to save a couple of hundred dollars of hard earned money, then this is my 2 cent. "Buy it, blindly" (else) "Go to a store nearby and compare the quality of every Dock ever manufactured. 2 hours later, you'd still buy this one" Why? Pure "Music Magic". The SDP blew away every Dock on the shelf (of similar portable size).

Sounddock Portable (or) Soundlink???

Bluetooth is certainly a nice thing to have in a Dock Station, but Unfortunately SDP doesn't. But that isn't a deal-breaker and definitely not a reason you need to go for a Soundlink blindly. Soundlink sure is more portable (weight/dimension wise), but definitely slightly less on the volume front. And both Sounddock ($100 off) and Soundlink are same in price now ($299). I choose volume over portability and to fix the lack of Bluetooth, all I did was get a Sounddock Bluetooth Adapter for $15 off Amazon. So now, I have a truly portable SDP which can play music from almost anything using Bluetooth/IphoneDock/3.5mm AUX.
I already have the Bose MIE2i mobile headset so I really wasn't surprised over the clarity of the SDP or the Ergonomics of Bose products. What really surprised me is the difference the Waveguide speaker technology has over other Docks. No matter which end of the room you are sitting in, it almost feels like sitting in the best seat of a Music concert... Pleasing to the ears. I still haven't jacked it up to max volume cos it's so loud, I don't want the apartment neighbors to complain. Ideal portable player for outdoor camping, BBQ, indoor parties/workout etc. It just doesn't play music... it gets you into the feel of it too.  Bose has also paid attention to small practical problems of a Remote Control and frequently tangled up wires. You'll understand what I mean when you buy one.

Only possible Design Flaw I noticed till now:

I was a bit shocked at first, when I realized I had to keep adjusting the Iphone on the Dock for loose connection. Then I realized I hadn't docked in the iphone properly and fixed it again properly (need to apply more pressure than you would want to, on a $400 system). The Dock station pin looks a bit flimsy and MIGHT wear out eventually with heavy usage. But doesn't matter to me cos I'm only planning to use it with Bluetooth mostly.

My only reason for concern before buying is that, Amazon shows this product was launched in April 18, 2005 (atleast the earliest version of it). But after a lot of research I realized that this product (new version) is just 10 years ahead of the competition and the rest are still catching up. $100 off on a Bose might mean the next version is coming soon but who cares... I ain't no professional musician and I don't think my ears can differentiate anything that sounds better/crisper/nicer than this one. 5 stars!

This is an incredibly cheap tablet, which I feared would not work well but so far it done everything I expected a tablet to do. It came already 80% charged, and though the instructions say that you need to charge it for 10 hours before first using it, I used it after five or so hours when the battery showed 100% ready. It comes with a white USB cord and I charged this quickly and easily using my USB wall charger.

The tablet is smaller than others I've seen, about the size of a paperback book and very thin. This makes it great for toting in a backpack or handbag. Needless to say it's great for reading eBooks and watching videos. It takes up little room and is perfect for travel. The blue plastic casing feels a little cheap, however, so I'd be careful with it (this is the only sign, for me, that it's a less expensive tablet).

The touchscreen is predictably sensitive and I had no problems searching the Web and changing the wallpaper (it now boasts a photo of my current cat, Maggie). A few times I had to tap it a little harder, but nothing unusual about that - a lot of tablets have funky moments.

On a single charge, it worked well for three days, though I didn't use it for more than an hour at a time. By the third day, the battery power was down to 34%, but I think that's pretty good, especially if you're using it to supplement a smartphone while you are out and about.

Another thing that's cool - this iRULU is fully up to date and will let you download the latest apps out there. My smartphone has an outdated browser, which makes downloading new apps a headache unless I upgrade. With iRULU I was able to download the newest stuff, including that maddeningly addictive cat collector game, Neko Atsume.

Note: the user should be aware that this tablet is very Google-friendly, and in order to use some of the functions I had to give Google permission to sync the tablet with my Gmail and provide Google with all that personal information that it so greedily collects. Once you do this, it's a breeze to use, including the speak-only Google Now app, which allows you to search the web by voice alone.

In short, all the functions worked smoothly. The only area where I was disappointed was the "Camera" function. I tried to take photos of my cat, but they all looked blurry and not very sharp. I tried again and the same result. So, not impressed with this part of it.

Otherwise this tablet offers a lot of great features for very little money. Only time will tell if it is durable as well.

I'd done the research, checked the benchmarks, and read many a technical review before finally deciding on this card. I've had great experiences with ASUS in general, and their 680s have been getting good reviews. I have a really good gaming desktop, but it's 3 years old, and while I really enjoy my 480GTXes, the 680 has been a dramatic improvement.

FITTING IN
If you're looking to drop one or more of these in your computer case, you definitely want to check the measurements, as this card is LONG. It is just a tiny bit longer than my 480GTXes, but inside a case that may make all the difference, so check the dimensions before buying. I've also noticed that the heat-pipes stand just a tiny bit taller than the 480GTX, so if it's already close quarters between your side panel and your current card, check measurements. The card has two 6-pin power plugs. If you have 8-pin plugs, most allow you to separate the last two pins for just this purpose, but if for some reason you don't, then ASUS provides you with a power 'Y' cable that will convert two Molex (4-pin) plugs into one 6-pin video plug.

FIRING UP
The ASUS 680 GTX is all about small improvements leading to big gains: the two fans atop the heatsink are large, but the fan motors have noise dampening built into them. There were issues with the 480s getting heat trapped between the end of the card and the back of the case, so slight changes to the shape of the vents have fixed this problem. Because there is a monstrous amount of metal hanging upside down off the card for heat blocks, fans, and pipes, the backplate is the size of the card and the countersunk screws tightly hold everything in place. NVidia have introduced a technology called GPU Boost that raises and lowers performance on demand and will eagerly push the clock speed and voltage envelopes while keeping an eye on temperatures. ASUS also adds a software utility that makes it very easy for you to raise the bar yourself: you can set voltages, clock speeds, fan sensitivity and speeds, to all have a higher floor. Unfortunately, you cannot disable or control NVidia's GPU Boost at this time--Tom's Hardware groused that this made managing their benchmarking sessions fairly difficult--but if you use the ASUS software to adjust settings you may find you have some control over how low the usage goes.

FLYING HIGH
Installation was as cut and dried as it should be: uninstall all NVidia software, shut down, swap old cards for new, check connections, power up and install the new drivers. One reboot later and I was ready to rock. After popping into Skyrim and trying 2D and 3DVision, I was amazed at how much 'sharper' everything appeared to be: not just a framerate improvement, but a kind of clarity that reminds me of an eye doctor's office: "Better or worse?" "Oh, man...definitely BETTER." Skyrim, Bioshock Infinite, and Planetside 2 all ran smooth as silk at 1920 x 1080 and of course there was not a hiccup when dropping down to 1280x720 for some 3D gaming.*

I haven't run every performance benchmark I can think of yet, but I did run Futuremark's latest "Extreme" benchmarking test for games. With the 480s, I was above-average, but not Superman. With the 680s, I instantly hit the top score and was 1,000 marks above my nearest competitor. The fact that I can run anything at the highest possible settings is overkill, and I think based on benchmarks I've read that the fact that this is a 4GB card makes a substantial difference: the 2GB is quite an excellent card, this one just gives the GPU so much more room to play.

If you have the money, and like me you were watching for the 700 series to put some downward price pressure on the 680s, the ASUS 4GB GTX680-DC2-4GD5 is definitely a huge bang...it's just still a somewhat sizeable amount of bucks.

Tech Specs:
Intel Core i7 Xtreme 980X Processor (six cores), overclocked to 4.2GHz using Intel Performance Tuning
3 x 4GB DDR3 gaming RAM, overclocked using Intel XMP
Samsung 830 Series SSD with Windows 8 Professional 64-bit installed
4 x 1TB WD Caviar Black (RAID 5) for programs
2 x ASUS 4GB GTX680-DC2-4GD5 graphics cards (SLI enabled) rendering to a Vizio 46" 3D HDTV

*a word about online games like Planetside 2: no matter what machine or how fast a connection, if you are in a world with a lot of people and a lot of combat, you may see slowdowns that have nothing to do with your hardware and everything to do with the game servers trying to manage all that traffic. When Sony sold 'fireworks' guns on the 4th of July weekend, my Planetside 2 sessions became a mess of massive battles combined with groups of people standing around shooting off fireworks all over the place...everyone's performance dropped.

Well, just under three months of using the nuvi 265WT, and I returned it to Costco. For the first time Garmin has let me down. I am truly disappointed - the first out of 6 Garmins I have owned (fitness watches 301, and now 305; Street Pilot 330; Nuvi 350; eTrex Vista, and this 265WT). I gave it every opportunity to come through, to deliver on the promise of an improved nuvi, but nearly every aspect of this unit is a step behind my dear, departed (gave it away!) nuvi 350:

1. Confounding  Interface - As an example, they moved the custom POI from the Favorites, down another level to EXTRAS. Why? In the 350, selecting Favorites gave a list of Recently Selected, Saved Favorites, and Custom POIs, if there were any installed. You now have to go to another level, on the second screen (page down) for EXTRAS, and the only extra is Custom POIs. Why?

2. Exasperating Interface - It always annoyed me (even on my 350) that there was no quick way to get back to the main menu, or the map, after having to do a menu dive for POIs or, even worse, entering an address. "BACK, BACK, BACK, BACK." Until you hit the main menu and are able to select "Display Map." Now, if you are programming a multiple stop trip, you have to enter the first destination, wait for the trip to calculate, and then begin to go back through the menus to add the next destination. Once again, "BACK, BACK, BACK, BACK" through the menus. But now, there is a trip in progress, and down in the lower left corner of the main menu screen, the same place that the BACK button was, is the STOP button. Hit that corner one too many times, and your trip is cancelled - start again. Exasperating.

3.  Traffic - this was THE primary reason for me to upgrade. The free traffic reports directly to your GPS. I travel 90 minutes one way on my commute. A lot of roads and good traffic reports are my best friend. And reports on radio are not good - you have to wait 10-15 minutes for them to come up, and then they are 20-30 minutes behind. I was hoping the real time updates to my GPS would be the ticket. And they would be IF THEY WERE EVER RIGHT. I know many people out here have said they are great. My trip entails the Garden State Parkway, and sometimes the New Jersey Turnpike. Two major roads in a major metropolitan area. The traffic reports are so bad, I simply ignore them. I stopped getting mad because the reports were wrong; I now get mad when they are right. Which is RARE. To those readers living in NJ, try the NJ 511 service. 511 from your cell phone, and you get the most current traffic reports. Fantastic; it has taken the place of radio and the nuvi.

4. Sudden Muting - I turn on the GPS, and no sound. I have to go to volume, adjust the volume (up or down, it doesn't matter) and then the muting ends. This happens regularly. Others have reported the same problem.

5. Helium Voice - Every once and awhile, the GPS stop responding.  Touch the screen and it slowly comes out of a "slumber" - only to awaken with lungs full of helium. They voice has turned high-pitched. Only a hard reset will fix it.

6. Bluetooth problems - if you setup a connection to your Bluetooth cell phone, but the phone is not in range when you turn on the GPS, you get a connection failure message (for example, I get in the car, start up the GPS, go back into the house to get something and come back out after the GPS has started). No problem. Menu dive DEEP into system settings to set up the connection. The GPS will lock up EVERYTIME. I have learned that I just do not turn on the GPS until I know my phone will stay in range.

7. Strange Direction Changes - I go home the same way everyday, along the GSP. The only way is by NJ 208. Typically, the 265WT will correctly send me down 208 to NJ 4 and then the GSP. But strangely, every once and awhile, it will send me down back roads, through Patterson NJ. Or at least try to. I know enough now to simply pass that instructed turn off and it will re-calculate. Originally I thought it was because Navigation setting had "Avoid Traffic" as the default. (Which in and of itself is a problem - why would that be the default, especially when "Avoid Traffic" is an option when reviewing traffic reports). But it is not the problem - I long ago set that option off. That route, even on the best of days, is at least 10 minutes longer, although a few miles shorter (and no, I do not have the GPS set to SHORTEST ROUTE).

8. Advertisements - I do not mind the ads, and I understand they pay for the "free" traffic reports. But I have, over the 3 months I owned the 265WT, seen the same ad - Best Western! That's it! 3 hours a day, 5 days a week, and the same lousy ad over and over. And it pops up all over the place, not just when you are on the map looking at the directions. Do a search - there's an ad; select a POI - there's an ad; check the settings - there's an ad. The ONLY ad. Best Western. And, to my mind, selecting the ad should make it disappear. I saw the ad, selected it, read it, now GO AWAY. Nope - keeps popping up. Over and over and over again.

What can I say, up to this unit, I loved my Garmins. Before I sprung for this GPS, I considered just keeping my trusty 350 and updating the maps. But the lure of wide screens, bluetooth and traffic reports vs. spending $60 for a map upgrade, well, I sprung for the new. And gave away my 350. And regret that decision.

Hey, there area lot of 4-5 star reviews for this GPS, some by first time Garmin or GPS owners, some by long timers. Maybe there was a problem with mine unit, but based upon the feedback read here about similar problems, I think not.

Some might say, why not contact Garmin support? Well, the reason is, if there was a problem, they would want the unit for repair/replace. The problems:

1. I pay for shipping
2. I am out a GPS until they repair or replace
3. The replacement is almost ALWAYS a refurb - trade my brand new unit for a repaired? I don't think so
4. Costco has a great return policy - no questions, 90 days. If I exchange it, I get a new unit, or I can return it for a full refund. Which is what I did - get a refund.

I have my money back, no nuvi 350, and I am searching again for a new GPS. The 755 looks tempting, but I see similar problems with THAT unit too! I may have to go to the dark side - and consider TomTom or Magellan. I hope there is a Garmin out there that fits the bill.
Electronics.summary: Oh! How I Miss My Nuvi 350!

Electronics.reviewText:
I have purchased Poetic cases for everybody in my family over the past few years. They used to be fantastic, and are still holding up for everyone. Everyone, except me.

I have been so annoyed by this case I needed to post a review. The first one I received had gouges out of the cover, horrible condition. Sent it back.

On the second one, I use my iPad about 15 times a week, never in portrait mode, and I never drop my gadgets.

The first crack started about two weeks after purchase, but it was small so I didn't care, it was more, "Wow the reviewers on Amazon were right, this has weak plastic". Then, two nights ago, I'm holding it in portrait mode reading news, and plastic pieces start falling off the corners under my hands. Absolutely unacceptable. Now, whenever I hold my iPad, I'm holding sharp edges of plastic. Beware of the weak plastics Poetic used in this model of case.

Two stars because the product itself is great, but they really tried to skimp on the plastic in this model compared to other models. Charge me more money for a more robust plastic- I love your product- but don't give me some flimsy thing that degrades your brand because it can't be used for more than a few months.

Unfortunately, I'm probably going to buy another one because they're so slim and the cheapest, relatively high quality case I have seen.
Electronics.summary: Weak plastic, does not compare to other excellent Poetic cases.
