Electronics.reviewText: This was comfortable but did not hold up. I don't think it was made for books. One of the straps ripped out from the stitching. I do like the design, so it allowed me to put so much into it, but the stitching did hold up. Also, the big front flap only has magnetic posts to keep it held against the the bag, and to keep it from flapping up and down when you walk. So if you put something heavy or not entirely flat in this front flap's pouch, or the inner pouch to which this flap's magnetic posts attach, the flap does not stay attached to the face of the bag, and you end up having the pouch flapping up and down as you walk. This bag needs a mechanical fastener, like heavy duty snaps, instead of the magnetic posts. The layout is great. It has all the right pouches and compartments in all the right places, yet, the assembled product needs heavier duty thread, fasteners, and zippers. Makes me want to make my own bag. Needs memory foam too. It is comfortable as it stands. If you do not plan on putting more than 3-4lbs in this, you should get a couple of years out of it. In sum, great design, poor craftsmanship.

I've had a DLink DIR-655 for about five years.  Its an AWESOME wireless router - I can receive throughout the house and even across the street in my neighbors house, the signal going several hundred feet through two brick walls and a couple of room walls.

So it seem logical that the "new improved" DIR-645 would be even better, right"  WRONG!  I bought this for my lake house.  It has barely ten feet range on a good day, almost no signal through walls, etc.  So I bought a DLink DAP-1360 wireless extender, which DLink claims works in several modes.  Again a lemon: It locks up the entire network when connected via cable to the router.  It works in "wireless repeater" mode - sort of - but the entire thing, router and range extender, has less range than my old router.

Don't waste your time with this, get a DIR-655 instead.

I've had mine since September and took it along on a short vacation to Michigan and Florida.  I came home with maybe 150 images set mostly on Aperture priority for the trip.  Thinking the f8 setting may help the sharpness I can't say it helped at all.  Possibly the dof changed but I'll have to push it a little harder with some more challenging dof requirements.  As others have mentioned the GPS does draw down the battery quite fast especially in log mode in a couple of short days for me. I did drop the camera once onto concrete from 2 ft or so.  It damaged the metal band near the flash but otherwise all works well.

Pros:  Lightning fast start-up and shutter response.
The GPS is handy.
Very good low light performance.
 Not a bad price point.

Cons: The GPS is handy but slow to acquire a location (  100ft) and draws down the battery fast.
Weak flash.
Colors get muddy in the fine details, yellows and green especially.  I find this true in my other Canon Power shot A710-IS as well and the fall colors in Michigan especially took a hit.
Edit:  October 2013.  I've started getting lens errors occasionally and have to power off the camera to "fix" it.

Edit:  March 2014.  Getting "lens errors" continuously now and the camera shuts off.  So I guess it's all over for this one. 2 1/2 years was it's life span.
  I've down graded the rating to two stars.

I am giving this product a low score because it did not work.  The extra star is because I bought the product from Buy Accessories and I expected it to be in a brand new package which it wasn't.  It could be possible that even though I paid for a new product that I was shipped a used product that did not work.  With that in mind it is possible that the product may very well be a great product but I was an unlucky buck.

For me,the product did not work from the beginning.  The blue light turned on, but the numbers never showed and after a few seconds the light slowly dimmed into nothing.  I ended up buying a tune fm transmitter which was cheaper and works fine [...]

I'v had this unit for about a year, and have had lots of little problems with it- nothing that required actual repair, but lots of software/functionality bugs.  I'm particularly upset that the TV Guide Plus channel that's included is now no longer available on my cable system, so now I have to program everything manually.  So instead of a nice browser list of program names, all I get is a list of channel numbers and dates. I have another similar Philips unit that has been even worse.  I'd probably never buy another Philips product.

I got this because I needed a basic router that could handle multiple connections and not break under the strain.  I needed all 4 ports for a desktop (gigabit Ethernet destroys wireless for ping on multiplayer games!), PS3 (same reason), and two networked printers.  I also have three or four devices that connect wirelessly.  This router was easy to set up, had good security options and seemed to work fine for a couple of months.  But I found that YouTube on the wireless connection with a Windows Update running means that my Android smartphone net speed slows to a crawl.  I pay for a 20mbps connection and Speedtest shows that this isn't giving it to me.

This router cannot handle multiple connections very well.  Downloading large open-source code packages via P2P networks chokes the pipe to a crawl OR kills it altogether until an unplug and restart.  I have a 1000 square foot apartment with this in one bedroom and when I'm on the other side of the apartment, I don't get full signal.

This is a good basic router for a single user who primarily streams YouTube or Netflix to one laptop at a time.  If you are a power user or really need good range, then you need to spend more money on a N600 or N900-level router.  Additionally, since this router does not specify compatibility with IPv6, a more expensive router might be more future proof.

I never used the USB port so I can't comment on it.  I never flashed Tomato to it, so I am not sure if that it a good thing or not.  I just know that this router is not really optimized to take advantage of superfast modem speeds.
Electronics.summary: If you need Tomato to make it better, it isn't that great to begin with!

Electronics.reviewText: This product was a bit disappointing.  The installation should have been pretty straight forward, as it says it is vesa 200 compliant.  Well, the mounting holes line up, but they did not provide the M8 screws necessary for my 40" Samsung LED (sorry, I can't provide the exact model number). We went to the hardware store to pick up four M8 screws - and then realized that those screws will not fit through the mounting plate.  We ended up using a dremel to increase the hole size to allow the M8 screw to pass though. After that, it worked fine and we didn't have to buy a different mounting plate.  It was just a lot more work than I was expecting for a product that should have been fairly easy.
Electronics.summary: The mounting plate does not accept M8 screws

Electronics.reviewText: I've gone through several of these due to internal issues (probably due to faulty wiring). Even when I take care of these as carefully as I can, over time one or both of the headphones will stop working. This happened to my last pair recently, so I contacted Yurbuds customer service and got a replacement pair - but the replacement pair that they sent me was already broken (the right headphone flickers in and out of working)....I contacted them again explaining that they sent me a faulty pair, and I haven't heard back for 2 weeks now. They get 2 stars for being pretty much the only headphones on the market that fit in my ears right, but I'm fed up with them breaking so often, and now especially with my last experience with their customer service.
Electronics.summary: Break on their own too often

Electronics.reviewText:
I'm not an intense user of GPS. I use it once or twice a week and it has been useful. My Garmin nuvi 1450 suddenly lost its voice. It seemed to navigate ok but without the voice its useless to me. Its out of warranty. I called support and they told me it had to be refurbished for $110. I can get a new GPS for not much more.
I had the thing fully charged all the time. It seems that the critical files on the device were somehow corrupted and couldn't be restored.
Its too bad because I liked using it. It was accurate and easy to use. It did the job for me when it was working.
It makes no sense to me to buy another Garmin, just to have it crap out on me again. I had another 1450 before this one for a few days and that one failed as well. I simply returned it for a new one figuring it was a fluke.
I have no complaints about their support. They responded quickly. I'll try a TomTom next and see how that works out.

Just finished comparing this $70 amplified Mohu 50 antenna to a $6 flat blue non-amplified antenna from eBay that I have been using for a year and guess what?...They are identical in terms of number of channels pulled (39 for me from 5-14 miles)! In fact, this amplified mohu did much worse in terms of signal strength for several channels that had higher strength with the blue antenna. Very disappointed, taking it back to sams. I stuck both antennas outside to the side wall about 10 ft above ground for this comparison since indoor reception is really poor (and comparable for both). BTW, I have tried several antennas so far and the best reception I get is from an attic mounted DB8, however, on rainy/cloudy days, I get unstable signal from ABC and NPT. Hence, the experimentation with new antennas continues......  Next to combine signals from two differently oriented antennas since these two channels are ~120 degrees apart from the rest of channels. They added flexible orienting capability to the new DB8e in which you can face different panels in different directions. Maybe I will ebay my DB8 and buy a DB8e.
Electronics.summary: Don't fall for this and pay $50 more than cheap flat antennas.....

Electronics.reviewText: This seemed "broken" to me because some of the keys didn't type what they are supposed to type...  like hitting "m" gets you a comma!  Well, now I know that it is acting like a "AZERTY" keyboard (that France likes), not a typical "QWERTY" keyboard that most countries and the United States uses.  If it were just a few letters, I could have lived with it, but all the characters above the numbers are screwy as well!  I can't find anything on the internet that addresses this for these tiny, cheap keyboards, so I will probably have to return the next one that I ordered as well, since it operates exactly the same way.

This is my first ipod. All over, it is a well done product. A lot of cool apps to keep you from boredom. But this ipod as a media player...it's just average or even below average in some cases.

My other MP3 player are the Sony Ericsson i750 & Sonly Clie TJ37, they blow this ipod away when it comes to the sound quality. It's hard to believe there's no EQ for ipod Touch, sound quality is flat as the result of all genres play on one flat EQ setting. iTunes 8 is extremely slow on Windows XP doesn't help much neither.

Video is cool, instant access to youtube. Once again, lack of video controls. It only has brightness control, no contrast (I might be wrong on this)

Pro:
- Near perfection integration between iPod & iTune, very easy to use
- Display lyrics on screen (if lyric is loaded on iTune)
- Superb user interface
- Accelerometer really brings fun out of the games, kinda like Wii.
- Supports microphone, which enables to use VOIP such as Skype over wifi
- A tone of cool apps and a tone of junk apps

Cons:
- Too large and fragile to be an everyday portable MP3 player, unless you have a man bag. lol.  One drop, it is gone. I've dropped my i750 many times and it still rocks.
- Average sound quality with no EQ support. What is Apple thinking?
- Turtle speed with iTune 8 on Windows XP
- Average earphone
- expensive accessory. $15.00-30.00 for a piece of thin silicon skin that is made in China?

If you want a solid and durable MP3 player, this is not the one for you. But if you want an average MP3 player with lots apps to keep you entertained, then this is a great gadget for you!

Update 3/08:
Good news, it does have an EQ. Bad news, it is buried in the Setting->Music->EQ.The difference between the EQ settings is barely noticeable, it's better than none.

It also a bug, its clock will go crazy when it connects with the PC where iTunes 8 is already running. You have to make sure iTunes 8 is not running on the PC before plug in the USB, otherwise you have to set the clock each time.

Apple, iTunes movie rental is a great idea. But $3.99 for 24 hours on a tiny screen? Hmmm...you should have a 0.99 rental for iphone/ipod touch category.
Electronics.summary: an average media player with average sound quality

Electronics.reviewText: The microphone is staticy and the headphone cord developed a short in it after a week or so of light useage. The microphone cord got a short two weeks afterwards. I typically used it for my laptop while on my bed. I'd plug it into the laptop, sit there and use it, then when I was done I'd unplug it and set it by my alarm clock, so there wasn't exactly any rough treatment of it.
Electronics.summary: The microphone is staticy and the headphone cord developed a ...

Electronics.reviewText: HATE IT! The only thing it was good for was storing music. Other than that it was useless. It took me about 5 hours to download the software from the site. Then once connected I didn't know that if I deleted the music off of the computer it will also delete the music I uploaded on the player (sync feature). Also since I have a huge collection it is hard to use this because I have to scroll to whatever song, album, or artist I wanted, and this would take a long time. Another big peeve was that the touch pad didn't work correctly. I would click on a song to play and it would take me somewhere I didn't want to be or I would try to change a song and it would display the menu where you can go to the artist or view song list. The good things about the player was its headphones (I loved them because the sound is really crisp), the radio being able to display the song title and artist (sometimes it didn't work), and that it came in red.

I used this to listen to music streamed on my phone while in my car, plugged into the aux of my stereo. Rather inexpensive and it worked ok for a year.

The controls on the unit allowed for play, pause, and skip forward and back while connected through Bluetooth. Sometimes it would remember to power on with volume at full, and other times it was at minimum.

The Mic was unintelligible when used with Bluetooth calling.

An intense feedback sound started to happen close to one year of use and then it quit. It's not a bad product if you don't mind replacing it after a year.

The touchscreen,especially the right edge of the tablet must be randomly tapped six or seven times to launch any apps. When on threads,it is hard to consistently give a thumbs up or thumbs down. When playing games it is frustrating since right side of screen has to be tapped over and over. Even scrolling from the right is a challenge. The only useful purpose of this tablet is listening to free radio but I can do that from my phone.

I bought this HTS because of the brand. My previous Philips HTS worked GREAT!! I absolutely loved it!! You could control the amount of bass you wanted. So I figured this updated version would be just as great. NOPE!! The sound is alright, not the best I've heard. In fact, the older version sounds WAY better. Although when watching DVD's, I had to readjust the different types of sound just so my subwoofer doesn't blow. That's pretty bad I guess. Playing DVD's is a pain sometimes too because it would freeze or shutdown on its own. I got this the ending of November 2009 and up until September 2011, I barely used it. I mainly used it to play my iPod, which was the only good thing. It gave out on me already to where I couldn't get it to turn on AT ALL. There was literally no life left in the poor guy, the little red light was totally out. I was lucky it gave me back the rental DVD before it went to electronic heaven. But seriously?? It should've lasted WAY longer than a few years because my previous Philips HTS lasted from 2005 until I had to get a new one. The only problem with that was it wasn't reading the DVD's anymore, or barely. So, the moral of the story? Invest your money in something that would last longer than just a few years. I wish I did, would've saved me over $200 plus the cost of getting a new one!!
Electronics.summary: Invest your money in something better!!

Electronics.reviewText:
I have a thing for sleep keyboards. This one was a decent price and had decent reviews, so I thought I'd give it a shot.

Everything seemed well at first. I purchased it for my office, so I threw the box away after I thought I was satisfied with it, so it wasn't cluttering up my office (first mistake).

I instantly noticed that the keys seemed a bit hard to depress. This isn't a defect, but I think they require too much pressure than they should, and I feel it slightly decreases my typing speed.

Now, the problems. I've only had it for about a week, and multiple keys have started to squeek when I press them, especially the spacebar. It's not a problem, but it's an annoyance. I like a quiet keyboard, and squeeky keys don't accomplish that. Second, the "-" key is broken already. I first noticed it whenever I would type a "-" and it would come up with doubles. I didn't pay much attention to it at first, but after I investigated, it turns out the key is just broken. The slightest touch on the key without depressing it causes it to register, which typically results in doubles whenever I press it.

Overall it's a decent keyboard for the price though. However, if I still had the box, I would definitely return it, as it isn't very high quality. I wouldn't recommend it to anyone. If you like a slim keyboard, I would spend the extra $20 or so and get a Logitech Illuminated Keyboard. I have that at home, and am very satisfied with it.

This zipper case is actually padded with cheaper polyethylene foam--and only on the 2 large-panel faces of the bag only.  The polyethylene foam panels are encased in a jacket of wafer-thin neoprene on the outside and nylon in the inside.  Note that the edges of this bag are comprised solely of the thin neoprene/nylon shell, which I think most people would agree is not sufficient padding for your precious laptop.

The only reason I don't give the ICON4-BLK bag a lower rating is that I've seen worse construction.  Buyer beware--don't buy this bag sight unseen.  Outer dimensions are 14.75 x 12.75 x 1.25 inches.

I don't use the Bluetooth speaker much for a few reasons. The voice notifications are not volume controlled so don't take this to a library or connect while your baby is sleeping. The range for this item is what's lacking the most as it starts sounding garbled at about a 10 foot distance. Maybe the strap is to hang it from your ear for optimal reception and sound quality. I'm not that mean a person to 1 star this product, but I'm sure they're out there listening.

First battery came used/dented. Had to contact Anker directly to get them to send new. Second battery did not work at all. I followed all of tips and tried charging with my laptop off for 12 hours. But, laptop would not recognize battery or turn on at all. Made sure all of the specs were correct for my laptop, but did not work for my 13" Alum. Macbook late 2008. Had to send second battery back.
Electronics.summary: First battery came used/dented. Had to contact Anker directly ...

Electronics.reviewText:
Wow, I can't begin to tell you how absolutely terrible D-Link products are!  Bad, Bad, Bad!  I purchased a D-Link DWL-G650 Wireless Cardbus Adaptor for my Dell notebook running XP professional.  I also purchased a D-Link DI-524 wireless router.  I can tell you the "D" in D-link stands for "Don't work"!!!

First, the router has terrible transmission problems.  I barely get a signal one room away, and it will flip from "excellent" to "poor" reception constantly.  I also get kicked off about every 30 minutes.  It doesn't work at all more than 25 feet away.

Second, the wireless card has a lot of difficulty connecting to the router.  It takes anywhere from 30 seconds to 4 minutes to acquire the signal.  I also had huge problems trying to use other networks while on the road.  I developed a problem where I would try to connect to a network and my computer would completely crash!  I would get a message saying something like:  "A problem has been detected and windows has shut down" my computer would then go into DOS and I'd need to power down.  This happened almost every time I tried to use the cardbus adaptor.

I've tried to call D-Link support but just wait on hold for more than 30 minutes.  I gave up and bought a 3-com cardbus adaptor and have never had any crashes.  The router still works like crap though.
Electronics.summary: I have all kinds of problems with everything D-Link!!!!

Electronics.reviewText: Claims of range are way overstated here, I they are clarified in the actual packaging and instructions but if you're expecting anything more than line of sight for a few hundred yards you'll be sorely disappointed.  Battery life for the included rechargeable batteries is dismal and since it only holds 3 AA batteries loose rechargeable are a tough option (for those of us that use & track sets for performance & life expectancy).  Buttons are inconstant, you can feel a click without actually triggering the microphone at times.  Weather alerts only work when in that mode, not when the radios are being used for two way communication so you still need a separate alert system and the information about the emergency alert these claim to be able to send is vague at best so I won;t be counting on anyone (especially emergency services) picking it up regardless of range or location..  I can't get any of the voice activated modes to work and haven't tested the waterproof or floating features yet but that's not going to save my impression of what's supposed to be a high end radio system.  The emergency whistle belt clip is far from loud (compared to a dedicated emergency whistle) and far form effective at keeping these attached to belts and backpack straps but they seem to survive the regular 3-4ft falls pretty well.
Electronics.summary: Expected better from Motorola, especially at this price point.

Electronics.reviewText: I purchased this unit so that I could use my wireless headphones. The manual says that the unit will pair with 0000, 1111, 2222, and 3333 devices but it did not. I tried everything that I could to get them to pair but it would not pair with my headphones. My headphones pair right away with my tablet and smartphone so it was not a problem with the headphones. I returned the item to Amazon and ordered an August MR250 wireless receiver and it paired up with the headphones immediately. If you have the same problem the MR250 may work for you as well.
Electronics.summary: Did Not Pair With My Headphones

Electronics.reviewText: This clock was one of the most attractive items in my trash bin.  The tiny labels to the buttons are hidden by the display.  No matter how you angle it you can't read them.  It only lights up when you push a button, which you have to grope around for in the dark.  I can understand not constantly lighting because it is battery powered only.  But that puts it in the class of travel alarms, and this is way too big for that.
Electronics.summary: How could anyone design, much less manufacture something so impractical?

Electronics.reviewText:
This product simply does not work as advertised. The so-called "Easy Set-Up" is a complete crapshoot.  There is a chance that it will work exactly as advertised and that your computer and network will engage automatically with the Sonos system without a hitch.

If it doesn't, be prepared to spend hours uninstalling and re-installing firewalls,anti-virus software, and any other program that may limit access to your PC. A "clean" install of WIndows may be required.  In short, if it doesn't work automatically, be prepared to spend 10-15 hours on the project.

After three months and numerous exchanges with Sonos customer service (expect 24-48 hours to pass between contacts and the "diagnostic" you prepare is apparently completely useless) I finally was able to access the Sonos from my PC. Only to encounter, the apparently near-universal issue with Windows 7 that "Your folder cannot be shared" preventing me from accessing my music folders . . .

Unbelievable.

Bought one of these 65 days ago. After 29 days the case, where the pin strap is anchored, broke. Returned to Amazon and got another. 32 days latter (outside the return window) same problem. Now have to deal with Casio whose online warranty states that it does not cover the case. With the first watch the Bluetooth seemed to work well and remained connected.  With the seond watch the conectivity was hit and miss. If my Iphone 6 was in the back pocket of my bicycle jersey it would drop the connection. When connected the buttons often responded slowly or not at all. I would not waste money on this poorly made product.

I picked these up trusting that the Monster name might ensure above average quality sound, but these headphones have almost no bass response. Even the midrange and treble they seem tuned for sound harsh and unpleasant. The build quality is good, the in-line pause button is probably the best I have ever seen, and the magnets that can hold the buds together is a great idea, but the sound is garbage. Sound quality is so wildly variant among headphones, that we are sometimes forced to spend too much money hoping for a decent pair of headphones. These are easily the worst pair I have ever heard.
Electronics.summary: garbage, no bass - I have $20 headphones that sound vastly better

Electronics.reviewText: Purchased this set on 12/3/13. Started failing on 12/5/14. Called customer service and they had me do a reset which worked for about2 days and then the same thing happened. S\hut down with a 2/5 light code. Customer service had me contact a local repair facility who was unable to get information about this code from Sharp's own engineers so they had to end up trying a few things. It ended up being a defect in the panel itself due to the power supply. Sharp finally closed the case end of January with an offer to send a refurbished model when one comes in but they have no timeline on when this will get replaced. So far it's been a month and a couple phone calls later and the line is "When we get one in we will ship it right out to you. We get shipments every day but since we don't get shipping manifests we cannot be sure when we will get one in" They have no other info for you, So based on my dealings with "Customer Service" I would not recommend this or any Sharp product.
Electronics.summary: Can't recommend due to poor customer service.

Electronics.reviewText: S***** and doesn't even fit together. Poorly machined screws and the top doesn't fit into the base. Took the time to put it together finally and its a POS. If I could give 0 stars I would. Amazon should seriously consider refunding my money, and I should have opened and inspected this garbage while it was still returnable. Probably the lowest quality item I've ever come across from Amazon. It's going in the dumpster, unless they want it back.
Electronics.summary: I want my money back Amazon!

Electronics.reviewText:
I was excited at the price and to get them so quickly.  I saw the product title saying "data sync cable" but had no idea it was possible for the same cable to not support charging too.  Very disappointing, and not worth the cost to send back.  It would be great if the seller would mention it in the ad that this cable does not supporting charging.

I had tried using this cable on the following devices:
* Ipod Touch 3rd Generation
* Iphone 3GS
Electronics.summary: As stated, data sync cable ONLY

Electronics.reviewText: I needed a stable middle-clickable design for 3D software for all the panning and zooming. This looked like the perfect mouse because of the big flat middle button. Most scroll wheel mice are unsuitable for this small task (give me a break).  This mouse turned out to be unusable too. The cursor would skip and jump around everywhere no matter what type of surface I tried.  My super cheap Logitech M225 is smooth as butter in comparison.  Also, I found myself accidentally scrolling too when a finger would just graze the middle touch area. Returning it immediately and keeping old mouse and will just remap hotkey in Maya to enable TrackTool and avoid middle button panning entirely.
Electronics.summary: Erratic regardless of surface, inadvertent scrolling

Electronics.reviewText: Both of my two 8gb sticks of DRAM failed less than a month after receiving them.  The warranty begins on the purchase date so time spent in shipping counts against you (it took 15 days in my case).  Your options after the warranty expires is to create an account on corsair's support page, create a "ticket" for your product,  and then wait for it to be approved.  I've run into multiple error codes and broken links attempting to insert standard billing and shipping information.  I have found that some replacement options are only accessible through contacting support directly.  It has now been a week of multiple calls to customer support and buggy web pages and I'm still at square one.  I would not recommend corsair DRAM at the risk of dealing with their apathetic support.
Electronics.summary: Customer/product support after warranty expires is exasperating.

Electronics.reviewText:
Waited a year to see if Westinghouse would fix the HD Tuner that randomly locks up when changing channels or powering on.

They won't admit there is a problem with this model only their 47".

I use OTA (rabbit ears) to get my HD channels and when it is getting the HD signal the TV will occasionaly (about 4 times a week) lock up.  Lock up completly the only way to unlock it is to pull the power cord from the wall.

Where is the option for Zero Stars? Right out of the box, does not work period. Will not play any disc, even brand new Blu Ray Discs out of the factory sealed packaging, or any DVD I tried (0 for 20 folks). It says "checking disc compatibility", the spinning disc appears on my tv, then it just stops trying to read and the door reopens. What a terrible product, save your money, do not buy LG brand. I will admit I bought this at Wal Mart, I won't hide that fact, but come on man, doesn't even play any disc, any format... nada,, zilch, bumpkiss. Hopefully this review will steer someone who works hard for their money in a different direction.

Originally, I overlooked the negative reviews because there were so many affirmative ones. I was wrong to do so. Though it looked fine (except for coming with a few scratches), it was incredibly difficult to get the USB to connect to my PC, and I had to buy a USB extender cable in the end just to be able to view my files and charge the player. The charge only lasts for about an hour at most and the touch screen is very insensitive. And less than two weeks after I purchased it, it randomly stopped working. It wouldn't turn on and my PC wouldn't register its presence. So, in the end, this is a warning. Do not buy this product; use your money wisely somewhere else. I am incredibly disappointed.

I've been using this monitor for 2 weeks.  2 weeks!  Last night the handheld had a blank screen, no sound either, would not turn on or off.  Out of desperation, i thought to take the battery out of the back to "reset" it.  As i did, a 6 inch flame shot out of the battery.

Called customer service, talked to a nonchalant rep.  said they would replace the whole thing, but i have to pay to ship it back, and the whole process can take 7-10 days.  So.......  have to move baby back to my bedroom to sleep in something other than her crib during this time.

Please do yourself a favor and don't buy from this company.  And if it has any effect whatsoever, this is the second review i've ever written (first was back in 2006!).  That's how angry I am.
Electronics.summary: this is another "don't waste your money" review

Electronics.reviewText:
Not only did this SD card fail to meet the standard operating procedures of any other SD card I've ever owner, but it also came fully equipped with spyware/malware and/or a virus. The only thing that changed in aspect to my cellphone was the insertion of this memory card. Less than one day upon using, my Android Galaxy informed me that my phone was being attacked and my information may have been accessed by a third party without my consent. I immediately had to factory reset my phone, change all my passwords, lose my files/pictures/videos/etc. that were previously saved to my device, etc. VERY FRUSTRATING AND UNNECESSARY!

DO NOT BUY !!

There is nothing "Ultra" about this memory card. I purchased four of these to use in a couple of dash cams I purchased  for my cars. Shortly after installing the cameras, I began to have issues with the cameras shutting off intermittently. After spending a lot of time with tech support, I figured out that this memory card was the problem. It turns out that this memory card is not suitable for use with a dash cam. Nowhere does it mention that on Amazon. I replaced all four of these cards with 32gb Transcend High Endurance cards and the problem went away, so I'm out over $60. DO NOT PURCHASE THIS CARD FOR USE IN A DASH CAMERA.

I live in Chile (southamerica) and , when i was in USA, I bought this item thinking it is CERTIFIED, but it have failures, .. I installed it to my computer and it work fine but when i goes to take a SHOWER, or clean my hands, I allmost die electrocuted!!.. what was my surprise?.. the GROUND connector its connected to the Fase!!! so ALL MY HOUSE ARE CONNECTED TO FASE!. CERTIFIED?? WHAT KIND OF CERTIFICATION!??.
I wrote to COIRSAIR company and they just tell me "SEND THE PRODUCT TO THIS DIRECTION" with automatics mails, but the problem its that to send this HEAVY product to USA from Chile its more expensive that buy a new one!.
They don't give me solution, I lost my money, i will never buy a corsair product again, and I recommend to be really sure before buy a "certified Corsair" product.

- NEVER TRUST ON A "CERTIFIED" PRODUCT. -

This is the fourth digital camera I have owned.  I wanted a smaller lighter camera with a little more zoom and better video capability.  I use it mostly for the grandchildren, around the house and yard, and on vacation.  I tested this camera over a wide range of conditions, inside and out.  MANY of the images were blurry.  And yes, there is an audible click in the video when you operate the zoom.  I would have put up with that if the images had been consistently clear. I own two SONY cameras and a Nikon CoolPix 8700.  The SONY's had their little bugs,BUT they were consistent and I knew what to expect. We are camera crazy and also have a Canon digital SLR, and my husband has a Canon Powershot SD880 that he is very happy with.  So I think it's fair to say I know when problem images are related to 'operator error", which was not the case here. It's small and light, and the features are acceptable for my needs, but I could not get past the image problems.  My search continues.

This could be a great product if they didn't made the claim that it could support devices up to 95W power consumption. I purchased one from the crowd funding site. They shipped one to me back in November. It failed to power my MacBook Pro 15 inch which uses a 85W power supply. According to ChargeAll's own claims on the crowd funding site and the user manual: "anything under 95W should be OK". So I contacted them and they said I've got a defective unit. They ask me to take photos or videos to prove that the unit didn't work right. So I did and shipped it back to them. After a full month's wait and several emails, I got the replacement unit yesterday. Charged it up and connected my MBP 15 to it. Well, the replacement unit did exactly the same thing as the first one: it shuts down after less than 30 seconds of powering the MBP. So I guess I got yet another "defective" unit, or, are they all "defective"? I don't know, but tired of taking photos for defective products for sure.

To be fair, both units can power/charge my MacBook Air 11 inch (45W) and iPads/iPhones just fine. Just don't expect it to power things anywhere near the claimed capacity. But for the money they charge on this device, there are so many other options that would do the same thing at a much cheaper price. Don't be fooled.
Electronics.summary: This could be a great product if they didn't made the claim that it ...

Electronics.reviewText:
First of all, on the spray bottle I received the directions are completely ludicrous. The directions say to "put a drop on a small wad of tissue." Well, this is a spray bottle that spritzes out a very fine mist. There are no drops.

I have no idea why the manufacturer would put the above directions on a spray mist bottle. Makes me lose some confidence right away.

But I proceeded to ignore the label directions (since there is no way to put a drop on tissue...and doing so defeats the whole purpose of buying a spray bottle version in the first place, of course) and spray this product on my eyeglasses. I noticed a strong smell of alcohol right away.

I used a brand new, high quality microfiber cloth designed for eyeglass cleaning. I was very dissatisfied with the result. I saw streaking, and not clarity. The company included a new cloth, and I tried that as well. Same disappointing results, on 2 separate pair of glasses.

I am sorry I bought the spray.

The Formula MC version that comes in a squeeze bottle is much better, in my opinion. (I bought the spray thinking it would be as effective, but that was not the case for me. So, in the trash the bottle goes, and I am out $12.51 total ($6.35 for the item and $6.16 for shipping).
Electronics.summary: Wrong Directions on the Label. Spray Left Behind Streaks.

Electronics.reviewText:
I bought this machine to do one thing, and one thing only: play blu-ray discs. It did, for the first six weeks. It came with the newest firmware installed (I went to update it initially and was told that it was current.) The remote was a bit too small, but I was satisfied with the unit overall.

Now, about 50% of my blu-ray discs bring up a message stating that the disc is not in a format that the player can read. Discs that I specifically tested out on the day I bought this machine no longer play. I reset everything to the factory defaults, but that did not fix the problem. It simply won't play half my movies now.

At this point in time, I can't return it to the store. I am not even going to bother with the warranty, because the shipping is nearly half the cost of the unit, and when I get it back, how long before it fails again if brand new it only lasted 6 weeks? I would give it 0 stars if I could.

Don't buy this television. Read the reviews on the internet and you will find that within the first year this model will no longer power on and Sony will be of little help in correcting the problem even though the tv is under warranty. My 9 month old tv will not power on. A search on the internet turns up post after post of this very issue. I've had to now schedule a technician to come out, but from everything I read this isn't going to end well.
Electronics.summary: Skip Sony and look at Samsung or LG

Electronics.reviewText: After sending this back the seller asked for a review why I sent it back. This is what I wrote them. I'd be more than happy to give you my review on this product. First, I was so excited to receive this camera. A 4K camera at a great price. I received the box, opened it, and the camera came in an awesome looking package. That's unfortunately was the best part of the camera. That's about the best thing I can say about the camera was the packaging. I also purchase the MicoSD card that was recommended with the camera as a package. 1. I opened the box. The camera was in the water proof case. First thing that I noticed was a small aluminum "O" ring that was loose and in the case. Before I even opened it. Luckily the camera had plastic protection over the lens. There would have been a good chance this broken piece could have scratched the lens in the shipment. 2. Unwrapped the batteries and charger. I immediately charged the batteries to full. Once charged I went to place the battery in the camera. That was beyond FRUSTRATING. The plastic cover to the battery compartment is horrible. One, it's extremely hard to open it. You slide the release mechanism over but nothing happens. My fingernail would not open it. I un-did a paperclip, but the paper clip width (gauge) was to thick. I had to go get a eyeglass straight edge screwdriver to lift the cover off. If I'm out filming and need to change the batteries that would even be more than frustrating. I placed the battery in the camera. The battery has a little cloth flap to make it easy to remove. However, the flap does not allow the plastic cover that contains the battery to be placed back on. I tried for over 30 minutes. That's way too much work just to insert or change out a battery. 3. I added the MicroSD card. I placed it in. I wanted to see how to remove it. It's ridiculously hard to remove. When you push on it, the spring mechanism should pop-it out a little bit, enough to grab on it and pull it out. Most the time it doesn't. When I finally got it to release it popped out enough where I had to get tweezers to grab it in the slot. It came out about 1/4 mm. Again, when you're out in the field and need to switch out sd cards this is to hard. But...all that said. Nothing worse than the image quality. The video was horrible and it would cause doubling/blurring of the object. You don't need to take my word for it. Here is the testing videos that I did of my two dogs outside. (...) (...) (...) VERY DISAPPOINTED.

Electronics.reviewText:
The drive is cool, quiet and fast. USB 3.0 is 4 or 5 times faster than USB 2.0. I only took delivery on it a couple of days ago so I can't comment on it's dependability or longevity.

Update: I've used it a month now and it's still quiet, fast, cool and inexpensive...knock on wood!

Another update: It's now May 2014 and the original drive is still working perfectly. I just ordered and received another 3 Tb drive and it seems to be working the same way...although I've only had it for a few hours.

They transfer OK but will not show up in the music menu unless you "rebuild library" each time. I tried working the problem with both iRiver and Rhapsody tech support without success. I don't think it's a Rhapsody issue as I experienced the problem on two different computers running Rhapsody and I have not had the issue with the Sansa players that my kids use. I was also not satisified with the "fit and finish". The D-click user interface is very innovative and easy to use, but the top part of the device shell feels loose and wiggles around. I'm concerned it might come off.

So what could have been a delightful product was instead a big disappointment. I'm shipping the Clix back to Amazon for a refund. I hope this review will help others avoid the frustration and waste of time that I experienced with this product.

Brad Freeman

Original review:  I ordered this as a second charger for my Asus laptop.  I have used the charger several times and it works with my laptop.  The only reason I am giving it a 4 star review is because it does get quite hot while charging.  It's not hot enough to burn, but hot enough that I would be careful where it is while I am using it to prevent any overheating or possibility of fire.

I want to mention to any prospective buyers that the manufacturer sent a card with my charger requesting a 5 star review and stating that if  5 star review is written and they receive an email with proof that they will send a mysterious gift.  Now, I want to be clear that I have no problem with this product or the manufacturer, but I feel that giving gifts for high reviews may bias the reviews.  I contemplated giving a 5 star review, but decided that my gut tells me 4 stars.  So, here you have it.

1/2/14 update - Still using this charger as my primary charger without problems.

1/14/14 update - Since my update last week this charger has begun to run dangerously hot.  It's always been on the hotter side but I could still hold it in my hand.  Now it's much hotter and makes a faint buzzing sound.  I've lowered my rating to one star and I'm throwing it away.  Apparently, this charger won't hold up.

OK ... sorry for the 3 stars, but I just wanted to point out that these binoculars have a whopping 20 feet close focus distance.  That's about the worst I've seen.  For example, the Eagle Optics Denali 8x42 Roof Prism Binocular have a close focus of 7 feet.  People new to binoculars often don't think about close focus, but it's highly desirable.  For example, one may be looking at a bird in bush or tree and step closer to get a better look.  At 20 feet, you may have to actually step back.  Also, for younger kids, they like to look at objects closer to get used to using binoculars for the first time. Sometimes it's useful to look at insects, snakes, etc. that aren't 100 feel away but more like 10-20 feet.  I just wanted to make those aware of close focus, so you can make your own educated decision.

CAD ZOE review

There are a tremendous number of USB recording microphones on the market now, ranging from cheap units designed for communications or gaming use, up to $600 (the MXL USB.009), and there may well be even more expensive USB microphones I'm not aware of. Most designed for home recording are in the $50-150 range, which is right where this unit falls.

The Yeti is small, kind of cute really. Its mostly plastic, with a few bit of metal where needed, like the threaded microphone stand insert in the base Most users, I suspect, will use the included tripod stand, which turns the ZOE into tabletop microphone.

I've had several USB microphones, but for the past few years I've been using the Blue Microphones Yeti for my home recording. To my ears, it sounds pretty good, and it tends to come in at or near the top in most comparison articles I've read. This new microphone from CAD is in the same approximate price range, so I thought comparing the two side by side would be useful.

Looking at the specs, the Yeti seems to have almost all the advantages. It has a wider frequency range (20Hz-20KHz, versus 50Hz-16KHz), along with the same resolution (16 bit) and the same sampling rate (48KHz). The CAD does boast a more powerful headphone amplifier (300mw vs 130mw) plus a processing chip that is said to improve the monitoring, but this doesn't affect recorded quality.

On the other hand, that extra 4KHz of audio range doesn't necessarily contribute much to recordings of voices, acoustic guitars, and a lot of other instruments. Some of the really legendary recording microphones, like the Neumann U-47, had a significant falloff above 15KHz.

One clear advantage of the Yeti is its switchable recording pattern- you can choose omnidirectional, unidirectional, or figure-8, which pretty much covers any recording application you can come up with. The CAD is limited to an omni pattern, which is great for most music recording, but might be limiting for other applications, like recording voices in a noisy environment.

What it really comes down to is the sound quality. How does the ZOE sound, compared to the more expensive Yeti? I set them up side-by-side and recorded a few different acoustic guitars, mandolin, and upright bass, using Garage Band on my MacBook Air.

Recording, what struck me was that the CAD ZOE has significant latency compared to the Yeti. Its not a lot, but its enough that you have to anticipate where the beat is when you're adding additional tracks or playing along to a drum beat. It shouldnt be a problem in non-music applications, though. ON playback, the ZOE sounded good, almost the same as the Yeti, really, through the old Sony headphones I was using. On double bass, the Yeti had better response on those low notes on the E string.

In summary, Id say the ZOE sounds pretty good, has a good headphone monitor amp built in, and for Skyping or similar uses it is not a bad choice. But Id have to say that for multitrack recording, podcasting, voiceover narration and similar uses the Yeti is a lot more microphone for not that much more. With heavier duty construction, multiple patterns, better low end response and the option of single-point stereo recording, the Yeti makes the CAD ZOE look like only a fair value in comparison.
Electronics.summary: Good sound, some latency issues, limited flexibility  compared to the Yeti

It looks authentic.. box art, screws, adhesive tape on attachments, case, logo on camera, logo upon startup, interface, etc. But just for kicks, I decided to go to sjcamhd.com/safe and enter in my serial number just to be sure. To my surprise, it said the camera was a fake!! I rechecked the numbers 3 times just to make sure! I'm just at a loss of words at this point as I did my research to find an authentic cam. I don't know whether to believe my eyes or a website. (Bought from Mol-EleMall).

The Good:

The headphones have a good sound, comfortable fit, keep out most noise, and a nice coiled wire for emergency stretching.

The Bad:

The ear pads have a high affinity to wear and tear, will start to slip off, and getting them back on once they fall off is pain in the neck. The connector of the wire to the ear piece is a bit lack luster, and unfortunate tugs on the wire may cause sound loss.  The wires that travel through the head band are extremely fragile, but a lot harder to damage.

I found myself needing a new pair every 6 months for one reason or another, biggest issue is ear pad replacement followed by wire damage. Too expensive for such a quick replacement time.

i ordered this simply because the older i get the less i hear. i recently went to the movies and had some difficulty hearing some of it so i figured i'd try this to see if it would help and it does. for the money it cost i did not expect a lot from this device however it works better than i thought it would. it's very compact. the only thing i am noticing is that you sure don't want loud noises close to it when you're wearing it. my 3 Star rating is as it says, i think it's OK and i'm happy with that.

Got these headphones last year and they were a pretty okay quality. The sound wasn't excellent, but it wasn't total garbage. The earbuds didn't fit perfectly but they stayed in. Then after a few months the sound in the left ear became significantly lower than before. I eventually just gave the pair away to a needy friend. My sister also got the same pair of headphones and not only did her left ear go out but the bottom part disconnected from the rest of the headphones. You're better off $10 skullcandy headphones, at least you'll have some good quality sound before they break.

I got my headset with the intent to use with my iPhone for running. I figured I could use the button on the headset to advance songs, and take calls while I was out, since it's difficult to access my phone when it's in its armband.

The remote button has worked reasonably, it's a bit of a reach to get to, but I can click to play/pause, double-click to advance, and even hold down the button to activate voice recognition.

As a set of headphones or a hands-free unit, it performs satisfactorily. Sound quality is okay, but not great. The people I've spoken to tell me the microphone is a bit hollow sounding, like I'm using a speakerphone, but it was acceptable.

For outdoors use, the way the eartip sleeves are design, it really picks up a lot of wind noise, to the point where it drowns out your music. The eartip sleeves are really poorly designed, when you put them in your ear, they can pop *really* loudly because of the way they trap and release air.

To summarize, I think it's a reasonable set of earphones for $22, but it is not usable outdoors when it's windy.
Electronics.summary: Adequate, but not good for outdoors/running

Electronics.reviewText: The Samsung Galaxy Note 8.0 has some interesting features that may be of interest for some people. As usual Samsung's multitasking modification for the Android OS is a plus and the Spen is truly innovative. The screen is extremely responsive to the Spen and I have never had any trouble with this particular feature. In my opinion I feel that this tablet is a bit underpowered and can get sluggish at times if you have too many open applications which I feel is under par for the price range. Also the screen resolution for the price range is horrid. I really do not know what Samsung was thinking when they decided to go with this screen. The battery life is also less than optimal and I always bring a spare charger along so I can get a long day out of it. Despite these three things it is a good Tablet but I wouldn't purchase it for more than 150-180 bills.
Electronics.summary: Despite these three things it is a good Tablet but I wouldn't purchase it for more than ...

Electronics.reviewText:
I bought this system mainly because of its price and the decent reviews across the web of the company. It is not a high end system but it will do for regular home surveillance.  I tested the product out of the box and everything I tested worked fine.  The cameras came on and the DVR was functional.  (did not test the system over the internet)  The IR is not the best outdoors but you get better IR inside the home due to the reflection of the IR light off the surfaces in the home.  The Cameras will do well for facial recognition within 10-20 feet this would be the typical range in which you'd expect to find that in this price range.

I gave this system 3 stars due to its ability to be tampered with and the fact the images of the cameras lead you astray.  I live in a ranch style home meaning I'm in a single story and I cannot place my cameras up high enough that they could not be tampered with easily.  The wires attached to the Camera for both power and video feed are exposed to the elements which leaves them highly susceptible to vandalism.  Other systems have a "vandal-proof"  design where it goes through the post and is covered.

The camera system should be enough of a deterrent but some criminals consider it a challenge and will look for blind spots or vulnerabilities.  I'd rather not welcome the challenge and make it easy.

Other than the mentioned security risk this system is a sound investment especially for internal building surveillance as well higher than one story mounting outdoors.  I'd recommend this purchase for people in those two situations that are looking for a cheap system for security surveillance.
Electronics.summary: Decent System for Price Minor Security Problem

Electronics.reviewText:

This lens was purchased for use with the XTI.  For me this replaced a 300mm F2.8 FD on an F1.  The detachable lens shade is frail and bulky and therefore of little use to me (the discontinued Type I apparently had a built in hood).  The tripod ring should be kitted with the lens, not sold as an accessory.  Images with 1.4 & 2X extenders appear softer than they should be at maximum aperture.  I think my results with the 300 plus extenders (and film) more consistant.  Having said that, advanges include ability to use conventional filters (77mm polarizer) and great savings in weight, bulk, and cost for essentially the same field of view.

I was looking for a small simple case that would cover my computer from scratches when I put it in my shoulder bag.  This one looked like a cool option and it said it was custom made for the 15" MacBook pro.  I was a little disappointed.  The case was about 1.5" too big in every direction.  It is really hard to stuff into my shoulder travel bag.  It adds a huge foot print to my sleek computer.  It's not practical for what I need it for.  I may try to re-sew it but I don't want to make a mess of things.  I wish they had just made it right to begin with.  Maybe it made for an older bulky MacBook.  I have a newer model.  I am now stuck with a case that I don't really like.  I will be shopping for something more streamline.
Electronics.summary: Case it too big and is impractical.

Electronics.reviewText: It didn't work for me with a late 2013 iMac running windows in boot camp. After around 5 minutes the video would freeze. In Mac OS it ran fine, but I don't use MacOS to stream. I think it was more of a compatibility issue with Windows on an iMac than an issue with the item itself since it worked fine in MacOS. So just be aware if you are using this specific setup, it might not work for you. I even reinstalled Windows 10 and it had the same issue. Both in OBS and the Elgato software.

The item purchased didn't work 100%. The "enter" buton doesn't function. Now, I can use the Forerunner, but not the way I expected to. I could not replace it because it was delivered to my wife in a hotel in USA, and she is back already. Also and unfortunatelly, I will not ask for refund because, beeing here in Brazil, I will not buy another one at the same price I found with the delivery in USA. So...

Thanks,

Ricardo

So I have had these for about a year, and they fit in the respects that they cover the headphones and are very nice and comfortable to wear for 8 to 10 or more hours a day.  (I wear my headphones all day at work) But.... they fall off all the time.  The part that is supposed to hold them in place is not big enough all the way around, and I would have thought that they would have had some way for them to stay attached like a little bit of elastic, but they do not.  I am probably putting these back on at least once a week if not more.  I will see if I can find something better for next time I need to replace them.
Electronics.summary: comfortable but...  Does not stay on

Electronics.reviewText:
I got these Bluetooth over the ear headphones mostly for my husband, but I have used them a few times too. We have different sets we use for running and working out, and while I like those for that purpose, I wanted a pair that was a little more comfortable. I just don't like the earbud kind as much so these really appealed to me. We've had them about a week and a half now and I've been able to use them a handful of times.

I love the size and weight. They're not so light that they feel cheap and flimsy, but not so heavy that they're cumbersome. The band is adjustable to fit many head sizes and the actual headphone portion is an average size. There's a light to easily indicate when the unit is on, which is helpful. The included directions were more than sufficient and getting the headphones paired with our phones was fast and easy. I haven't used them during a phone call yet so I can't speak for that, but the overall sound quality is very good. Similar to that of my much more expensive corded headphones. I'm not a sound guru by any means but I'm confident the average user would be pleased with these.

The only thing I'm not a huge fan of is that the headphones get a little warm after about an hour of use. Not quite "sweat pouring down my neck" hot, but noticeably warm. It became a nuisance after a while and I took them off. That only happened the once - after a longer period of use - so maybe it was a fluke, but it is worth noting. With small children around, I don't typically wear headphones longer than a half hour here or there so it's not an issue for me. Overall I really like the set and would definitely recommend them to friends.

I was able to purchase these headphones at a slight discount so that I could review them, but I did still buy them, and my opinions are genuine. It's a great pair of headphones - comfortable, stylish, and great quality. I'm very satisfied with my purchase!

I am not a audiophile, but I do want to have a clear listening experience with the full range of sound.  This set of headphones does sound better than my stock headphones, blocks out a great deal of noise and is pretty comfortable in my ears.  I used them on a couple of trans-pacific flights and they definitely allowed me to block out plane noise for the most part. They are not claimed to be active noise canceling, but they do block a good deal if you fit them properly.
Electronics.summary: Great headphones at a good price.

Electronics.reviewText: BUT I did want to comment on it as I was extremely happy with it & know that when I am researching something I'm desiring to purchase I like to read a thorough review. When I first researched this & about 100 other cameras, I was looking for something user friendly, both with the camera's features & it's techy connection to my computer. I'll have to say this has been the one new digital anything that I've gotten that I am completely satisfied with. I'd recommend the 1G xd card when you purchase it. The pictures come out crisp & clear & has many wonderful features like the image stabilization & a natural light/flash feature where it'll take the same pic in both lights, safe them, giving you the option to pick which one is better. The low light, night shots are spectacular. It's F30 model is only different if you want to have a manual appiture. Otherwise, for the money THIS is a fantastic deal.
Electronics.summary: First, I'll admit I DID purchase this camera elsewhere...

Electronics.reviewText: Purchased this to replace the stock HDD in my PS3 slim as 119 GB of the 120 GB were used and the setup was quick and simple(only needing a screw driver and a flash drive to load the drivers/updates from the playstation website) . Drive was noticeably quicker on setup and continues to be faster Now a year and 4 months later, although lately it's noticeably noisier , sometimes being picked up through my headset while playing online

As a disclaimer, I'm not an audio snob, so take that as you will while reading my review. I'm really glad that I purchased these headphones. They are simple to use and provide very good sound. I bought these because I was not about to drop the $300 on the much more expensive Beats brand headphones who charge you more if you want wireless headphones. They are very comfy and fit on my ears decently. The only thing that slightly irritates me about the fit is that I have my ears pierced and even though I only wear studs, they make it kind of uncomfortable when wearing these headphones for a long time. Maybe that's just me. I use these with my iPhone, and my PC laptop and the headphones' Bluetooth capabilities are adequate. I have answered the phone while wearing these and the person on the other end was able to hear me loud and clear. The battery life is also excellent, and I've worn them for hours on end without the battery running out. I will say that if you are very particular about bass, or want a lot of bass, these are not the headphones for you. The sound quality is still good, but the bass is not loud and doesn't provide the same feeling you might want when you listen to a bass-heavy song. Overall, I'm satisfied with my purchase and would recommend them.

This is a decent dash cam to have for any reason wheather you are using it for a dash cam just to save you if you get in an accident or you are using it to record just a day in the life type of video. It is decent for the money you will spend on it.

The camera itself: 5 out of 5 stars is very lightweight so you don't need to worry about it adding weight to anything like your rear view mirror. I was a little disappointed with the lightness to it just because it makes it feel cheap but once using it the weight did not bother me. I mean if it were heavy then you risk the rear view mirror falling. The plastic that it is made out of seems to be pretty decent, I haven't had any problems with it even on warm to hot days, all of the seams are very well put together no gaps or holes in it at all.

The screen: 4 out of 5 stars When I first turned on the camera in was in a different language so I had to figure out which setting was for the language to change it over to english. It wasn't that hard to figure out though the booklet helped me navigate so that I could change it back to the original. The screen is decent it definitely isn't the best of the best in display quality but it is only 2.7" so you really can't complain that much.

Video: Quality 4 out of 5 Stars The video record modes are great you can tweak a few features to make it better for you and what you are using is for. You can use it while driving in day or night. Which is great because not all accidents happen in the sunlight most happen at night when you least expect it. The night mode is not the best of video quality there is a smaller range due to the headlights and distance of which they reach, I mean it isn't that big of a problem but it doesn't allow you to record what happens before a vehicle hits you unless it is head on and you see them coming at you. The dat light recording is great it is in 1080P HD which is very decent quality. The video doesn't come out grainy or pixelated it is very clear and crisp you can make out things that are at a pretty far distance. I really like this camera mainly in day mode so that you can see everything.

Sound: Quality I would give it 3 out of 4 stars mainly because it sounds like you are in a tunnel or a barrel...I mean if you are recording for accident problems you really don't even need the sound feature unless you are speaking with a person that hit you or that you hit for insurance purposes. The sound isn't a huge issue because even though it is a tunnel sound or barrel ( just muffled sound like you have your finger half over the mic) you can still understand everything that is being said.

Software installed on the camera: 4 out of 5 stars. The software seems to be a little dated, I mean this is coming from a different country and is made for a different country so it isn't terrible at all it all responds well and with ease all the buttons when push respond very well. It just needs to be a little more updated so that it comes across the screen a little clearer.

All in all this get 4 out of 5 stars from me. I think that this is a decent dash cam to have for the price it is really a steal my only hint would be to use the correct wall plug in to charge the camera in the booklet it tells you the correct one to use. I used a different one the first time that I charged I didn't think that it would matter, but it did it only had about 30% after 45 minutes of charging so use the correct things with this camera. I have another dash cam and this one hooked to the bracket that I already had on my mirror this comes with a nice suction cup holder so you don't have to mount it on a permanent level and you can take it in and out of any vehicle which gives this camera an extra little bit of value to me.
I would highly recommend this little guy to anyone that is in the market for a dash cam.
I received this item at a discount for my opinion, others may vary depending on their own opinion of the product.

Bought this for our new media center when we decided to "cut the cord."  Does the job well.  Does not have a "previous channel" button on the remote, but that's not a deal-killer for me.  I have to say that the IR receiver usb connection seems a little flimsy.  On mine, if you move the IR receiver, even a little, you can hear Windows make the "be-doink" sound as if a device is being connected/disconnected.  since I am keeping it in a stationary/permanent place, this is not an issue for me.
Electronics.summary: Bought this for our new media center when we decided ...

Electronics.reviewText:
Bought this to hook up my G15 viera  to the wireless-internet with an earlier netgear wireless client I had connection reset issues and was required to release renew the ipaddress for new sessions.
This one on the other hand works like a charm.

This also serves me as a AP-Repeater increasing the signal strength to the other side of my house.
The reasons I gave it a 4* is because:
* It just has only one ethernet port allowing connection to only one device
* It has a supersized AC power-adapter! air-link could have downsized it a bit.

The quality is high and I'm very satisfied with the product the way it is, however for my purposes I am disappointed that the pocket is so shallow. I endeavored to keep a few notebooks, a mouse, and other junk a few inches thick in the pocket, but the flap and pocket are so shallow that it will not adhere with anything more than one or two inches thick. Be cautioned if you are a pack rat in denial like me
Electronics.summary: The quality is high and I'm very satisfied with the product the way it is

Electronics.reviewText:
This is what a PC should be.  Touch screen is intuitive.  Design is beautiful and setup couldn't have been simpler.  Just plug in the power cord and follow the prompts.  Aesthecially, HP has also hit a home run.  The display is fantastic and the piano black finish fits the modern day flat-screen TV look.  No one should have a problem with this PC looking like a piece of hardware in their living room or elsewhere.  The HD TV tuner also works great once you connect the antenna.

About the only gripe I'd have is that Vista will not run some older software very well.  I've mainly had problems with some kids' software which will likely force me to buy some new programs for the 3-year old since she can't use her older siblings' hand-me-down software.  This is not an HP problem, though.

The Bluetooth is such a great idea. Not only can I use it for my PC, but also for my phone (iPhone for now, but I'm counting the days to switch back to Android and it works on that, too).

The battery seems to last a long time. I've only charged it once and I've owned this for a few months and I type for about 10 hours every day.

Unfortunately, while typing, a few times a day, the connection will pause and I'll have to wait about 5 seconds until the blue light shows up again. It doesn't help to turn it off and back on and it isn't because of low battery. It just happens intermittently and I have to just wait until it comes back.

I'm glad to see they added in some common function keys (volume and calculator, hallelujah!) which were sorely missing in my previous Freestyle keyboard.

My biggest complaint is that the keyboard really should come with the risers and palm rests and the palm rests from the previous version don't fit this one, which was frustrating.
Electronics.summary: The most comfortable keyboard, but overpriced.

Electronics.reviewText: I've had the NB-90 for a couple of years, and I MUCH prefer it over either a wired mouse or a battery operated wireless mouse.  The latter eats up batteries or need recharging, whereas the a4tech mouse does not.  Through the magic of some sort of magnetic field (not the kind that attracts metal to it), using the mouse on its included mouse pad allows it to function accurately and smoothly and without the hassle of a cord tangling or restricting movement. However, here are a few caveats: 1. you need a space to put the pad next to your keyboard. 2. the space cannot have metal 3. you can only use the mouse if you use the included mousepad, as this is where it receives the signal via the USB port.  4. the USB connection on this model does have a cord that runs from the computer circular calibration disc (about 2.75" in diameter), which in turn is wired to the 9" mousepad.  Thus, consider if you have this amount of free space available. 5 Having had this mouse a couple of years, I'm finding that now it needs calibration more often, and it seems less accurate. I'm not sure if the pad's field diminishes or if it physically wears out or what. Also make sure you have an extra USB port that you can dedicate to using this mouse. I also have not used the software that came with it, so I cannot use all the functions.  Still, it works well with the mouse drivers in WINXP.  The a4tec website does not list an Apple OS compatibility with this specific mouse, but they do with the NB-30, although do not list OS 10.

I recently purchased the Pentax Optio M50 8MP Digital Camera with 5x Optical Zoom.  I love it!  I had a 3x Zoom on my previous camera and missed many pictures because the zoom wasn't adequate.  This little camera is terrific.  It has features that I wasn't looking for but am glad they were included.  It is very easy to use and I would recommend it to anyone looking to purchase a digital camera.

I purchased this projector in 2008 and it was well worth the money.  I am still on my original bulb and we watch at least 2 movies per week and some big games.  The key is allowing the bulb to cool before turning off and not leaving the projector on at all (unplug it if you have to).  I upgraded from a 720p DLP to this one and overall it is better, but the DLP had better blacks.  I just purchased an Epson 5010 due to the sale of our home.  The buyers originally wanted all the equipment to stay, but now the do not want to pay for it, so if you want a good projector (and screen) drop me a line!

I just received my netbook and it is smaller than I expected.  I have been shopping for another laptop when I read the reviews for the Acer Aspire One.  I was going to buy the Acer but I read complaints about fan noise.  I had never heard of a netbook until last month.  I wanted portability and internet access on the go.  This netbook fit my needs.  The keys are so small that it is easy to make silly mistakes.  The right shift key is next to the page up key and because of this, I have noticed the cursor moved somewhere else.  The left shift key is tightly placed next to the caps lock key and I had pressed it by mistake.  It will take awhile to get used to the cramped typing space.  I am a woman with small hands so if anyone with bigger hands buys this; it could be a deal breaker.  Accessing the internet is easy.  Easy to toss in my bag and take anywhere. Light weight and functional.  The price is right and some places offer it for as low as $250.  I decided to get it from Amazon because of their great customer service.  They have worked with me in the past and I know if I have any problems; they will do whatever is necessary to accomodate me.  I kind of wish I bought the eee pc 1000HA if only for a larger keyboard.

They aren't real high quality, but seem pretty solid once you get them snapped together, which is pretty quick. I ripped my whole music collection and really don't use my CDs ever, so I really only open these to add new discs to my collection. As such, these do the job and were pretty cheap. If I used them more, I would want something more attractive and useful. Until you fill the case, the discs rattle and slide around, which I guess is going to happen with any loose case that doesn't have slots. While slots may hold the discs in place, they are a hassle to insert a new disc in the order.

They gave me peace of mind when I lived in an apartment by myself for 2.5 years. I bought one for every window. Unfortunately the sensor is very sensitive and it would go off during thunderstorms or when my cat would pounce on the glass when she saw a bird. It scared me a couple of times but it was a false alarm..at least I knew it worked. I live in a house now with a home security system so I don't use them anymore.

This was easy to set up, and I've had no problem with it at all after 4 months.  I purchased some longer cables and ran 100 feet without a problem.  It took zero effort to view the live stream on my Android phone, which was very impressive.  They have some kind of registration system with their servers that eliminates me needing to worry about IP addresses and router settings and you just enter one passcode to set it up.  There are 2 reasons I would give it 4 stars not 5  1) the cameras are not really clear enough to read license plates in my driveway even from 15 feet away in daylight but you can identify car make\model .  2) The motion sensor recording doesn't work well: At night the infrared lights attract bugs and this sets off the recording most of the night, as does any slight breeze in the landscaping.  But also, I tested it during the day by walking past all 4 cameras and only 2 of them triggered a recording of me.  So I had to turn that feature off and record full time, but with motion sensing turned off it's hard to find activity - you have to watch it at 16x speed and react quickly to even realize if something happened, rewind and watch at normal speed to see it.  For the price, it's hard to complain much.  Overall, I am pretty happy with this - if there is a break-in or somebody steals packages off my porch, I am pretty confident I will have some kind of recording to look at.  At closer range (10 feet) you can see faces pretty clearly to identify someone.
Electronics.summary: Easy to set up but you get what you pay for.

Electronics.reviewText: After many frustrating hours stumbling through the poorly written instructions, I finally got the DPR-1260 to work perfectly wirelessly (caveat: I have yet to test a multifunction printer).  This was one of the only print servers I found on the market that could handle multiple printers and work wirelessly.  It was also one of the least expensive print servers I came across.  To set-up the wireless settings properly, make sure to have the print server hard wired to your router AND your computer wired to your router (do not try this wirelessly!).  I set up the print server using an ibm laptop and firefox.  I can also print wirelessly without a problem using an apple laptop.  To add a printer, simply  plug the printer into the print server and run the printer wizard on the set up screen through your browser.  To add a printer on an apple, simply go to the print center, select "add printer" and select IP printer.  For location put down the IP address of the print server (you can see this on the print server status screen through your browser) and for queue name enter the name listed on the same status screen.  I would have given this print server 5 stars were it not for the terrible documentation.
Electronics.summary: Works very well, but documentation is terrible!
