At the time of the release of the 2 best-selling albums of Sinatra's career, the Duets albums from the mid-'90s, I was elated. Many of us simply didn't want to believe, in fact rejected the unthinkable, i.e. that Sinatra was finished, so these latter-day gifts were sufficient cause for celebration.  And for the first month or two after each of the two releases, I played them repeatedly.  But soon the novelty wore off, and I had no interest in these concoctions, especially with the vast Columbia catalog, the priceless Capitol recordings with Nelson Riddle, the final extended chapter of his Reprise years all beckoning to be revisited.  Apparently, others felt much the same (recently, I've seen either disc going for a buck or two used).

The Bennett Duets are less "tricked-up" than the Sinatra ones, which involved long-distance, call-in performances by his partners.  Moreover, Tony sounds almost as good as ever, much more vibrant physically and in control musically than Ole Blue was after 1990.  Moreover, the program comprises winning songs from the Great American Songbook, with Tony so confident and secure that, rather than being "carried" by any of his younger, more vigorous, partners, he's the one who makes up for their deficiencies with this material.

Perhaps the track with the greatest interest will be "Body and Soul" with Amy Winehouse.  It's the most recorded popular tune in music history (check out the numbers at jazzstandards.com or allmusic.com), partly because much of its satisfaction comes from the challenge of executing it--difficult but ingenious and logical chords, unforgettable melody, mediocre lyrics--but Bennett and Winehouse (who sounds mature lightyears beyond her actual age) pull it off quite nicely.  Listening to Amy's first album--"Frank," the one before her hugely popular "Back to Black"--it soon became clear that the very young girl at this time knew jazz phrasing and could swing. Once she finished the daunting "Moody's Mood for Love," you knew right then that she was capable of delivering the goods in more than one style or genre.

The one thing that may be slightly off-putting is Amy's attempt to sound rougher, more blas, even a bit inebriated (stoned--or an affectation?), than either she or the song requires.  The same could be said about Lady Gaga's otherwise sparkling performance on "The Lady Is a Tramp" (what a travesty this number becomes when certain latter-day singers substitute "champ," which not only wastes Lorenz Hart's clever, subtly ironic, lyrics but actually destroys the non-conformist, free and independent spirit of the lady portrayed in the song).  But Lady Gaga sings the song and the word "Tramp" with the most assured conviction (it's Tony who almost messes it up by (only once) substituting what sounds like "champ").  Though she could do without a couple of "growls," Gaga proves that she's more than some sort of insubstantial hoax, one-trick pony, or year-round Halloween media creature.  Like Tiny Tim (whose musicianship won me over after the initial shock wore off), the person who plays the role of "Lady Gaga" is a wonderful "straight"performer, perhaps even a first-rate musician.  Sounds like she's listened to Sinatra.)

The duets with Michael Buble, Natalie Cole and Dana Evans (Queen Latifah) are predictably right in Tony's wheelhouse.  He could easily make an entire album of arresting performances with any one of these musicians, who have jazz sensibilities similar to Tony's.

The rest of the album will score big with some listeners, especially those who responded favorably to Michael Bolton singing with Pavarotti.  But to my ears the album tends to get a bit thick and mushy, even "injured" by musicians who simply can not swing.  I appreciated Merle Haggard's lengthy interview in the NY Times shortly after his "jazz" album.  Whatever one might think of the result, there was no question that Merle knew he was in unfamiliar territory, over his head and studying up as hard and fast as he could about the elocution, phrasing, and timing required to deliver a classic Gershwin ballad or swing tune and do it justice. Willie Nelson keeps revisiting the "American Songbook," but I have yet to hear him adapt to its standards.)

Bocelli and Groban contribute to the schmaltzy quality weighing down stretches of the album (The solo version of Tony's early signature song, "Stranger in Paradise," is far superior to this new version.  Inexplicably, Aretha goes after a song that was one of the highlights of the first Duets album, "How Do You Keep the Music Playing."  My advice: revisit the first version with Tony and George Michael or simply forget about it.  Aretha is one of the all-time great soul singers (starting out as a jazz singer, despite the popularity of her dad's recorded sermons), and she was delightful on the Sinatra Duets album, providing much needed life.  But here she takes on a freely structured song that goes no where unless the singer is able to take it somewhere.  She's in good voice but the effect on this listener is: "Been there, done that."

As for the others, if you prefer a duet for Harold Arlen's wrist-slasher, "One for My Baby," make it any Sinatra version, or even the Kurt Elling-John Pizzarelli meeting.  On this occasion, the song, which is a musical soliloquy, or a Robert Browning dramatic monologue addressed to a silent auditor, and moreover a haunting cry of despair (one of Sinatra's greatest "suicide songs"), was a mistake from the very beginning (I can imagine the Arlen estate even being offended by this insult to the the memory of Harold Arlen and lyricist Johnny Mercer).  Performed as a duet by Tony and his youthful counterpart, it comes off as little more than slightly mischievous and lightweight albeit pleasant musical conversation.  In fact, there's a bit too much pleasant, pretty music on the album--nice-sounding voices, thick layers of sweet-sounding strings.

But for Tony and the highlights on the album, the result, on balance, still amounts to a winner: 3 stars, a definite thumbs-up  though certainly not a high-five.  This time I'm not as quick to pull the trigger as was the case with the so-so (in retrospect) Sinatra Duets.  I could readily list (and produce from my collection) a dozen albums by Tony that trump both Duets dates--timeless performances, some with just Tony and the piano of Bill Evans, or Tony with Flanagan's or Sharon's trio, or Tony with Count Basie.  The man unquestionably knows the routine (to quote from the aforementioned Arlen song), and on a number of his solo recordings, he's gone beyond and above it--way above it, reaching artistic heights  on the level of the best by Armstrong, Astaire, Garland, Holiday, Crosby, and even Frank, singing his heart out just for the joy of it (and not a fiddler in sight).
CDs_and_Vinyl.summary: Not essential Bennett but definitely worth the price of admission.

CDs_and_Vinyl.reviewText:
This CD is a crap shoot at best, so as the saying goes, "Caveat Emptor" ('Buyer Beware'!).

This show was apparently taken from an FM Broadcast from October 1, 1975 in Vancouver. That being said, the sound quality is iffy throughout a lot of the show. There are rare times when it shines, but most of the time it is somewhat painful to get through, due to over-modulated vocals, music brown-outs (where the sound seems to go from 2 channel stereo to a bad audience recording), and just a mess of a recording in general.
It truly sounds like the original recording used to make these discs was a badly deteriorating set of tapes that were about to literally disintegrate. I know because I have a lot of live shows in my cassette collection that have like 1 or 2 good listens to them before they will self-destruct (I try to play them once, and on that one play, convert it to digital for posterity). The tape that made these discs must have literally been in tatters, and you can tell how bad it is at times when it's just a swirl of good to bad sound and then back again, much like many of my old cassette tapes.
It's too bad that the people who released this could have made at least an attempt to clean up the sound and inconsistencies when making the digital master. However it sounds like they simply used the bad tapes to make this copy, add some reasonably nice packaging, and release it for sale to the masses. If Frank were alive, he'd no doubt grab this one for another round of the 'Beat the Boots' series to simply re-route the cash flow back to his own pockets.

That being said, the content is nevertheless interesting. This show is sort of the mid-seventies pseudo-Mothers show (Roy Estrada is still playing in the band) but with one great exception, Terry Bozzio is on the skins, and that alone makes for an interesting show, especially this early on in his performance relationship with Frank. Napoleon Murphy Brock as always keeps it entertaining, and the band is rounded out by Andre Lewis and (of course) Frank.

After I listened to the first disc, I felt kind of ripped off because the sound was annoying, and even during instrumental sections like 'Chunga's Revenge', it was a mixed bag of good and bad sound. The highlights for me on Disc 1 is a really nice version of Carolina Hardcore Ecstasy and a much slower Illinois Enema Bandit, two songs just finding their way in these early workouts by Frank. Other than that, it's a crap shoot.

However my appreciation for this release (and why I now feel like it is worth buying, at least for me) was after listening to Disc 2. Sure the sound is still at times all over the place, but this disc is worth buying for the series of songs that go into each other that fills the majority of Disc 2: Canadian Customs Routine (which is hilarious!) > T'Mershi Duween > Zoot Allures > Sleep Dirt > Black Napkins. These 5 tracks alone make this disc worth buying. The sound stays relatively static during this set of songs, and it is not bad at all. I love Zoot Allures here because it is performed a bit differently than what eventually gets released on the album of the same name, and Frank makes some sweat sounds during this one, very smooth, mesmerizing, almost trance-like. The horns are absolutely wonderful on T'Mershi Duween and Sleep Dirt, and the Black Napkins (also still in experimental phase) is phenomenal, nothing short of brilliant. Adding Terry Bozzio on drums was one of Frank's smartest moves in the mid 1970's and this version of Black Napkins drives that point home. It's just a very nice sequence of songs, I can't say enough of how much I enjoy listening to this chunk of music on this disc. Of course, the last 2 songs after it, which are the encores, the sound goes back to being crap (the 'Advance Romance' is cut at the beginning and although the 'I am the Slime' is a great version, the vocals are drowned out in the background).

So as I said previously, 'Buyer Beware' but for you die hard Zappa fans like me (who is always looking for more live shows that the Zappa Family Trust is not releasing), it's worth picking up. Historically it is worth owning, and the price (at least when I purchased it) did not break the bank.

Having waited for seven years since Enya's last release, I suppose was hoping for something more grand. That is not to say Dark Sky Island is not good, it certainly is. Still, I was left wanting. I certainly was not hoping for any significant changes in her musical style, and I rejoiced that the overall production remained true to the "Enya sound." However, I felt a bit disappointed by a perceived lack of reach or growth. In short, after waiting for seven years, the new album sounds almost indistinguishable from her earlier works. Perhaps it is best not to tamper with the tried and true formula, but I suppose I was hoping for more and am left wondering "what might have been."

Oh, and speaking of tried and true formulas... One final comment on the packaging. Yuck.

This album apparently marks Enya's departure from the traditional plastic "crystal" CD case package, in favor of the lighter, much cheaper (read: more profitable) cardboard sleeve. Beautifully done, to be sure, but the purpose of the case is, after all, to protect the disc. This one failed miserably. The disc arrived coverd with countless tiny scratches on its playing surface. So much so, that the disc looked "hazy." Indeed, it looked like a used CD purchased at a swap meet. Really? After paying full price for a product, it it unreasonable to expect that it be in excellent condition? Perhaps this is how they plan to force people to migrate from physical discs to digital files. (I enjoy and use both, by the way.) Look, I want to save the planet as much as anybody, but let's be honest here. This is about profit margin, not the environment.

End of sermon.

CDs_and_Vinyl.reviewText: Despite it's significant commercial success, "The River" is without doubt Bruce Springsteen's weakest recording with the E Street band. Perhaps due to incessant critical pampering, perhaps due simply to a creative lull, "The River"  for the first and ONLY time in his career, sees Springsteen sounding uninspired and repetitive. The first record is definitely the stronger of the two with the pop smarts of "Hungry Heart", the moving father/son ballad"Independence Day" and the sorrowful lamentation of the title track, displaying Springsteen in top form . For the most part however, he is caught in mediocrity, chugging out bland rockers and cheesy, overwrought  ballads, many of which would not be out of place on a Bon Jovi album.(see "Crush on You," "Drive all night"  ). Furthermore, the production is a mess with the vocals often being swamped by  muddy and irritating guitars and Weinberg's drumming slipshod at best. Critics of "The River" have often queried why Springsteen felt the need to record a  double record and certainly a more strict culling process  would have made this a more coherent release if nothing else. My personal contention however relates to the songs Springsteen left off the record. "Roulette","Where the bands are" and "Held up without a gun" were all recorded during "The River" sessions and are far superior to much of the pedestrian  material on the actual release. Of course this is obviously opinion and Bruce probably sees the whole thing in a different light. All the same, I'm pretty sure I'm right.

David Sylvian has been as of late full of surprises.  2003's "Blemish" found Sylvian experimenting with minimalism, electronic noise, feedback, and loops, a brilliant and personal album.  His latest effort, a collaboration with brother Steve Jansen and Burnt Friedman under the name Nine Horses, is quite the opposite.

In many ways, "Snow Borne Sorrow" is as much a logical successor to "Secrets of the Beehive" as "Dead Bees on a Cake".  Or perhaps better still, it feels like the child of the unreleased "Little Girls With 99 Lives" material (some of which saw the light of day as b-sides to 'Dead Bees' singles) and 'Beehive'-- keeping the jazz-tinged sound and textures of the former but eschewing lush textures in favor of a '99 Lives'-like modern noir sound.  In better words, its sort of like a modern, loose take on Sylvian's jazz-infected composition.

At its best, the pieces have an unnatural energy to them, from the loping bass of opener "Wonderful World" to the guitar-driven "Darkest Birds" or the bizarrely folky-filtered through Miles Davis "The Day the Earth Stole Heaven".  But at times, the album seems to overreach, primarily in a couple overlong pieces as the title track and closer "The Librarian", neither of which particularly go anywhere.  But on the other hand, something like "Atom and Cell" feels like a lifeless harmony-laden pop song that somehow manages to wholly captivate.

All in all, I find this a pretty mixed record-- at times satisfying, at times I lost interest.  Then again, I didn't get "Blemish" at first, so maybe I'll change my mind in a dozen more listens.  There's enough here to keep me coming back, but not enough to get me raving about it.

This 1987 CD from the now-defunct Conifer label marked the first commercial recording by the City of Birmingham Symphony Chorus (CBSO Chorus), under the direction of their long-time chorus master Simon Halsey. One work from Elgar is featured, the original version of his op. 27 "Scenes from the Bavarian Highlands", with words "imitated from Bavarian Volkslieder and 'Schnadahuepfler' by Caroline Elgar, wife of Edward Elgar. The work is generally lightweight in tone, which the solo piano accompaniment would be expected to emphasize, compared to the version for chorus and orchestra.

The first of the Holst selections, "Dirge and Hymneal", is a 1915 setting of a poem by Thomas Lovell Beddoes, reported here as the world premiere recording. Even though the notes give this away, it's still a bit of an aural surprise to hear melodic material in a choral work that wound up later in "Saturn, the Bringer of Old Age" from Holst's "The Planets". Holst's op. 43 Two Motets, from 1924-1925, set poems by Henry Vaughan ("The Evening Watch") and Digby Mackworth Dolben ("Sing me the men").

The final work on the album, the Five Partsongs, op. 12, actually has the most complicated preparation history behind it. Holst composed the op. 12 in 1902-1903. However, only 3 of these songs were published at first, No. 1 ("Dream Tryst" by Francis Thompson), No. 2 ("Ye Little Birds" by Thomas Heywood) and No. 4 (the anonymous 16th century poem "Now is the month of Maying"). Holst did not complete No. 3, the first verse of "Her eyes the glow-worm lend thee" by Robert Herrick, but Imogen Holst, Gustav Holst's daughter, edited this setting towards the end of her life. No. 5 is a setting of "Come to me" by Christina Rosetti, although the notes don't indicate who was responsible for editing this setting. In any case, this recording was thus the first recording of the complete op. 12.

The CBSO Chorus does a good job throughout, clearly well trained by Simon Halsey. Where things fall short is in the recording quality, where the sound seems rather recessed and the chorus comes off as sounding rather small-scale. The piano is reasonably well blended with the chorus, with Richard Markham doing a good job. But again, the overall sonoroties seem rather diminished, if that makes sense. There is also a small issue of presentation where the timings of the selections are nowhere to be found in the booklet. The timings of each of the tracks are given on the CD itself, but that's the only place where the timings are indicated. The whole CD runs 53:09.

Overall, this CD would seem aimed at aficionados of English choral music, and admirers of the CBSO Chorus and Simon Halsey, primarily. It's an OK, if not necessarily earth-shattering or mind-blowing album.
CDs_and_Vinyl.summary: Good CD of Elgar & Holst partsongs; other factors bring down the rating a bit

CDs_and_Vinyl.reviewText: My sister gave me this album because she had bought it on impulse and regretted it. I have been unable to pass it on to anyone else since. This  album is poor. I feel like the boy in the story of 'The Emperor's new  Clothes' because everyone else likes it but there you go. It is stuff like  this that turns me off guitar music. The title track is good, but generally  this album can't match Oasis' debut 'Definately Maybe,' or indeed their  contemporaries Blur, who, unlike Oasis, are still producing good albums.  This was maybe the biggest selling British album of the 1990s. But I don't  think people were buying the music, they were buying the attitude. Whenever  a guitarist wants to jam he breaks into 'Wonderwall,' thus ruining any  pleasure from the session. Come back Stairway to Heaven, all is forgiven.

This is about half a good album (another time I clearly wish for the capacity to give half-stars).  "Know Your Rights" is as snarling as anything on Greensleeve, "Ghetto Defendant" is a great song to put on a mix tape right after "God Save the Queen", and "Rockin' the Casbah" is all kinds of fun. And as for all you stiffs still whining about "SISOSIG", lemme ask you this: Why is covering a Gene Vincent song ("I fought the law"), good music, but writing a song in his style and adding a chorus in Spanish "selling out"? Just because non-punk fans like it doesn't make it a bad song, guys.
The rest, however is nothing that puts any strut in my step. "Death is a Star" and "Sean Flynn" are okay, but just okay. The rest I can't summon the energy to comment on, and "Overpowered by Funk" is the single most irritating song this side of "Shiny Happy People". I get the whole playing with reggae deal, but this song wears out its welcome in a hurry. IT JUST WON'T END. Instead, the Clash did. Just goes to show you: experimentation is a fine thing, but trying to pretend you're something you're not is not what kept the Ramones going all those years...

CDs_and_Vinyl.reviewText: I must admit, I was somewhat disappointed with this CD.  It's true, it has some wonderful tracks by relatively obscure composers (Marcello, Locatelli, Corrette), although these particular selections often appear in Baroque compilations.  Some of the renditions on this album lack subtlety.  Bach's "Air on a G-String" is appropriately slow, but shows no variation in dynamics, and the piece lacks its characteristic depth.  The Mouret Rondeau (the infamous "Masterpiece Theater" theme) is overblown and bombastic in this recording, possessing none of the dignity for which the piece is so well known.  Curiously, both the first and last track are Pachebel's Canon: upon first listening, I thought perhaps they would have a different version at the end of the album.  No.  They just have the exact same track twice, a somewhat ungainly version with the organ replacing the double bass, and again, no sensitivity with dynamics.  The booklet claims these classics are "memorably performed by some of the world's finest artists", but fails to name any performers!  This low budget disc contains no documentation with information about the pieces, the composers, or the performances.  For the connoisseur seeking definitive recordings, this CD should not even be a thought.  For some who doesn't know anything about Baroque music and simply doesn't know where to start, I wouldn't recommend starting here.  Start learning about Baroque music with Bach's Brandenburg Concertos, not with this odd compilation.

It's been eleven years since the last Aerosmith studio album, 2001's Just Push Play (and there's also been the 2004 covers album Honkin' On Bobo) which was really a product of its time with the band collaborating with producers that gave them a clean modern pop sound. This time around they brought back producer Jack Douglas who worked on some of the band's best albums in the 1970's. With the inner problems in the band and the near breakup, Steven Tyler doing American Idol fans were beginning to wonder if there was any recording going. It took a long time but Aerosmith's 15th studio album, Music From Another Dimension is here. Initially the band said it would be a throwback to Toys in the Attics (1975) and Rocks (1976) and there are glimpses of that, but there's also glimpses of the 80's and 90's Aerosmith too and a LOT of ballads. It's as if all eras of the band are blended in one album and that's their sound in 2012.  I got to hand it to them, for a band of men in their 60's there's some pretty rocking material here, and I find that the band does vocals harmonies quite a lot this time around(actually they sound like they wouldn't be out of place on a Def Leppard album). There's some good but to me it's an overall underwhelming Aerosmith album.

The ups with MFAD are the strong rock track. In fact the album starts off rather with a string of three solid rock songs. "LUV XXX" starts out with a spoken intro before kicking it into high gear, I wish the entire album was like this, it's genuinely one of the best Aerosmith songs that's been done since the 1970's. It has that vibe from Toys/Rock era and it's fantastic. "Beautiful" is commercial Aerosmith at its best, it's catchy, the vocal harmonies are excellent and the songs is very likeable as a whole. " Legendary Cild"  is a Grip a Grip era song that never saw the light of day. I was intrigued at first and when I listened to it I thought to myself "this could work", and it does it rocks and it's catchy enough I really like this one. "Can't Stop Loving You" with Carrie Underwood is puzzling, having her on an Aerosmith album is obviously not going to well with some of the fans and it's just not that good of a duet. "This Could Have Been Love" was chosen as the single and no surprise, it's a ballad.  I actually like this one, even if it's a 1990's Aero ballad rehash sounding or cheesy or sappy, I can acknowledge all of this but it still works for what is. "Street Jesus" has more of a classic rock edge to it, with even some jamming parts and the result is a longer, more vintage sounding track that works fairly well, it's one of those the hardcore fans will enjoy the most. The Joe Perry sung track "Freedom Fighter" is one of the best songs on this album for me, it's got a good Perry riff and even thought his voice isn't particularly great the song manages to rocks. "Another Last Goodbye" is a fitting ballad to end the album, it's a good one but it's overshadowed by the fact that there are too many ballads on MFAD to truly stand out.

The first half of the album, I have generally good things to say about and it sounds promising and it makes you think that yes, maybe Aerosmith has some of the old rock sound we love back and it's going to be an entire album like this. Then there's the second side, filled with ballads and it really breaks the album's flow. A big part of the problem is that the album suffers from the too much ballads syndrome that was present on albums like Get A Grip, and they sound mostly like 1990's Aerosmith ballads. Six/seven (depending on who you ask) ballads on an album is just too much, and I like ballads but these are for the most part just sappy and rehashed songs that they've already done, except not as good or passionate. There's just no overlooking that many ballads is overkill. The worst part is a duet with Carrie Underwood, no offense but what's she doing on an Aerosmith album? Especially one which was reported as "back to their roots".  I found some of the lyrics here to be the band's most juvenile yet, which is rather humorous coming from men in their sixties. Then again the album has 15 tracks, maybe a little too much and if they removed some of the ballads and Diane Warren songs (still using outside writers it seems) it would have come across as a tighter effort, it comes across as a modern version of Get A Grip (some good rock songs, plenty of ballads and it has over 14 songs and an outtake from that album as well) . Most of those ballads sound like they're trying to be part II of "Amazing", "Crying" or "Don't Wanna Miss A Thing". 15 songs may just be a little too much, if they cut some of it down it would have made for a shorter, tighter more Rock album, that's my take on it.

Like many fans, it's hard for me to hide my disappointment. Still better than Just Push Play that's for sure, but I expected more from the hype Aerosmith had around this release. There are things to like but there's some that bring down the experience ultimately. I listened to it a few times by now and I can honestly say my rating is a 2  out of 5. Some of the Rock tracks are reminiscent of classic Aerosmith and energy charged tunes but overall it comes off as an album that didn't know what direction it wanted to take. There have been some great releases by Classic bands this year, but sadly Aerosmith's is not one of them I'm afraid.

Everyone likes to think that their favorite artist can't be best-of'd, because, "Man, the ALBUMS, man."  But in reality, most folks enjoy Pink Floyd and Radiohead compilations, even if fans and critics pull out their hair, wondering how such an injustice can be contained in a small piece of plastic.  So I'm well aware that complaining about compilations is not fresh territory.

But when I first listened to Canon - already owning all songs on the first disc - I was nonetheless shocked.  It just didn't go together, it was wildly uneven, and songs that should've made it were omitted in favor of songs that really only made sense as a part of their respective albums.  Out of Range, one of Ani's best and certainly her most accessible album, is only represented by two songs.  Many albums have none.  Not a Pretty Girl has four, and, though I can't begrudge it that, I CAN take issue with the four picked.  ("Coming Up" over "This Bouquet"?  Really?)  In all, it's a hodgepodge that doesn't represent its artist well.  At all.  And the rerecorded songs are just plain awful.

If you insist on getting a physical, store-bought representation of (almost) her entire career, this is, unfortunately, your only choice.  However, if you just want to get some good Ani DiFranco, skip this and get Out of Range.  If you like that, get Not a Pretty Girl.  Then Like I Said.  Then maybe Dilate or Little Plastic Castle or something like that.  MAYBE Living in Clip or another live album, although, like most live albums, what's gained is less than what's lost.  (It doesn't help that's it's a double-album; a little Ani goes a long way.)  Or just get the album with the song you like, or even just the song, or have a friend make a mix; it's almost certain to have a better selection of songs than this.
CDs_and_Vinyl.summary: Not the right place to start

CDs_and_Vinyl.reviewText:
I''m sorry to say but Michael Jackson Thriller days are over. This album is bad. The songs are bad. It's overproduced, corny, borign, cliched and overall poor effort. Michael spend to much time on it and the resluts were overall poor. the album flopped. And by the way fans of Michael say it's sold decent 10 million copies.
This albums sold 5 million copies world-wide. It did well in the first week. Sold around 350,000 copies in the US. However quikly began falling off the charts all over the world and today nobdody is buying this album.
Most of the songs sound like they're B-sides of his predeseccor History which was overall not very good album. The single You Rock My World sounded like Black Or White and the video was ludicrus and not that good.
Michael spend 2 years and 30 million dollars on this and Sony spend huge amount of money promoting it. If you don't believe me. You should have wathced VH1 in october 2001. They showed the entire You Rock My World video every hour for like 3 weeks.
He didn't tour nor did any interviews so the album did allrigt due to the fact it was so bad.
Michael glory days are over. I don't even think he will release another album. He's released 6 albums in 22 years. He will never top the popularity he had with Thriller and is ego has become so big that I doubt he will ever top Invincible again.

It was always what Prince said, he had to 're-release' songs because he was told that he didn't own his own songs. Now that he's not here, the company is going to release the material and make as much $$ on it as possible..
Prince's fans know what he went through with the contract - SLAVE- and what owning his music meant to him. To pick 17 songs out of Prince's repertoire and put "The BEST OF" on it, leaving out so many great albums, no mention of some of the newest. IMHO, just not a complete listing, if it was going to be done. For someone of Prince's caliber, the label could have pulled out a two-CD set and made it a more all encompassing of his career.
CDs_and_Vinyl.summary: PRINCE deserved a 2 CD set that encompassed his career, not their abbreviated version of the Best Of...

CDs_and_Vinyl.reviewText: This CD wasn't worth the money spent.  There isn't any production value in it unless you like taped campfire songs with a guitar background.  Leonard's voice and a tinny guitar background aren't enough to keep me from fast forwarding through the entire CD.  It's no where near the 1997 album "More Best of Leonard Cohen" which really has production value and I've listened to over and over both at home and in the car for years.  I'm still looking for CD's by Leonard that measure up to that one.  His 2001 CD "Ten New Songs" comes very close indeed.  Save your money on this one folks.  All of his early pre-1997 albums sit on my shelf too.  That's where this one is going
CDs_and_Vinyl.summary: Save your money and pass on this one.

CDs_and_Vinyl.reviewText: Let me just say right off that I usually hate greatest hits releases because the always miss the mark and this one does as well. I was at one time a huge fan of Ratt, but this greatest hit compilation does not do such a great band justice. The major problem here is that it's in chronoligical order and you're getting the best material first and the second half just falls flat. The material while good is by far not the best. There is a multitude of good stuff missing and the song picks from Invasion and even Dancing Under cover is quite skimpy and yes this could have been ten times better without the cheesy Lovin' You's a dirty Job and Shame Shame Shame. These songs just suck and could have just been omited because it shows a band at their creative worst. Hopefully there will come a better and maybe even a double disc compiltation that surpasses this dissapointing greatest hits package and just covers the bands best material and omits the cheese from Detonator. I would only recomend this if you had no idea who Ratt was and even then I would recommend that you skip this and begin by buying the individual albums cos you'd be a lot better off. Well maybe skip Detonator and Reach For The Sky.

Listening to these songs makes me physically uncomfortable.  It's not Rage and it's not Soundgarden.  The vocals and the instrumentals just don't mesh very well.  Throughout the entire album I felt like Chris Cornell and Tom Morello were each doing their own thing, without 'speaking' to each other.  Cornell's prolonged yells just don't suit the music very well at all.  It's obvious that Tom Morello is still brilliant, but some of the riffs sound recycled, and the rhythm section plays an uncharacteristically low-key role.  The tempo of the CD is unRagely slow -- mostly because Cornell's vocals are somewhat sluggish.  He certainly doesn't have Zack's agility.
On a different note, I looked at the Audioslave (the name's a little weak isn't it?) website.  Though the band attempts to keep one foot in politics, the content and selections just don't have the personalized, hand-picked feel that Zack's material had.
In a nutshell, it feels like both parties deviated from their extremes in an attempt to accomodate each other, and the result is a watery Frankenstein monster.
CDs_and_Vinyl.summary: Makes me want to pluck Morello out of the mediocrity

CDs_and_Vinyl.reviewText: Hope of the States' The Lost Riots comes with no small amount of instant mythmaking.  Signature guitarist James Lawrence killed himself before the completion of this debut.  Instead of packing it in, the remaining members have soldiered on, releasing their debut to much acclaim in Europe.  A pre-release gig in L.A. confirmed their ramshackle potential - they put on a sloppy, passionate show.  But The Lost Riots, as a recorded experience, is lackluster.  It's epic songwriting - not so modern as Radiohead; more like progressive icons Genesis or Yes or Jethro Tull - that falls flat as lead singer Sam Herlihy's voice.  (Which I don't understand - live he was excellent.  Here, he can't hit a note to save his life.)  What interest the CD holds is in the musicality of violinist Mike Siddell and a generally simplistic, sincere approach to the epic form.  And I would gladly listen to tracks like "Enemies/Friends" and "Nehemiah" - the best ones here - if Herlihy wasn't singing.  It's one thing in rock to have a bad voice - that's legion - but something else to have one that's uninteresting.

This is one BIG Snoozefest!  Love the Boz to death.  Been a fan since "Memories" in 1971 but something went wrong with this one.  Why duz this sound like a 78 rpm recorded at 16rpm???  Boz is sleepwalking thru this one.  Great songs but why the turtle pace?  Couldn't he pump some life into a few of the cuts?  2 stars only because it is OK music when you have guests over to dinner & one wants some nice "lounge lizard" music in the background at low volume.  Very disappointed.  Could have been a great album.

04/30/18  I have changed my opinion of this recording after repeated listening.  A nice, quiet cd to be played when one is in a mellow mood.  I enjoy it now!!  Can't wait to see Boz in concert this Summer!!

I distinctly remember the day that I brought this disc home & listened to it for the first time.  As track after track played I thought "what the (bleep) has happened to one of my favorite singers?"  I tossed the disc on my 'never to be listened to again' pile and promptly forgot that I even had it in my collection.

Fast forward 8 years and I had a mini Chante Moore-athon and decided to give it a 2nd try.  I really had to suspend my memories of Chante's previous albums so that I could listen to this without any prejudice & comparisons to those brilliant first 2 albums.  Overally I truly understand the bind that music artists faced around this time, particularly African-American females in the r&b field.  It was the dawn of the 'hip pop' era and EVERY artist was being forced to work with rappers and add elements of hip hop to what was traditional r&b/soul music.  This collection was too drastic of a change for me as a Chante fan and to this day, I still can't recommend it to anyone.

Out of the 12 tracks, I only like 4:  LOVE'S STILL ALRIGHT, TRAIN OF THOUGHT, M-A-N & BETTER THAN MAKING LOVE.

If only she'd been able to work on more tracks with Jimmy Jam & Terry Lewis  - the ones that they produced made Chante's voice shine and featured lyrics and song sentiments that I enjoyed listening to (since comments have already been made about the horrible chorus of BITTER - I won't add my two cents).

Chante's voice still shines even on the less desirable tracks but that's the main problem I have with this album - there are too few enjoyable tracks from the strong vocalist I love and far too many unmemorable filler tracks.

If I were Janet right now I would be stampeeding to my local studio. This album is the biggest Turkey I have ever heard from her. The songs all sound dated and retreads of everything she has already done but not good. Trust A Try is the only stand out track on this cd that even compares to anything on Velvet Rope. You ain't right sounds like an old Karen white throw away track. When I first listen to this CD,the first 3 tracks were mediocure and then the big nose dive into foolishness! How in the world do you take 9 steps down from your last album? Janet you must gradually drop not immeadiatley! This doesn't even remotely resemble the artist that came up with Velvet Rope! If Renee didn't have a huge input on things, There will be a hard road to convince anyone of it. I can believe Jimmy & Terry would even allow this to come out of the studio. I guess they are getting older and careless, time to find new producers or be Washed Up! The only reason this recieves 2 stars is for the DVD. And this special edition is nothing more than a way to make up the lack of sales of the first fiasco! Hurry up ...get back in the studio Janet or B washed Up! I bought this cd basically off of credibility but never again I will have to hear it first. How do you do 4 amazing lp's to something like this? Each album she elevated and this is the best she could give? And on the Dvd you can here them making excuses for this fiasco! Janet needs to listen to "Mandalay" they are doing her better than herself ! If you are going to do slow music it has to be done with style and class not foolishness! Madonna would even be helpful in this situation goodness! Hurry Up! Time is running out or B WASHED UP!
Suggestion: MANDALAY...EMpathy and SOLace (Great Cd's)
CDs_and_Vinyl.summary: Janet redeem yourself or Be WASHED UP!

CDs_and_Vinyl.reviewText: The music its self is fine but nothing special. The spoken word poetry is a bit annoying. Some of this is just based on my expectations but the music does not seem to having anything to do with relaxing cats. It had no effect on any of the cats in my house or the kittens I am currently fostering, nor did it help to calm me. Amazon has free samplers of music for meditation and massage that seem to be far more effective for calming cats and humans. I don't begrudge Mr. Joseph's musical abilities but I don't think the album does anything useful outside of not being poorly played or composed.

I think what made Blake Lewis so interesting in American Idol was the fact that each week we could not wait to see which hit song he would take and put a cool spin on it. He would take classic hits as well as more present hits and switch them up and make them different and fun. That being said - his set of original songs are quite boring and bland. The majority of them sound the same therefore they all kind of blend together. He sounds like a cheap knock off of his favorite band: Maroon 5. I bought this CD knowing that he does not have the best vocals but knowing that he had an ear for production and originality. I am quite disappointed here as nothing really jumps out and grabs my attention on this set.
There are a few songs that are fun and catchy. "She's Makin Me Lose It" is by far my favorite song on here. It has an old school Prince like sound to it from the beat to Blake's screeching vocals. A good song. Another ok song on here is "Gots To Get Her" which takes the melody from the classic "Puttin On The Ritz". That's about the only 2 standout songs for me. The rest are just weak considering seeing him do his thing on AI.
If you are a Blake fan I would seriously consider  purchasing his EP of songs that he did on American Idol and maybe sampling this before purchasing it.

~~~~~ JAC  07'

Starsailor brings up an image of something peaceful yet exciting, an interesting band that is one of those that is really good but never gets any airplay.  The name alone is almost enough to sell this group's debut album, Love Is Here.  As it turns out, the name is deceptive as to just what is contained on this disc.  To explain: imagine Coldplay (those guys that brought us "Yellow"), give them a bad, perpetually whiny singer singer, muddy up the sound so it sounds like they're playing live from your sister's room, call it Britpop, and you've got Starsailor.
The saddest part is that the musicians - James Stelfox on bass, Barry Westhead on keyboards, and Ben Byrne on drums - are overflowing with talent.  But the mixing job and the singer, James Walsh, has an almost constant whining gets begins to grate after a few songs.  The combination of excellent musicianship, bad mixing and sub-par vocals soon inspires only frustration.  Two songs, "Fever" and "Good Souls," are exempt from this lethal combination and are truly excellent, and it's a shame that these two are lost in a sea of mud and whine.
It's difficult not to want to like these guys, ...

OK - I understand the concept.  Rock songs like all others have a basic music construction that lends itself to other arrangements, other styles - blues, swing, pop.  But there just seems to be something here that isn't quite right. Like a dream that may be pleasant but is also skewed so that a new reality is the only way that the dream can work.

Paul Anka swinging to Van Halen's Jump?  Paul Anka turning Cobain into - what? - Sinatra?  Certainly this is nothing new - an aging pop star decides to record standards to keep his fan base happy and connected (like Rod Stewart).  Nothing wrong with that necessarily. And Anka has a nice voice, a good style and certainly can still sing.  But this conversion of several rock standards to another format just doesn't quite measure up.  What does this mean for the future?  An aging David Lee Roth singing Cole Porter?

It's not that the rock standards are so sacred that new arrangements cannot be made.  Maybe if the listener had never heard these songs before it would work.  But the original of several of these haunts Anka's version and almost gives mind to a "Weird Al Yankovic" for the geriatric set (of which I am quickly becoming one) to the point where the version seems almost hilarious.

There are some nice attempts on here.  For example, "Eyes Without a Face" comes across almost as a Sinatra-esque late night at a saloon type song.  But the overall effect just doesn't quite live  up to the concept.

I read the previous listener review and was curious to check out this music as I had honestly never before seen this album.  The review had me interested but cautious because of some of the word choices and phrases used to describe the mood created.  In addition, songs like "Classical Gas" didn't seem like "snuggling" music to me.  I chose to check out an online site that has 30 second clips per song to review the music prior to buying this cd -- I'm glad that I did.
This is not Barry White music.  It has no smoky, sultry sound.  Not the gentle, emotional guitar touch that Chet is capable of.  (If you're looking for that I might recommend "Sails" or either of the Chester and Lester CD's--although none of these are quite "snuggling" music either)  You would have to enjoy "Swanee River", "The Streak" or maybe "Convoy" as lovemaking accompaniment to consider this music as "lower the lights after dinner and snuggle" music.  This could only be romantic music for people who like feather boa laden women calling them "Big Boy" in a nasal tone -- GOT THE PICTURE?  Again, CLASSICAL GAS?  Electronic sounding drums.  Bad, shrilly 80's sounding keyboard tone.  Mood Music?  I don't think so.  It's more reminiscent of grammar school kids marching to an assembly.
I felt compelled to steer away those of you who might, like me, have been searching out that warm, soothing music that we think might exist out there but that we're unaware of.  Needless to say, this is not that album.  If you want that sultry, subtle, warm, non-generic smooth jazz sound I might recommend Earl Klugh "Late Night Guitar"(nylon string guitar with soft string accompaniment, some light percussion) or Ben Webster "Jazz 'Round Midnight"(Tenor sax with soft piano, some very light drums).  I think you will be real happy with these albums for that after dinner mood music, or with a nice candle lit dinner, for that matter.
No feather boas.  No Ray Stevens.

This is not a great album. You can tell it comes from the same sessions as 'Kid A' as there is a distinct lack of innovative guitar work ( if isolated, the thing that made radiohead songs vital to the ear?) and no real regard for melody. I understand that the band needed to experiment, needed to move on - but they seem to have lost their way. Like Kid A , a lot of this is meandering around in search of a song foundation. To do it once is an acceptable statement, to do it twice could be taking the [dive]. It reminds me, to an extent, of the way that REM spluttered after going gargantuan and never reached the heights we hoped for. If this were a new band, we would all say "Hmm, when they grow up they could be quite good" and they would attain minor indie status. I fear the best of Radiohead is past us.

What a disappointment! This was the first Simpson CD I've ever purchased and it is terrible. I watch the Simpsons all the time and I know there are many many great songs on the show. But did they pick any of those great songs? No! It had way too much talking on it, and a couple different Simpson theme song paradies. The songs were short, I guess I was hoping they would elaborate on the songs a bit more. There were only two songs on it that were fun to sing along with. I based my CD choice on the reviews of this product and I don't know where those people were coming from, but this CD is not the one with all the good songs on it, so pick another one or build your own off itunes.

This is a rewrite and reappraisal of my previous review of this album. I've now listened to this album about a dozen times, wanting to have it grow on me and trying to give every opportunity for the music to impress me; It has failed to do so.

I have mixed emotions about this album from Transatlantic. I'll start by saying that the technical ablility of the individual musicians is beyond reproach. None of the musicians have anything to prove and they don't use this platform as a showcase for thier individual glorification; they work together nicely as a band. Indeed, this album has a couple great moments but hardly any instances of pure musical brilliance. Some of the transitional passages are akward, others so hackneyed as to be laughable. There is one sound, (I'd call it noise), in the first track that sounds like a dentists' drill to me. I'm not sure what they were going for there, but I find it irritating to the point of distraction each time I hear it. Overall, the performances are competent enough but the music is not well written.

Another problem I have with this album is with the vocal presentation of the lyrics. The solo singing voice is fine, but the lyrics seem to lack any sense of phrasing or rhythm, as though no thought at all was given to the cadence for the performance. He may as well be reading a technical manual. I found the lyrics themeselves largely uniteresting and, in spots banal. The backing vocals are dodgey, at best; in some instances they are downright bad.

If this album was purely instrumental, I might have given it 3 stars, but as it is I can't go that high. This isn't any better a performance than the first Transatlantic album, and I don't find it as satisfying as the works from the four bands represented here. In the future, I'll spend my money on Dream Theater, Marillion and the rest, leaving Transatlantic on the shelf.

I'm a delirious fan and have all of their previous CDs, however I have to say that this CD is a bit of a disappointment and I don't listen to it often.
Many of the songs are weak in the melody department - a strength of previous Delirious offerings. Martin Smith sounds like he is trying to channel Radiohead at times and ultimately fails in my opinion. The focus of the songs on this CD seems to have shifted away from outright Christian themes to more general life themes of love and loss. Don't get me wrong, I don't want to keep them stuck in the Christian ghetto with everyone else, I just think that tackling more general themes leaves them with a less distinctive voice than they had previously.
If you are a die-hard fan like me then you'll buy this CD anyway. If not, steer clear of this particular offering........

A few of the tunes with Jerry leading and Merle filling with organ are as good, or nearly as good as the Saunders/Garcia material from the Live at the Keystone albums. The other material here is stuff that one does not wonder why it stayed in the can so long. The arrangements and the singing (even Jerry's) are less than stellar. From a host of recordings, there might be a few that stand out as high enough quality, exceptional enough to warrant release. This album is the stuff leftover, that was held back from release. One listen and you can tell why. It's not bad, it's just nohwere near what they are capable of doing.

If you like Merle and Jerry (and Kahn and Vitt), and I certainly do, stick with the Live at the Keystone albums, Vol.s 1 and 2 and Encores.
CDs_and_Vinyl.summary: Mostly Mediocre -- get the keystone performances instead

CDs_and_Vinyl.reviewText: After the monster success of their first three albums, Pearl Jam did the time honored tradition of recording a self indulgent, non-commercial album that's more for themselves than their audience.  The band is to be applauded for branching out and stretching themselves, but as with most bands, they would have been better off sticking to what they do best.  The band is influenced by Neil Young, especially his work with Crazy Horse.  The band tries to ape the sound of Mr. Young's work from Rust Never Sleeps on "Red Mosquito" and "Smile" but they come across as bad imitations.  They go curiously into a world beat sound on the "Who You Are" (flip flopping the title of another major influence, The Who's "Who Are You") and "In My Tree".  The latter song is particular bad.  Stone Gossard steps in front of the microphone to sing "Mankind" and he shows why he is the band's lead guitarist.  The album is not without its merits. "Hail Hail" ranks as one the band's all-time best songs with its driving guitars and powerful Eddie Vedder vocals and "Lukin" is another strong rocker.  Many people love this album for its eclectic nature and the fact that it doesn't sound like anything else the band has ever done.  That's the problem No Code suffers from, it doesn't sound like a Pearl Jam record.

Ok.  I am a sucker for most anything that is released in 5.1 surround sound (very few available), so, not knowing much about Primus and relying on a review in a popular magazine, I purchased the CD/Blu-ray version of this album.  As I was listening (and watching), and my wife was attending to kitchen stuff, she asked a very pertinent question: "Did you pay for this?", to which I answered "Unfortunately, yes".  I have since loaned it to my son who is 33 (I'm 65) and asked him to offer his opinion.  No word yet.
It bothers me somewhat that with all the really good music that was initially produced in Quad (what's that you ask?), and other classic albums, that very few have been chosen to be re-released in surround sound.  Steven Wilson of Porcupine Tree fame has been hard at work on groups like Yes, King Crimson and Jethro Tull, all of which are much more suited to my taste than Primus, whose release I can only describe as pretentious noise.
That's my opinion and I'm sticking to it.

I bought this because I was told it did wondrous things for soothing the screaming baby beast.  Not so much.

My daughter is 14 months now, and is just starting to handle car rides.  From the time she was born she would scream like she was being killed and never fall asleep (hour of screaming... yep).  I tried everything I could think of and the internet suggested.

The first time I put this CD on, she did stay calm for the 45 minute drive we had to make.  After that, she stayed quiet for 15 min.  Then it just angered her more.

I did not enjoy the songs.  There were several religious ones and there were themes that conflicted with an attachment philosophy.  I would gladly listen to the CD if it soothed my child... but it didn't.
CDs_and_Vinyl.summary: My baby is not calmed by it

CDs_and_Vinyl.reviewText:
After the long string of the single greatest albums of Pink Floyd's career, it had to come to a head eventually. From Dark Side Of The Moon to The Wall, they seemingly could do no wrong. Then came The Final Cut. A HUGE disappointment. For one thing, David Gilmour and Nick Mason had almost no influence on the album. Second, Rick Wright isn't there. Third, Roger Waters has this idea that people want to hear him ramble on about politics with few actual musical sections. He'd take this idea into his solo career. Meanwhile, for the last Floyd album featuring him, we got The Final Cut.

This is a pretty bad album overall. I love the message behind it but I listen to music for... well... music. However, there are four songs that make this album worthwhile. "Your Possible Pasts", "The Gunner's Dream", "The Fletcher Memorial Home", and "Not Now John".

"Your Possible Pasts" - A Wall outtake which is probably why it's so much better than most songs on this album. The main attraction here is that Gilmour lays down a hell of a guitar solo.

"The Gunner's Dream" - One of the most beautiful songs I've ever heard in my life. God, this song is just so great. One of the best songs ever in the Pink Floyd discography. The piano, the sax, the vocals. Perfect.

"The Fletcher Memorial Home" - The vocals on this one are slightly annoying but the guitar solo makes up for it.

"Not Now John" - The second best track on the album. The only one with any real David Gilmour influence as well. David sings on this one and also plays a solo which turns out great. This sounds like a Wall song frankly. It's great.

Everything else you can pretty much skip. "The Gunner's Dream" is easily worth the price alone.
CDs_and_Vinyl.summary: Four songs make this album worth listening to alone.

Gift_Cards.reviewText:
Ordered a gift card.

Got a gift card.

But wait...it doesn't work?!?

Apparently someone phished the number of a physical gift card sent to me. Some nice fraudulent redemption here.

To add insult to injury, Amazon refuses to replace it. After two phone calls and three emails, they coldly sent me to the gift card terms and conditions page so that I could interpret their fine print and realize I was stuck holding the bag.

Thanks, Amazon. As my gift to you, I'm ending our 18 year relationship. There are many e-tailers who I'd rather do business with.

Peace.
Gift_Cards.summary: Bye bye, Amazon.

Gift_Cards.reviewText:
I was so happy to be able to send my friend a last minute present for her Birthday. However, the way that the gift certificate was sent, made it seem like just another Happy Birthday card. After almost a month, I finally asked what she had gotten with her gift certificate, and she said she never realized it was a gift card, but thought that it was just another Birthday Card greeting. And since it was sent to her Facebook account, she has been unable to locate her gift, since it is not account that she uses as email.

The advantage of the last minute gift card was to have it delivered before her Birthday had passed. Having to make it clear that, "Hey, I sent you a gift card" took that advantage away. Now, she has been completely unable to find or access her gift card. Can you please send her the gift card again, in a way that it is more clear that it is a gift certificate and not just a Birthday wish? I would truly appreciate it.

Thanks so much,

Andrea Orr Koon
Gift_Cards.summary: where is my gift?

Gift_Cards.reviewText: This is terrible and I expect so much more from amazon!  Unfortunately I have had two instances with buying a gift card from amazon that was shipped to us and was not loaded with the amount.  Thankfully I checked the card balance prior to gifting it (only to find out the card wasn't even valid).  So ridiculous that this is the service provided. I would advise against buying gift cards from amazon but if you do, then I advise to check the balance so you don't do what we almost did, which is give someone an amazon gift card that WAS INVALID!

Gift_Cards.reviewText:
Nearly four hours devoted with Amazon tonight to resolve issues about unwanted merchandise delivery and failure by Amazon to accept returns.
Next step is a FTC complaint (Federal Trade Commission) where a possible 100 million dollar fine is likely.
There is no clear way to remove orders from the cart and once merchandise is received it cannot be returned to Amazon by any methodology.
This is obviously a Deceptive Billing Practice which is forbidden by the regulations administered by the FTC. The agents have no ice to circumvent this chicanery since it is a money making ploy for Amazon - this the FTC complaint.

Gift_Cards.reviewText: I, too, bought a couple of Amazon gift cards for Christmas gifts and the recipients were thrilled. The difference was that i bought them from a gift card kiosk at a local grocery store. The store personnel activated them in front of me so there were no glitches or shipping delays/charges. I just lucked out - it never would have occurred to me to check reviews on gift cards from Amazon. I just stopped to look at the gift card display in the store and was pleasantly surprised to find Amazon cards as one of the choices. It's ironic that the whole joy of the Amazon shipping experience for me is the online ease and fast, efficient delivery and that's the very thing that caused so much frustration for so many people this holiday. Now, I'm inclined to wonder about some of their electronic systems. I hope they work out their problems..
Gift_Cards.summary: Amazon Gift Cards are also available at retail locations near you!!

Gift_Cards.reviewText: I went on Forever21's website and tried to order a gift card for my niece.  Four days after my order, I was contacted stating there was incorrect information and instructed to email or call their customer service line.  Immediately I emailed stating this was a valid purchase and that there shouldn't be a problem as I always use the same payment method, address, etc. and to be contacted if additional information was needed.  I never received a response back from their customer service.  Instead, two weeks later, I received a notice that my order was cancelled for insufficient information.  I then replied to that email referencing the one I sent two weeks prior.  All they could say was go back online and order again.  Awful!  Amazon.com really came through and offered this pain free gift card.  Thanks again Amazon!... as always.
Gift_Cards.summary: Better than ordering from Forever21

Got the Domino's Pizza E-Gift card. It came 27 1/2mins after purchase. Then had the Taco Bell & Burger King gift cards sent to my Address on the road. When online at both to check balances after they showed up 24hrs later.
This even after the payments I'll end up making is far better than freezing or being hungry.

Gift_Cards.reviewText: Liked how this comes in a box for gift giving except that the bow was flattened and ugly and couldn't be "poofed up" or removed to make it look better. Perhaps including a bow/ribbon that the giver could apply would be a better option.

Gift_Cards.reviewText: I buy the amazon kindle gift card for my self. I did find it a little difficult figuring out how to purchase it and apply it to my account. That being said it is very nice being able to do that on line and I am not a computer savy person.
Gift_Cards.summary: I like being able to purchase the Kindle gift card on line. I did find it a little difficult figuring out how to purchase it.

Gift_Cards.reviewText: Being able to customize the gift card with your own photo is a nice touch. The only glitch in the process was that I was not able to view an image of what the final product (the full size 'card' with photo) looked like before sending it off.  I would have found this helpful to judge if the scale of the photo looked good or not.
Gift_Cards.summary: Convenient & probably safer than sending a check in the mail

Gift_Cards.reviewText: The only thing that I take exception to is the fact that I was not given the option to receive this by mail, until after I had already processed the email version.  I had to make a small certificate to put in a small box, so that I had something to put under the Christmas tree for the recipient.
Gift_Cards.summary: Thanks for a great last-minute gift!

Gift_Cards.reviewText:
I am giving this only 4 stars because the cards didn't come in secure mail, they were just dropped off at the door step, no signature required.

Otherwise I am extremely happy to have the amazon cards!  Easy to catalog the serial number of the card along with the claim code in my Holiday gift list book.

Then I email my friends/family instructions on how to load the card on their amazon account.  I ask that they reply with results so that I know they loaded the card on their account.  Then I use a permanent marker to mark the card with the recipient's name and log it in my book!

It isn't our business what they "buy" - just nice to know the card is loaded on their account for them to choose what they wish and hopefully we get a Thank You note!

Thank You Dave & Joy for being my first success in sharing holiday giving!
Gift_Cards.summary: We Love to Give Amazon Gift Cards!

Gift_Cards.reviewText: Love using this product service. Just make sure that you have correct email address. If you are sending more then once gift card to different people then I would do each one individual to prevent any confusion or loss of money. Other then that, it's great and really fast! A lot better than paying an extra $2 for shipping when you send it to someone's home. I recommend!
Gift_Cards.summary: So easy to send!

Gift_Cards.reviewText:
Hired as bodyguard for a feisty elderly writer, Shelby goes up against her clients nephew, one Special Agent Nelson Kane. Shot when the FBI worked another case with Shelbys employer, Northstar Security, Kane is prejudiced against her, until he sees shes a consummate professional. Shelby is not only willing to die to protect his beloved aunt, but she also cares for Rosalee, as well.
The chemistry between Shelby and Kane is immediate, building from a bubbling froth to a potential combustion. Each is skeptical of a long term relationship working, but neither can walk away.
Fletcher builds tension by moving the reader from one attempt on Rosalees life to the next, as well as intriguing us with the growing connection between her two protagonists. The story includes characters introduced in earlier books in the Northstar series, increasing my interest in reading the others. The author has a flare for writing unique metaphors that grabbed my attention, such as his own love life was much the same. Catch and release. The naturally flowing dialogue makes it a fast, easy, straight-through-to-the-end read. You can have an entertaining time with this book.
Gift_Cards.summary: such as his own love life was much the same

Gift_Cards.reviewText: What a fun and attractive way to send a gift card.  My grandchildren love sitting on the computer and shopping on Amazon for their favorite birthday presents.  I don't have to guess and guess and possibly disappoint, so it's a win, win situation.

Gift_Cards.reviewText: I really liked it - the colors were great along with the picture.  The only thing that I would change is to have an option of printing and folding a 8.5 x 11 paper into the four sides or what I would like is have it print front to back so that it could be printed more on cardstock.  This way it would look more professional.

Gift_Cards.reviewText: This is a fast and easy way to send a gift. I do have twi issues though. 1 you cannot indicate a time you would like to email to be sent. It is either midnight on the day you indicate. Or you wait and order it at the time you want it sent. 2 you need to include your name in the message line because the recipient does not see the "from" section.

I was ordering for five different people I work with and had planned on getting a different greeting card for each person.  Every card I clicked on said not available.  There was only one design available with a Christmas theme, which I chose for all five. So no matter if you get this on sale like I did ($10), you aren't going to get full value on the card because you're going to be paying them a fee each time you use it.  I won't be buying one again, not when I can get tickets at the theater or their website for the normal price.

totally ruined the surprise

Gift_Cards.reviewText:
I was unimpressed with the online gift card email delivery.  Thought an Amazon gift card with a special picture would be a great gift for my Mother-in-Law, right to her email so I purchased it in advance of her birthday.  Per the option on Amazon to deliver it to her email on a scheduled day, I scheduled for email delivery to her on her birthday.

When I checked in with her on her birthday, she had not received it at all. (She also checked her junk/spam folder, although she is already an Amazon customer and nothing there).  When I contacted Amazon about it, they apologized for the mistake and thought there must have been a glitch in their internal system.  They were nice about it and corrected it, but the element of surprise and timeliness of delivery was a fail.

No concessions were offered and just got an apology.  I don't feel confident to purchase an online gift card as an option again.

Gift_Cards.reviewText: The Amazon gift card was supposed to be white...which goes along very well with the new baby theme. But the one that was just delivered to me is black, which doesn't match the baby theme of the packaging as well.

Gift_Cards.reviewText:
I received a gift card from my daughter for Christmas.  Later, with certain items in mind I placed an order which became complicated, because I wanted to combine two items together for economy in shipping.  The result was that each item was separately assigned for shipping, so I could not take advantage of free shipping with orders totaling more than $50.  Furthermore, I was informed that, if I failed to use my gift amount at that moment, the gift amount would be reduced by $10.

I was frustrated to the extent that I contacted Amazon to cancel both orders, but one arrived anyway.  I was told to return it unopened, which I did, and eventually I find that my original gift from my daughter has been credited to my account, and I am now awaiting to use it.

The entire episode was fraught with confusion, but ultimately I still have the gift amount awaiting my use.  The problem was trying to combine two orders into one delivery.

I asked whether I could submit the redemption by phone and was told they can't get into the system either.  It's now after that and I tried again and am getting the same message.

A day later, the system allowed me to request a redemption, and I received an email confirming it.  Goplaygolf contacted the course to make advance payment, but was told it is no longer participating.  Emailed me right away to let me know.  I was impressed by and appreciated the follow-up.

Gift_Cards.reviewText:
Great alternative to a gift card, but widely unpopular with the cashiers I've met with.  A manager was needed on both occasions that I used this product to verify which took awhile.  In other words, purchase the actual gift card if you're one of those people who seem to always be in a rush.

Perfect gift for college kids in need of groceries!
Gift_Cards.summary: Not for everyone.

Gift_Cards.reviewText: Usually have no issues with Amazon, especially gift cards, but these came loosely in a fold over box with pull zip.  One tin good, one tin with bow detached and one without a bow at all.  I am receiving a replacement order, but makes me wonder why a person wouldn't catch that in the packaging/shipping process.  Obviously a gift card is a gift, it has to look nice.  Seems like no ones cares about quality much anymore.
Gift_Cards.summary: Quality Control needed

Gift_Cards.reviewText: I ordered a baby shower gift card and printed it at home.  I have a good printer, good paper and a new color cartridge, but the card came out green rather than pink.  I think having it mailed to me would have resulted in a nicer looking gift.
Gift_Cards.summary: Flimsy gift

Gift_Cards.reviewText: Amazon gift cards are convenient and easy to send. the proof of use/collection by the intended recipient is buried in clicks and layers of programming. How many forgetful people never collect a gift card and what happens to the money tied up in an uncollected gift card?
Gift_Cards.summary: Gift cards: easy to send; hard to prove it was used

Gift_Cards.reviewText: You can't go wrong getting a gift card, and there wasn't a thing wrong with it, but what are you to do when the gift BOX arrived dinged up and with some spot stains on it (as if someone splashed coffee on it)? Not cool. I'm now faced with finding a suitable replacement.
Gift_Cards.summary: card accurate, box wrecked

Gift_Cards.reviewText: For some mysterious reason you can't order a $30 gift card in the "Thank You" card. That's right - you can send a $25 gift card but not a $30 gift card in the card printed with "Thank You" on the front. Can there possibly be a reason for this?
Gift_Cards.summary: Dumbest restriction ever
