Am enjoying the music and performers, but this made-on-demand CD-R has many pops, clicks and other defects on tracks 15 and 16.  Tested on three different CD players.  I have professional sound de-clicker software that could not fix it.  No way to tell if the problem is in the original audio files or just my CD-R.  Booklet is no more than a listing of the tracks.

"What would you think, if I sang out of tune, Would you stand up and walk out on me?"

Famous words sang in a famous song, sung by a famous drummer. No Ringo, wed never walk out on you. Never. Not even if theres a fire. But the same can no longer be said of the Flaming Lips and their extremely old and stale shenanigans. I think Im honestly one of the remaining few that have held on up to this point. I championed The Terror, that Peace Sword S/T, and that 7 Skies H3 album they released last RSD(I honestly thing 7 Skies H3 is some of the best stuff theyve done since Embryonic.) Man, Ive taken every bitter pill theyve sent my way and Ive loved every weird trip theyve taken me on. But this cover album of Sgt. Peppers Lonely Hearts Club Band? Nah, I just cant do it anymore. Im through. There needs to be some sort of intervention for Mr. Coyne. Shut down his Instagram. Take away his gummy molding machine, and all of his plastic doo dads he covers himself in on stage. He needs to seriously get his head out of whatever fumes hes been inhaling and breathe in some untainted oxygen. The jig is up, you fearless freak.

Let me first say that Im not some Beatles extremist. When I first heard the Lips were covering Sgt Pepper I was thrilled. I was and still am a huge fan of their take on The Dark Side of the Moon. I felt that in their own way The Flaming Lips stayed true to that album without compromising any of their weirdness. If they were to do that with Sgt Pepper, then we were going to be in for a real treat. I mean, Sgt Pepper was a massive statement. A milestone, and an album that in many eyes can never be replicated or matched. The Lips created that for me in 1999 when they put out The Soft Bulletin. That album was pure, child-like honesty put to otherworldly and ethereal music. It encapsulated the wonder and fear of life and death, all brought together by Wayne Coynes wavering and breaking voice. I was 24 years old when that album came out and it affected me much like Sgt Pepper affected so many folks 32 years before. How could Wayne Coyne and company screw this up? I don't know, but they did.

This album really comes off as a big, noisy mess. Its as if Coyne and company weren't even there. They let special guests(and there were quite a few) in the studio, locked them in, and proceeded to pump in nitrous oxide through the vents to see what would happen. Its a real shame, too, as underneath it all theres some great performances by The Autumn Defense, Dr. Dog, Phantogram, and My Morning Jacket. Those performances are covered in clumps of audio fuzz, grime, and over blown excess. Yes, Im aware Im talking about the Flaming Lips when Im complaining about excess. Heres the thing: the Lips have always excelled at excess. They do excess beautifully. But here the excess is excessive. A beautiful vocal performance by the Autumn Defense in With A Little Help From My Friends is completely stunted by pairing them with Black Pus. Sgt Peppers Lonely Hearts Club Band is shat upon by a overzealous guitar solo by the wonderful J Mascis at the end. Getting Better, featuring Dr. Dog, seems like a completely incredible combination until you throw Chuck Inglish in there as well and it just kinda falls flat on its face. I wouldve loved to have heard Dr. Dogs full access on this track, with the Lips noodling on the knobs and faders a bit. Instead we get this detached Chuck Inglish vocal over top Dr. Dog with some pretty great stereo drums. Its so close to perfection. A Day In The Life, while not bad, seems to just fall a little flat. This shouldve been monstrous, explosive, and beautiful. Instead, we get the most restraint weve seen on this covers album where it shouldve been the biggest statement possible.

A lot of people have bitched and moaned about Miley Cyrus connection to the Lips and Coyne, and especially her inclusion on this album. Well Im here to say she is not to blame for the issues here. She does fine, really. She is featured on A Day In The Life, as well as one of the album highlights, Lucy In The Sky With Diamonds. They go big for Lucy and it works beautifully. Electric Wurms cover of Fixing A Hole is also a nice surprise. They pretty much stick to script here, with some nice, dreamy effects. Sorta like Yes covering the Beatles and it works. Shes Leaving Home is quite melancholy with Phantogram, Julianna Barwick, and Spaceface. It has an 80s electro vibe with all of the original tracks mournful feel. Being For The Benefit of Mr. Kite! with Maynard James Keenan is a perfect fit, actually. It has a carnival of souls aura and Keenan makes the track his own. Within You Without You with Birdflower and Morgan Delt keeps the mystical vibe of Harrisons original, with some modern touches that aren't too overbearing. Most of the rest? Kinda just there, really.

The strangest thing is that you wouldnt even know this was a project curated by The Flaming Lips if it weren't for the production. You hear them in like two tracks. Other than that, who knows? Even with something like Heady Fwends you got the feeling Wayne, Steve, and Michael were in the room with their fwends. Not so much here.

I look at classic albums like Sgt Peppers Lonely Hearts Club Band, Pet Sounds, and Odyssey and Oracle and I compare them to classical pieces by Mozart, Beethoven, and Debussy. They fall under the canon of timeless pieces of music and should be interpreted and endeared by future musicians and artists. Weve done this for hundreds of years and it is a practice that should continue for hundreds of years to come. The Flaming Lips, I felt, were a band to do such a thing with The Beatles. They did right by Pink Floyd. Theyll do right by The Beatles, right? Even for Coyne, Drozd, and Ivins this is pretty far out there. Theyve taken themselves and a bunch of great artists and covered their covers of Lennon/McCartney compositions in so much noise its hard to discern anyones original intent.

This certainly isn't a phoned-in tribute. Its ambitious, ballsy, and grand for sure. But even Pollack knew when enough was enough. Wayne, sometimes less is more. I still love you, but Im gonna have to walk away on this one.

Particularly in reggae music, it is always very interesting to go back and take a listen to one of your favourite artist's earlier material in comparing it to the vibes they are currently releasing. It has always been to my experience that in reggae (and I MIGHT say the same thing about hip-hop as well, but not too many other musical genres), it is so easy to mark an artist's progression in overall skills and experience in all facets of the music, in the studio, with the pen and ESPECIALLY on the stage. Over the past few years probably the most remarkable and OBVIOUS example of this, has been in dancehall prodigy Assassin (and the next best example, in the dancehall, would probably be Mr. Peppa who was downright AWFUL the first few times I heard him), who rather swiftly went from being known strictly as the protg to his mentor, longtime wicked dancehall veteran Spragga Benz, to being an artist able to look the truly elite dancehall artists in directly in the eye from a skill standpoint. Assassin added new and newer facets to his game in leaps and bounds and not to say that his early material was off-point by any degree (listen to some of those earlier tunes like Bad From or Wah Gwan and some of them are literally saturated in remarkable potential), but he has undeniably become an artist for the new generation boasting skills alongside a level of maturity perhaps unseen in the dancehall EVER, at his age. Similar situations in the recent dancehall landscape exist; such as Aidonia going from a Bounty Killer clone to a tongue-twisting juggernaut of a lyricist and Busy Signal, seemingly peaking so early in his career, only to vanish and return with an even deeper bag of lyrics as well. In the roots game, the situation has been very similar in Jamaica. Check Natural Black, who has developed from a somewhat RAW artist with top notch natural ability and vibes, but VERY inconsistent at the beginning of his career; now into someone who has to be considered one of the most dependable names in roots reggae to deliver quality vibes EVERYTIME. There's also the case of Richie Spice whose meteoric rise to prominence coincided only with his equally meteoric rise in vibes and ability, which, at their absolute heights, make Spice an artist who literally EVERY tune which he releases has the potential to be a bonafide HIT. And I would be just wrong for not mentioning former Richie Spice label mate Chuck Fender whose middle of the career change in his approach took him from being a `run of the mill' (virtually indistinguishable from the rest of the pack) Bounty Killer clone, into being one of the most crucial roots voices in reggae over the past decade. Just observing them throughout their careers (and still time to come definitely for them all) is really one of the best things of listening to such a segmented, yet ordered, music such as reggae.

 Outside of Jamaica, where the international scene is a bit easier to follow as it is dictated by albums, as opposed to scattered singles for scattered producers, things are still very interesting. Take, for instance, the case of Ras Attitude who, at this point, is in the process of establishing himself as really one of the TOP flight modern Caribbean reggae artists from outside of Jamaica, if he isn't already (and I think he is), alongside names such as fellow Virgin Islanders Pressure Busspipe, Midnite, Bambu Station and the various lights from the French West Indies. The `advantage' the St. Croix native Attitude seems to have over his peers, at this point, is his WELL POLISHED style. You would almost have no choice but to look at more experienced names such as Luciano,  Bushman and Junior Kelly (and interestingly enough, I think I'm now throwing Tarrus Riley in that list as well who, like Attitude, seems as if he were created to make reggae music) to hear a more CONSISTENT `shine' on the vibes and the overall presentation of music than you'll find in Ras Attitude. This is a quality which makes his music more presentable to greater masses (especially in Jamaica) and more accessible to fans (unlike the many who  tend to find the music of Midnite to be somewhat odd). Besides Ras Attitude himself, undoubtedly much of that polish has to be credited to Attitude's producer/fellow artist/and good friend Batch. Most, if not all, of the early material you'll find anywhere from Ras Attitude is almost certainly a Batch production as the VI musical genius produced Attitude's first two of now five albums, Happiness and Love Live for his very own Sound V.I.Zion  Records. Very early Ras Attitude and the well crafted and sculpted version of the artist we see today are almost night and day in terms of quality (which is saying a lot as the early version is definitely not unimpressive on any standards). Much of that VERY EARLY material is catalogued in Ras Attitude's very first album release, Happiness from Sound V.I.Zion which, in 2001, had the distinction of becoming the label's very first full length studio release for a single artist (if I recall correctly, it had previously done a compilation before Happiness actually reached). Even before Batch would bring forth HIS OWN debut, 2003's Who You Are, he would do Attitude's Happiness, showing a great bit of confidence in the artist investing so much of himself on a chance in the artist (the entire reggae world now owes a great big thank you to Batch for taking that chance). The results on that initial album were definitely mixed as Attitude had yet to show (or maybe even develop them at that early point) a few of the things which now make him one of the most refined artists in the business. Happiness is a look back at what is definitely destined to be one of the biggest names in Virgin Island reggae music of all time and an undeniable reggae force overall.

The thing, for me, which tends to exemplify and individualize Ras Attitude's vibes from his countless peers is his personality. Much like Junior Kelly, he has an almost indescribable ability to push a bit more of himself besides writing the words, developing the melody and singing the track. It is a quality which is definitely rare, but also makes his a talent which is more in demand as I think you could take a more experienced artist and a similar artist (perhaps such as Kelly himself) and have him sing Attitude's tunes (or vice-versa) and not be able to dem them the justice by the originator. That is a quality which hadn't been exactly tweaked on Happiness, thus, while in terms of vibes, it is not too much different from the powerhouse which would immediately follow it, Love Life (Batch himself had developed a bit as a producer between the two albums as well), but it doesn't have that `certified' Ras Attitude feel just quite, still it does a fine job in introducing the world to a name to keep and eye and a half on in reggae music these days. Getting things started on the album after a brief Nyahbinghi intro, Happiness gets started with what is one of the four tunes which really go to be the strength and identifiable tunes on the album altogether, the sublime Back in the Hills. The tune opens itself to a very nice comparison to a far more recent Attitude tune to show a very nice contrast, Trodding Home. It wouldn't have been out of the question to me for the same artist who had made the wonderful Back in the Hills which is a song speaking about leaving babylon and returning to the Motherland, would have someday developed into the artist who could make the SUPREME Trodding Home years later in his career. Back in the Hills isn't as refined or direct as Trodding Home would ultimately prove to be, but it's still VERY good and an excellent way to start things here. The second track here, Pop Off is one of the harder and harsher vibes on the album and pretty much a straight forward conscious dancehall track which doesn't find Attitude at his best (there are a few dancehall tracks on Love Life as well, but most of them, if not all, really hit their mark stronger than most of the dancehall pieces on Happiness, again showing the development in Attitude's game). Finishing the opening of Happiness is a very fine interlude which goes a bit into introducing Ras Attitude the artist to the masses. While typically not a big fan of interludes I have absolutely no problem with it here and actually I think it's a good idea for debuting artists.

The second of the `big four' tunes on Happiness rolls out just after the opening with the very BIG The Voice. The tune is a vibes which is a bit of a musical celebration and a celebration of His Majesty at the same time (the entire album could be described as such, as could Attitude's entire career for that matter). Batch also comes top notch as well, providing Attitude with a big LUSH sounding vibes over which to deliver what may just be the most memorable track on Happiness, if not the best overall (although I don't think so). Topping The Voice is definitely the LOVELY Jah Trees which may just be the single most popular tune to have emerged from the Happiness album and definitely the one which has been the most discussed (at least by me) over the years. The tune speaks of His Majesty providing the world with all the things in nature that it needs to survive as well as the things which endanger what HE has done for us. Just a lovely big vibes and one which I someday hope to see Attitude perform live. However, it is the final track here, Glorious, which gloriously tops the entire album as my favourite track here overall with a vibes which could have EASILY fit in on any of Ras Attitude's later and just BETTER albums and not dipped the vibes AT ALL. Glorious is a track which shows EXACTLY what I mean by Attitude's personality effecting a tune: The tune itself is a song about going to meet His Majesty and how GLORIOUS the moment will be (and indeed it will) and Attitude adds spice to the track (which rides a master class one-drop) which, even at that early stage of his career, make the song of his unique own vibes style. Definitely a BIG track. While I don't think much of the album really matches up to those four big tracks, there are still a few pieces here which standout on a smaller level. Check the pounding Rasta Empress which would definitely be something out of Batch's own style as he is known for throwing together some MASSIVE anthems for the Afrikan female on his own albums. Attitude is smart and he brings Batch along to sing on the tune as well, and anytime you can get the two together vocally on a track it is definitely something to witness. Rasta Empress is no exception at all. The other official combination here features Dominican born jack-of-all-trades musician/artist Jerome Austrie, who is a VI (in particular Batch himself and Sound V.I.Zion) favourite as well. The two make a strong reggae/r&b combination which focuses on bringing a bigger level of love to the world. The title track for Happiness is, oddly enough, on a more fast dancehall vibes, which are present throughout the album. I was actually a bit surprised to see that it wasn't a more straight forward rootical number (based strictly on the title probably), but it, like many of the dancehall-ish tunes here, does carry a strong message, I just don't think that it was best for Attitude at that point to be delivering on so many faster riddims at that point as sometimes he doesn't appear capable of peaking with such a tune on such a riddim. A similar situation occurs on the very nice (lyrically speaking) Who Mek Man on which Attitude employs the young DJ style of throwing "you know" behind his words on his first verse. Its definitely a move you'll see more with the youths (or in freestyles) and I wouldn't expect to see it from Attitude as of now. Lastly, I'll mention the tune Hyah, which, again, shows the youth. You would DEFINITELY not hear such a tune these days from Attitude as it comes off as an almost COMPLETE freestyle and together with Rock Dem (I have no idea what happened with that one!) represent, in my opinion, the only two REAL missteps on Happiness altogether.

Overall, I'd almost say that the Happiness album would have somewhat of a `collector's item' type of feel to it as we see exactly what Ras Attitude has `grown up' to become. Happiness was strictly a `warning shot' of what was to come. Its interesting because, although solid, I can imagine there were so many potential fans who didn't actually `stick around' to see what was coming next (I myself actually got the album after I had already heard the Love Life album which is probably still, to date, my favourite Attitude album). What they missed out on was one of the most compelling artists in the game today regardless of country and an overall show of a downright SUPERB display of potential throughout Ras Attitude's career and it started at Happiness.

I was a little bit disappointed with Marks latest  album. It does not come close to 'Get Lucky'. Probably did not need to be a double cd, could have put 13 or 14 tracks on one. Saying that the title song is vintage Knopfler at his best. I have tickets for his show in two weeks and am really looking forward to hear him perform some of these songs live.

If you are a fan of Bring Me The Horizon you will eaither love this band or you will ultimately hate this band. Asking Alexandria does a good job at keeping you interested with they're simple but heavy breakdowns and they're Dance/Trance beats but let's go over the album as a whole.

*Negative*
So the first song I ever heard from Asking Alexandria was "The Final Episode", it started off pretty strong and had me going up until the vocalist screamed the words "Oh My God" over and over in unison with the breakdown. If that wasn't bad enough I had to endure the overly annoying 2-string picking that happened right before the vocalist screamed "OMG". Also, they do this a lot through out the album which really annoys me.

*Positive*
By now (if you are a fan) you probably hate me for the negative comments. At least with this band there are some redeeming qualities! For instance, after the slow, boring, cliche breakdown it gets kind of interesting. Finally, the Trance beat comes in and even though it really isn't much it still seperates the dull boring part of the song from the awesome parts. Somewhere near the end of the song you can actually hear how intricate some of the guitar parts are. In fact rather than playing in the scale they were playing in they change it up with some augmented notes that make it sound amazing.

As for the rest of the album, it all sounds the same in my opinion. It's like they are afraid to deviate from the formula that they made themselves and rather than being innovative and experiment a little they tend to always open up with a breakdown or a really simple riff. It really sucks because if you listen to one of they're songs only half of it is worth listening to....but that's my opinion.

If you are really into Post-Hardcore bands or Metal-Core you should at least check this band out on Youtube because if you buy it you are only getting half of what you payed for.

Also! If you are into Bring Me The Horizon you will most likely think that this band is a crappy version of BMTH with Dance beats.
Digital_Music.summary: Bring Me The Horizon with dance beats

Digital_Music.reviewText:
I'm looking at my collection of Vivaldi 100 Supreme Masterpieces, and noticing I have lots less than 100 pieces here. The track numbering goes like this: 1-12, 23, 35-79. That's an attrition rate of over 40%. I'm not that picky, either.

Who survived my pruning? The Drottningholm Baroque Ensemble. Most of what they do is very good, and their 4 Seasons is a very nice, "not crazy," rendition. You also get another piece from opus 8, number 10. These are incisively played, and the ensemble plays with very good attention to detail.

Likewise, when they team up with Jakob Lindberg on the Vivaldi lute pieces, the results are as good as you will find, even if the music is a bit light weight.

The group London Baroque gets a couple of chamber pieces here. They should have gotten more. The variations on La Folia are fun. They play with more vibrato than the Drottningholm Ensemble (which essentially uses none).

Dan Laurin teams up with the Drottningholm Ensemble for a couple of pieces and also with the Bach Collegium of Japan. Laurin is a good recorder player, but he tends to "noodle around," particularly in the slow movements.

The Musicians of San Marco are a group that appears mainly in compilations. The reason? They don't stand out. They are not well recorded; they sound distant and muffled. None-the-less, the second movement of the violin concerto Il Ritiro is quite good. The rest of what they do is passable.

La Tempesta is also recorded at a distance. They aren't too bad on the instrumental pieces, but the Magnificat sounds like it was recorded in an echo chamber. It doesn't help that the counter-tenor can't sing runs, and the soprano tends to go sharp.

The Conrad von der Goltz Chamber Orchestra plays Vivaldi in that good old 1950s style: Recorded at a distance, and everything sustained as long as possible.

The Petersburg Soloists are recorded somewhat closer, the better to hear that tremendous vibrato, and all the other 19th century add-ons.

I've haven't heard of the Camerata Rhenania. Their recording of the trumpet concerto uses slow tempos, partly because the trumpeters don't sound like they could handle anything faster. The concerto, op. 3, no. 11 features slow tempos, and lots of vibrato. The recordings are distant and mushy.

The renditions of Vivaldi's L'Estro Armonico by the Janacek Chamber Orchestra aren't too bad, however. Their ensemble playing is sloppy, and they know very little about Baroque performance practice, but they play with some verve, even if their Allegros are all the same, exact tempo. I didn't keep them because I already have three better versions of the complete set.

Bottom line, currently the set costs $2.00. Get it and keep what you like.

I beg to differ slightly with the previous reviewer, Robin Yokoyama, who claimed that most of these tracks are not by the "original people."

Actually, after reviewing the titles/artists AND listening to the samples at amazon, I've concluded that about 27 tracks are by the "original people," but of these, only about 10 of them are the originally-released versions; the remainder are by the original artists, but are nevertheless remakes which differ either marginally or substantially from the versions initially released. Consequently, I would have to say this CD is neither for collectors NOR for those who are younger and simply want to take a curiosity-seeking hejira to the fifties and sixties.

The "erroneous" tracks (meaning that they are not by the original artists) are Alley Cat (originally by Bent Fabric, NOT Bill Pursell); Apache (by Jorgan Ingmann, NOT Dennis Coffey); Guitar Boogie Shuffle (by The Virtues, NOT Dennis Coffey); Green Onions (by Booker T & the MGs, NOT Dave "Baby" Cortez); and "Grazing in the Grass" (by Hugh Masekela, NOT Bill Justis). There are probably a handful of others suffering from what might be called misattribution, but they are either songs I'm not sufficiently familiar with, or are simply incidental items that should probably have been deleted in favor of better and more important songs.

Tracks that are by the original artists but are remade versions (almost all of them inferior to the originals) are "Raunchy"; "Beatnick Fly"; "Reveille Rock"; "Let There Be Drums"; "Our Winter Love" (yes, this WAS by Bill Pursell, but rendered better initially); "Sleep Walk" (attributed here simply to "Santo," rather than more accurately to "Santo & Johnny"); and "Let's Go". Again, there may be a small handful of others I'm uncertain about, but these are among the less-important items anyway for the most part.

Also, I think it should be pointed out that the samples for "Perfidia" and "Lullaby of the Leaves" are mistakenly labeled. When you click on the latter, you hear "Perfidia," and vice versa. Also, just for the record, "Perfidia" was already an old standard dating back to the Big Band era at the time the Ventures recorded it, and, to my knowledge, had usually been performed as a vocal prior to the Ventures version. The Ventures original version of "Perfidia" IS, in fact, on this disc, but someone simply goofed on the title. I only mention this since, in my opinion, "Perfidia" is one of the greatest instrumentals the Ventures ever recorded - a real gem that still carries an awesome sense of momentum.

My last bone of contention (and one of my pet peeves) is "Tuff," by Ace Cannon. I'm fairly certain this is not the original version released in 1961. Nevertheless, from the snippet I sampled at amazon, this CD has a version that is closer to the original than anything I've sampled from any of the Ace Cannon CDs under his own byline. "Tuff" is an extremely difficult track to find on CD in its originally-released form; all the versions I've heard thus far at amazon are remakes that incorporate trills and other artifacts that were not in the 1961 version. Also, they are slightly speeded up, whereas the original was quite slow. In fact, it's the EXTREMELY slow tempo of the version on this CD which makes me feel that it has greater fidelity to the original version (that, and the fact that the organ work in the background sounds identical to the original as I remember it)). So this, if not the authentic original, is extremely close to it. I know this because I own the original version on an old 45 RPM copy (now almost totally worn out), and I remember it virtually note-for-note. I've belabored my point, but this remains a questionable track.

So - to repeat - this is not a recommended collection. There are plenty of better compilations of oldie instrumentals available (the problematic status of "Tuff" notwithstanding), so I'd strongly dissuade anyone but the most casual fan from purchasing this disc.
Digital_Music.summary: A strange hodgepodge of originals, remakes, and miscues

A group seven years in the making, Brooklyn to Milwaukee connection eMC, Masta Ace, Wordsworth and Stricklin, with Punchline up until his late 2014 departure, were record collaboration partners before uniting as an official crew thanks to the encouragement of fans on internet message boards. Pairings of the members appeared on Juice Crew legend Masta Ace's 2001 album Disposable Arts and 2004's A Long Hot Summer, and in 2008 the four released their first collective LP, The Show. Following The Show's critical underground success, they left the scene for six years, returning in 2014 with the solid Turning Point EP. In capitalizing off their recent comeback velocity, the former quartet now a trio are back with an LP, their second, called The Tonite Show, not to be confused with Freddie Gibbs' 2014 EP of the same name.

The songs on the album, which follow no particular storyline, are arranged around a series of skits that document a bad day in which eMC are snubbed from an appearance on a farcical Tonight Show, "The Tonite Show starring Jimmy Falcon." They're playful and sprinkled with a smattering of light humor, even if they're a bit cumbersome and annoying to experience at parts. The actual songs find the emcees either hitting or missing the mark lyrically, sometimes putting on a smart, complex rhyme-show and other times laying back not trying extremely hard with their lines. Laid out on the table are numerous put-downs and critiques of rivals and male groupies (eMC call them "moopies") plus the group's experience with lovely crushes but also dysfunctional relationships, not delicious grub for heads to chomp on but possibly all the guys could come up with in less than one year's time.

A low-key showing of guests including emcees B-Real, Xzibit and Sadat X lend variety and Rosie Perez, Timoor Anunnaki, and comedians Tony Rock (younger brother of comedian Chris Rock) and Russell Peters serve as the guests and host of The Tonite Show. To make matters more mundane, the old style beats, provided by a group of B-List producers, are straight out of a poppy, outdated r&b playbook. It can be argued that The Tonite Show was rushed and is mainly the desire to cash in on the hopes of old curious fans, but it's better than nothing as further holdout from the group could have given us no product at all. The absence of Punchline hurts but doesn't debilitate, and while Masta Ace, Wordsworth and Stricklin are all still fantastic in their own individual respects, the great group dynamic and chemistry they once had might unfortunately be unreproducible at this point.
Digital_Music.summary: eMC take advantage of their comeback momentum with 'The Tonite Show'

Digital_Music.reviewText: So in listening to this, a few notes.  Dave always scatted and half sang the songs live in between flying around and dancing so that's here as well, expected that.  The mix on this album and their previous album is where we have "Classic Van Halen" vs Modern issues.  It's a live album for sure but there's no way that the microphones they had set up would have captured the amount of reverb that's on this album.  The result creates a bit of a mud fest making the vocals at times difficult to perceive.  The reverb needed to be dialed back and EQ'd to get it more out of the way.  No doubt it has to be there in some for to produce the "live" feel but it needed to be less up in the mix.  The over all mix is compressed in a homogenized fashion so that we lose a lot of the dynamics of Alex's Tom's, Eddie's low end chugging.  It's there but it so heavily compressed that it doesn't grab you.  It's a flat mix. I also feel the vocals could have been mid boosted a little to help them cut through a bit better without being obnoxious.  Ed's still got it.  Alex still has it.  Wolf is okay.  Dave is a caricature of himself in the 80's and there is literally nothing he can do about it. People have to accept that or just not listen to them as they are now.  There's no way on earth that Dave will ever be able to pull off all the things he used to be able to do.  So bottom line I think what really hampers their efforts on this album is the mix.  It seems as though with out Don Landee at the helm, Van Halen does not sound as effective as they did with Don Landee.
Digital_Music.summary: I think the mix is what hurts this release.

Digital_Music.reviewText: Without any doubt, this is one of the worst "interprations" of Mozart's late symphonies - both recordings, this one and the other one (Nos. 38 and 41), are beyond painful to listen to.  I am not kidding.  Firstly, and this I say with all sincerity, the sound is as perfect as it gets, the Freiburger Barockorchester demonstrates one of the most finely crafted performances - but the issue lies with the conductor, who has taken a work and butchered it to the point where I could not help myself but go back and listen to parts just to be sure I heard it right.  Jacobs clearly has no faith in the music itself because he feels the need to change things to his own liking, to the point where I think the essence of the music is lost beyond repair.  For example, tempi are chaotic (not creative or powerful), piano and forte are confused - I don't think he remembered what "crescendo" and "diminuendo" means in music (yes, I'm being cheeky, but seriously, you'll understand once you hear these performances).  I felt insulted as the listener to expect a "forte" instead getting a "whimper" - come on...at some point a conductor must maintain some professional decorum and show some respect to the music as printed on the paper in front of him.  The 40th symphony sounds like a comic opera - actually, not even that - it sounds like a divertimento.  I was disgusted by it, so much so that I listened to it a few times just to see if maybe I was "missing the point" - no, I was not missing the point at all.  Jacobs slapped me in the face with his vomit he dares to call a "fresh" interpretation.  Pardon me, but I have nothing against interprations (hence why I own mulitiple recordings of the same music), but this is not an interpretation, this is something else.  In any even, I gave it 2 stars, and those 2 stars it only received due to the first rate technical prowess of the Freiburger Barockorchester, and for the sound quality of the Harmonia Mundi label.  Other than that, Jacobs also costed this recording 3 stars.  Nothing to be proud of.  If you think you'll be getting the usual "superb Jacobs" here, well, you won't ... you'll be getting a Jacobs you never knew was possible.  I was floored, and not in a good way. Thanks for reading this.  Cheers!
Digital_Music.summary: The only recording by Jacobs which floored me, in a bad way...

Digital_Music.reviewText: This compilation does no justice to Isaac Hayes, his artistry or his visionary genius. Why? Isaac was an artist whose music needed to be heard (or, more accurately, EXPERIENCED) on a full-length basis to be appreciated. While most of these songs were (out of necessity) released as singles it goes without saying that the full-length LP versions of such immortal Hayes classics as "Walk On By", "I Stand Accused", "The Look Of Love", "Joy" and "Never Can Say Goodbye" were what sold their respective parent albums. If you really want a compilation of Isaac's hits then I recommend getting the now-deleted "Best of Isaac Hayes " Volumes 1 & 2 (both released in 1986) as these at least give you the original album versions without any (unnecessary) editing.

You can look at Bashmet's Apollo in two ways, I suppose: His sudden, loud outbursts in dynamics, coupled with exaggerated softness at other times, along with his lurching tempos and his oddly skipping, almost staccato phrasing, could be said to "enliven" things. And they undoubtedly do--at times. But they can equally be seen as elements that make this music fragmented and disjointed--and this they also undoubtedly do. This reading lacks cohesiveness and continuity; the whole ends up being much less than the sum of its disjointed parts.

Stravinsky's music for strings has a rich but understated and austere beauty, composed in "a palette of white on white," as someone once described it. Like most of Stravinsky's ballets, it works equally well as concert music. I have always found its melodicism, its classical beauty and poise, absorbing enough without histrionics. But if you don't find the music meaningful without dancers on a stage, or if you need some thrash metal injected into your classical music, Bashmet is the guy to do it for you. What makes this performance work as well as it does is the sheer tonal beauty and virtuosity of this ensemble, coupled with the excellent quality of the recording. For that reason, there are undeniably some moments of beauty on this disc. But this kind of tonal beauty and virtuosity is enough to inject all the freshness this music needs, so that Bashmet's flailing about as he strains to make interpretive points becomes totally unnecessary. If it weren't for the quality of the playing and recording, I think we'd hear this for what it is--rather badly over-interpreted Stravinsky.

Some, but not all, of my favorite recordings of Apollo in the past have been by Jarvi, Esa-Peka Salonen, and Jukka-Pekka Saraste.

Update
12/04/2013

So I have used this on multiple rides and even when I am not on a bike.  It is perfect for winter riding and just keeping your face and neck warm on those ole so cold days.  The fit is indeed perfect.  I can get a great fit with hair on my head and even if my head is bald.
You can also easily pull the mouth part below your jawline if the heat gets a little too much.

The only issue I can find, and I really have to make it a issue. Is that it is not an great fit i your wear glasses.  It because of the way it is positioned on your face it can cause your breath to raise right into my glasses and cause the glasses to fog up a bit.  Though this only really happens on days when the temperature is below 25 For so.

I would recommend this item for anyone who wants a great fitting and warming head covering.

I needed rain protection for myself and a nephew for an unexpected last minute mid-Spring hike in the Olympic National Park (one of the wettest areas in the US). I'm in the process of moving so my Gortex pants are in a storage unit. And the kid doesn't own a nice pair of rain pants.  I needed something for the both of us that was cheap, but also something breathable. I was not about to hike in plastic rain pants....that would be worse than wearing cotton on a hike! I purchased these Frogg Toggs after reading the reviews. I can now add my total support to the positive reviews. These pants were amazing! They endured an arduous 12 mile hike in near constant rain.....even a brief flurry of snow couldn't penetrate the Frogg Toggs.

When I took the pants off after the hike there was some moisture on my base layer. I think this was condensation from sweat rather than rain penetrating. The knee length zipper made it possible to put on and take off the pants over my hiking boots. the draw cord waistband kept the pants up.

The pants are made of a paper-like material and coated with the breathable waterproof membrane.  After 12 miles of hiking the pants did begin to show wear on the inner thigh where the legs rubbed against each other. Our hike was mostly on a well maintained trail so I wasn't concerned with brush tearing the pants. I would be hesitant to rely on these pants for off trail adventures...but come on, they're cheap disposable rain pants after all! I'll keep the pants because they seem to be in good condition...not sure if they will hold up for another use or not but I sure got my money's worth from the one time I did use them!

Keep in mind what these are - "paper" disposable rain pants - and you shouldn't have any issues. These are great for the price!
Clothing_Shoes_and_Jewelry.summary: For what these are they are great. Disposable rain pants. They endured an arduous 12 mile hike in near constant rain.

My first thought was WOW they are super lightweight--tennis shoes have come a LONG way (or maybe just compared to the Target-brand tennis shoes he had before.) The pediped were also very light...so the test came in putting them on. And, as I mostly expected, the pediped won out easily...the elastic pre-laced laces of the Stride Rite just did not easily accommodate my son's thick foot. I probably could have stretched and pried and fought...but who wants to do that? So, they get three stars because I liked how they looked and I would have definitely kept them if they had fit.

This is a flimsy poorly cast cheap plastic mask with a stretchy band on it.. Not impressed unfortunately. Worst purchase I've ever made on Amazon.

MUCH too small.  I am 5'8" and slender (135 pounds).  Also - my legs are not especially long - most of my height is in my long torso. These didn't even get to within 6" of my crotch--not even worth trying to stretch with that much of a deficit - I would have shredded them trying.  Chose to return before I did any damage.  Also, the color on the website looks kind of pale green, which is what I wanted and expected.  These are bright Kelly Green.  Would be good for St. Patrick's Day for a much shorter person.  The sparkle is pretty.  I saw that other reviews commented they were small but some said they fit just fine.  I took a chance.  Thankfully Amazon makes it easy to return!

This item is a joke. I tried to gauge the sizing based on other reviews, and I ordered the x-small because I'm 5'3" 116lbs. The product I received looked as though it was used previously. Any way, I wanted to give it a try. When I tried it on, it looked like I had on a toddlers outfit. It was a little tight, but it was really short. The outfit even has boob padding (I guess to add a little extra cleavage in that area) but since the fit was so weird, it was closer to my neck. The material was flimsy too. Long story short, this was the worst purchase ever.

Had me so happy in this chain but unfortunately this is very ugly! I. This chain should be of stainless steel, and the butterflies of onyx but unfortunately it was not stainless steel and no Onyx!, I would say that it is here to brass ! Will they want to return again!

I love the design of these shoes. They were to small so I had to send them back for a larger size. When I got the new ones I noticed right away the inside of the shoes are not glued in they in fact slid right out. Not sure if it's a design flaw or ment to be replaced with more supportive ones. The back also rubs your heal. Not a great deal after all and I may still send them back for a full refund.
Clothing_Shoes_and_Jewelry.summary: I love the design of these shoes

Clothing_Shoes_and_Jewelry.reviewText: I'm a teacher and on my feet for 10-12hrs per day. I got these shoes as I had heard good things about Naturalizers and they had good reviews. At first they were comfy but after wearing them for a few days my feet really hurt (I bought expensive insoles and it helped but not a ton). After wearing them for 2 weeks (in the classroom only) the sole starting to come off! I am returning them for a refund. Don't waste your time or money.
Clothing_Shoes_and_Jewelry.summary: I got these shoes as I had heard good things about Naturalizers and they had good reviews

Clothing_Shoes_and_Jewelry.reviewText:
I was expecting the shoe as pictured and it is not what i received.  It my have been fault the color said grey but i was thinking the base of the shoe was grey with the multi colors throughout instead the what i received was an all grey shoe with the mulit color swirls only at the ankle.  I did not care for it and will return.
The fit however was great i ordered an 1/2 size larger.

I ordered the Birkibuc sandals because the straps are vegan leather. Unfortunately, the sole is lined in real leather, so it's pretty much pointless to buy the fake leather ones (at the same price, especially). Not really sure what Birkenstock was thinking, and the description really needs to be updated to reflect this. Sending these back, huge bummer.

This did not work for me at all. If you are a curvier girl (I am 36 bust, 28 waist, 41 hips), you will probably have trouble getting this over your hips, as there is no stretch. The way the V shaped waistline was sewn made me look very pouchy and frumpy in front, even though my stomach is pretty flat. I think this was due in part to the fact that I couldn't pull it down all the way. It looks lovely on other reviewers, but sadly it is not made for my build.

Second time wearing this watch, it broke after a swim. Stating on the back cover of the watch. 30m water resistant. I was no more than 5 feet in the pool. A couple hours later I had realized it stopped working. I am very disappointed to say the least. Especially since I have passed the allowed return time frame
Clothing_Shoes_and_Jewelry.summary: I am very disappointed to say the least

Clothing_Shoes_and_Jewelry.reviewText:
These boots are well made, BUT, you would need the help of Houdini to get your feet into them..  I have narrow feet so I was surprised that I couldn't get one on --I was exhausted trying for over 15 minutes.  I gave up.  There is obviously some type of defect.  I wished I had read the reviews prior to purchasing, but as a huge fan of Keen products, I assumed I would love them.
Lessoned learned.  Will be returning.

This bag is cute, but it sticks out too far from your waist to be worn as a waist pack. It needs a narrower profile.  It is unfortunate because it could be very useful.  There are 3 layers of pockets, which make this too deep when worn as a waist pack.
Clothing_Shoes_and_Jewelry.summary: It is unfortunate because it could be very useful. There are 3 layers of pockets

Clothing_Shoes_and_Jewelry.reviewText: The shoes were cute but needed a size bigger.  I called about exchanging them for the next size, which was no problem, but the price had increased from $27.79 to $51.00 and I was told that instead of an even exchange I would have to pay the new price for the bigger size.  I would have liked to have known this before the purchase.  So I returned the shoes and did not reorder.  Plus I had to pay return shipping. From now on I will only order shoes from a site that has free return shipping.

I bought this exact pair a few months ago and it was perfect. I ordered another pair last week, and they were 4 sizes too small. How in the bleep does this happen? The material also seems thinner and cheap. I miss the days of American made and quality. I'm lost for words at how disappointed and disgusted I am with most products today, and this reinforces it.

Since I love the CowCow skater dresses, with their heavy, stretchy, comfy jersey like fabric, wide variety of attractive prints, and great fit, when I saw that CowCow had maxi dresses available, I thought I would give the maxis a try, and ordered three of them.  Delivery took six weeks, not later than promised but still longer to wait than previous CowCow orders, probably shipping from China and not from U.S.  When the three dresses arrived, this one was the first I tried on.  It was a total disappointment and an absolute waste of money.  The buttons hook into a little elastic loop instead of a buttonhole, and the bust is so tight, and the elastic stretches so much, that the two sides of the dress are an inch apart in front.  I didn't measure, but there is no doubt in my mind that the bust measures a lot less than the advertised 50 inches.  The fabric is a light, sheer chiffon that has no stretch to it.  If it fit, I would need a slip under it so as not to show my underclothes.  I used to think CowCow was one of the few brands that got it right when it comes to size, and I could trust their dresses to fit my big boned frame.  Not any more!
Clothing_Shoes_and_Jewelry.summary: Way Too Small, Way Too Sheer, Zero Stars

Clothing_Shoes_and_Jewelry.reviewText: When I received my purchase I was very happy and excited to wear it. When I put it on it was itchy so I decided to wash it and then when I took it out of the washer  the liner on the hood was ripped. On the sweater there is no tag to tell you how to care for the sweater so I was not expecting this to happen. So now I wasted my money on something that I didn't even get to wear!!! Not to mention it took some time for me to get my item!
Clothing_Shoes_and_Jewelry.summary: very disappointed and upset with purchase!

Clothing_Shoes_and_Jewelry.reviewText:
Worst shoes I have ever owned in my life. They are not even close to waterproof. They RUINED my feet. All I can wear now is sandals until my feet heal. The seams were all busted out in less than 2 months.
Awful, awful, awful shoes. Will never buy Columbia footwear ever again.

I COLLECT DRAGONS. SO I WAS VERY HAPPY TO SEE THAT SOMEONE CREATED THE PERFECT DRAGON EARRINGS. I ORDERED THEM. WHEN THEY ARRIVE I WAS COMPLETELY HAPPY. THEY WERE BEAUTIFUL. BUT THEY ARE NOT EARRINGS AND THE POSTS ARE TOO THICK AND THEY EASILY BROKE. I WOULD NOT ORDER THESE AGAIN.

SINCERELY

DISAPPOINTED (NJ)

These shoes are made to wear without laces. How is that possible? Oh, the tongue is sort of welded and melded to the sides of the shoe with some metal clip thingy. Very clever!! But VERY UNCOMFORTABLE if your foot is a little taller/thicker than most. Oddly, the right shoe fit ok. The left shoe hurt like it was locked in a vice grip.

I am 5'5", 150 lbs, and I have tried a lot of shapewear.  I thought this would be great because it's strapless and it's a compression garment, meaning it helps you maintain a natural figure while keeping you sucked in.  Boy was I wrong!  I ordered the proper size according to the chart and tried it on immediately after I arrived (and let me stress although it is "easy up", it is NOT easy down!).

It has two strips of cheap plastic boning in the sides that dig into your rib cage and create weird bumps when you sit down.  Other than that it's not particularly uncomfortable.  It's a nice length too, but it's made of thick material that would be extremely unpleasant in the summer.  On top of all that, it really does nothing to slim you down - it's way too elastic.  If you're looking for shapewear in the form of a compression garment I suggest Kimaro... it's not strapless, and it could be longer, but it's WAY better than this piece of garbage!

There is ZERO support in the bust area.  The pic makes it look like there is a lil sumthin supportive up top.  Wrong.  There is nothing but cheap, thin bathing suit material.  The neck strap isn't adjustable and is way too long.  The shirring ends up looking weird because the material is so thin.  A Wal-Mart bathing suit would put this one to shame.
Clothing_Shoes_and_Jewelry.summary: should have listened to other reviewers

Clothing_Shoes_and_Jewelry.reviewText: Ive worn 501s for 30 years now every pair fits differently and the material has gotten real thin used to be STF was stiff and would take many washes to even lossen up not any more Bye Buy Levi's Take your fake denim overseas for suckers who never new real Levi's

This is the first time that I have ever been disappointed with this brand, and it worries me. Lowbrow/BlackMarket Art has been my favorite t shirt,as well as art print brand for years now. My wife and I own several t shirts and art prints from this brand. I'm completely thrown off by this t shirt. The printing is see through, and the shirt itself fits awkward. What is going on Lowbrow/BlackMarket? I hope this is not a sign of things to come

Easily the ugliest, most unflattering pair of pants/leggings I've ever owned.

I would rather walk around in my underwear than wear these in public. The material is thin and clingy, creating a glorious look at every wrinkjle, crevice, and bump from your hips to your thighs.

Looking for pants that will accentuate your cameltoe, cellulite, and panty line? You've found the right choice.

This item has a wrong size description. Medium size is saying that fits children 8 to 10 years old in the amazon web page. This is a mistake. When I received the product, Medium size is saying that fits only from 5 to 7 years old. It doesn't fit to my daughter and she will not have a custome for her birthday. This was really furstating...

Of all the Saucony's I have bought, this is the most poorly made.  The sides are gappy and not stuctured well, the 8 1/2 women's was way too short, so that my toes touched the tip of the shoe, and the inside was not comfortable.  Definitely want to return these.  Please send me a return label and have the seller contact me.
Thank you.

Janet
Clothing_Shoes_and_Jewelry.summary: and the inside was not comfortable. Definitely want to return these

Clothing_Shoes_and_Jewelry.reviewText: Had to exchange them because they were too small for my normal size.  Got the next .5 size up and they fine. However, they killed my feet!!! I tried to break them in for a couple weeks but they never got better. So I had to get a refund. Too bad, they were really cute :(
Clothing_Shoes_and_Jewelry.summary: 5 size up and they fine. However

Clothing_Shoes_and_Jewelry.reviewText:
Though it looks sturdy its a fairly thin shell. The wheels are very loud and not smooth. perhaps this would be fine on dirt but not great in the airport. Straps are too long and can't be snugged up for flight unless the bag is full.
Update! The zipper broke already! Now its gone from two lousy stars to one star. It would zero if I could.

I love the shorts. Would wear them to work in everyday as I intended to, but as a shorter guy (5'8") the "9" inseam" leg is way too long. Now, I measured the inseam, and it is actually 10", which is NOT what is advertised, and that extra inch makes all the difference to me in comfort: below or AT the knees... the crotch is 10" long! These are made for tall people, so if you like shorts at or above the knee, and you're under 5'9" LOOK ELSEWHERE. Tall guys: enjoy these shorts.

These are very comfortable shoes and New Balance comes in widths, which is great for me. They are the only brand athletic shoe or trail shoe I've found that truly fit. However, the materials these are made of are not of the usual durable quality I expect from New Balance. These began to show unusual signs of wear on the sides of the toe box of each foot after only 2 months, and the suede split holes on the insides of the ball of each fit where the big toe joint meets the foot. I expect to get a year or more of wear from a shoe in this price point, and am very disappointed with the lack of quality of the materials.

I was under the impreasion that it was a pkg of different colors, i recieved it and it was only one. I could have baught 6 of them for this price... was very upset paying 7 dollars for one headband. Wont be ordering like this again. But the ONE i got was pretty.

This is third pair of platform pumps I've returned.  They have all just been a little too large in the heel.  Not worth keeping them, and falling flat on my face with every step I take.  I tried all the inserts and heel grips.  It didn't do the job.  For your reference, I am a 6 1/2. I even went down to a 6, and they were too tight.  I finally found another pair at the department store I could try on. I wouldn't order this shoe on -line without trying it on first.

As of today, I've only worn these shoes for 4 work days so far. The shoes are very nice looking compared to others on the market.  However, like most new steel toe shoes, they are very uncomfortable in the toe and top of the foot area which makes for a long day.  I have only found one steel toe shoe that is comfortable from the first day I tried them on and they have been discontinued by the manufacturer.
Clothing_Shoes_and_Jewelry.summary: The shoes are very nice looking compared to others on the market

Clothing_Shoes_and_Jewelry.reviewText: I invested in these boots because they are waterproof, and I expected them to last for years. Also because I loved that they were gray, and would look good with most anything. Within about 2 months (wearing only a handful of times in light rain), the gray rubber started to turn dark green. The green looks awful against the gray/teal top. What's worse, is that they started to leak after just about 1.5 years of light use - I literally only wear them when it's raining, or one week a year while camping. I splurged on these boots, hoping that it was a worthy investment, but have been very disappointed. They're also rather heavy, and difficult to get off - especially when my feet get wet from the leakiness.
Clothing_Shoes_and_Jewelry.summary: The gray turns green within weeks, and they leak!

Clothing_Shoes_and_Jewelry.reviewText: Very nice print I think this is a one size fits all. Fits me nicely... The fabric is a little tooo shiney for my taste but it is still a pretty skirt for a very good price.....but the zipper has come undone on me  various times and I haven't even worn it out yet.

One shoe fitted perfectly the other one was tight and the shape of the shoe that was tight looked misshaped.
I've never had that problem with any shoes that I have ever bought.
They are cute but at the end of the day one foot has become swollen because has been tight all day long.  The other foot with the ok fit shoe never swells. This never happens with any other pair of shoe I wear daily.
Clothing_Shoes_and_Jewelry.summary: One shoe fitted perfectly the other one was tight and ...

Clothing_Shoes_and_Jewelry.reviewText: this item lookslike a nice pair of sun glass but when i recerive it, it was very small and made with cheap hard plastic. do not let the picture of these glass mislead you. they are made to fit a very small face, like a child face. i return them. thank you amazon for excellent customer services.

When the product was shipped and received everything was separated, the plastic covering around the band was pealing off.  I do not think the watch is authentic, there was no plastic protecting the face of the watch when received.  I was very unsatisfied because this was a gift.  I do not see myself ordering another one from this site.

I've had two of these. I really like the heat/no heat feature. The noise complaints on other reviews are correct though it never bothered me since we leave it in the garage. My issue is the timer. The first one lasted about 9 months and I thought maybe it was just 1 bad part so purchased another to replace it. Same exact part broke on second one after maybe 6 months. I won't buy another! The plastic gears in the timer mechanism break and the dryer won't turn on. Save your money and buy a better quality machine!!
Clothing_Shoes_and_Jewelry.summary: I really like the heat/no heat feature

Clothing_Shoes_and_Jewelry.reviewText:
Great Team!  No Division I team has won more football games than the MICHIGAN WOLVERINES!

Lousy Service by the Manufacturer!  How rotten is Fossil customer service?  Amazon does not allow enough characters here for me to begin to get into it.

Clothing_Shoes_and_Jewelry.reviewText: Pants look fine except that the waist is too tight. I ordered the same size but in a different color and they fit perfect and still do after a few washings. These pants are just too tight to be a comfortable fit and will have to send them back for a replacement or credit.
Clothing_Shoes_and_Jewelry.summary: Pants look fine except that the waist is too tight

Clothing_Shoes_and_Jewelry.reviewText: It's a beautiful concept, but poor quality fabric makes it unwearable. The fit is okay, a little tight in the hips but stretchy so it would've worked. I am 36/28/40 and got a medium. You definitely can't wear any underwear or bra with this and the thin fabric in the "solid" areas makes it impossible to wear in public. Had the manufacturers kept the double lining on more than just the chest area it might have been okay, but thin single lining everywhere else makes it too see through. Probably best as a night gown instead.
Clothing_Shoes_and_Jewelry.summary: If only the fabric was a little bit thicker

Clothing_Shoes_and_Jewelry.reviewText:
I am very disappointed in these pants...they may have the Russell Athletic label, but the quality is very low!  The Russell Athletic brand has been around for a long time, and has a reputation for high quality products.  I have previously purchased the same Russell closed bottom pant at a local sporting goods store (seven years ago)---this old pair of pants still has better elastic, thicker fabric and a better fit.  Who were they making these pants for?  Certainly not, for a normal size large.  And I will not purchase these online again.

P. Sunderland
Clothing_Shoes_and_Jewelry.summary: Russell Athletic Pants--Not just large----extremely large

Clothing_Shoes_and_Jewelry.reviewText: The calf is wide as it is suppose to be which is awesome!! However, the width of the actual shoe part is incredibly narrow which is ignorant considering someone with wide calfs probably doesn't have a really skinny foot! The boot is beautiful though and looks exactly as the picture. I would love it if the actual shoe part didn't feel like it was suffocating my feet!
Clothing_Shoes_and_Jewelry.summary: ... wide as it is suppose to be which is awesome!! However

Clothing_Shoes_and_Jewelry.reviewText:
I decided to return it as soon as I tried it on. I had read reviews that said that it had a 'pointy' 'madonna boob' shape, and I thought that it would be fine as long as it was 'filled out properly' but I was wrong! It really had a grandma shape to the cups, that point slightly down in an unflattering way. I also felt like there was not enough fabric/ coverage on the inner part of the breast, it was not like it was a plunging style design for low tops, because of the under layer, but there was something lacking in the support of that part of the breast.
I have ordered another Anita nursing bra, this time hopefully it will have a better cup shape and coverage.
Clothing_Shoes_and_Jewelry.summary: Returning it due to 'madonna' boob look :(

Clothing_Shoes_and_Jewelry.reviewText: I have been an avid reef lover for the last decade. When I saw these I was so excited because they looked really cute but they had gotten mixed reviews. I am sad to say that when I got these the moment I put them on my feet I knew I had to send them back. The straps were an uncomfortable leather feel that was sure to give me blisters between my toes. However the bigger problem was that the straps didn't form over the top of my foot. They didn't even touch! So this is a no go!

This is cute, but one size fits "most", it's not. The skirt is large. The waist is elastic and stretches a lot, but when completely relaxed isn't that small. If you have a 22" waist, it's probably too big. This skirt could easily be L-XXL. I have an ottoman that's 40" around and this skirt fits around it with no problem. On the other hand the top is tiny and I can't even put it on. The top would fit a skinny 12 year old. The skirt fits an ottoman lol. I do wear the skirt though and it is cute. My waist is 31". It's very short, doesn't cover your butt. Bedroom only.
Clothing_Shoes_and_Jewelry.summary: skirt is too large, top is too small. Skirt is cute if it fits you.

Clothing_Shoes_and_Jewelry.reviewText:
I am dissatisfied with this product. The costume comes in many pieces,but it comes with no instructions on how to put it on.
Many pieces of the costume are very thin and not high quality material. Many of the pieces of the costume are not color accurate to the movies they're based on; for example, this costume comes with dark brown pants even though the movie costume has a more light tan color pants. the costume comes with a vest instead of a movie accurate long sleeve shirt, so your arms are visible under the robes. The worst part about this costume is the whole costume is held together by a Velcro belt. There are pieces of clothing that go over your shoulder, but they are always falling off because there is nothing keeping it on your body. Your costume always feels like it's going to fall off. It's very frustrating. This product is not worth the asking price, and I would not recommend it.
Clothing_Shoes_and_Jewelry.summary: This costume is not very good

Clothing_Shoes_and_Jewelry.reviewText:
I read all of these amazing reviews about this bra, and being someone with large breasts, I thought this was my saving grace. The shipping was decent, the fit was amazing.

Until the wire came right through. Not even after my second wear did it rip. Both wires came up the top of the bra and through the fabric. And I couldn't even return it! I was furious. But, it being a new bra, I just decided to attempt to sew it up, thinking it must have just had some loose or weak threads. I made multiple layers of thread and made sure it was super tight. Thinking everything was fine, I put the bra on. An hour later, the wire just found a new hole and went through the fabric once again.

I am so disappointed and will never buy one of their bras again. Also, freya's return policies were very unhelpful.

I bought these slipper boots and they are so big they slip around when you walk and you end up walking on the outer edge of the sole.  I tried to tie some of the excess material together on top of my foot so they would stay on better.  No luck.  I went to WalMart bought a pair of boot slippers for $14.00 and they are great.  They are more comfortable, stay on and cost a third of what these cost.  Never will buy this brand again.
Clothing_Shoes_and_Jewelry.summary: They are hard to keep on.

Clothing_Shoes_and_Jewelry.reviewText:
Although this shirt is described as "Cotton Blend Women cut T-shirt" and the photo indicates it would be a Women cut T-shirt (slender toward the waist) it is just a plain old t-shirt.  As a matter of fact it is a little larger than one would expect in the waist as it flairs out more than it cuts in.
Overall it is of average quality cotton t-shirt.  I wouldn't buy it again though.

I choice 5.5 big girls, but it is 37.5 in european size, i will wait my daughter grown, it feel very hard, i am not sure if is real reebok, the color is different, not pink, it's pink phosphorescent, looks nice but it can't use for the moment, I don't know if is confortable or no.

But overall  probably won't ever be wearing these again:(
