Sports_and_Outdoors.reviewText: I've been using this for the past 5 months and have beyond enjoyed it. It became my go to water bottle immediately after purchasing it. Love the size.  It's large enough to carry a good amount for hikes and still for into a cup holder. Its material is lightweight and leak proof. One thing I'd like to note is that the inside of the bottle collects a film- like layer after a few days. Would recommend cleaning it every few days if consistently used.

If you have been looking for a good hat that was comfortable and cool then look no more.
I used this hat this summer for fishing, canoeing, golfing and bike riding. This hat performed. No sun on my neck and my head stayed cool.
If this hat wasn't good enough during my adventures it got dirty so I tossed it in the washer and it cleaned up like new.
By the way the hat does repel bugs even after washing it.
On top of everything else the hat folds up and fits it your pocket. Very cool.
Good hat. Well worth the money.

I'm an ultra-distance runner and I like to track my runs with an app on my phone. I also use the phone for listening to audiobooks or music while on 10-30 hour runs.  On supported races, I prefer not to wear a backpack, but I still need some place to put my phone.  In the past, I've tucked the phone into my compression shorts, but it tends to fall out slowly, need constant adjusting, etc.  I hate armband phone holders that always end up sitting in my elbow and bouncing around.

So I decided to try the Running Buddy.  IT'S PERFECT.  It snaps into place easily and doesn't bounce at all.  It just sits there, holding my phone, doing exactly what I need.  GPS works great, my tracking app works great, and my phone is right there (I did text my crew a couple times to let them know I was coming in - so it was nice to be able to grab the phone out, use it, and tuck it back in - takes a few seconds only).  I used the Running Buddy during a 50-mile race during a massive rain storm (8" of rain during the race) with near freezing (sub-40 degree temps the whole time, with lots of mud and river crossings.  Phone was perfectly well protected in the water resistant pouch, and I never had to think about it.

The caveat, however, is that you do need to tie the string in your shorts.  If you don't tie it well, you will feel your shorts slipping because of the weight - I use a Samsung S5, in an otterbox case (so... quite heavy already!), and the RunningBuddy itself isn't super light, so the combination does require tying that string nicely.  Normally I don't tie the string at all, so that is something to note.  You don't need to make the shorts tight, you just need them tight enough not to fall down, but I did use a "shoe lace double knot the bows" (whatever you call that) knot to keep the knot from coming undone.

Since there's two pockets on the inside and I knew I'd want to take the phone out from time to time, I put my ID and some cash in the smaller pocket, and the phone in the outer.  I love it and it's going to be on all my runs from now on!
Sports_and_Outdoors.summary: Perfect for ultra-marathons and training, if you like to have your phone on you (for Strava/Runkeeper/etc)

Sports_and_Outdoors.reviewText: I was surprised by the generous size of this microfiber towel so it works as a body wraparound as well.  My daughter used it after teaching her Aqua Zumba class and it quickly wicked up the water from her body after class.  Because it absorbs so much water, it is a good idea to wring out the extra moisture before hanging it up to dry.  The towel also has an elastic wrap so it is easy to roll up and take along without having to refold it.  The storage bag is a nice bonus to easily tuck into the car to dry off from an unexpected rain shower. I would highly recommend this product.

Precor recently dropped their prices on their entry-level ellipticals, so I took the plunge and purchased one (my first elliptical). Of course, their entry-level ellipticals are still more expensive than the top of the line models from most other manufacturers, so it was with some trepidation that I ordered it from Amazon (how do you repack and ship out a 200 pound elliptical if you decide to return it?) Anyway, I'm pleased to say that the Precor was everything I hoped for.

Assembly was straightforward, but you definitely want some help to get it out of the 7 foot box and to put it together (having a dolly was a lifesaver since I had to turn the damn thing around when I found out it was facing the wrong direction). There are no wheels, so you are basically lifting and moving extremely heavy pieces. Precor includes all the tools you'll need, and all the parts fit very nicely together (which is a major major plus if you've ever dealt with the maddening experience of building Ikea furniture).

The elliptical itself is sturdy and exudes quality. The motion is extremely smooth - with my eyes closed it would be hard to tell the difference from the club-quality Precors. Where you really come to realize how this is Precor's budget line is in the feature set. You have to program all your info (weight, etc) each time you start. There are only a few programs built-in (if you crave a lot of variety, you'll need to pony up the extra bucks for the 5.25 or higher). The incline adjustment is manual and can't be adjusted on the fly. And as one previous reviewer noted, the power switch is in the most inconvenient location near the bottom of the machine, at the rear.

However, if you know all these issues up front and just want a high-quality machine to get a great workout, this is definitely the model for you. Note: you can save about $400 and get the 5.21 if you don't need the moving arms.

I love this camping pocket knife for all the great things it can do. It's Victorinox name means quality. I can saw wood, cut things ( 2 blades), open cans, open bottles, cut moleskin with scissors and more. I opted for the cork screw over the Phillips screwdriver because when a great bottle of wine is made available you should be prepared to open it and share with others. TSA won't get this one from me
!
Sports_and_Outdoors.summary: A great all around pocket knife

Sports_and_Outdoors.reviewText: This lantern is super coolwhen I received it, I actually couldn't find the lantern part. I unscrewed the bottom part where you put the batteries, and I asked my kids if they put the lantern attachment somewhere else. So I played around with it, and Voila! When you pull the metal handle bars in the upright position it pulls right up, and then it goes right back down for storage. Had I looked at the pictures on the box I probably would've figured it out faster. It is so cute and tiny, but gives off a great powerful light. They say its waterproof so I believe them and I guess will test that out on my next camping trip. Although I am not excited for our next power outage, I am excited about keeping this right next to my bed just in case. It is small enough to fit in the corner of your night table or even in one of your drawers. I took pictures of it closed, half way open and then all the way open to show you how cool this is. It's like magic. The battery compartment is sealed on the bottom. Definitely would recommend this lantern.
Sports_and_Outdoors.summary: Adorable compact lantern with great light!

Sports_and_Outdoors.reviewText: This little unit cooked my can of soup in under 3 min. I am very happy with it. It looks nice in is well made. Everything fits right and is simple to use. The igniter works very well. The plastic carrying case is rather cheaply made and cracks right away but I will fix it the good old American way, duct tape. Functionally I don't think you will be able to find any better, not to mention the excellent price. I also ordered their fuel. Can't say enough, thanks
Sports_and_Outdoors.summary: As tony the tiger would say "THEIR GREAT"!!!!!

Sports_and_Outdoors.reviewText: Bought this case over 3 years ago, have traveled with it at least once a month (I work in the golf industry), and it's been a champ. Such a great case. Finally, one of the wheels gave way. I'm not sure how it happened, I picked it up at the baggage claim this way. Anyway, I reached out to SKB to see if I could buy a new wheel. Frankly, I expected either no response or expected them to say I needed a new case, like most retailers. Instead, they shipped me a new wheel with instructions on how to put it on. Looks easy. No cost to me even though I'm probably out of warranty. I couldn't be more impressed. I'll be an SKB customer for life.

I bought this to carry in my day pack when I go on vacation.  You never know when you might catch the sunset on a beach or find a fun band playing music in the park.  This is perfect to have when you are on the go, it's lightweight and compact and totally easy to fold back up.  This little gem will be going on many adventures.

This Premium Solar Camping Shower Bag is amazing!!  This is such a great idea!!!  This Camp shower bag is made of very heavy duty PVC plastic waterproof material that holds an amazing amount of water five gallons!!!!  This is very easy to fill with the very large filling valve and easily hangs from the very durable handle.  This Solar camping shower bag has an amazing easy to use on/off shower nozzle head that turns easily while showering.  This solar bag also has a water temperature gauge that lets you know how warm your water is and lets you know if it is ready to use.  This also has a nice front pocket that you can place items in such as shampoo or soap.  This camping solar shower folds up nice and small when not in use and is easy to travel with.  This is such a great idea for camping or boating when you do not have showering facilities easily accessible.  We like to use this while boating when we are not at a marina for a nice quick shower.  I would highly recommend this!  I did buy this at a reduced price for an honest review, but would highly recommend!
Sports_and_Outdoors.summary: GREAT solar camping shower for camping or even while boating!

Sports_and_Outdoors.reviewText: This is a great bottle. I've used the first one I got for 3 years now, put it through hundreds of miles on my bike and backpack, and it still doesn't leak a single drop, even with the JetValve "open". Through no fault of the product itself, the mouthpiece of mine did get moldy when I left it unclean for a while. All the pieces (there's about 5 pieces to the jetvalve) come apart easily and were easy to clean. The best part is it still works as good as new!

This is a weird concept.  But it does melt inches.  Well, half-inches anyway.

I have 2 of these, a small and a medium.  They actually fit true to size, even though there are reviews of people complaining they're tight.  If you're a size 4 or below, order the small.

If you're a size 6 - 8, order the medium.

If you don't know what to order, don't panic - even if they're too big, they'll still do their job.  I know because:
1. I asked the company,
2. One of mine is too big and still does it's job and
3.  I've lost a bunch of weight with these and the 17 Day Diet and now both pair are too big but still work.

They do smell when you first receive them.  Wash them once and it's gone, not a big deal.  In terms of reviewers saying that these are noisy, I think they mean, if your legs rub together.  A good fabric softener should help, but these are basically a scuba fabric, so you'll expect a bit of noise now and then.

You will get hot just from wearing them.  Even on a chilly day.  So even if you're just wearing them while you do laundry, they're doing their job.  If you wear them for exercise, they work even better.  Hope this helps!

This pack is amazingly inexpensive, extremely light and has many great features that I have only seen on packs costing 3 times as much.  The straps can be cinched up tight, there are great keepers to prevent them dangling in the way.  The pocket on the back is a great place to carry some snacks - I can reach them without taking the pack off by simply unbuckling the waist belt, grabbing the top handle and pulling the pack up.  The bungee cord is a great way to strap in a super light rain jacket or other item - also accessible just like the back pocket.  I have recommended this pack to other runners (and cyclists), and everyone loves it.

Cons?  Obviously, no one wants to carry the extra weight, but dehydration can be your worst enemy during and after a long run. Also, it does not have an external fill port, so you have to open it up to refill it - not an issue for me or my friends, since we don't stop for refills anyhow.
Sports_and_Outdoors.summary: Far better than my Camelback packs

Sports_and_Outdoors.reviewText: After using so many different brands of water bottles, this seems to be the winner for our household. My kid was a biter so a few of the other brands she chewed teeth marks into the plastic spouts deeming unsafe to use. This one is silicone and soft so it's not as easy to damage with those sharp little teeth. It's a little more work to take everything apart and wash. Just saw there's a special brush you can purchase to clean the inside. The exterior of the bottle itself will eventually scratch with drops and toddler abuse but it's still quite sturdy and good quality. My almost 1 year old just started sipping from this too and found it easier than actual sippy cups because she didn't have to lift the bottle up.
Sports_and_Outdoors.summary: Sturdy and good quality water bottle for toddlers

Sports_and_Outdoors.reviewText: My husband and son decided to go winter camping but needed a tent large enough to hold their -40F sleeping bags. They used much sturdier spikes as the ground was frozen, but the tent went up quickly and worked really well. They had enough space inside once their sleeping bags were opened up that they were able to store their gear. It seems to be really well made and I know it will come in handy for many other trips.

Bought this boat about a month ago. I would take this boat anywhere creeks, rivers, and any lake. I did install a custom wood floor I'm a big guy and I like to stand up so after doing so I could.  Don't get scared by the other reviews for the money this thing is worth it. I've take it out about 10 times in lakes and creeks with stumps protruding out of and just under the water. No fear not tares no leaked boat is awesome.

I love how protective the Pelican cases are.  We have a number of them in different colors and they are durable and protect cameras from the damp environment on our sailboat.

This is a much larger case than we normally get but it is much more adaptable and can be set up for multiple purposes. We tried it with multiple variations of cameras and lenses.

In the end, we were able to put a 4 x 5 field camera, two light meters, two lenses, and several film holders in this case.  This is all safely packed and easy to move around.  I love how adjustable the Pelican cases are.

Usually I roll my eyes at made in China -esque knives on amazon as I look for name brand like Benchmade and CRKT and get disappointed in their steep prices. Nothing against these companies, theyve built a reputation for reliable and great knives, its only fair they charge more for it. But while I have my higher end knives for field use, I needed something smaller and more discrete/reasonable to have at work that wouldnt break the bank. To me it seems pointless to drop near $100 on a smaller knife that just won't see the level of abuse the manufacturer guarantees it can handle. So this time I didn't ignore the amazon blue light specials and I have to say Im pretty happy for it.

In the last year or so the made in china knife industry has really overhauled their quality output, and this Kubey is no exception. Other than the ponderous name (unisex) its a very serious little knife. What I love is for a $20ish option it only says Kubey and D2, no made in China. It doesnt have assisted opening but depressing the flipper will immediately spring the blade out and locked. Lockup feels amazing, despite being a liner lock. Aesthetics are actually pretty decent, simple slim profile with sufficient texture for grip. The blade is decently thick and out of the box was sharp enough to shave arm hair. For my purposes, it outperforms at work.

This is a knife that if stamped CRKT or SOG or Benchmade, people would want to know the model name to buy one. As it is, Ive just found a new source for great edged presents for friends/family, and will not overlook the cheap amazon listings again. If there was a way to incorporate the auto axis design that other next gen made in china knives have copied (Ganzos) I would happily pay x2 the price for this one.

I first purchased this hat for my boyfriend.
He loves it..Really well made and attractive. Seems very warm and comfortable.
I ended up getting one myself in the brown-peach color and I am really looking forward to wearing it. (It has not been cold enough yet)
I have lots of hats, but I have a feeling this winter my new sheepskin hat will be a favorite!
I need to mention also that the customer service of this company was very responsive and accommodating.

I've used this product exclusively on my firearm.  It does everything as advertised!

I started by 'seasoning' the new firearm three times with the paste.  First step was to clean all the grease used to preserve a newly manufactured gun.  After that, heated the firearm, applied the paste with a small brush, let the firearm cool and then wiped clean with the included microfiber towel.  Repeat.  Love the blackened look this product leaves on the slide and other parts.

Now after shooting, I field strip the gun and wipe down with the 'Pre-Saturated EZ-Cloth'.  This quickly cleans any gun powder while leaving behind a nice coating.  For the barrel I add some SEAL1 liquid to a brass brush and run it through the barrel a few times and then follow up with some patches lubed with the liquid.  Next I add a bit of 'extra' liquid to the high friction surfaces (rails).  Reassemble and wipe down.  I'm left with a perfectly functioning and perfect looking firearm.

Smells great.  Even the wifey doesn't object.

Good stuff.  After 10 yrs of having the same net it was time for a new one.  My old one finally caught its last baits when I snagged a rock.
First toss w the 10 foot 3/8 inch heavy net --50 ballyhoo! Opened up beautifully.  1.5 pounds is good and heavy.  But it opens up very easily and I was throwing into the wind.  The mesh is nice and thin and takes up very little area on my boat.
Sports_and_Outdoors.summary: Good stuff. After 10 yrs of having the same ...

Sports_and_Outdoors.reviewText:
I can't believe I used bleach and iodine pills for so long! I waited a while for the best price on the Sawyer Mini, but the truth is the price doesn't fluctuate that much and it's well worth the price.

I ended up with a pink filter due to lowest price, which I'm not wild about, but it -does- make it easier to find in my pack and when I'm backpacking with a group of friends I never end up in the argument about whose blue filter is whose.

The filter works so smoothly I don't think the back flushing syringe is a necessary bring along unless you're going to be out for a long time in a place with particularly scummy water. In most instances using a smart water bottle with the tapered drinking nozzle works in place of the syringe and saves you a little bit of weight. That being said, it's nice to have something to thoroughly clean the system when you get home.

Also make sure you get -all- of the water out of it before it gets anywhere approaching freezing. If you're going backpacking in the winter/cold temps it's not a bad idea to tuck your sawyer filter in your sleeping bag with you, as the filter freezing is the easiest way to bust one.

I particularly recommend setting this filter up as an inline system, especially for anyone annoyed with slow flow rates.
Sports_and_Outdoors.summary: Awesome filter. Don't buy any more water treatment pills!

Sports_and_Outdoors.reviewText: I love this knife. Everything about it. I carry it as my EDC(every day carry) because of its capabilities. Perfect blade size(legal carry size in most states), perfect color(even though when you receive it, it not exactly the color it looks on the computer, but i love it anyways), and the blade comes hella sharp when you get it. Just a matter of keeping it sharp. BUY TODAY!

I could write a lengthy review but it really just comes down to one thing,  "nothing feels like a Precor".  The motion follows the natural movement of your foot perfectly and your heel never comes off the foot pedal.  It's the only piece of cardio I have ever used where the work is primarily felt in the glute muscle, a really tough muscle to work.

I research major purchases for up to a year, and tried virtually every elliptical made.  I can't understand why you would buy anything else.  If it is not smooth and comfortable, I am not going to use it.  Finally, not sure how you would top the warrantee.  10 year parts including wear and tear?  That would be like a car manufacturer giving you new tires if you wore them out before the warrantee was up.  I have never had to use the warrantee but am glad I have it.

Very well thought out product.  The case is good quality, it's organized really well, and it seems to have everything you need and none of what you don't.  With the exception of a pretty serious injury, you should be good to go with this kit.  I took it backpacking, and it made me feel a lot more comfortable than some of the other seriously lacking kits that seem to be so prevalent in local stores.  With the MOLLE-style attachments on the back, it secured easily to some webbing on the outside of my pack.  It was readily available if needed, but I didn't even notice that it was there while hiking.  I even had enough room to add some extra things I thought I could need (super glue, meds, and mole skin).  When not on the trail, I keep it in my truck, and I actually had to break it out the other day.  Nothing too serious, but definitely more than a simple bandaid was going to handle.  I was glad I had it with me.  I highly recommend this kit.
Sports_and_Outdoors.summary: The case is good quality, it's organized really well

Sports_and_Outdoors.reviewText: Great knee pad, but not what I need.  I admit, I have particular needs as a circus performer that works primarily in post-industrial sites (lots of gravel, concrete, etc).  I was looking for something that was low profile, could be worn for a long time without chafing, and would provide superior knee protection (I have suffered several knee injuries).  It succeeds in being relatively low profile for the amount of protection it gives me, but the fit isn't perfect enough to prevent chafing over long term use. Definitely not worth the money!! It is basically one of those crappy inflatable mattress with foam pad stuck in the middle. The craftsmanship is terrible with seams that are cheap and won't last. After playing the first time, one of the pieces broke trying to get it apart to put away.  We were very dissapointed in the quality of this produc.  You really do get what you pay for!

Sports_and_Outdoors.reviewText: Tires have great roll and traction but it's at a massive lack of longevity.  I put 100 miles on one tire before the sidewall failed and caused a blowout.  Within the next 50 miles, the second has developed the exact same distention of the sidewall that the first had before it's blowout. Sports_and_Outdoors.reviewText:
The foam in this strap is hard and pretty hard.  As a result, the strap does not conform to the body in a carrying position.

There is a crinkling sound when the strap is flexed; the sound is not pleasant, giving one the feeling that one is in the presence of truly cheap materials and workmanship.

The strap can be attached at the bottom by winding the strapping around the bottom ring on the bag (if such a ring is still present and has not been tossed with the old strap), and weaving it back to the sliding buckle. IMO another fastener on the bottom strap, similar to the fastener on the top, is called for.
Sports_and_Outdoors.summary: The foam in this strap is hard and pretty hard. As a result

Sports_and_Outdoors.reviewText: This chair is sturdy! With a nice wide seat! I did sit in it one time briefly before having to put it out in the sun to air out the smell. The bag and chair smell heavily of a mulch scent. The smell is very strong and undesirable. It came poorly packaged, it came with the shipping sticker taped to the chair bag. It had no box or protection of any kind. The chair bag is ripped and unusable due to this poor packaging!

This is better sounding than it actually is in action. On a tile floor, every ball will bounce off the cups, roll to the baseboards and keep rolling until they rest under or behind he only immovable objects in the room. On short napped carpet they are better controlled. They do carom and it is possible to hit one ball into a cup with the cue ball.

The problems begin when you miss a shot to the side or by hitting it too far. The cups only have access on part of one side. This modeling of the holes to be like the corner pockets on a pool table makes this more frustrating than fun. Those misses have to be re-hit to get them to the front of the cup which may, geometrically, take more than one shot.

Unless you have a very large, empty, carpeted room, the game as designed is unplayable. When a nine year old and a ten year old are bored in under ten minutes you know you don't have a winner. I was bored before they were. Who play tested a mock-up of this before actually developing it for market? Disappointing.

I bought this system about a year and a half ago. I was excited at the prospect of not having to scoop because I had always had a regular box.
Initially, the system worked ok. The rake frequently got stuck and many times, there ended up being a bunch of litter underneath the box that captures the waste.
I was also not happy about the smell level and did not find that this system did a very good job at smell control. I was changing the bag up to 3-4 times a week.
One other problem was the amount of litter that got stuck behind the rake.
I tried taking it apart multiple times and cleaning it out but continued to have problems.
It was difficult for me to justify throwing out an expensive piece of equipment so I kept hoping it would get better.
Then about a month ago, the motor burnt out. The motor kept running but the rake would not go. Again, I cleaned it out and replaced everything but that did nothing.
Finally, I ended up throwing it away as it was not functional anymore.
I briefly went back to a regular box but now I am the proud owner of the Scoopfree automatic litter system.
My fingers are crossed and I am still cautiously optimistic but this system is already 1000% better than the Purrforma.
No odor, easy to put together, better functioning (rake goes both ways), and just overall a better product.
I suggest to anyone having an issue with their Purrforma to check into this other system.

Bought this at christmas for my daughter who is a runner. The headphones lasted less than a month. I was completely disappointed in the cheap flimsy plastic the products are made with. I think the app was free anyway, so you're paying a lot of money for some Mickey-Mouse headphones and a chest strap.  Also, the chest strap doesn't fit super thin/small framed folks very well.  My daughter said the app itself is pretty cool, so we'll give it an extra star for that.

Not more than two weeks after receiving and using this treadmill the control panel malfunctions and now no longer displays anything other than a lit up blank screen. Also in trying to follow their self-fix guide, I found that one of the bolts securing the motor cover is faulty and will just rotate in place and not actually come off...this made things difficult but was still able to get to the motor compartment.

The only good thing is that customer support responds to you each business day but I don't know if they actually read the correspondences thoroughly since I had to re-provide information I already put down previously...and that they somehow sent parts to the wrong address...so it's been about a month now since I opened the warranty case and now I am told their parts are in back order after the failed delivery...which means another month of waiting or more and then probably more waiting to get their recommended technician out to fix after parts are delivered.

So suffice to say, if you want a treadmill that you can just start using and not worry about problems in the first month of purchase, this is likely not for you. And if there are already problems not a month into use, I can't wait to find out how much worse it's going to get while I still have warranty, let alone when warranty actually runs out.

Now aside from the above, this treadmill is actually pretty sturdy...moving up the stairs was no easy feat since the "easy fold" mechanism causes the bottom bars to automatically fold down when you lift the treadmill...and it's quite a heavy treadmill. Assembly was very easy and as others have stated the start-up beep is quite loud and piercing and there seems to be no way to turn this down since the volume rate resets after you end a session....

Bought the watch yesterday, and its going back to Sports Authority today. I've had a Puma heart rate monitor for 2 years, and wanted one with a calorie counter and a little more features. Never had these problems with the Puma.

The touch feature is a great concept...However, it is very annoying and cumbersome to use as it will say "Touch" on the screen for 10 seconds, and then afterwards it will take another 20 seconds to recognize if you are using a HR belt or not. So every time you accidentally touch your watch, you will lose 30 seconds of accurate data measurement. I have heard some people say sweat also sets this feature off, but I did not use it long enough to verify this.

The instruction manual is not logical, and I'm an engineer who has written consumer manuals. Took me a good amount of time to figure out how the watch functions, but I eventually got there.

I wanted to wear the watch to work all day today, and see my average heart rate and calorie consumption, but I just keep getting crazy readings. 220+ bpms, which sends the calorie consumption through the roof and just sets everything off. I bought the watch for that purpose, and if I can't get accurate data its useless to me. Yes, I am looking for exact measurements otherwise I would just use a calculator...

I gave it 2 stars only because I think the features and capabilities of this watch are good, its just that they don't work right.
Sports_and_Outdoors.summary: Not for anyone interested in accurate measurements

Sports_and_Outdoors.reviewText:
I purchased two of these as I walk and hike outside often. The temperatures in Klein/Spring Texas, where I live, have been hotter than I've ever felt them, with day upon day of 100 degrees F air temperatures. I had first used some kind of "cooling cloth" which just used evaporative cooling via water, but that didn't help at all. I then researched the reviews for cold-pack cooling neck wraps and I decided on these. In 100 to 105 degrees F temperatures, the item helps a little, but not enough. I guess it would work if one considered the 80s to 95 degrees F temperature range to be "hot," but, if it's hotter, then this item doesn't really have enough of a cooling effect. Also, at least in the temperatures in which I walk and hike, the cold pack strip starts to thaw and it turns into a collection of liquid in about under an hour. In addition, I have to tighten the neck wrap so much, so that the wrap is flush with my skin, that it feels like I'm choking -- if the wrap is not tight then it doesn't work very well.

So, minus one star for melting/thawing in under an hour and minus one star for not having a great enough cooling effect and minus half a star for having to tighten the item so much.

I'd still recommend this item, but if you're in 100+ degrees F temperatures, then I suggest you invest in an actively cooled cooling vest, or, maybe a space suit :P

UPDATE : The cold-packs that slip into the neck wrap are now leaking in two places. I'm going to have to look for a better quality product. With all the problems, I do not recommend that anyone buy this item.
Sports_and_Outdoors.summary: At least it takes the edge off...

Sports_and_Outdoors.reviewText:
I was very excited to buy this water bottle. The idea is great and the company seems to be socially conscious. After using my bottle for a couple of weeks,  I called the company to complain about the frequency of it leaking. They said that it must be defective and quickly shipped me a replacement.  I was thrilled with their customer service and very appreciative of their willingness to accommodate me.  Unfortunately, the second bottle had the same flaws as the first.  There are just too many moving parts and if any one of them is not aligned perfectly, the bottle will leak. Also, the ring that moves to allow you to fill the bottle doesn't snap firmly into place and can easily be moved into a position that allows water to pour out. I NEVER felt comfortable throwing it in a bag and it became onerous having to constantly be aware of the placement of my water bottle. I don't use it anymore and have resorted to using the BRITA squeeze bottle, which is less of a pleasant drinking experience but keeps my bag, car, lap, and office dry.

The filtered water tasted great.  I hope they are able to tweak the design to make this bottle more useful. I'm rooting for them.

Tricot pockets? WTH. Tricot is revolting anyway, but really awful with dry skin on hands. I couldn't bear putting my hands in the pockets. I was incredibly bummed out b/c this is overall a brilliant jacket. I had to return.

My older model which needed replacing was very water resistant, windproof and extremely warm in temps down to 20s because of that. Plus it made a great inner coat when temps dropped to singles and below. Bc of the tricot pockets I didn't get to try this newer model in cold weather.

If you want a cheap work cup or something then go for it. If you want something to keep your beverage warm or cold for a few hours, this isn't the cup you were looking for.

Sports_and_Outdoors.reviewText: I would recommend going to a local sporting goods store that has a variety of stands before buying this one.  I lift downstairs in a carpeted basement that my grandkids have access to and I worried about the stability of this stand.  In the store, I used this as well as the U-125 stand and there was no comparison as this column stand would tip with the powerblocks on it.  Active kids could get hurt with this stand and that's why I went with the U-125 stand I now have downstairs.  I asked the manager if there were any sales on Powerblock stands and she was very gracious in giving a 10% discount.  With tax, the U-125 stand cost $191 and change, not a lot more than this column stand.

So I was looking for a extremely low profile red dot that also had recessed glass. This looked like it fit the bill perfectly.  Unfortunately, it does not. While it is very sturdy, and the glass is well protected, the back end of the sight covers a good portion of the glass. You only actually use the upper 2/3rds of the glass. That was very disappointing for me.

Other points:
The windage/elevation screws don't click. You could see this as a good thing, since it allows very fine tune adjustments. However it makes me strongly doubt this sights ability to hold a zero as I was able to turn the screws nearly effortlessly.

The red dot is indeed 3 moa outdoors. It is plenty bright for outdoors use, even on lower settings. Unfortunately this means it doesn't have any settings for indoor use that aren't too bright. You will get a starburst effect even on lowest setting in any kind of indoor environment.

It is very well waterproofed. There is a rubber mat separating the base from the sight, providing a excellent waterproof seal.

UPDATE: The Sight does not hold zero at all. I can turn the adjustment screws with my fingernail with 0 resistance.
Sports_and_Outdoors.summary: Not as Low Profile as the Pictures let on.

This product promised a great deal of fun during the snowy months. However, it was not meant to be.
I purchased it in October but did not get a chance to put it together for at least another month. Once I set it up, I had a hard time getting the break component working. I contacted Tacx but no response except an automated email saying not to send too many emails or they will tag my emails as junk mail! I waited for my son, who is more tech savvy than me, to try and set it up during the christmas holidays. But he could not get it working either. Still no response from Tacx.
I finally contacted Amazon and the company I bought the item from. Bike-a-mile. They were wonderful and have great costumer service. They responded quickly and tried to help me set it up. They suggested that there maybe a wire loose and with pictures showed me how to connect it. Once I did and plugged it in, I heard and saw a puff of smoke. Bike-a-mile people quickly sent me another break motor module and I replaced it. It worked for a short period but kept heating up and shutting down at speeds over 30mph. For the price, this is a decent bike.
I bought it (in white) for my 9yr old daughter. It is her first "big kid's" bike.
The white with pink accented decals fits the "girl" style fine.. though I don't know why the listing says "boys".
The drop-style top tube allows for easy on and off.

I'd give it 5 starts except..
The brakes and shifters needed to be reinstalled to work properly. Shifters were upside down on wrong ends of the bar. That force brake levers way too far down to work with smaller hands.

Be prepared to take this bike to a shop and have a once over before you put your kid on it and find out the hard way that some things may not be in tune.. And that may not be cheap.

Also.. this is a 24" wheel bike.. By definition it is designed for smaller bodies. Why Mongoose puts a full reach handle bar stem on this.. and a full size grownup's-butt seat on it.. is beyond me. This forces a smaller person to have to reach WAY out to get hands in position and its an uncomfortable (and unsafe) position to ride in.. more akin to a track bike or a triathletes lower "aero" position.

A full size adult might fit the seat to handlebar distance.. but a full size adult would go to a 26" wheel (or larger) frame.

Mongoose is not the only company that makes this mistake.. Have seen it on many mid to low end bikes.
Simply not thought thru well enough. And yet the answers so simple.

So I swapped the handle bar stem for a much shorter reach one I had in my spare parts box and I reversed the seat clamp mount.
That shortened the overall reach by about 6"(1) and now my 9yr old rides comfortably and safely.

Summary. Great kids bike in terms of build and components in terms of price.. but will need considerable work to work safely and properly, and that balances out any price savings.
Sports_and_Outdoors.summary: Handlebar reach is too far for a smaller person

Sports_and_Outdoors.reviewText:
I've been using this rack for about a month, and so far have pretty mixed feelings. I like the narrow design of the rack, as I just want something to clip on to and don't need a lot of surface area in the back. Riding a bike without mounting points on top, I needed something that would hook behind the brake like this as well.

I do have mounting points above my rear axle, but the rack instructions online recommended just mounting through the rear axle of the wheel so I initially did that. However, this puts the rack dangerously close to the tire. The nuts securing the flat metal piece on top were maybe a centimeter or less from the tire. Wheel sizes are standard, so I'm a little confused as to why they would design this rack to sit so close to the tire, as other reviews here have mentioned. Granted, it shouldn't budge while moving, but it's still pretty scary. Over the course of using the rack with a ~15 lb bag every day, the rack sort of 'settled down' another few mm (because remember, the bottom mounting points are on this extension, meaning they can 'roll back' causing the rack to drop down). Now I had maybe 4mm of clearance from the nut to the tire, which left me super uncomfortable.

I recently remounted the rack to use my rear-fork eyelets instead of the wheel axle, which propped everything up 2-3 inches and now I have ample room. I did have to force the rack to fit into that mounting point, as it is a little narrower than using the axle mount, but it seems secure and I don't think will cause future problems. This also caused me to adjust the flat metal piece that secures to the brake, and this introduced yet another problem. This metal piece slides right underneath the top of the rack (down the middle of the spine, so to speak). Well, I had to slide the piece back a bit more than I had before so it went up to the first metal cross piece (maybe 'ladder rung' makes more sense, if looking down at the rack?). My bag could no longer clip on, because the clip was blocked by the metal piece and I didn't have enough length on the rack to shift over a segment. I then had to push that metal piece back so I had enough room for a clip.

I'm going to continue using the rack, as once you have it set up it works great, but there could be some serious design improvement here. If they want to advertise mounting to the rear axle, this rack should be 2 inches taller than it is. Also, the metal bar on top shouldn't inhibit from clipping in. Either set it lower down, make it narrower, make it shorter, etc. but it vastly reduces the amount of clippable real-estate you have on the rack.
Sports_and_Outdoors.summary: and so far have pretty mixed feelings

Sports_and_Outdoors.reviewText: As the title says, on of the bags came and there was paint on the inside from a broken ball. Other 3 are okay. Paint looks cheap but it's fine for the price. It seems a lot harder than the field paint I use. Shipping was outstanding! Ordered it at 11:30 on Thursday and got here on Saturday. If looking for target practice paint, this is the stuff for you.

It's not the easiest thing to put on correctly but is reasonably attractive. My biggest complaint is that it's only mostly waterproof.  It'll keep your bike dry in a light rain, but anything heavy or sustained seeps through (and then get trapped and not dry off).  I'm satisfied with it as a temporary solution, but am looking for something heavier as an upgrade.

I bought 2 of these bags online and unfortunately you can't tell by a picture how something is really going to look.  I was surprised that the wheel design and placement for a bag that is made to handle 3 bowling balls was extremely lacking.  The wheels are very small, placed close together and the bag is constantly falling over to one side or the other as you're pulling it behind you, no matter the type of surface you're on.

I have a bad back and carrying the bag using the handles isn't an option I can use every time I am transporting my bowling equipment to and from the alley, hence the need for wheels and ones that do not flip to one side or the other causing strain on my back.

I really like the separate bags for shoes and other small items that are removable and the extra side zippered pocket.
Sports_and_Outdoors.summary: It's OK, but could be so much better

Sports_and_Outdoors.reviewText: They are decent muck bags, but I'm disappointed that it was imported.  It seems hit or miss with Rothco.  I've gotten items from their brand that were American made, these were not.  They are made decent, but I would not put anything too heavy into them because unlike the bags these are based upon, the handle do not wrap around the bag, they are sewn into one of the side seems.  Also, as others have mentioned the external side pockets are not one long pocket.  They are broken up into 3 so don't expect to be able to put an armorer's wrench or saw blades in those.  I just look at them as reinforced side areas because they are actually kind of useless.  If the bag is packed up, the pockets unsnap and are pretty limited as to what you can put into them due to their size and location.  Being untreated cotton, the first thing you should do is treated with a water repellent.  I spray the top and side of mine with Kiwi waterproofing spray and then coat the bottom with Snow Seal by heating it with a hair dryer then quickly rubbing it down with the compound.  Make sure to let it set up/soak in for about a 2+ days before use.
Sports_and_Outdoors.summary: An OK bag for mucking around and light tools or car camping supplies.

Sports_and_Outdoors.reviewText:
My intention for buying this product was to use these with an older pair of Oakley sunglasses as a temporary replacement from buying another new pair of snow goggles. I would strongly recommend NOT doing this since you could suffer serious injuries if you don't know what you're doing or if you break your glasses...

I got the product on time (within a couple of business days) but I'm still a bit skeptical about using them on my oakleys'. Oakley glasses/sun are a bit different than the rest of the glass world by making their side pieces go straight back instead of your typical curve down behind the ears. Furthermore, the sun glasses I have don't have thick rubbers where they would hold on to your head above the ears. I did try them on and pulled the chums off and with relative ease they came off. That said, I'm still going to give them a try (since I could care less if I loose/break this pair) but I wouldn't use them with my more expensive Oakleys. If they work, I definitely plan on using them when we go out boating in the summer!

The adjustment piece is great but as another reviewer noted, they don't fasten too close to give you a tight fit around the head. Instead the tightest fit (for me) still had 2-3 inches of slack behind my head.

I definitely still plan on giving them a try with my Oakleys when we hit up the mountains this weekend (snowmobiling and snowboarding).

Recommendation: To be updated later but for now yes I would recommend since its a lot cheaper than buying a new pair!

I own six different styles of Gransfors axes and hatchet's.  Up until now, I have been overly pleased and completely happy with their tools.  This hatchet however appears to have been made by an apprentice, as it is no where near the quality of my other Gransfors. The metal seems to have been shaped before it was ready...many large pits and rough finish.  I suppose it will serve as an adiquate tool, but many of mine are displayed.  This one will unfortunitely end up in the tool box.

Works fine but not much brighter than my light that is rated at 2000 LM.  Thought the step switch wouldn't be that big a deal but my other lights turn back on to my last used level and I miss that. Seems to be pretty sturdy ad I have taken a couple of MTB spills and it still works and doesn't seem worse for wear. Battery life is comparable to my other lights about 2.5 hours on high. Best thing about this light is price. Less than half the cost of what my other lights cost.

I purchased a 20 ounce one and 16 ounce one in the same order. But I had to ask replacements for the 16-oz bottle two times before I started using it. I read so many reviews before the purchase and this one seems to have a sort of insulation problem sometimes. In all three of the bottles I bought, there is a fault inside the bottle ( especially at the welding line of the bottom and the cylindirical wall). So having read the reviews, I thought this fault might be the problem. I insisted on this brand because this is the only one claiming very openly that it does not contain any leaching chemicals or agents. In the end, I gave up replacing and wanted to give the third one a try. ( There is no fault inside the 20 oz bottle by the way)

Yes, it insulates for the stated periods of time.

Yes, the loop cap  is for insulation and there is no spilling or leaking.

No, the mug lid is not not spill-proof; the label on it specifies that very clearly.

No, the mug lid is not for insulation but for making it easier to drink your hot beverage from the wide mouth bottle. You should be using it only when you are actively drinking from the bottle. If you will use this only for cold drinks, you won't need it.

Unfortunately, there is a terrible petrolium-like smell in the loop cap, especially when you are using it with hot beverages. But it persists with a cold drink as well. I used a warmer to hotter water when cleaning it for the first time and kept it waiting for several hours. And yes, there was this awfully chemical smell with the lid. The first time I used the bottle, I had room temperature water just to see if there would be any smell interfering. Yes, the loop lid gives out a strong smell which makes me reluctant to use it.
Sports_and_Outdoors.summary: The bottle is fine but the loop lid gives out a strong chemical taste and smell.

Sports_and_Outdoors.reviewText: I'm new to regular swimming and this is my first cap (since I was a kid). It gets 5 stars for looks. My hair is wet after I'm done swimming, so this cap does leak. (I've since learned the trick of wetting your hair in the shower before swimming, so your hair doesn't absorb as much pool water.) It hurt my ears two ways. One is that after I've swum for awhile, my ears hurt where they touch the cap, as if it's rubbing on them. Also, twice the next day after swimming, I've noticed crusty skin on my ears where they touch the cap, like an allergic reaction.
Sports_and_Outdoors.summary: Looks pretty, leaks a little, hurts my ears

Sports_and_Outdoors.reviewText: I purchased this saddle right before I started training for a IM70.3 to replace my stock saddle on a Cannondale Slice.  In a couple of reviews from other websites I noted comments that stated these saddles break down faster than most, "if you purchase a new one compare it to your old and you'll see".  With that in mind I purchased this saddle and was very happy with the upgrade.  In the last weeks or month of my training I noticed tightness in my hamstrings coming off the bike (on the run) as well as pain in my lower back after 2.5 - 3 hour rides.  My last serious ride left my upper abductors feeling like I beat them and my hamstrings really tight and sore. I estimate this saddle probably lasted me about 3 months, maybe 90 hours usage, before I should have replaced it.

Unless you are lucky enough to have this stock fit your Mosin perfectly without any alteration.... its not really worth the money......about 2 hours worth of sanding and material removal and the Mosin finally dropped in without a problem. Then I had an issue with the magazine not wanting to feed. Took me a while to figure out what I needed to do to fix that problem but finally got it done! Its not a bad quality stock at all....just the fitting issue is not something I wanted to deal with. I knew what the possibilities were when I ordered it but I was in high hopes I would not have to mess with it. But to say the least it looks good. Id buy this stock again....only if it was $30.

I race sailboats actively on San Francisco Bay, and travel around the country and the world for racing when I can.  I've been through a lot of watches.  Until recently, there were not many sailing specific watches.  The Sunto was too expensive, and the old Ronstan was laughably large, though iconic.  It was great to see so many new introductions this past winter (eg. Ronstan, Freestyle, Gill)  What I've never figured out is why none of the great sailing companies can make a sport specific sailing watch that is even nearly as good as a Timex Ironman.  This new Ronstan is a case in point.

The good.  First, the display is fantastic.  Big numbers centered on the face, with the bonus of still being able to see the time of day at the bottom.  Second, the race timer is top-notch with its ease of use and the great sync feature which allows easy correction of a missed start signal by letting you easily with one button reset a missed 5 minute gun at the 4 minute horn.  That is the most important feature.

The bad.  Nothing is intuitive.  For example, the "Set" button doesn't set the time - it just sets the alarm.  To set the time you hold "Sync", and then press it again to advance the numbers.  Even using the watch every week, I still need don't remember how to switch from race timer mode to clock mode (hold "mode" and then press "sync"). Forget about switching from 5 minute countdown standard race mode to 10 minute match race mode, or adjusting the 3rd user programmable race mode. I have to keep a copy of the watch's instructions in my gear bag.  Compare - I don't even know if an Ironman comes with instructions.  It is perfectly intuitive.

The worst.  The band.  Great on the outside of a spray top for dingy sailing.  Against skin it is definitely not comfortable.  That's forgivable, not all watches can be comfortable for all people.  What is truly awful is that you can't replace the band.  I'm sure someone had a good reason for this design, but all I can say is try it on before you buy it.

I got this Ronstan as a holiday gift, and I'll keep trying it this season, but right now I'm expecting it won't make the cut.  For me, I really like The Band on my Ironman. http://smile.amazon.com/Chums-Band-20mm-Watch/dp/B001AQTKEA/ref=sr_1_2?ie=UTF8&qid=1402092850&sr=8-2&keywords=the+band+watch+band
Sports_and_Outdoors.summary: Maybe the best among a poor set of options

Sports_and_Outdoors.reviewText:
It seems like it will be sturdy.

The bolts have square necks near the head and all the holes are round. Thus, it requires two tools to tighten the nuts and the heads of the bolts protrude slightly. That's not the safest, but since I know about it and am the only one who uses it it should be OK.

Left and right is not clearly labeled on the base pieces so it took a couple tries to assemble (50-50 shot failed), but it was quick to assemble so no big deal.

It is tall. I am 5' 10" and had to adjust a ceiling tile in my drop ceiling in the basement to allow full arm extension.
Sports_and_Outdoors.summary: Sturdy- should it have square holes punched on some connections?

Sports_and_Outdoors.reviewText: The spring they use to keep the lid up is a terrible design. It naturally kinks and then no longer works at all.  I now have to use a dowel and that is a poor fix.  Its also at best a four day cooler and the walls are no thicker than my five day cooler.  Ultimate extreme?  I wonder how long the ice will last in one of their 3-day coolers?
Sports_and_Outdoors.summary: Another poor Chinese design that doesn't meet their claims

Sports_and_Outdoors.reviewText: Within 5 minutes of putting it on my belt I sliced my trigger finger on one of the metal clips.  Not a good way to build confidence.  The quality of the metal clips are definitely lacking and you should check for burrs and sharp edges and address with a file before using.  I wore if for a few days and it is comfortable but does require pants with some extra room in the waist.  The leather backing also pushes into the kydex opening making it more difficult to re-holster.  Holds the gun securely and works well to conceal the pistol.  I decided to give it a try and ordered the optional kydex clips which look and feel much better than the metal.  I would recommend ordering them from the start.

PROS:

- Intense workout

- Stores in a small space (I live in NYC)

- Kinda fun when you get the hang of it

- Easier on my knees than running

- Different and pretty fun

CONS:

- Hard to balance at first (could be dangerous for some)

- Surface not slippery enough out of the box

- User needs reasonable ice skating experience

(hockey skating is best)

- No illustrations in directions to show you best usage

- Slightly overpriced

As the directions suggest as an option, I sprayed some furniture polish on the plastic surface so I could slide better. And then I realized why they don't have a marketing partnership with Pledge... it gets DAMN slippery! They probably have a few lawsuits on hand (I almost fell once). I found without the furniture polish, it wasn't very fun and it really didn't work.

Make sure you WEAR SNEAKERS under your booties. Even if you have small feet that probably means you need the small booties (did I just type the word booties?). Wearing sneakers improves your balance and protects your feet from the contact with the end bumpers.

My girlfriend, who was at one point a serious figure skater, had a lot of trouble with it in the first 5 minutes. I had a much easier time because I use hockey skates and this is very similar in motion.

So, this is a pretty good item but I think you could make the same thing at home with some linoleum and a 2 X 4. the booties are just cheap nylon. Doing it yourself would probably cost under $20 as opposed to well over $100.  It's definitely not a rip-off but in my opinion it should retail under $100.

If you can't ice skate, DO NOT buy this.  If you haver poor balance DO NOT buy this.  Also, I would not recommend this item for older folks who may get hurt if falling down.

Overall, this is a nice departure from the normal exercise routine and I'm getting a great workout in my NYC apartment while having a little fun. If you get it, try holding hand weights while using it.  That makes for an even more intense workout.

There were no reviews when I purchased so I hope this helps you!
Sports_and_Outdoors.summary: Intense Workout With A Few Small Catches

Sports_and_Outdoors.reviewText: Decent entry level range-finder.  You'll struggle at low light to see the display so you just need to pick reference points during the daylight and remember you distances.  Don't plan to range a deer with it near dark.  Also it doesn't always seem to find the distance immediately and often have to try several times.  Also sometimes I'll get a different distance twice in a row from the same spot (within a yard or two).  But it works for what I need it to do, and as long as you aren't hoping to get the best you can buy, you won't be too disappointed.  As stated before, I pick my spots, range them and then put it away and wait for the deer to show up.
Sports_and_Outdoors.summary: Decent value, not great but it does the job

Sports_and_Outdoors.reviewText:
I bought this watch 7 weeks ago and have been using it extensively in outdoors 10k runs and in gym activities (spinning & weightlifting).  I wore the HRM strap throughout.

* Setup instructions were quite clear and the initial setup was smooth.

* Coming from the Polar camp (S625X) I had some doubts if the HRM strap would be comfortable. It is.

* The watch looks nice, and it's not too thick.

* The display is good, except one flaw: most athletes are interested in the % of the max HR, not in the bpm. Yet the display shows large bpm digits and small % of the max HR, and there is no function to reverse the order (large %, small bpm).

* PC link: tried it once and it worked OK.

* Charging works well, but be careful with the special USB cord  if it gets damaged, you may not be able to get a new one (see below).

* Water resistance: sweat and very light rain seem to cause no damage.

* GPS function: cold start on a clear, sunny day on the beach, outside temperature 14C (57F)  lock in about 90 seconds. This is OK, somewhat below average (comparing to other GPS watches). GPS accuracy: consistent 1.5% error (1000m are measured by the watch as 985m). Acceptable.

* HRM function: signal is lost quite a bit. I double-checked HRM is On, pairing completed successfully, strap battery is fresh, watch fully charged  and yet the signal sometimes is lost, for minutes (or more) at a time. Unacceptable.

* Calorie counting: starts at rest (60 bpm), unlike Polar which starts at 95 bpm. Polar is preferable  you want to measure the intensity of your training, not your normal breathing  Worse still, kcal/min is roughly linear relative to bpm: at 76-80% of the max HR the watch measures 8 kcal/min; at 81-85%: 9 kcal/min; at 86-90% 10 kcal/min. This is VERY different from Polar, and also from the counters in the Precor gym equipment (treadmill, cross-trainer and stationary bike)  they rise slowly in low HR and quickly at high HR, pushing you toward intensive training.

I asked Pyle about their calorie counting algorithm  they didn't bother to respond.

Other functions (compass, waypoints) - untested.

Bottom line: this is an inexpensive, somewhat inaccurate sports watch, from a non-responsive company. Yet its quite functional for the non-demanding athlete. 3 stars.
Sports_and_Outdoors.summary: An inaccurate but still quite useful sports watch for non-demanding athletes

Sports_and_Outdoors.reviewText: I ordered this jersey in an XL. The packaging of this jersey was great though overdone. The quality of the material itself is very nice. However the stitching was coming apart in the box it shipped in. There were several seams coming apart before I even put it on the dog and as he's young and active I'd be worried they'd bust right open. When I put it on to test fit it it fits snugly. My dog is 45 pounds and has a fluffy coat. It fits him but looks snug due to that. As this isn't advertised as a small dog item I fail to see how this is an extra large. It's the size of a baby onesy.

I wore the traction cleats on a trail that was predominantly packed snow and ice, but also with some rocks.  The spikes look like they've been worked over with a hammer.  Some are folded over entirely, all of them are bent.  They provided excellent traction for the first 4 to 5 miles, but then they started slipping somewhat, presumably due to the spikes getting bent out of shape.  They were fairly easy to put on, perhaps 2 minutes each, and quite easy to take off.  They stayed in position well

I am looking for stronger cleats that won't get bent out of shape so badly in mixed conditions.  I weigh just a bit over 200 pounds.
Sports_and_Outdoors.summary: The spikes look like they've been worked over with a hammer

Sports_and_Outdoors.reviewText: Nice board, but all 4 wheels do not touch the ground.  It does when you stand on it. I'm not experienced enough to know if the trucks need to be loosen or why it's off.  When we try to twist it so the right front wheel will touch the ground, then the back left wheel lifts off the ground.  I give up.
Sports_and_Outdoors.summary: Nice board, but all 4 wheels do not touch ...

Sports_and_Outdoors.reviewText:
UPDATE:  so I can't use this thing but they gave me a refund so I'm bumping the stars up.  I'd rather have a reliable inflator obviously but appreciate the effort from PRO Bike.

I really don't get the reviews here.  Maybe people haven't actually used this thing?  I had a flat and this is what I found - first off it leaks from the valve. It is is also very hard to get a good seal around a presta valve.  The valve on the inflator itself is somehow both loose and hard to use with one hand.  Lastly and most importantly, it actually froze on my presta valve and was hard to get off. Very poor design in my opinion.
Sports_and_Outdoors.summary: It is is also very hard to get a good seal around a presta valve

Sports_and_Outdoors.reviewText:
I bought these and a few other pair of Wigwam socks as my feet are always freezing and I didn't want to shell out the buck$ for SmartWool.
These socks seem like they would be incredibly warm if they were not altogether too large to be of any use.
I wear a 7.5 women's shoe and ordered Medium (as the size chart seemed to indicate) and these are flopping around on my feet like potato sacks. Giving them to my partner (size 11), hopefully he'll get some miles out of them. The other socks I ordered from Wigwam are fine.

Overall great. I'm not sure about the QC though. When I first got mine I noticed there was a bit of fraying in the seams by the knee already. Hopefully this will still last. The fit is as expected except the waist portion is a bit huge. I feel like it's going to fall off regardless of tying the strings together.

It feels great! It's thick and it seems to last long. I feel like my leg day are much easier with this, might be placebo but I definitely like it and recommend if it you don't want to shell out too much for it.

-1 for quality control
-1 star for durability due to quality control
Sports_and_Outdoors.summary: Quality control is a bit bad but overall good.

Sports_and_Outdoors.reviewText: This would be good for someone who is not very active but would like a low-impact workout to do at home.  I couldn't get my heart rate up enough to get an effective workout with this product, but I am already in decent physical shape.  I was looking for a cheaper, more space efficient alternative to a treadmill or elliptical machine.  I guess this is that, but just a little too easy for me.

my husband is in the army and has to have pens on him at all times, most pens are too fat to fit in the provided slot in the uniform, we are from oregon and so i tried these as part of his birthday gift, HE LOVES EM! They write well and slim enough to go into his uniform, we WILL be buying more!

I bought this and a more expensive one (90 bucks ish)
This one feels lighter, is dull, grip is made of rope instead of leather, stand looks less impressive, has way more "errors" in design from the original movie-sword.

It's very cheap, but it doesn't look or feel very cheap.
The value is excellent, you'll get more than what you've paid for.
But if you want something that is closer to an exact replica I recommend a more expensive one.

Magazine_Subscriptions.reviewText: For years I enjoyed reading Real Simple for it's comparison articles, life tips, and quick/easy recipes. However, recently I realized that more and more of the articles weren't really helpful or interesting. The products recommended to 'simplify' were expensive and would just add clutter to my home. The recipes weren't that tasty when I made them at home and I felt many of the recommendations were actually paid advertisements in disguise. So, I allowed my subscription to run out and browse their website once in a while.

I've subscribed to this magazine ever since it was first published. It was great the first year or 2, but seems to have lost something along the way. There are not as many manufacture coupons in my subscribed edition, however I happened to notice that in-store editions do seem to have more coupons in them. Subscribers should get the same coupons. Because of this I may not be nenewing or may even cancel my subscription if this doesn't change. The magazine does have lots of good tips on everything from fashion, make-up, food & more. The other thing I noticed is you used to be able to find better deals when subscribing to this magazine. I could not find 1 site with a lower reduced rate or where you could use a coupon code. I feel it had such a great start that now they are too full of themselves to offer those deals. There are plenty of other magazines you can purchase for half the price with almost as much information & more coupons.

I subscribed to this magazine for an interior design class I'm enrolled in--the magazine is OK, the special Art edition is not something I'd buy again and the "free tote bag" is worth as much as a free tote bag would be expected. So far, I'm not impressed and can't see renewing my subscription in the future. It did not meet my expectations--focuses on celebrity designers and their stuff.

As a teen author, I subscribe to various teen magazines just to keep my finger on the pulse of whatever is happening in teenworld. Where Teen Vogue is definitely not mainstream, like it's Mama, VOGUE, it's filled with the dream stuff rich folks wear / do / go / ascribe to. Whatever. Like reality TV in a magazine: fake, fun, paper. Discard when done.

People magazine, it seems to me, is getting its bootie kicked by US Weekly. People doesn't seem to have the "inside" hot, juicy gossip that US Weekly has. I still read People every week, but it just doesn't seem to be as "in depth" as US Weekly. And no, I do not work for US Weekly ... I'm simply a college student, who enjoys the hot gossip out of Hollywood, and US, in my opinion, quenches my thirst more so than People.

I grew up reading my dad's subscription and each issue offered insight and education into all the world's secrets. I felt like it was an educational experience shared between father and son. Now that I have a son, I thought it would be something I could share with him as well. Needless to say, sometime in the past 10 years evidently there's been a change at the magazine. I realize that you can now find an amazing amount of information on the internet, and maybe PM felt they couldn't compete, but I am very disappointed. There is no educational benefit. This is now nothing but fluff. A magazine for the "Barney Generation." Small articles about how to throw a baseball or sharpen an axe. No longer an education of the great strides being made in alternative energy or space exploration or even home construction, but rather a blurb about the endless pursuit of Eddie Van Halen changing the tone of his guitar. Do you realize Steve Vai added a 7th string to the guitar nearly 30 years ago? THAT's engineering! That is noteworthy. When my 12 months are up, I won't be renewing. I can read about EVH's company on Yahoo!... I know how to sharpen an axe. Thanks anyway PM.
Magazine_Subscriptions.summary: I felt like it was an educational experience shared between father and ...

Magazine_Subscriptions.reviewText: I used to love this magazine, but it seems like with each issue there are fewer and fewer pages, less actual content, and more ads. I just received the March 2014 issue and a big chunk of the magazine was taken up by a catalog insert for cheap-looking, plus-size polyester clothes! What does that have to do with country dcor? It makes me sad, because this used to be an excellent magazine, and the actual pages of content (not many) are excellent, but it's just not worth the money anymore.

Always loved this magazine but since Sarah Gray Miller took over as editor the quality has deteriorated.  Country Living has become very niche oriented - featuring the grungiest stuff you'd find in a rotting barn on the verge of collapse along with an unsettling fascination of all things taxidermied.  I'm only renewing my subscription after some reflection and the hope that the tide will turn and a new editor will bring this once enjoyable magazine back to its former glory.  Plus it was really cheap LOL.  Check it out at the newsstand before you subscribe.
Magazine_Subscriptions.summary: A shadow of it's former self

Magazine_Subscriptions.reviewText:
I would like the Guide much more if the program schedules started at 7:00 a.m. every day.  For me, there's
entirely too much space devoted to TV personalities..  I enjoy the "news" aspects of their lives, but can do
 without the hype.
You tend to  beat a subject to death.  We've all heard  more than enough of poor Paula Dean, Sandra
Bullock, Michael Jackson and others.  As they say in a popular tune, "You gotta know when  to fold."

I signed up for the 3 year paper subscription for $36. A 3 yr subscription for the Kindle version is $60 :(. When I called Cosmo they told me that it's up to the publisher if they want to include a digital version at no extra charge. This is not Amazon's fault people. Get it together Cosmopolitan.....when people travel we don't want to carry 3 or so magazines because they get heavy and us readers have better things to do on vacation besides lugging around an harmful of paper. Besides, if you can offer a 3 yr paper subscription so cheap, why can't you offer a digital copy for the same price? Come on Cosmopolitan, get it together.

I think at 50 I am a little too old for the target audience of this magazine.  Or maybe I am just too rural.  Either way I didn't really care for the trendy nature of it.  I am a guy who likes technology and is up on it in many forms.  I can build you a PC, repair your smart phone or tablet, and set up your wireless/wired network.  But this magazine was just not for me.

I use Amazon for most of my purchases and update my reviews if anything changes with the products. I do this so other Amazon users can get a real feel for the life of the product. You can look at my review which will be close to my purchase date and tell how the product is doing as time passes.  I am not associated with any company and all opinions are my very own.

This is a good newspaper with TONS of financial data on individual stocks.  But their recommendations are typically very reactionary and are pure momentum picks(where the stock has already appreciated substantially).  Rarely are there any sort of contrarian picks or stock that have not already moved a good percentage in price.

Also, as has been mentioned before, their editorials are so right-wing that it makes for nothing more than sensational comedy.
Magazine_Subscriptions.summary: Good Stock Newspaper but very reactionary

Magazine_Subscriptions.reviewText: I was so sad to realize how bad the advertisements had gotten. Part of the beauty of having magazine subscriptions are the relaxing moments of leisurely flipping through the pages; browsing all of informative and visually appealing pages it has to offer. Unfortunately, in comparison with it's competition, Better Homes and Gardens magazine doesn't seem to offer this anymore. I'd rather just jump onto their website. Very disappointing.

It's a dollar more than buying the paper copy at a magazine stand and 1.25 more per month than having it mailed to Canada from Analog. Update May 2012-- It appears that DELL Magazines/Amazon has listened to all the complaints and matched the U.S. price for us Canadian subscibers.  I am currently subscibing but am unhappy about the lack of abillity to bookmark a page in the current format. As soon as the nook software is available to Canadian customers I will switch my subcription to get the bookmark feature.
Magazine_Subscriptions.summary: Price has been fixed, how about bookmarks

Magazine_Subscriptions.reviewText:
As a magazine, Men's Health is an interesting read for all men, well written with simple exercises, health tips, easy but delicious recipes, and general life advice.

However.. buyer beware.  They will send you promotional items that they will automatically bill you for, unless you take the time to fill out a card and send the items back within the preview period.  They'll also give your information out to multiple promotional companies whose junk now fills out my mailbox.

I compared the March 2nd Kindle version with my print version.  Everything is there except for: "The Editor's Desk", "Perspective" (the quotes section), and the science article (I checked and there's a big chart in the print version). Each article has pictures at the beginning of it, but there definitely are images missing which are in the print version.  It's definitely convenient to have this available - I'm not sure if I'm ready to cancel my print subscription yet though. If they included the Perspectives section somehow (which is my favorite section) then I'd be more inclined to do so.
Magazine_Subscriptions.summary: Not Bad for an Electronic Version

Magazine_Subscriptions.reviewText:
I can't tell you enough how disappointed I am with my former long time favorite, Country Living. My Mom used to subscribe when I was a kid and I always looked forward to it and especially in my teens. I loved the heavy stock shiny cover and the tall format. .....and of course the contents! I have never had a year since my early 20's that I haven't had my own subscription.
A few years ago another editor made the magazine wide and floppy with a dull, cheap cover. The worst of it is that it is loaded with ugly advertisements for medicines ! Imagine looking at a beautiful kitchen on the left and to the right is an ad for Lyrica! Really!
The last few issues have been so thin I wonder why I even bother.
If you want a great Country Living switch to Country Living UK! Worth every dollar! I look forward to it so much and their ads are beautiful stoves, rugs and furniture as it should be. Just saying........

I really liked the magazine, however, it took FOREVER to start the subscription. I'm not exaggerating it took a couple months to even start. The ideas and photos were pretty, not real practical, but pretty. One thing I would suggest if you plan to subscribe is to go to the Southern Living website not only will the subscription start faster but its a lot cheaper.

The main thing I don't like about Redbook is that each month the cover story is about an actor or actress.  It's always the same type of interview - they are almost interchangeable.  We hear some some TV or movie star talk about how they are just a "normal" person, struggling to make dinner and take care of their children.  Then there's usually the part about how their spouse is the love of their life and how they balance work and marriage.  Then don't forget the part about how he or she has now FINALLY found peace and happiness in their life.  If I had a dollar for every one of these celebrity relationships that has ended, many in nasty breakups, I would be rich.  And does anyone really believe that their lives are normal?  I really, really wished Redbook would switch up their cover stories. How about covering an issue?  Or maybe just a recipe on the cover?  But, all in all I like Redbook for it's low cost and it keeps me in "the know" about fashion.
Magazine_Subscriptions.summary: Good magazine but please stop with the celebrity cover stories

Magazine_Subscriptions.reviewText:
If you like the "quick and dirty" format that is conducive to a busy lifestyle, you'll like this magazine.  As a long time runner, I have been a long time subscriber.  Many times, I read a headline on the front page only to find a paragraph or two devoted to the advertised subject.  A recent example mentioned a faster recovery from long runs.  Sounds great.  At the age of 49, I'm up for anything that helps with recovering from a 20 miler.  The "article" was a couple of paragraphs on soaking yourself in an ice bath.  It even suggested biting on a towel so you don't wake the neighbors!
If you're the type who would rather run by a fast food restaurant than cook dinner, or prefer CNN's Headline News format to their "regular" news because you don't want to be bothered with all the extraneous discussions, you'll like Runner's World.  Personally, I devour it as soon as it arrives, but I rarely find myself referring back to old issues.
Magazine_Subscriptions.summary: Fast food and headline news for the runner

Magazine_Subscriptions.reviewText: Tatler is an utterly splendid magazine.  Anyone who knows anything about Britain, magazines, and the British upper class knows that a regular perusal of Tatler is the sine qua non of a gentleman's or lady's monthly customary.  That said, this subscription is catastrophically ghastly because one does not receive the essential supplements that come with the regular magazine.  Anyone who knows anything about Tatler knows that the amazing supplements constitute about forty per cent of any subscription.
