I therefore stopped my subscription after one run and now buy my Tatler at a wonderful British shop in Grapevine, Texas which, thank God, includes the supplements along with the magazine.  Currently, I am reading a wonderful supplement on the Queen's 90th birthday.  The poor, poor subscribers via Amazon miss out on such an amazing part of the magazine.

Now that Oprah Show is officially off the air, maybe this magazine ought to be retired also. It seems to be getting old. Every issue there she is on the front cover. all airbrushed and made miraculously thin. Occasionally we get a glimpse of Mrs. Obama or Ellen with her but its usually her out there grandstanding and taking your money again so she can tell you what she knows for sure and what items she likes best. Well, after she basically came out against Christianity, I'm not sure if I care for her opinions. And, I sure can't afford most of the things she likes best. So, retire OPRAH. Come out with a OWN magazine with a new format and let's see what you got. P.S. She does usually have some good book reviews.Belloccio Airbrush Makeup Bag Airbrushing Cosmetic Bag

I love fine food and wine, but some of the recipes this past year have been way out of my league.  I have never heard of some of the ingredients they ask for, and wouldn't have a clue where to find them!  Of the ones I have tried, however, they all were very good (albeit time consuming).  I love the pictures and the articles, but I just don't have the money to keep up with the food.
Magazine_Subscriptions.summary: Great food, but not for a budget

Magazine_Subscriptions.reviewText:
Is this an interesting magazine for Christians, as well as a good information source about movies and music?

Yes.

I was exceptionally excited to see a sample subscription arrive at my doorstep, I read it feverishly. The topics they cover are interesting and cool, and the photography and design is awesome. The bands they interview are the bands I listen to--and they do a heck of a job at it! I love reading their interviews, they're extremely informative and interesting.

Is this magazine relevant to the lives of the Christian youth, of whom I am one?

No.

As I read through the magazine after my initial hopping around through the various movie reviews and artist interviews, I decided to move onto the more theological stuff, the columnists. I could not have been more disappointed. What I read was wishy-washy Christianity. They take a stand for nothing, most of the articles either being about tolerance or some other "important" issue. Their theology is far from relevant in today's youth. Even an on suicide how we should remember that we're made in God's image in the January/February issue, came across as unconvincing, and was badly edited at best.

If the editors of this magazine want to claim Relevancy, then they need to push a message other than tolerancy and "understanding". And I'm not saying these aren't bad ideas. I'm simply saying that there are more important things to be thinking about in a world falling apart at the seems.

This a good magazine for someone who wants to learn to play folk or fingerstyle music. I have tried all of the other magazines and this magazine as far as content and price are above the rest. That being said, this magazine is only a good suppliment for your guitar learning. Even if you don't desire to do anything but strum an acoustic guitar, I don't think this magazine can be your one source of literature. I would recommend that this magazine be purchased along with one of the mainstream magazines such as Guitar One or Guitar World.
Magazine_Subscriptions.summary: A Good Quality Acoustic Guitar Magazine

Magazine_Subscriptions.reviewText:
Family Circle,
I have been reading your magazine for decades and it is one of my favorites, but the September 2015 issue has gone to the dogs.
There are too many dog advertisements.  More importantly, your section on 70's retro fashion is a big FAIL.  I give it two thumbs down.
I feel that tip-toeing around the 70's is a lost opportunity.  You should have gone all out.  Get some designers who aren't "chicken".
Let's do the time warp again!
Best Regards

Believe it or not, I have well-rounded, intelligent, curious, fun children aged 11 and 15 who do NOT like this magazine. I ordered it for them based on the product description and the many glowing reviews. They've always been voracious readers but this magazine doesn't appeal to them. Why is it such a miss? I think Muse presents information in a "fun" manner but the information isn't something my kids long to tap into. They're natural learners and certainly not dullards but, at this point in their lives, are not spellbound by presentations about eccrine glands, biometrics, organ transplants and biodiversity. If your child has very adult interests, this will be great. My kids will get there someday but they're not there yet. I'm giving away the nearly untouched editions to a local charity in the hope that someone will enjoy it.
Magazine_Subscriptions.summary: Are the ratings for Muse driven by parent hype?

Magazine_Subscriptions.reviewText: Like everyone else, I think this mag used to be far better.  It is now too glossy and sales oriented, but hey that's where the money is, right?  I do like the personalized touch of regional maps (most of which are pretty useful).  It is a good mag to get you to trails if you are new to hiking.  I always appreciated that Backpacker isn't as over-the-top, Xtreme like many outdoor mags.  I have no desire to climb Everest or jump out of a plane with a snowboard.  I hope the editors will get back to basics, but, as for now, it is a good pick for people who want to get into it or for people who just like to drool over cool gear and imagine that they are into it.

It used to be much better. Something has changed in last few years. Not as clear or helpful. Other services are available which compete in specialized areas, internet helps people compare and get content other places.  Their strong support of the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau, without reforming the CFPB to benefit the consumer is a bling spot they need to address. The CFPB takes in  hundreds of millions of dollars of fines for the CFPB's own benefit, not helping the consumers harmed, but use consumers financial abuse as their whipping stick to stuff their bank account and gain more legal clout. The next time Consumers Union walks up the CFPB multi-million dollar crystal stairway they built in their offices to have a chat with Richard, perhaps they could fight for the individual consumers vs large monetary awards to payoff another quasi-government bureaucracy in Washington.
Magazine_Subscriptions.summary: It used to be much better. Something has changed in last few years

Magazine_Subscriptions.reviewText: 8 Days is more of a entertainment and lifestyle magazine that is specially tailored for Singaporeans. True, there may be gossips of the entertainment scene inside, but they are rarely as saucy as those that you can find in the US. You might want to buy it for the Fashion section which usually features trendy clothings and accessories popularized by Japanese and Koreans, who I would say are the most trendy people in Asia. Buy if you got money to spare, unless you are living in Singapore. ....
Magazine_Subscriptions.summary: Might not be of much interest to people in the US

Magazine_Subscriptions.reviewText: I've been getting it for the past 6 months and its the best magazine ever. It gives you great ideas on how to organize the house, hand make little things, use stuff around the house that you otherwise would throw away, print recepies for simple healthy and elegant meals. And the best part - they include coupons! Ladies how great is that? I absolutely recommend this magazine. I got subscriptions for my friends to this magazine as Xmas gifts and they all already got the first issue and love it!

Naval History is the single best history magazine I read. One small thing that makes this outstanding is that often those who made the history comment in the letters to the editor. This contains the work of the best history writers today and often spans the ages in its articles.  What is really special is that several times a year they commit an entire issue to one historic event.  They include fold out maps and articles from various authors.  Naval History is highly recommended.
Magazine_Subscriptions.summary: Naval History - Of the 5 others I read this is the best

Magazine_Subscriptions.reviewText:
A friend brought me a copy of Red while she visited Oxford.  I spent hours with it. This magazine is superb; the articles are well-written and engaging.  The only thing that bothered me was the references to certain products, many of which are available only in the UK, with prices listed in pounds.  (Yes, I know this is a British magazine but I was mildly annoyed.  Call me shallow.) This didn't bother me enough to make me stop reading at any time, however. After the first read, I wanted to read it all again.
About the only thing that stops me from ordering a subscription is the high price.  Perhaps when I win the Publishers' Clearing House Sweepstakes I will subscribe to Red.
Magazine_Subscriptions.summary: Once You Read It, You'll Read It Again

Magazine_Subscriptions.reviewText: I subscribe to the Weight Watchers magazine.  I love the personal stories about weight loss.  It is encouraging to me because I am trying to make "eating right" a way of life.  I try not to look at it as a diet.  I am now eating healther than I have ever eaten in my entire life and I feel great doing it.  I LOVE IT!  The recipes and coupons are excellent.  It is a wonderful magazine.  I would recommend it to everyone.

I have been reading Woman's World magazine for about 2 years and have not missed ONE.I keep all of the magazines and refer back to different articles from time to time. I have encouraged all of my friends to purchase this terrific magazine and of course they are hooked. For the price of this magazine and the wealth of information it contains, I feel like I have saved thousands and learned so much. Keep up the great job and I would recommend WW to publish books by topics such as good health, home and family,food and nutrition etc.... LOVE THIS MAGAZINE  THANKS
Magazine_Subscriptions.summary: A magazine no woman should be without

Magazine_Subscriptions.reviewText: I love birds. I love feeding them.  I have always enjoyed bird watching. I enjoy reading about birds and have always loved this magazine. I have always found it to be very interesting. I would recommend this magazine to anyone who loves birds and bird watching because it is very informative, such as giving you ideas on how to make your own bird feeders and offers tips on how to keep pests away.

The NG still has what it take to show us so many parts of the world and its goings on that most of us will never get to experience for ourselves and do it in such a wonderful way. The photos are always top notch and the information is very enriching so much so that it makes you dream of all of the exotic places they have been and wish you could be there too.
Magazine_Subscriptions.summary: Still a great magazine after all these years

Magazine_Subscriptions.reviewText:
"O" Magazine might have its quirky idiosyncrasies (like the fact the Oprah appears on every cover), but that aside, this is a phenomenal publication that I am near giddy over each month when it arrives in my mailbox.  (In fact I have to discipline myself to not buy it at the grocery store when it is there a week before I get mine!)
This is a magazine for readers, book lovers, thinkers, and people STRIVING to be more mentally and spiritually healthy/balanced.  I USUALLY (I was going to say "often", but it is more often than that) find reason to laugh out loud and also shed tears in each & every issue issue.  I love it so much personally, that I want everyone to enjoy it and find myself moved to give a subscription as a gift (which this particular 2 year subscription was).

I have been a fan of AHMM since the 1950's when I was in high school and enjoy it just as much now as I did then.  I Was so glad to see that is has become available again in this day and age.  Will continue to subscribe to it as long as it is available for me to do so.  Kudos to you Amazon for bringing this magazine back because it has been so hard to find in stores.  If you haven't read these magazines in the past I urge avid readers to give it a try, I guarantee you'll be hooked too. And finally, if you were ever a Hitchcock fan in the past this is the magazine for you.

Having said that, there is one problem with this publication.  The print is too small and I cannot enlarge the print to fit the screen on my kindle fire HD.  If I enlarge it by spreading the page with my fingers then I cannot get one page to fit on my screen.  On my kindle fire it provides an option of "page view" and "text view" and by selecting "page view" you get an entire page to the screen like a regular novel.  For that reason I am considering not subscribing to future issues.
Magazine_Subscriptions.summary: The return of this magazine is too good to be true!!!!!!

Magazine_Subscriptions.reviewText: Another reviewer refers to Allure as a "guilty pleasure".  Actually in my opinion this is not one to feel guilty about!  I might be embarassed about something like Cosmo, but Allure treats its readers as intelligent people who are interested in science and technology as well as cosmetics, et cetera.  My mom and I have been subscribing for years now... it's a classy magazine.

I just ordered a 2 year subscription, does it charge $15 every time I get a magazine? I have a gift card for $25 and spent it on this so far. I've never done this so I'm not sure. If it charges every time I get a magazine more than it's supposed to I'll have to get rid of the subscription and I don't want to because I love alternative press.

I used to read it monthly when I was much younger (in high school) but kind of lost track of it when I joined the Air Force back in 1980.  Then a couple of months ago while browsing the magazines at Books-A-Million I ran across it again and had to purchase a copy.  I sent in the subscription card about the same time I ordered my Kindle from Amazon.com.  I received my Kindle back in early January of this year and did a search for Isaac Asimov books. Imagine my surprise when I discovered that I could subscribe to Asimov's Science Fiction an have it delivered directly to my Kindle every month. I jumped at the chance and immediately started my trial subscription. When I received the bill in the mail for the print copy that I ordered, I marked it "Cancel" and stated my reason as being I was already a subscribe on my Kindle.  Now I can't wait every month to receive Asimov's Science Fiction.  I love the stories and poetry, and, unlike some other Sci-Fi magazines that print stories that aren't even remotely science fiction, they are always Sci-Fi stories and poetry.

I will be a subscriber as long as I have my Kindle, and if something were to happen to THAT there's always the print version.

I don't normally write reviews, but this is such a fantastic product I had to let everyone know.  We've had our subscription for about 4 months now.  My son got it for his first birthday and he is now 16 months.  He loves getting these "magazines".  They are high quality and actually hold up better than the board books that we have.  I run a daycare, so these get a lot of reading (some of them as often as 4-5 times each day, at least), and even the first one that we received 4 months ago is still holding up.  Many of the board books we have don't hold up that long, and all of my kids from the 1 year olds to the elementary school kids like to read them.

The writers seem to have a fantastic concept of how much text children this age enjoy.  There are animals throughout the books as well as many other concepts that little ones enjoy.  I would highly recommend this to anyone with an infant or young toddler.

Thank you for this magazine Amazon. I love it.  I have not read everything as of yet. Very resourceful and great meaning in the articles i have read. There is one article about women and her body and I decided to look at the website right away. The item I can not mention here but I looked into it and it was exactly what I needed for me since I have been having problems. I have tried other products and they just didn't work for my body. Love that web site all because of Dr OZ. Thank you Doctor OZ for the article and for helping me.
Magazine_Subscriptions.summary: I love it. I have not read everything as of ...

Magazine_Subscriptions.reviewText: I've read Mother Jones for years. It does an excellent job of analysis, and in-depth investigative reporting on news that is important to everyone. On the most recent issue is coverage of the way Big Ag is trying to outlaw the type of reporting that has exposed animal slaughter houses and helps to ensure food safety. Sunlight is the best disinfectant, but apparently Big Ag and the legislators in their pockets don't want to be bothered. These issues affect all Americans, and whatever your political stripes, why would anyone want to eat food that hasn't been in a safe and healthy manner? If issues like this are of concern to you, then by all means you should subscribe to Mother Jones. I highly recommend it!

I ordered a bunch of magazines from amazon at the same time. This magazine was the first to come of the bunch, which is appreciated.
The first delivery was also about a third of the time they told me it would be. They said about 6 weeks, and it was about 2. Fast delivery, and I got it on sale. Not to mention a great magazine. The first issue I got was great as well. +

... I highly recommend this magazine to anyone interested or immersed in the graphic design industry. I have kept every single issue and frequently refer to them for ideas, reference, or to simply get those creative juices flowing. HOW's biggest asset is their dedication to helping the reader understand the business side of the industry and the all important client relationship. HOW does not exclude anyone in that they address the different issues agencies and freelancers face when conducting business.
Magazine_Subscriptions.summary: As a subscriber for over 3 years...

Magazine_Subscriptions.reviewText:
I am glad this is available on kindle now so ppl like me living abroad can easily read anytime anywhere, Thank You.
It provides great & practical tips and techniques for overall health & healing based on ancient indian Ayurveda practices, also a great universal spiritual literature based on excerpts from great Indian Self Realized (Nirvana attained) Saint H.H. Shree Asharam ji Bapu's Spiritual Discourses.
Magazine_Subscriptions.summary: Amazing book for health & spiritual well being

Magazine_Subscriptions.reviewText: GQ is still the definitive men's style magazine, but it's also much more. The monthly mixology column is slowly helping me build a bartenders guide that is informative as well as useful, The Style Guy is keeping me from looking like an idiot, and the fiction and features are keeping me full of interesting stories to help me sing for my supper. The bottom line is this: if you want a magazine with guy advice... but don't want something as snarky or "hip" as Maxim or FHM then GQ has just the kind of class you're looking for.
Magazine_Subscriptions.summary: The men's magazine for "men of letters"....

Magazine_Subscriptions.reviewText: If you're looking mostly for affordable coastal decorating ideas, this is probably not the magazine for you. Five years ago (or more), the magazine content was different - it had fun, affordable coastal decorating ideas. If you're subscribing based on familiarity with the magazine from a while back, you may be disappointed. I gave it 5 stars because it does deliver on what it says it has - luxury coastal getaways/vacation/resort areas. I ended up canceling my subscription after about 8 issues, but it was no fault of theirs; just my incorrect assumption that the content hadn't changed.

This publication appeals to this engineer, because motorcycle reviews are detailed and objective without the hype present in magazines with advertisers.  I have been a motorcycle rider for 40 years, a retired automotive engineer and journalist / photographer.  This is my favorite cycle mag.  for current products.  The riding safety tips, health, and legal advice columns are my last read of the issue but well worth my time.

This is my second year purchasing National Geographic through Amazon. When I first ordered the subscription it took about two months to start arriving. I thrilled that I not only received the current month, but also previous months of the year, since I started getting it March. When I was sent a renewal reminder via email from Amazon, I decided to renew. This time there was no gap. I started receiving them right away. I received an offer from National Geographic and it was a few dollars more than the offer here. This is such a great magazine. I look forward to it every month.

I really like this magazine.  I just received our first copy yesterday and am looking forward to future issues.  This magazine was recommended to me through my Catholic homeschool curriculum provider as a supplement to the science lessons.  What I really appreciate about it is that there are no advertisements included in it.  I find it interesting to note that the readers of this 'zine seem to be as young as 7 or 8 and go up to age 14 or so.  So, I know that I can use it with my sons for many years to come.
Magazine_Subscriptions.summary: Nature Friend Magazine  - Great Zine for Christian Kids

Magazine_Subscriptions.reviewText: I am a professional Handyman with many thousands of service calls  and 45 years of repair experience under my belt. This is a good magazine for today's homeowner. I am saddened to see as many negative reviews for this product. This magazine covers home repair from novice to experienced . It's a print magazine so it is only fair to expect a lot of ad space dedicated to tool and product suppliers. Each issue is also filled with tips to make life a little easier . What I like is every issue has at least one idea that I haven't run across yet. You can teach an Old Dog new tricks while also reminding him about tricks he forgot. If just one article a year increases your skill set you will be money ahead. I find it humorous how often I share simple tips found here with other contractors and their amazement at simple shortcuts. In short I subscribe to this magazine because it helps me make money and leave satisfied customers.
Magazine_Subscriptions.summary: This is a good magazine for today's homeowner

Magazine_Subscriptions.reviewText: I purchased this magazine for my thirteen year old grandchild. I did not want the usual "tween" magazine who's main focus was on fashion, or  celebrities behaving badly. I read Seventeen when I was a teen,many years ago, and it has only gotten better through the years.  Her first issue got my grandchild talking over some important articles she had read with her mom, without the embarrassment and difficulty that usually occurs when teens and parents talk. The articles really relate to today's teens,and provide positive role models, something that is really needed for young girls in this day and age.
Magazine_Subscriptions.summary: They don't have to be seventeen...

Magazine_Subscriptions.reviewText:
As someone who loves to read, and finds it increasingly difficult to find time to do so in a time crunched world, I rely on Audiofile magazine to point me in the direction of what will provide a great listening experience. It provides reviews which I find are very accurate and illuminating. Through the magazine I have been guided to many authors, narrators and subjects that I might previously have been unaware of, or overlooked. The review section covers several different categories of book in every issue, describing content, and highlighting excellence. Sometimes the authors of a book will be interviewed with the review of a narrators work side by side. This I find fascinating.

The articles give an insider look at an ever changing industry, and "connect up the dots" of this fascinating, mysterious world by discussing anything and everything that is audiobook related.

Audiofile is the only place I can count on  to recieve accurate information about  this growing and rapidly changing industry, that remains largely unsung elsewhere. It is a highlight when I recieve the latest copy, go through it and plan what I am going to listen to next. It has led me to many works I might never have considerd and helps me follow my favorite narrators,  audio related events etc. Whether you are an everyday listener or an industry professional,AudioFile is a lifeline! Life would be a lot duller without this irreplaceable guide.
Magazine_Subscriptions.summary: A must  for all lovers of the spoken word

Magazine_Subscriptions.reviewText: I love this magazine.  I'm more of a "Real Simple" than a "Woman's Day" type of magazine aficionado.  Midwest Living gives me useful information without being unrealistic about the average person's life.  They show you how to make simple cakes and meals that don't take six hours to prepare.  They give trip itineraries that would be enjoyed by couples and families alike.  Their articles on gardening are great because they focus on my general area and don't show a lot of plants that would never grow in a cold weather state.  I think that, if you live in the mid-west, you deserve it to yourself to give the magazine a try.  Even if you don't, it's worth picking up an issue for trip and recipe ideas.

I absolutely adore this magazine!  I first learned of Femme Actuelle in 1994 while studying French in university.  A friend in France would send her copies to me in California.  The magazine covers all aspects of real French life, focusing on issues important to ever woman (and a good number of men) in France.  This is not a glamour magazine, filled with haute couture or haute cuisine that most woman would not wear or prepare.  This is an everyday magazine, filled with fashion and food recipes that you can follow with ease, all rooted in proper French style and sensibility. Each weekly publication gives the reader a window into every day French life and is almost as good as being in France. Well almost!
Magazine_Subscriptions.summary: The Magazine Most Read By Women In France

Magazine_Subscriptions.reviewText:
This is the best crochet magazine on the market today. Not only does it feature a variety or crocheted patterns, it uses easily found material that are not ultra-expensive. I love their columns and designers. I especially like the Crochet Potpourri column that lets me write in and ask other readers for particular patterns. They have been publishing for over 25 years and boy, do they do it right! I tell all my crocheting friends about this terrific magazine.

Stella

This is my 4th year having subscribed to this prayer book. It has the daily reading from the Catholic Bible, which contains more books than the Protestant version, and in three years, if read daily you will have read the whole bible. It has morning, Mass, afternoon and evening prayers, plus the saint of the day, benediction and a specific special old masterpiece art with background of of work and artist. A very special prayer book all the way around!

My wife and I are voracious readers.  We read the papers every day, as well as books and magazines.  This magazine (Midwest Living) focuses on living in the Midwest but has articles and features that may be of interest to anyone no matter where you live in the U.S.  I just finished reading the June/July 2015 issue which had some interesting and informative articles and departments.  The following is just an example of the material in this magazine:
Notes of the North was about the beautiful music, art, and wilderness of the Apostle Islands in Bayfield, Wisconsin. Flower power showed some of the floral fabrics, wall papers and accessories that brighten up a home. Viva Mexican night gives 14 delicious recipes you can spice up your dinner time.  They also have shorter articles on travel, the Midwest life, discoveries, events worth writing for and reflections.  Even though this is a magazine that appeals to women more then men, it often has articles and features men might enjoy reading as well.  It is also reasonably priced at about $2.00 an issue when you subscribe.

If you live in the Midwest you might want to check out this magazine.

Rating:  4 Stars.  Joseph J. Truncale (Author:  Haiku Moments: How to read, write and enjoy haiku).
Magazine_Subscriptions.summary: An interesting and informative magazine for anyone who lives in the Midwest part of the country.

Magazine_Subscriptions.reviewText:
If your issue (pun intended) with Kindle's Popular Science offering is with the magazine itself, I would remind you that Popular Science has always been about science-for-the-non-scientist.  If you're expecting anything else, you'll be disappointed.

However, I was a subscriber to the hardcopy version of the magazine for years and recently allowed that subscription to lapse so I could get the Kindle version; same magazine, different medium.  I also discovered (pun intended) another publication which is somewhat more in depth, but Popular Science is still a good source for so-uh-whats-happenin-in-the-science-world (or a nerd-world view).

The Kindle presentation is easy to navigate and easy for these aging eyes to blow up to a readable size (tap above the page and select "text view")

I chose a less than perfect rating for this magazine because if you are new to quilting you might want to buy this magazine and stash it for later use as you learn new techniques and move your way up to some of these tougher quilts patterns. Instructions are very good but you will need some experience to work your way through most of these quilts featured in this journal. But we all had to start somewhere. So go ahead and use it as that goal you are working your way towards meeting. Dreaming about quilts it called inspiration and this journal will give you plenty of that.
Magazine_Subscriptions.summary: Not for beginners but dare to dream...

Magazine_Subscriptions.reviewText: I LOVE "Real Simple".  When I was growing up, my mother read "Family Circle" and "Women's Day" -- magazines that seem hopelessly dated.  For me, this is the modern, classy equivalent.  RS offers cleaning tips, decorating tricks, and recipes, but the recipes span American classics and a wide range of ethnic cooking. It provides practical advice that many of us should have learned from our parents but didn't, like how to handle a confrontation or comfort a grieving friend.  The photography is gorgeous and the amount of content has been increasing as the magazine gets to its feet (I've been a subscriber from the first issue).  Sure, some articles are simplistic and naive, but I don't mind paging through them to find the gems.
Magazine_Subscriptions.summary: Upscale, worldly but domestic mag for women

Magazine_Subscriptions.reviewText: love this though I wish it would come out more I know science is not a fast moving subject though many think it should be and as we progress we regress, wish they would also cover some of the history of science in it.. would help a lot I think if people were also shown the x before the y and as to how we come to z.
Magazine_Subscriptions.summary: love this though I wish it would come out more ...

Magazine_Subscriptions.reviewText: I love to cross stitch! I've always had a problem that most of the cross stitch magazines out there are ones that feature designs/charts that are of no interest to me. I was very near giving up buying any more of them but something has drawn me to Cross Stitch Gold. I ordered a subscription and boy was I shocked.  I found project after project that interested me!! I would strongly suggest that if you're looking for a cross stitch magazine, don't let the price worry you. I'm certain there will always be a few objects in each issue that will want to stitch!

I'm viewing the magazine on an iPad 3 using the Kindle app. Images and text looks great. Can zoom too. I only have one issue that I downloaded so far and reading the reviews for Star and US, I'm hoping my issues come on time. The only thing I was hoping for, is that have the websites in the magazine can be actual links that I can go directly to the ads website. Do that and it will be a 5 star review!

Ok, you can say that Downbeat reviews are neglectable for a top Jazz addicted reader.

Also forget those unnecessary annual reader's polls and reviewers' polls, another neglectable part of Downbeat historical existence.

Suppose I am a Jazz instrumentalist or singer and I claim desperately for success. Then suppose I buy some 50 Downbeat subscriptions and distribute them as a gift to 50 different people under the condition they vote for me in the reader's annual poll. Well the game's quite ready for my career to be launched under Downbeat's poll parameters. Be sure I would hit a wonderful position in the poll and Downbeat would not have any chance to contest it. Quite fragile!

The good side is that there's a lot of good and updated information on albums, performances and artists. Also a good interview in each issue. Also the interesting Blindfold Test which exposes an artist to his memory capacity to idendify peers' recordings.

That's Downbeat, not the best, not the worst of Jazz magazines.
Magazine_Subscriptions.summary: Downbeat is what one should expect from a Jazz magazine

Magazine_Subscriptions.reviewText:
I am giving Esquire four stars because it is so cheap, and occasionally features well written award winning articles. In general, each issue is filled with ads that serve to subsidize the cost of the magazine to subscribers. Which is why I am getting this magazine at less than $0.40 an issue, which doesn't even cover postage. I subscribe to Esquire for the occasional article that is insightful and illuminating. You get what you pay for.

Pros
- Cheap
- Literary Tradition
- Occasionally features well written articles

Cons
- Full of Ads
- Most articles are boring

Who doesn't want to look her best????  Yes this magazine does use space to talk about clothes and looking good.  One of my favorite fashion pages is where they have three different readers/models wear an outfit and comment on it.  All the women are over 40 and the comments aren't always flattering - it seems real.  There also is some serious commentary and subjects broached that overall appeals to women over 40 and other intelligent people.  I don't believe that if you are a woman over 40 you will regret subscribing to this publication.  Just flip through an issue at the newstand and you will be convinced.
Magazine_Subscriptions.summary: Well over 40 and LOVE this magazine......

Magazine_Subscriptions.reviewText:
I absolutely love having Slate delivered to my Kindle.  Each morning it's like a treat waiting for me, a great companion on the train or bus to the office.  The writing is fantastic:  left-leaning and intelligent, just how i like it.  :-)

I know that I can read Slate for free on the web, but it's so much more pleasant to read on a Kindle screen (and have it available underground in the subway)... it's absolutely worth the 8 cents per day!

Great magazine but in Australia I have almost annual subscription problems and I have been subscribing for 10 years.  Neodata/Road and Track almost every year seem to not send me January, February and/or March editions until I notice they are missing and complain. They don't seem to have many back issues and they are hard to find in Australia. They keep suggesting I change to a digital subscription but that is not what I want. if it wasn't for these ongoing subscription issues I would have scored it a five.
Magazine_Subscriptions.summary: One of the World's Greatest Car Magazine but Unreliable Subcription Service

Magazine_Subscriptions.reviewText:
My son is 8 and a sports freak.  When this magazine arrives in the mailbox, he jumps on it and reads every word.  It helps him stay up on the latest so he can be the "expert" out on the playground!

As a mom, one thing I like about this magazine is that in addition to covering the major sports (baseball, football, etc.) they also have features about less common sports from time to time.

I wish there was a bit less advertising, of course, which is why I gave it 4 stars instead of 5.  But it's much better than some other kids mags I've seen.

I thought about buying regular Sports Illustrated for my son.  He's an advanced reader and would be able to keep up, and it's certainly a better deal money-wise, what with it being a weekly publication.  But another reviewer made a great comment here that I changed my mind: adult SI has lots of articles about athletes with drugs, personal life issues (divorce or whatnot), legal issues and so forth.  These are not interesting or appropriate for my little boy.  He doesn't want a scandal sheet, he just wants to read about *sports*, and that's the focus in SI for Kids.

(PS: based on other reviews for this and other magazines here on Amazon, I have taken to ordering all magazines directly from the publisher.  I hope Amazon starts carrying more reliable magazine distributors because it would be nice to handle all my subs right here.)
Magazine_Subscriptions.summary: one of the better kids' magazines

Magazine_Subscriptions.reviewText:
Bottom-line: "Money Magazine" is my new personal financial advisor and hopefully its sage advice will help me navigate the pitfalls of personal investing.

Okay, I'll admit it my latest job move left us with a little more disposable income, and a pay raise last month helped immensely. So we now have more money to invest, but I do not want to pay someone to do it for me, I want to keep my hands on my own stash thank you very much. But I will admit I need practical advice on where to invest my money, not only for retirement, but for my 11-year-old's college education.

I briefly though about subscribing to Fortune Magazine, but quickly dismissed the magazine: too upscale with little practical advice to the average middle class American. I have long read the Money Magazine section on CNN.com, and found the information timely and utilitarian in the extreme. So I decided to subscribe to the print edition.

"Money Magazine," which bills itself as the magazine "For you, your family, your f... Read more
Magazine_Subscriptions.summary: Every Amateur Investor Should Subscribe; Information You Can Actually Use

It's a fun read - like talking with a lot of friends about fashion trends, make-up, recipes, etc.

My favorite is the advice - love Martha Beck.  Haven't seen Dr. Phil in the last issue or so.  Wonder if Oprah dropped his column.

So, it's a fun skim.  Like the upbeat, positive articles.  It's a feel-good magazine.

My elderly grandmother picked this out for our then-7-year-old son and we have continued the subscription for about 2 years now. Magazine_Subscriptions.summary: My 97 year old grandmother picked this out as a gift for our 7 year old son.

Magazine_Subscriptions.reviewText:
I like this magazine because it actually TEACHES you about cooking.  By explaining what different types of ingredients and cooking techniques DO, it helps you learn how to cook better with or without a recipe.  It's really nice not to be married to my cookbook every moment.
Also, while there are many recipes too complicated for me personally, there are at least 3 recipes per issue that are things I can use.  Those that I am not likely to use are good anyway, because by reading the text about the cooking methods I can learn techniques to use in other dishes.
The only thing I don't like, and this is the reason I will not renew this year is that the emphasis is entirely on taste and appearance of food.  Concequently, I often end up with great tasting, beautiful, extremely fattening or calorie laden food.  So for those of us who are health conscious, it is harder to use this one on a regular basis.  If I could afford more than one cooking magazine, I'd keep this one, but since I can't, I'll try something new.

This magazine makes a good addition to my PC World Magazine. They seem more devoted to the high tech then the daily "tweaking" but they do a pretty good job of filling a magazine. I think any computer geek would get something out of each issue. This is probably not for the casual occasional PC user but more for the person that isn't afraid to "open the box.

Read Shutterbug for Years and enjoyed it.

I have to compare it to the now defunct Popular Photography which was more multi-level in its approach. I think that SB recycles some of its content, too, though its s often very good material. There is a strong editorial bias, of itself not a bad thing, but this limits the magazine somewhat.

I have enjoyed it, and look forward to seeing it prosper and grow.

I've subscribed for years. The gold box price is better than I've seen elsewhere. I'm pretty up on tech stuff, but some of the articles go over my head. The articles have a bit of edge at times, but that's not necessarily bad. They will outline products that you won't find in mainline PC magazines, and give some deeper tips not seen elsewhere. I've never built a computer and am not a gamer, but knowing what the cutting edge is helps me put the mainline products in perspective. If you do build computers, put in a lot of improvements, or do a lot of gaming, this magazine is for you. For non-gamers/less intense people, there are also columns like on privacy, articles on windows tips and multimedia, reviews on software/hardware (although as commented on earlier, they do have more ads it seems in the magazine and their website has more reviews). Worth the price to try today for a year.
Magazine_Subscriptions.summary: Some of the articles are pretty deep but still worth it.

Magazine_Subscriptions.reviewText: I'm a TV nerd, I admit it and I don't want to miss anything so getting the print issue of TV Guide works great for me. I appreciate the "highlights" listed for each evenings primetime viewing and I like the grid format A LOT. At a glance I am able to see whats new for the evening so I can program my DVR quickly and get it done with. On occasion I have used the Kindle edition and found it fun too, but I much prefer the print. (Same with my books though, so take that for what it's worth, ha ha). Also as an aside I enjoy the "thumbs up/thumbs down" TV review on the back page each week too!
Magazine_Subscriptions.summary: Handy to have the print issue

Magazine_Subscriptions.reviewText: I'm not sure how many (25?)years I've been reading this magazine but it continues to be the "bible" of cycling enthusiasts.  It is slanted more towards the road rider as opposed to the mountain biker but they do publish a partner magazine entitled Mountain Bike. I've had many on and off again subscriptions only to return to reading or fantasizing about the latest toys and people's adventures on bikes. This is the time to gear up! You may see the cyclosaurus out and about in their colorful spandex outfits, bronzed bodies in all shapes and sizes, grazing on  a protein energy bar or sipping a carb loaded drink as they motor through traffic propelled by their own energy. Or you might see the cyclosaurus counterpart off road in a more trendy,  lined baggy shorts and t-shirt, sipping from a hydration pak on their backs as they kick up dust barreling down an exhilirating single track. In any event this is the time of year when weekend warriors become Lance Armstrong or Dotsie Cowden. The magazine for the cyclosaurus is Bicycling because of it's informative tidbits of information that tells you where the best organized rides are, the latest product developments, training and nuitrition tips and the exciting outdoor adventures that can only be experienced  on bike. One of the mainstay features are bike recommendations that can run the gamut from a cool $3-$5k to the more sensible priced deals at around $1,500.  Whether you want to know about the latest road shoes available, bibs, shorts, helmets, tandems, tape, tires, cages, bottles, sunglasses, tools, timers or trainers, it is all here for the cyclosaurus. Recommended for bike riders everywhere,  as Willie Nelson once sang, it just might get you back "on the road again."

History from one perspective
Reviewer: tiptoprog from Danforth, ME USA
An excellent magazine. A great way for Vietnam Vets to come to terms with the past effects of the war. Only wish that more information was forthcoming from North and South Vietnamese sources. After all, the war is over. No more need to keep up the act of patriotism and prove we were righteous, or more able than the other side. What would an American Civil War history be like if it only interviewed and told the story of the Union troops? Pretty one sided and boring, I would say. This magazine would improve if they truly became military historians, and did more interviews with the opposing forces. That's my opinion. Still a good magazine to put on your gift list this year. WELCOME HOME to all Vietnam Vets!

I have been reading Entertainment Weekly since issue #1. While I do agree with some reviewers that state that the mag we used to get was better than what they offer now, I still think its the best entertainment magazine out there. I would like to see them return to the irreverent magazine it was when it 1st hit the news stands. But there is still good reason why this magazine is still top of the heap for me. It does not sink to levels of tabloid reporting like many so called 'entertainment' magazines. I used to read TV Guide for their fall previews but have long since given up on reading TV Guide for anything other than what is on tonight. Entertainment Weekly provides me with a detailed analysis of the new shows (or the new music or the new movies) so I can make a more informed decision on what I am going to spend my time on. It has pointed me in the direction of a good TV show or an artist that I have not heard of more times than I can count. Its one of the few magazines I actually read cover to cover--and not just flip through. Entertainment Weekly fills an otherwise entertainment void in decent magazines.

I like the auto renewal...unlike other magazines that hassle and call you a year before your subscription runs out, Entertainment Weekly never bugs you about that stuff at all. Too bad other magazines do not realize that sometimes its better to stop reading their publication than to get woken up too early on a Saturday to be asked 'hows that subscription coming along, are you getting it week?'. With Entertainment Weekly, I found then never reminded me that my subscription was running out so auto renewal is king. Frankly, even that is classy.

Hopefully Entertainment Weekly will keep on producing informative, interesting issues and leave the crap to US Weekly and the Inquirer. I like my entertainment just fine with ET.
Magazine_Subscriptions.summary: still the best entertainment mag out there

Happy Reading

I don't like all the changes to Newsweek in the last couple of years, but realize that magazines are struggling to stay alive.  I rather like the one page articles - better described as editorials - and still find value in this subscription.  It is a good value for my money, but it seems every issue has less and less content - even letters to the editor are gone.  I don't utilize the website, and maybe I'm missing content I'd like, but I subscribe because magazines are portable, on your schedule, and easy to put down and later return to.  I'm just afraid that the era of magazines is dying out quickly.  It's too bad.

Magazine_Subscriptions.reviewText:
I have a Kindle Fire HD and am able to download the Android app and run it. The transition process from print to digital was not easy (and I've written about it in the Newsweek app for Android review) but the app works pretty well and seems to have all the content of the print version. If you have a KF or KFHD and are having difficulties installing the app, see the reviews for the Newsweek Android app for tips.

However, it appears that people who have a regular Kindle, not a Kindle Fire, are either seeing a different, watered-down, app or are unable to get Newsweek at all. When they announced the transition to digital, Newsweek never informed their print subscribers what devices will be supported. Under their FAQs, it says it will be available on all devices that they support! Talk about a non-answer! I assumed it would be able to get it on any type of e-reader, tablet, phone, or PC. I didn't have a Kindle at the time, but I asked for one for Christmas. Since I wanted to be able to see things in color I asked for the Kindle Fire, as opposed to the Paper White or regular Kindle. Thank goodness that was what I received, as it looks like I wouldn't have been able to receive Newsweek on the other Kindles.

I think Newsweek "customer service" treatment of their loyal base -- their print subscribers - has been appalling. Especially those Kindle owners who assumed it they would be able to receive it on their device. I don't know if Time supports all devices, but their app on the KF works pretty well and they are still in print!

I think everybody who is having a problem getting their digital edition should go onto the Newsweek Facebook page and complain publicly.  They might be ignoring the Amazon reviews and blaming any complaints on apps, but it would be hard to ignore multiple public comments on Facebook.

Those of you who have cancelled... have any of you received your refund?

This PM subscription was described by Amazon as being either a new subscription, or a continuation of an existing subscription.
In the past, PM has always just added 12 months to my current subscription.  This time however, a new subscription was started with the same name and address.
As yet I've had no response from PM apart from an automated acknowledgment (no 800 number any more so all contact is either by email or post), so I've currently no idea whether it was Amazon or PM that messed up.
If my subscription gets extended as it should then great, if not then it was a total waste of money.
The magazine itself is fine, although the content assumes the reader to be a lot dumber when compared to issues from twenty years ago (more pics, less text, and an apparent assumption that the reader has a lower IQ).

Should the subscription issue be resolved I'll amend my rating accordingly.

If you like getting phone calls while you eat dinner, order National Geographic. While I was looking forward to the great photography, I regret ordering a subscription to NatGeo. Be warned, they will call you while you eat, to pitch "we will you send you a free world map, and a video and if you choose to keep the video, we will only charge you $.$$"
After a long day of answering phones at work, I don't want my home phone to ring. But NatGeo will call, they will call again, sometimes they'll just hang up on you, sometimes they'll pitch a product.
With many print publications dying off due to the internet, it's amazing that NatGeo is driving customers away by becoming a 400 lb gorilla.
And if they call my house again, I will cancel my subscription, take the loss and call it a lesson learned. (and then begin reporting to the no phone sales administration.
Really sick of it.

Magazine_Subscriptions.reviewText:

I was so excited that this magazine was coming out and I subscribed without bothering to see the first isssue. I'm sure some people will find it beneficial, but I want more. I'd save my subscription money and perhaps buy it off the rack if it is relevant on occasion.

I will not be renewing because I'm very disappointed in the content and quality of this magazine. It has so much potential, but falls drastically short. The content rarely, if at all, has enough information to be valuable in any category. The articles are short and not in depth enough to make an impact. The advice columns border on irresponsible and tacky. In some cases, I can't believe that the advisor is a qualified expert as they state. I still think Military Spouse could raise itself up and be an excellent magazine, but I will not buy it until I see that it has done so.

I've read and have been a subscriber for years. Vegetarian for most of my life.
The magazine goes through editors like we go through soy milk. They just can't find their way it seems.
These days, most recipes call for expensive and / or hard to find ingredients. Worse, some call for pre-made items that just can't be found. Case in point, the latest issue with the very yummy looking pizza on the cover? You will not find the recipe for the crust in the magazine. Funny, eh? Also, the magazine, for the most part, ignores the male reader.

After all this time, I'm saying farewell to VT. With a host of wonderful blogs on the net, and amazing cooks who generously share there "secrets", I'll save the trees it takes to produce this advertising biased magazine.

Update 7/3/12
The magazine now sells ad space that highlight items that are NOT vegetarian. (Solgar No. 7, in the most recent issue.)
Magazine_Subscriptions.summary: Where money is more important than values.

Magazine_Subscriptions.reviewText: I have been a loyal customer since 1999,  couldn't wait each month to receive it, then they make these changes and totally ruin everything it was all about. Not the photos alone, but EVERTHING it used to stand for. I do not even bother to take the wrapping off of it now, it goes directly into the trash can. I'm hoping to put all past issues I have (every one) in excellent condition since 1999 up for sale, 5000.00. Anyone interested?
Magazine_Subscriptions.summary: I'm hoping to put all past issues I have (every one) in excellent condition since 1999 up for sale

Magazine_Subscriptions.reviewText: I ORDERED AND PAID FOR MAGAZINES AND I HAVE NOT RECEIVED THEM ALL.  I HAVE NEVER RECEIVED THIS MAGAZINE.  I ORDERED 4 MAGAZINES, AMERICAN PHOTO, DIGITAL PHOTO, PHOTO TECHNIQUES AND SHUTTERBUG.  I HAVE NEVER RECEIVED DIGITAL PHOTO NOR THE AMERICAN PHOTO MAGAZINE.  2 OUT OF 4.  NOONE SEEMS TO BE ABLE TO HELP ME GET MY MAGAZINES OR MY MONEY BACK.  I WOULD PREFER THE MAGAZINES, BUT I WANT MY MONEY BACK IF THEY ARE NOT GOING TO SEND THEM.  I CAN'T SEEM TO GET ANYONE TO ASSIST ME.  ANY SUGGESTIONS?
Magazine_Subscriptions.summary: HARD TO REVIEW A PRODUCT I HAVE NOT RECEIVED

Magazine_Subscriptions.reviewText: WARNING!!  I was just notified by Amazon that this subscription does not include the disc that usually comes with this magazine when you buy it at the newstand.  Getting this disk and being able to play the upcoming game demos on it was one of my main reasons for subscribing.  Needless to say, I have cancelled my subscripton here and will be finding this magazine elsewhere.

I have been receiving The new republic for the past four years via my Kindle. I am annoyed that I cannot get pictures on my Kindle, in fact, I don't know if The New Republic has cartoons or pictures other than the cover. However, I always found several enlightening articles about interesting topics even if some of them were a little esoteric and academic. About a year ago the New Republic changed ownership or hired a new editor (I pay little attention to such things) unless the change affects the quality of the articles. I gave the subscription several months to return to articles that I could relate to and finally had to cancel. I say this for the New Republics benefit. I believe this country needs publications that lean slightly left from writers that have credibility , but the articles I have been reading lately gives credence to the term "pointy headed liberal". Or maybe the world is just passing me by.

I'm not one of those people that enjoys putting 1 star on everything out of spite, but honestly, if the thing won't download, how can I give it any stars at all?  I went round and round with "customer service" during the previous iteration of the app, and I'm not willing to go there again.

UPDATE 2/19/14
Shortly after my original review, Amazon contacted me out of the blue thinking I must have a technical glitch.  I never heard the outcome of that effort, but the n+1 issue seemed to be working fine, so I had meaning to increase my rating.  BUT I wasn't done reading the n+1 issue when the n+2 issue downloaded itself, SO NOW I CAN'T FINISH THE PREVIOUS ISSUE.  The  app still prevents me from reading the magazine, so it stays at 1 star.

I've been an Analog subscriber on and off for years, both paper and Kindle digital editions. I just canceled my subscription because they have just published a guest editorial in the October issue written by Stanley Schmidt that is overtly partisan politically oriented. It is essentially a primer on how incremental political ideology can lead a nation down the path to ruin. It is backed up by a detailed example of how Hitler and National Socialism condemned Germany. And, lastly, it warns that a vote for a particular candidate (as of April, 2016), unnamed, will take us down the same path.

At my age, I do not subscribe to Analog to start getting bombarded by partisan political commentary. It has been difficult enough trying to ignore the stories that have a biased liberal agenda that have emerged in the last year or two, but now they have crossed the line.

This item found its way onto my kindle after some free 'trial subscription'. I had not used my kindle in over a month only to pick it up and find this item. Then I cancelled it and somehow the biweekly newsletter got added. Was super pissed that I had to call and have this issue fixed. Beware of 'trial subscriptions' that automatically assume you want them because you didn't specifically decline them...especially if you ever go periods of time not using your kindle.
Magazine_Subscriptions.summary: Somehow this downloaded itself onto my kindle

Magazine_Subscriptions.reviewText: I got a subscription to this magazine, but they only sent me a copy every other month! I ended up getting only 6 issues when I paid for 12! I am sure of this because I saved every issue I got just to make sure. Also, in the September issue, on page 14, you can clearly see that MaryKate's lower back isn't real. It was edited. This magazine doesn't focus on anything interesting and it isn't good for older teens. I would never recommend this magazine to anyone!

I would look at getting your magazines from another website.  The description says 4-6 weeks, but I placed my order on March 8 with an estimated first magazine of May 2--more like 7-9 weeks.  Or is that 4-6 weeks to send my subscription to ESPN?  This is what happens when you try to save a couple of dollars by not going straight to the source.  If my first ESPN magazine actually arrives by May 2, I will give them back a star.

I've been reading Prevention in analog for decades and love the content, this review is for the digital version of the magazine... recently I have issue with the publisher not providing large type subscriptions, I thought a kindle version would solve that problem but no... The kindle version is worse!!!  You can't enlarge the pages in this "interactive" magazine nor can you adjust the type (not so interactive after all). I love kindle because I can adjust the font size for easier and more relaxed reading, and the "reading" tab in web pages makes surfing online so much more enjoyable.  Amazon do find a way to make digital magazines as accessible to older users as your e-books...please!

Don't sign up for the auto renewal.  I enjoy the magazine, but the auto renewal charged a business card and not my personal card since that was the last card I used to purchase something.  Now, I have to jump through all kinds of hoops to fix this and hope that it doesn't look like I am using a corporate card for personal expenses.  I had used the business card to get some prizes for a fun day for kids we were organizing.  I did not know it was going to stay on my account.

This  magazine focuses soooooo hard on making women over 40 feel young that it actually makes me feel old!
Can't stand this magazine.  Need the pertinent and relevant issues for a professional woman 40+ but don't need to read how to feel better about not being under 40.  This magazine should find a way to stop making excuses and finding justification for getting old.
Magazine_Subscriptions.summary: Ugh, could you be any older?

Magazine_Subscriptions.reviewText: I thought I'd give this a shot, right along with Details and The New Yorker, because of the free trial. Gotta say I'm very disappointed in it. Yes, it's fast and easy to use and the pictures look great but you can't read the articles without constantly zooming and scrolling. Plus, you have to scroll past countless ads just to get to any content. Maxim on the Fire is useless if you want to comfortably read the magazine. But if all you want are the pictures, then it's great. I gave it two stars instead of one because the photos look great. If I was rating it on legibility, then I'd have to go with one star. Compare this to The New Yorker, which is an app, and you'll see the difference between a great layout for the Fire and a horrible one.
Magazine_Subscriptions.summary: Can't read articles and way too many ads

Magazine_Subscriptions.reviewText: I cut Fast Company out of my magazine rotation after subscribing for 1.5 years and realizing the stack in the corner had given me all of about 20 minutes of reading enjoyment. Just not a good cost benefit ratio when i did my analysis...it reads more like a news feed than an in depth look at anything. A few bookmarked sites gives me the same "insights" at no cost or paper waste. For a magazine with such a environmental bent, you would think the editors would make better use of the precious paper they print on.

I have been reading Selling Power from the public library near my office and decided I should not be jostling with others for the latest copy, so I subscribed through Amazon in September this year.
3 months later, I have yet to receive my first copy and Amazon replied via email that my order was lost and they have re-processed it so I would have to wait 4-6 weeks again. As of today, I am still waiting for my 1st copy due to arrive in another month (hopefully).
I was outraged and they have refunded me a portion of the subscription (which isn't much, it still frustrates why can't they just do an express delivery?). I am not sure if this is the fault of Amazon or the publisher but looks like their motto is to sell well and forget about aftersales!

this magazine has waaay toooo much advertising. the articles are lame, i ordered a subscription after reading a issue somewhere, must have been their 1 good issue. I think i have 3 or 4 of the newest ones laying around somewhere, i don't even think they are worth my time now to read. however, if you need something to start your campfires, order this now. no one will be upset when you burn it.

I've been a subscriber since 1993, and I have kept every issue. Not sure why. Oh yes. It allows me to contrast the magazine's "classic" period with its current period - and it's not pretty. It's largely a fawning journal for fanboys. Maybe that's a reflection of the comicbook-driven decline of theatrical releases. Gone are the insightful stories. Now it's all "ironic" hipster-doofus commentary. The music section has largely disappeared, again likely a reflection of the industry's decline. I renewed my subscription for my wife's benefit.

Ordered this for my niece as a gift. They mistakenly sent the first issue to me (billing address) instead of my niece. I emailed to correct the problem. They said they would update the address, but said the October issue would also go to my address. The address correction would be for issues after that one. It's August! I'm cancelling the subscription and getting her a subscription to Animal Baby instead. My niece's older sister loved that one and I never had any issues with them.

All you is filled with advertisements, if thats what you want.  Very little in terms of actual substance.  Their secrets and tips are usually in reference to certain products and services to buy.  I've had this subscription for 6 months and haven't used more than 1 coupon contained in the mag. I would say this magazine is "nice" and "average"; Not much changes from issue to issue.  I enjoyed the first magazines, but now its just rehashing the same information and changing it per holiday or season. July - Try X Generic grilling recipe in summer, try bland soup for fall, and add bacon.  I will not renew this subscription when it runs out.

I live in Northwest Montana and have lived rurally in the area for 6 1/2 years.  I thought I was a Country Woman.  I thought the articles and particularly recipes were outdated.  Specifically, recipes using a considerable amount of processed (canned or boxed) ingredients vs local/seasonal/fresh (or home canned and frozen).  I kept turning the page and suddenly was at the end.  Ultimately, nothing to interest me or entice me to buy another issue.

It is  one of the best sell signals available - an excellent indicator for identifying stocks at their peak.
I used Money as a good place to get short ideas based on their (long) recommendations. I am surprised the magazine still exists with the poor (and late) stock recommendations it consistently offers up.

Magazine_Subscriptions.reviewText:
After several years of subscribing to Yoga Journal, I finally cancelled my subscription because the magazine has evolved into almost no yoga-related content (mindfulness, philosophy, better living) and is almost exclusively poses and product tie-ins related to Yoga Journal and/or their sponsors (articles about Yoga Journal tours, reviews of Yoga Journal sponsor resorts and trips, interviews with teachers of Yoga Journal classes, etc.). Gone are all the great articles about meditation, healthy mind-body, different yoga-related philosophies, etc.

I wound up subscribing to "Mindful Magazine" instead and it's more of what I was looking for. (What I *truly* wish is that Body and Soul magazine would come back. Anyone remember that one?)
Magazine_Subscriptions.summary: just a bunch of ads and photos of poses. No content.

Magazine_Subscriptions.reviewText: All I got was a bunch of colorful advertisements for different supplements. There were plenty of pictures and the occasional attractive female, but I learned how to read. Then it got into the sport and sometimes you got to read about exercises. I did a cycle of this mag. It just repeats itself. It got old and I felt like I just paid to get advertised to. They should have paid me to read this magazine.

When I was a teenager, this was the magazine to have. It was great reading to nourish my mind and imagination. Today, it seems as much a liberal propaganda machine as a science magazine. The thing is riddled with advertisements and liberal propaganda disguised as "science." Most of their articles on engineering and true sciences seem quite basic and uninformative now.. but maybe it's because I have multiple degrees in the sciences.. who is to know.

I got this magazine from unused airline miles and definitely regret getting it. 75% of the pages are for ads (fancy Iranian carpets, dinner sets, antique furniture blah blah). The design articles and photos seem to be for (a) the newly rich lottery winner or (b) middle class folk who may spend all their time fantasising about a wealthy lifestyle.

Avoid this magazine and you will be saving some trees.

I used to buy this off the shelf each month, but last November, my wife bought me a subscription.  I bought the December issue,...cause it hadn't arrived by mail yet. No problem.  In January, I received the November issue.  A few weeks later, in early February, I received the December issue, but not the January, so I went out and bought the January.  By the end of February, still hadn't received the Feb yet, so bought it.  Then, received the January issue and a few weeks later the February.  I was fed up.  I know they were getting 'caught up', but not only was I getting editions that I'd already bought off the shelf, but I figured these were counting against my 12 issues.  I cancelled.  They deducted a few bucks from my refund for "issues received" and had no apologies for the mess.

I like the magazine, but I will say that if you read it over time, it become redundant.  The suggested work-outs are mostly rehashes of past work-out routines.  Lets face it...there are only so many ways to work out and when you get right down to it, you gotta hit it hard and often, change things up, etc...bla bla bla...  The BEST part of the magazine are the few pages they dedicate to the correct way to execute a lift or detail what muscles are hit.  Lots of Weider ads...but then its a Weider publication, so what can you expect...

I'd buy it off the shelf because you'll eventually get tired of the same old thing...and their subscription program is iffy.

-D
